    Semifinals Web-Based Challenge

    jump:start-web-challenge

    Prepare for the Web-Based Challenge

    1. Pick one teammate to own it at Semifinals (Platinum and Gold tiers).
    2. Learn browser developer tools: page source, Inspector, Network tab and the cookie view.
    3. Learn the HTTP basics and the common encodings in the table below.
    4. Play the web and general skills categories on picoCTF and the first OverTheWire Natas levels each week.
    5. Read the Semifinals round instructions for the challenge's rules and allowed tools.

    #What it is

    Fact Source
    80 points at Semifinals, Platinum and Gold tiers (Silver does not have it) Official CP-19 challenges page; same in CP-18
    Platinum only in CP-15, CP-16 and CP-17 CyberSentinel newsletters
    Described as a "CTF-like challenge" Wikipedia's CyberPatriot article

    CyberPatriot has not published the format. Expect a set of web-based puzzles that each yield an answer or flag, done in the same 4-hour window as the images. At 80 points it is worth almost as much as one image, so treat it as a fourth image for one person.

    #Skills to build

    #Read a web page like a defender

    • View the source (Ctrl+U) and read the HTML comments, hidden form fields and linked script files.
    • Open developer tools (F12): the Inspector shows the live page, the Console shows script errors, and the Network tab shows every request and response with headers.
    • Check /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml; they list paths the site owner did not want indexed.

    #HTTP basics

    Thing Know
    Methods GET reads, POST submits, and a few others (PUT, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS)
    Status codes 200 OK, 301/302 redirect, 401 needs login, 403 forbidden, 404 not found, 500 server error
    Headers Host, User-Agent, Cookie, Set-Cookie, Location, Server, Content-Type
    Query string and form data Name=value pairs after ? or in the POST body

    Read a site's response headers from a Linux terminal:

    curl -sI <url>

    Read the raw page:

    curl -s <url> | less

    #Cookies and sessions

    • Cookies are name=value pairs the browser sends back with every request. Developer tools > Storage (Firefox) or Application (Chrome) shows them.
    • A session cookie identifies a logged-in user. Weak sites store readable data (a username, admin=false) in a cookie, which is why servers must never trust it.
    • A JSON Web Token is three Base64URL parts joined by dots: header, payload and signature. Decode the first two to read them.

    #Encodings and hashes

    Looks like Is Decode with
    %20, %3D URL encoding CyberChef "URL Decode"
    &lt;, &#65; HTML entities CyberChef "From HTML Entity"
    Ends in =, letters and digits Base64 Decoder, base64 -d
    32, 40 or 64 hex characters MD5, SHA-1 or SHA-256 hash Hashes are one-way; look for the original text elsewhere

    More decoding steps: Decode hidden text.

    #Common web weaknesses at a concept level

    Learn what each weakness is and how a developer prevents it. The OWASP Top 10 is the standard list.

    Weakness What goes wrong How it is prevented
    Broken access control A page or file is reachable without the right login Check permissions on the server for every request
    Injection (SQL, command) User input is run as code Parameterized queries, input validation
    Cross-site scripting (XSS) User input is shown as HTML or script Output encoding
    Security misconfiguration Debug pages, default passwords, directory listing, phpinfo Hardening, the same work as on the images
    Sensitive data exposure Secrets in page source, comments or backup files Keep secrets server-side
    Client-side checks only A rule enforced only by the browser's JavaScript Enforce it on the server

    #Practice resources

    Resource Use it for
    picoCTF (picoctf.org), picoGym Web Exploitation and General Skills problems, built for high school students
    OverTheWire Natas Web security levels, one password per level
    OverTheWire Bandit Linux command-line skills, also helps the Linux images
    PortSwigger Web Security Academy Free lessons and labs for every OWASP category
    OWASP Juice Shop A deliberately insecure web shop you run on your own machine
    CyberChef Decoding and encoding practice

    Practice only on these platforms and on machines you own. Testing a real website without permission is illegal and breaks the CyberPatriot Code of Conduct.

    #During the challenge

    • Read every question first and do the quick ones.
    • Time-box each question to 15 minutes, then move on and come back.
    • Keep notes of every URL, cookie and decoded string; answers often chain.
    • Allowed resources follow the round rules: no AI tools, no outside help (rules).

    National Finals and how to prepare

    jump:start-nationals

    Prepare for National Finals

    1. Give every image an owner and name one person who tracks and writes injects.
    2. Practice every image with no scripts; Finals ban them.
    3. Drill a service check every 15 minutes on each critical service.
    4. Write practice inject replies against a 30-minute deadline.
    5. Practice with a teammate attacking a practice image while you defend it.

    #What National Finals involves

    CP-19 National Finals run March 12-16, 2027, in person in Maryland, for qualifying Platinum teams. The CP-19 components are not published yet. The last three Finals used:

    Component What teams did (CP-16 to CP-18)
    Network Security Master Challenge Administer a small business network of several images: find and fix vulnerabilities, keep critical services running, answer business injects, and defend against a live Red Team
    Cisco NetAcad Challenge A networking quiz and a hands-on networking exercise
    Boeing Cyber-Physical System Challenge CP-16 and CP-17 only: secure an operational flight-information system

    A secondary CP-19 guide states that scripts are banned at the Finals, which matches the rules summary.

    #Split the work

    Job Does
    Image owners (one per image, usually three or four people) Harden their image, watch its services and logs
    Inject handler Reads every inject, assigns it, writes or edits the reply, tracks deadlines
    Network and Cisco Runs the Cisco challenge and helps with network-level problems
    Floater Checks services across all images, takes over an image when its owner works an inject

    With five people, the inject handler and floater are usually one person who also owns no image during busy periods.

    #Write business injects

    An inject is a task from "management" with a deadline: write a policy, produce a report, add a user, open a service. Graders read it as a business document.

    1. Read the whole inject and list every deliverable.
    2. Do the technical part first, then write the reply.
    3. Answer exactly what was asked, in plain business language, with evidence (commands run, results, screenshots if allowed).
    4. Submit before the deadline. A short, complete reply on time beats a long late one.

    Reply template:

    To:
From: Team <team-number>
Date:
Subject: Re: <inject-title>

Summary: what was done, in one or two sentences.

Details:
1.
2.

Verification: how we confirmed it works.
Next steps or recommendations:

    #Keep services up

    Check every critical service on a schedule and right after every change.

    Get-Service <service-name> | Select-Object Name, Status, StartType

    Restart it:

    Restart-Service <service-name>

    systemctl is-active <service-name>

    Restart it:

    sudo systemctl restart <service-name>

    Test it from outside too: browse to the website, log in over SSH, open the share from another image.

    #Watch for the red team

    Look for changes since your last check: new users, new admins, new listening ports, new scheduled tasks or cron jobs, and logins you did not make.

    Listening ports with their process IDs:

    Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen | Sort-Object LocalPort | Select-Object LocalAddress, LocalPort, OwningProcess

    Who is logged in:

    query user

    Members of Administrators:

    Get-LocalGroupMember Administrators

    sudo ss -tulpn

    who

    getent group sudo

    Follow the system log live:

    sudo journalctl -f

    When you find something: record it, remove it, change the passwords it could have used, and look for how it got in. The hunting steps are in Windows malware, Linux persistence and AD attacks.

    #Practice for Finals

    • Run full images by hand from the checklists, timed. Without scripts you need the commands in your head or on paper.
    • Have one teammate add a backdoor user, a cron job or a scheduled task to a practice image you are defending, then find it.
    • Write one inject reply per practice session.
    • Keep the Cisco skills current: the Finals Cisco challenge has a hands-on part (Packet Tracer checklist).

    Study plan to State and Semifinals

    jump:start-study-plan

    This week

    1. Sit Round 1 (October 22-25) on Windows 11, Mint 21 and the Cisco pieces.
    2. Save every scoring-report line from both images before the images close.
    3. Paste those lines into the line lookup in Tools and start each person's missed list.
    4. Ask the coach to download the Training Round 2 images when they open on October 30.

    #Team setup for five people

    Give each person a main and a second area so every image has a backup.

    Person Main area Second area Round 2 seat State seat Semifinals seat
    1 Windows 11 and 10 Server Windows 11 Server 2022 with person 2, then Cisco quiz Server 2019
    2 Server and Active Directory Windows Server 2022 Server 2022 Server 2022
    3 Linux Mint Ubuntu Mint 21 Mint 21 Mint 21
    4 Ubuntu and Debian, forensics Web challenge Forensics help on all images Ubuntu 24 Web-Based Challenge (Platinum and Gold), forensics help
    5 Cisco quiz and Packet Tracer Linux Cisco quiz and Packet Tracer Packet Tracer (70) and quiz (30) Packet Tracer and quiz

    Adjust to your people. The State and Semifinals seats follow the official round content in What is in each round.

    #Weekly sessions

    • One short session (about 2 hours) on a weekday: each person runs one image or Cisco topic and reviews it with the key.
    • One long session on the weekend every other week: a full 4-hour team mock of the next round.
    • Everyone reads their missed list before each session (practice method).

    #Week by week

    Week of Round events Images (persons 1-4) Cisco and web (person 5, person 4)
    Oct 19 Round 1, Oct 22-25 Round 1, then save all report lines Round 1 quiz (modules 3-7) and Packet Tracer (1-7)
    Oct 26 Training Round 2 opens Oct 30 Debrief Round 1 with the line lookup; first TR2 image on your main OS Modules 8-9 (net-m8-network-layer)
    Nov 2 TR2: Server 2019 (persons 1 and 2, standing in for Server 2022), Mint 21 (3), Ubuntu 22 (4). Weekend: 4-hour Round 2 mock with Windows 10, Server 2019 and Mint 21 Modules 10-11 and 21-22 (record the real titles from the Content Course); Packet Tracer 1-11
    Nov 9 Round 2, Nov 12-15 Read missed lists and the penalty sections; no new topics Subnetting drills, then Round 2
    Nov 16 Tiers announced after Round 2 Debrief Round 2. Person 4 starts Ubuntu (lin-ubuntu); person 1 starts Server as second seat Modules 12-13 (IPv6, ICMP)
    Nov 23 Thanksgiving week One session: everyone replays one TR2 image on their second area Module 14 (transport layer); forensics drills for all (question types)
    Nov 30 Weekend: 4-hour State mock with Server 2019, Mint 21 and Ubuntu 22 at the same time Modules 15-16; the Skills Integration Challenge from module 17
    Dec 7 State Round, Dec 10-13 Missed lists, penalties, README traps Module 17 (net-m17-small-network), then State
    Dec 14 Debrief State. Persons 1 and 2 start two-server work (srv-2019-vs-2022, srv-ad-attacks) Modules 18-20 and 23 (titles from the Content Course); person 4 starts web prep (Web-Based Challenge)
    Dec 21 Winter break Optional: one replay each, on the hardest image you have picoCTF web problems; Packet Tracer review
    Dec 28 Winter break Optional: hidden-item hunting drill (Scoring patterns) OverTheWire Natas; Packet Tracer 1-23 review
    Jan 4 Weekend: Semifinals mock 1 with Mint 21, Server 2022-style and Server 2019 at once Full Packet Tracer activity under time; one web practice set
    Jan 11 Semifinals mock 2 on team-made images with planted persistence; final review of penalties Weakest modules only
    Jan 18 Semifinals, Jan 21-23 (Thursday to Saturday); TR2 closes Jan 19 Missed lists and README traps only Rest the day before

    If your team qualifies for National Finals (March 12-16, 2027), switch to the Finals preparation in February: script-free image runs, inject writing and red team drills.

    #Cross-training

    • Every person must be able to run the first 15 minutes on Windows, Server and Linux (first 15 minutes).
    • Once a month, swap images for a whole session.
    • Pair the Cisco person with a second person for the State Round, where the Cisco pieces are worth 100 points.

    Planner rules for Windows 11 and 10

    jump:start-plan-windows

    Every rule the Image planner can show, grouped by what triggers it. Level tags show the first round where the rule matters: R1, R2, State, Semis, Nats.

    #Any Windows image

    • Don't R1+ Do not uninstall Microsoft Edge or the default browser even when the README does not list a browser. Removing a system component wastes time and can break the image. See Chrome and Edge.
    • Do R1+ Run the read-only PowerShell recon report and save its output before fixing anything. A baseline of users, services, ports and tasks shows what changed later and what is planted. See Read-only recon report, First 10 minutes.
    • Do R1+ Search C:\Users and shared folders for media files (mp3, mp4, wav, flac, avi, mov) and delete the files, keeping the folders. Removed prohibited MP3 files is on most Windows keys. See Find media files in user folders, Search the whole C: drive for media.
    • Do R1+ Uninstall Wireshark, Nmap, NetStumbler and similar network tools when the README does not require them. (not: README allows security tools) Removed Wireshark, Nmap and NetStumbler were scored on several keys. See Network tools.
    • Do R1+ Walk the Windows checklist final pass and confirm required apps are still in their default folders. Moved or missing required software is a penalty. See Final pass, Stop penalties before they happen.
    • Do R2+ Uninstall developer or AI coding apps the README does not authorize. (not: README requires developer tools) Removed Cursor was a scored unwanted software item. See Games and unapproved apps, List installed programs.
    • Check R2+ Check Run and RunOnce keys, startup folders, scheduled tasks and services running from user or temp folders. Backdoors such as Tini and netcat were found through their persistence. See Check Run and RunOnce keys, Check scheduled tasks.
    • Check R2+ List all services, including those with odd names or descriptions, and investigate any whose binary is outside Windows or Program Files. Round 2 images add hidden services and service-based backdoors. See Check services that run from odd folders, Message in a service description.
    • Check Semis+ Check WMI event subscriptions, Image File Execution Options debuggers, Winlogon Shell and Userinit values and the hosts file. Semifinal images hide persistence in less common locations. See Check WMI event subscriptions, Image File Execution Options debugger backdoor, Check Winlogon Shell, Userinit and other boot values.
    • Check Semis+ Work through the advanced settings list (ASR rules, LLMNR and NetBIOS off, LSA protection, WDigest off, PowerShell logging). Semifinal images add obscure settings beyond the basic security options. See Extra hardening for hard images (nationals level), Turn off WDigest plaintext credentials.
    • Do Nats+ Re-list local users and the Administrators group (and AD admin groups on a domain controller) every 15 minutes and investigate any new account or member. The red team adds accounts to keep access. See Watch for the red team, List users and administrators.
    • Do Nats+ Compare netstat -abno and the process list against your baseline regularly and kill new unknown listeners and connections. Red team implants show up as new processes and outbound connections. See Watch for the red team, Find listening ports and their programs.

    #Windows 11 and 10

    • Don't R1+ Do not uninstall README-required software or reinstall it into a different folder. Removing or moving required software cost 5 points each in K1, K2, K4 and K7. See Required software removed or moved, Required software.
    • Don't R1+ Do not delete or demote an authorized user, your own account, or a user's profile folder. Deleting authorized users or home folders cost 5 to 10 points in K2, G1 and G4. See An authorized user was deleted or demoted.
    • Don't R1+ Do not set the lockout threshold below 5 unless the README gives a lower value. Thresholds of 1 to 4 were penalized in K1, K2, K4 and K7. See Set the lockout policy, Penalties seen in past Windows keys.
    • Don't R1+ Do not leave wuauserv, BITS, UsoSvc or WaaSMedicSvc disabled. Windows Update service is enabled was scored in P1 and H1. See Update services must not be disabled.
    • Don't R1+ Do not disable Windows Update, Windows Event Log, Defender, Firewall, DHCP Client, DNS Client or RPC. P1 and H1 scored keeping core services on Automatic. See Services that must stay on.
    • Don't R1+ Do not delete a whole user or program folder to remove files inside it. Removal items check the parent folder still exists. See Rules the engine follows, Delete a file or folder.
    • Do R1+ Read the whole README and write down authorized users, administrators, critical services, required software and every 'do not' line before changing anything. Every user, service and software decision on the image depends on the README. See First 15 minutes on any image, First 10 minutes, README summary template.
    • Do R1+ Keep a change log with the time, the setting and its old value, and confirm the scoring report updates before you start. Lets you undo the exact change that cost points. See Keep a change log, Reading the scoring report.
    • Do R1+ Disable the Guest account and the built-in Administrator account (unless the README says it is used) with net user <name> /active:no. The Guest account is not enabled is scored in K1, G3 and G4. See Disable the Guest account, Disable the built-in Administrator account, Leave DefaultAccount and WDAGUtilityAccount disabled.
    • Do R1+ Give every account without a password or with a weak one a strong password, except passwords the README says to keep. User has a password and Changed insecure password are scored in R2, SR1, G2 and G4. See Set a strong password on every account, Set the team password on listed users.
    • Do R1+ Clear Password never expires, Password not required and Account is locked out on every authorized account. User password expires was scored in K1 and H2; G2 tested LockedOut=false. See Fix password never expires and password not required, Clear the lockout on an account.
    • Do R1+ Set Minimum password length to 10 or more in secpol.msc or with net accounts /minpwlen:10. (not: README states password policy values) A secure minimum password length is scored in K1, K2, K4 and G4. See Set the password policy, Recommended values.
    • Do R1+ Enable Password must meet complexity requirements and disable Store passwords using reversible encryption. Complexity is scored in K1, K4 and P1; reversible encryption in K1, R2, SR1 and P1. See Turn on complexity and turn off reversible encryption.
    • Do R1+ Set Maximum password age to 90 days, Minimum password age to 1 day and Enforce password history to 5. (not: README states password policy values) Ages and history were scored in K2, R1, SR1, G2, G3, G4 and N1. See Set the password policy, Recommended values.
    • Do R1+ Set Account lockout threshold to 10, lockout duration to 30 minutes and reset counter after 30 minutes. (not: README states password policy values) Threshold, duration and window are scored (K4, R1, R2, G3). See Set the lockout policy.
    • Do R1+ Run auditpol /set /category:* /success:enable /failure:enable. Audit items (Credential Validation, account logon) are scored in K4, SR1 and G2. See Turn on all auditing with auditpol, Audit success and failure for everything.
    • Do R1+ Enable Accounts: Limit local account use of blank passwords to console logon only (LimitBlankPasswordUse=1). Scored in R1, SR1, G2 and N1. See Limit blank passwords to console logon.
    • Do R1+ Enable both Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts options and disable Let Everyone permissions apply to anonymous users. SAM enumeration was scored in R1 and N1; the Everyone option in P1. See Block anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares, Stop Everyone permissions applying to anonymous users.
    • Do R1+ Set Interactive logon: Do not require CTRL+ALT+DEL to Disabled (DisableCAD=0). Scored in K1, R2 and G3. See Require CTRL+ALT+DEL at sign-in.
    • Do R1+ Turn UAC on at Always notify (EnableLUA=1, ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin=2, PromptOnSecureDesktop=1). UAC options appear in G2 and P1. See Set UAC to Always notify, User Account Control options.
    • Do R1+ Turn on the firewall for Domain, Private and Public with netsh advfirewall set allprofiles state on. Firewall protection has been enabled is on nearly every key (K1, K4, R1, R2). See Turn on all three profiles, Turn on the firewall with logging.
    • Do R1+ Turn on Defender real-time, cloud-delivered and tamper protection. Antivirus protection has been enabled is scored in P1 and H1. See Turn on protection in Windows Security, Turn on protection with PowerShell.
    • Do R1+ Remove DisableAntiSpyware and DisableRealtimeMonitoring policies, set Turn off real-time protection to Disabled and make sure WinDefend is not disabled. Planted policies keep Defender off after you toggle it. See Remove policies that disable Defender, Defender services.
    • Do R1+ Set Configure Windows Defender SmartScreen (Explorer) to Enabled with Warn or Warn and prevent bypass. SmartScreen has been enabled is scored in K4 and SR1. See Turn on SmartScreen, SmartScreen is greyed out.
    • Do R1+ Start Windows Update early and install updates repeatedly until none remain, rebooting as asked. (not: Updates restricted or version pinned) Windows updates installed is scored in R1, H2 and N1. See Check for and install Windows updates, 4-hour timeline.
    • Do R1+ Enable Configure Automatic Updates with option 4, Auto download and schedule the install (AUOptions=4). Windows automatically checks for updates was scored in G4. See Set the Configure Automatic Updates policy.
    • Do R1+ Enable Turn off Autoplay for All drives and set NoDriveTypeAutoRun=255. AutoPlay disabled is scored in K4 and H2. See Turn off AutoPlay and autorun, Turn off AutoPlay and autorun.
    • Do R1+ Stop and disable Remote Registry, Telnet, Simple TCP/IP Services, SNMP and Net.Tcp Port Sharing. Scored in H2, G4, H1 and SR1. See Services commonly disabled, Disable risky services.
    • Do R1+ Turn off SMB 1.0, Telnet Client, TFTP Client and Simple TCP/IP features and run Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB1Protocol $false. SMB1 removal was scored in K7 and H1. See Turn features off in the GUI, Turn off SMBv1 in the SMB server, Remove old protocols (SMBv1, Telnet, TFTP, Simple TCP/IP, PowerShell 2.0).
    • Do R1+ Turn off Remote Desktop (fDenyTSConnections=1) and disable its firewall rule group. (not: README requires Remote Desktop) Remote desktop sharing is turned off was scored in R2. See Turn off Remote Desktop when it is not required, Turn off Remote Desktop (only when the README does not require it).
    • Do R1+ Uncheck Allow Remote Assistance connections in sysdm.cpl (fAllowToGetHelp=0). Remote Assistance disabled was scored in R1. See Turn off Remote Assistance connections.
    • Do R1+ Set WinRM Service and Client Allow unencrypted traffic to Disabled (AllowUnencryptedTraffic=0). Scored in K1. See Block unencrypted WinRM traffic by policy.
    • Do R1+ Remove every non-default share the README does not describe, keeping ADMIN$, C$ and IPC$. (not: README requires Windows file shares) Custom share removal was scored in G3 and H1. See Remove a share that is not required, List the shares.
    • Do R1+ Stop and disable the Microsoft FTP Service, uncheck the IIS FTP Server feature and uninstall FileZilla Server, OpenTFTP and other FTP or TFTP servers. (not: README requires an FTP server) FTP removal was scored in K2, R1 and N1; OpenTFTP in K4. See Remove FTP when it is not required, Servers nobody asked for, Remove FileZilla Server cleanly.
    • Do R1+ Stop and disable World Wide Web Publishing Service (W3SVC). (not: README requires a web server and not: README requires an IIS application and not: README requires WordPress or a CMS and not: README requires PHP) W3SVC stopped and disabled was scored in R2 and G2. See Services commonly disabled, A web or FTP server is required.
    • Do R1+ Uninstall XAMPP, WAMP, Home Web Server and other unrequested web stacks and kill their processes. (not: README requires a web server and not: README requires PHP and not: README requires WordPress or a CMS and not: README requires MySQL or MariaDB) Removed Home Web Server was scored in G4 and H1. See Remove XAMPP cleanly, Servers nobody asked for.
    • Do R1+ Uninstall MySQL or MariaDB when no README service needs a database. (not: README requires MySQL or MariaDB and not: README requires WordPress or a CMS) An unrequired database server is unwanted software. See Remove a database server that is not required, Remove XAMPP cleanly.
    • Do R1+ Uninstall SQL Server Express when the README does not require it. (not: README requires SQL Server) An unrequired server is unwanted software. See Remove SQL Server Express cleanly.
    • Do R1+ Uninstall TeamViewer, AnyDesk, VNC and other remote access tools. (not: README allows a remote access tool) Removed TeamViewer was scored in K4 and AnyDesk in H1. See Check for third-party remote access tools, Remote access tools.
    • Do R1+ Remove game and chat servers such as Minetest or IRC daemons. (not: README requires a game or chat server) IRC and Minetest services were scored for removal in H1 and H2. See Servers nobody asked for, Games and unapproved apps.
    • Do R1+ List installed programs with appwiz.cpl and winget list, compare with the README, and use the vendor uninstaller when a normal uninstall fails. Unwanted software is 3 items on a State image (C1). See List installed programs, Uninstall a program, Run the vendor uninstaller when the others fail.
    • Do R1+ Uninstall cleaners, driver updaters, adware and PUPs such as CCleaner, SlimDrivers, RoboForm and Adaware. Scored in R1, SR1 and K5. See Cleaners, driver updaters and adware, Commonly planted unwanted software.
    • Do R1+ Uninstall Wireshark, Nmap, NetStumbler and other hacking tools. (not: README allows security tools) Scored in R1, SR1, N1 and P1. See Network tools.
    • Do R1+ Uninstall BitTorrent, uTorrent, BitComet and video downloaders. (not: README requires a P2P client) Scored in K5 and G2. See P2P and download tools.
    • Do R1+ Uninstall games and Store games such as TicTacToe and Tetris, using Remove-AppxPackage for Store apps. (not: README requires a game or chat server) Removed TicTacToe was scored in R2. See Games and unapproved apps, Remove Microsoft Store games and apps.
    • Do R1+ Update browsers, Notepad++, 7-Zip, PuTTY, FileZilla Client and Adobe Reader in place without changing the install folder. (not: Updates restricted or version pinned) App and browser updates were scored in K4, R1, R2, SR1, G2 and N1. See Check every app's version and install folder, Update without changing the install folder, Firefox and Thunderbird.
    • Do R1+ Find and delete prohibited media files (mp3, mp4, wav, avi) in user folders, keeping the folders. Removed prohibited MP3 files was scored in K2, K4, R2 and G4. See Find media files in user folders, Search the whole C: drive for media.
    • Do R1+ Run netstat -anob, end any unknown listener such as nc.exe and delete its binary from C:\Windows or user folders. netcat and backdoor items were scored in K4, K7 and G2. See Find listening ports and their programs, Netcat backdoor, Unknown backdoor on a port.
    • Do R1+ Run the final pass checklist and confirm every README service and program still works. Catches late penalties before time runs out. See Final pass, Stop penalties before they happen.
    • Check R1+ If the score drops, undo the last change from your log first. Penalties appear right after the change that caused them. See Fix a score that went down, Score went down.
    • Don't R2+ Do not disable the Event Log, remove drivers, turn on BitLocker or change settings the guide marks as check only. These break the image or scoring without earning points. See Settings to leave alone or only check.
    • Do R2+ Run the read-only recon script to save users, groups, services, tasks, listening ports and installed programs to a file before fixing. Gives the team a baseline to compare against the README and later changes. See Read-only recon report, Run PowerShell as administrator and allow scripts.
    • Do R2+ Empty the Remote Desktop Users group when RDP is not required. (not: README requires Remote Desktop) No one should hold remote logon rights on a box that does not need RDP. See Remove users from Remote Desktop Users.
    • Do R2+ Enable Force audit policy subcategory settings to override category settings, then run auditpol /get /category:* and confirm Credential Validation, User Account Management, Logoff and System Integrity show Success and Failure. These exact subcategories appear in K4, H1 and H2. See Make subcategories override categories, Verify auditing, Set the legacy audit policy.
    • Do R2+ Enable Interactive logon: Don't display last signed-in and UAC: Admin Approval Mode for the Built-in Administrator account. Both were scored in G2 (DontDisplayLastUserName=1, FilterAdministratorToken=1). See Hide the last signed-in user, Admin Approval Mode for the built-in Administrator.
    • Do R2+ Enable Microsoft network client: Digitally sign communications (always). Scored in K1 and G2. See Require SMB signing on the client and server.
    • Do R2+ Enable Devices: Prevent users from installing printer drivers. Scored in SR1 and H1. See Stop users installing printer drivers.
    • Do R2+ Remove every Defender path, extension and process exclusion and reset the exclusion policies to Not configured. Exclusion removal was scored in K7 and P2. See Remove Defender exclusions.
    • Do R2+ Update Defender signatures and run a scan after malware cleanup. Finds leftovers you missed by hand. See Update signatures and scan, Scan with Defender after cleanup.
    • Do R2+ Remove NoAutoUpdate, DisableWindowsUpdateAccess, a bogus WUServer and any update pause or deferral. Planted blockers make updates fail silently. See Remove policies that block updates, Advanced options worth setting.
    • Do R2+ Set Lanman Workstation Enable insecure guest logons to Disabled (AllowInsecureGuestAuth=0). Insecure guest logons disabled was scored in P1. See Turn off insecure guest SMB access.
    • Do R2+ Set the machine inactivity limit to 900 seconds and require a password on wake. Screen locking is part of Uncategorized OS Settings. See Lock the screen after inactivity.
    • Do R2+ Remove AutoAdminLogon and DefaultPassword from the Winlogon key. (not: README gives or protects passwords) A stored plaintext password is a common planted weakness. See Turn off autologon and remove the stored password, Turn off autologon.
    • Do R2+ Review Configured settings in gpedit Administrative Templates for planted policy, then run gpupdate /force and confirm with gpresult. Planted policies hide under Windows Components and unapplied policy does not score. See Where settings live, Apply and check policy.
    • Do R2+ Stop and disable the WebClient service and SSDP Discovery and UPnP Device Host. WebClient was scored in G2. See Services commonly disabled, Disable several services at once.
    • Do R2+ Set every README service to Automatic, start it and set its recovery action to restart. A stopped critical service is a penalty. See Keep README-required services healthy, Re-enable a service.
    • Do R2+ Remove Windows PowerShell 2.0 with Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature. PowerShell 2.0 bypasses script logging. See PowerShell 2.0, Remove features with PowerShell.
    • Do R2+ Run Disable-PSRemoting -Force, delete the WinRM listener and stop and disable the WinRM service. (not: README requires WinRM) Unrequired remoting is a remote shell for attackers. See Turn off WinRM and PowerShell remoting, Turn WinRM off completely.
    • Do R2+ Remove the Internet Information Services feature entirely. (not: README requires a web server and not: README requires an IIS application and not: README requires WordPress or a CMS and not: README requires PHP and not: README requires an FTP server) An unrequired web server is unwanted software. See Remove features with PowerShell, Servers nobody asked for.
    • Do R2+ Stop and disable the Print Spooler when no printing is required. (not: README requires printing) Removes the PrintNightmare attack surface. See Services commonly disabled, Fix: Print Spooler off (DC without printing).
    • Do R2+ Remove policies that block app updates, such as Firefox DisableAppUpdate or Chrome update policies. Firefox automatically checks for updates was scored in H1. See Remove policies that block app updates, Update apps with their own updater.
    • Do R2+ In Firefox, block pop-ups, warn when sites install add-ons and block dangerous downloads. Firefox pop-up blocker and add-on warnings were scored in H1. See Firefox settings.
    • Do R2+ Remove developer tools and editors the README does not authorize. (not: README requires developer tools) R2 scored removing Cursor. See Games and unapproved apps.
    • Do R2+ Uninstall media streaming and downloader apps such as Nexus Radio, Helium, TVexe and Plex. (not: README requires media apps) Scored in G3 and H1. See P2P and download tools, Games and unapproved apps.
    • Do R2+ Find and delete plaintext password files and hacking-related files and scripts. G3 scored removing a plaintext password file. See Find plaintext password files, Find hacking-related files.
    • Do R2+ Remove Tini and other small backdoors, keyloggers such as Refog, and cryptominers such as geth, with their services and tasks. Tini (R2), keyloggers (SR1, H1) and Geth (H2) were scored. See Tini backdoor, Keyloggers, Cryptominers.
    • Do R2+ Check HKLM and HKCU Run and RunOnce keys, both Startup folders and the hosts file, and remove unknown entries. Run keys are the most common persistence. See Check Run and RunOnce keys, Startup folders, Check the hosts file.
    • Do R2+ Review scheduled tasks and files in Temp and ProgramData for actions in user folders or encoded PowerShell and delete bad ones. P3 planted a task that crashed the PC hourly. See Check scheduled tasks, Find suspicious files in Temp and ProgramData.
    • Check R2+ Compare net user with the Settings list, check Winlogon\SpecialAccounts\UserList, and remove hidden or lookalike accounts such as guest_ or names ending in $. Removed hidden user and the guest_ lookalike were scored in SR1. See Find hidden users, Lookalike account names, Account names ending in $.
    • Check R2+ Review Backup Operators, Event Log Readers, Remote Management Users, Remote Desktop Users and Hyper-V Administrators and remove unauthorized members. P1 scored removing a user from a privileged group. See Check privileged groups, See a user's groups or a group's members.
    • Check R2+ Verify with net accounts and secedit /export, and if secpol is missing (Home edition) set policy with net accounts, secedit and the registry. Home edition images still score the same policies. See Verify the policy, Work without gpedit or secpol on Home edition, If net accounts says "The parameter is incorrect".
    • Check R2+ Review User Rights Assignment for Everyone, Guests or named users in Act as part of the operating system, Replace a process level token, Debug programs, Log on as a service and Manage auditing and security log. Planted rights were scored in P1 and H2. See User rights assignment, Find planted user rights.
    • Check R2+ Make sure mpssvc and BFE are Automatic and running, and remove the policy that turns the firewall back off. Planted policy keys re-disable the firewall after you fix it. See Check the firewall services, Firewall turns itself back off.
    • Check R2+ Disable inbound allow rules for unknown programs, any-port rules and programs in Temp or user folders. Backdoors ship with their own firewall rule. See Find suspicious inbound allow rules, Disable or remove a rule.
    • Check R2+ Find services with misspelled names, no description or binaries in Temp, ProgramData or user folders, then stop them and remove them with sc delete. Backdoors install as services and disabling leaves the binary. See Find unusual services, Check services that run from odd folders, Delete a malicious service.
    • Check R2+ Look for hidden or drive shares such as C or USERS$ and stop sharing them. USERS$ and C share removal were scored in K7 and G3. See Hidden and custom drive shares.
    • Check R2+ Reboot once and confirm the firewall, Defender and policies stayed fixed. Planted tasks can reverse settings at startup. See Firewall turns itself back off, Other quick fixes.
    • Do State+ Apply the full account policy from a secedit template so every value, including ones the GUI hides, is set at once. Faster and covers settings missed by hand. See Set everything with secedit, Edit an export by hand.
    • Do State+ Enable Domain member: Digitally encrypt or sign secure channel data (always) and Devices: Restrict CD-ROM access, and disable Shutdown without logon and Recovery console automatic logon. All four appear in H1 scoring lines with CyberPatriot wording. See Sign or encrypt the secure channel, Restrict CD-ROM access to the local user, Block shutdown from the sign-in screen.
    • Do State+ Add Guests to Deny access to this computer from the network and Deny log on locally. Deny access includes Guest was scored in H1. See User rights assignment.
    • Do State+ Turn on firewall logging of dropped and successful connections (16384 KB) and set every profile to block inbound by default, keeping required-service rules. Logging feeds later monitoring and default-allow inbound is a planted weakness. See Turn on firewall logging, Block a port or a program.
    • Do State+ Set Exploit Protection system settings (DEP, CFG, mandatory ASLR, heap integrity) to On and run Set-MpPreference -PUAProtection Enabled. DEP and heap integrity were scored in P1 and H2. See Check exploit protection system settings, Turn on protection with PowerShell.
    • Do State+ Back up the keys, then turn on LSA protection (RunAsPPL=1) and turn off WDigest (UseLogonCredential=0). Stops plaintext credential theft from memory. See Turn on LSA protection, Turn off WDigest plaintext credentials, Back up a key before changing it.
    • Do State+ Remove planted browser policies such as proxy settings, forced extensions and SafeBrowsing off in policies.json and the Chrome and Edge registry keys. Planted policies reverse settings you fix in the GUI. See Fix Firefox enterprise policies, Fix Chrome and Edge policies in the registry.
    • Do State+ Search for hidden files, folders and alternate data streams, and empty the Recycle Bin after forensics are done. Planted items hide behind attributes and ADS. See Find hidden files and folders, Check alternate data streams, Empty the Recycle Bin.
    • Check State+ Enable UAC: Only elevate executables that are signed and validated if required apps allow, and check EnableInstallerDetection=1 and LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy absent or 0. P1 scored the signed-executables option; planted UAC values weaken elevation silently. See User Account Control options, Hardening values table.
    • Check State+ Search Downloads, ProgramData and AppData for portable programs, and after each uninstall remove leftover services, tasks, Run keys and folders. G2 and G4 checked that the .exe and process were gone. See Find portable and hidden programs, Find every trace of a program.
    • Do Semis+ Set LAN Manager authentication level to NTLMv2 only, enable Do not store LAN Manager hash, enable Restrict anonymous access to Named Pipes and Shares and clear the anonymous pipe and share lists. Obscure security options show up at Semifinals depth. See Settings that only secpol or secedit can change, Hardening values table.
    • Do Semis+ Export with secedit /export and search every privilege line (SeDebugPrivilege, SeTcbPrivilege, SeBackupPrivilege, SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege) for unexpected SIDs. Hidden rights granted by SID do not show names in the GUI. See Set user rights with secedit, Find planted user rights.
    • Do Semis+ Turn on Attack Surface Reduction rules such as Block credential stealing from LSASS and Block Office apps from creating child processes. Adds depth expected on Semifinals and later images. See Turn on attack surface reduction rules.
    • Do Semis+ Turn off LLMNR (EnableMulticast=0), NetBIOS over TCP/IP where no share needs it, IP source routing (DisableIPSourceRouting=2) and ICMP redirects (EnableICMPRedirect=0). Network stack values are obscure but checkable. See Turn off LLMNR and NetBIOS over TCP/IP, Network stack values.
    • Do Semis+ Remove stored credentials listed by cmdkey /list and limit cached logons. Stored credentials let an attacker move to other machines. See Remove stored credentials, Optional sign-in settings.
    • Do Semis+ Remove Image File Execution Options Debugger values on sethc, utilman, osk and similar binaries. IFEO backdoors are classic hidden persistence. See Image File Execution Options debugger backdoor.
    • Do Semis+ Check Winlogon Shell and Userinit, AppInit_DLLs and BootExecute for extra entries. Boot values run code before anyone signs in. See Check Winlogon Shell, Userinit and other boot values, Check the Winlogon shell and userinit values.
    • Do Semis+ List WMI event filters, consumers and bindings and remove unknown ones. WMI subscriptions do not show in Task Scheduler. See Check WMI event subscriptions.
    • Do Semis+ Use Autoruns with Microsoft entries hidden if rules and internet allow. Shows every autostart location at once. See Use Autoruns when internet is allowed, Resources, scripts and AI.
    • Do Semis+ Search the registry for values pointing at Temp, AppData or powershell -enc, including PowerShell profiles and the Command Processor AutoRun value. Finds persistence in less-known keys. See Search the registry for a value, Read and change values in PowerShell.
    • Do Semis+ Remove Users or Everyone write access on service binaries, Program Files folders and System32. Writable service binaries allow privilege escalation. See Find folders where Everyone or Users can write, Take ownership of a file you cannot change.
    • Do Semis+ Enable command line in process creation events and turn on PowerShell script block and module logging. Records exactly what malware ran. See Log process command lines, Turn on PowerShell script block logging without gpedit, Turn on PowerShell module logging and transcription.
    • Check Semis+ Compare C:\Windows\System32\Tasks and the TaskCache registry with schtasks output to find hidden tasks. Tasks with a removed security descriptor do not list normally. See Check scheduled tasks, Services and scheduled tasks.
    • Check Semis+ When the score stalls, walk the hidden-items list by category against the category counts. State images hold about 31 items across 13 categories (C1). See Hunt hidden items when stuck, How many items each category holds.
    • Don't Nats+ Do not block all inbound traffic or unplug the network to stop the red team. Required services must stay reachable to be scored as up. See Keep services up.
    • Do Nats+ Assign one teammate to watch logs and services full time while others harden and write injects. Finals add live red-team activity and injects. See Split the work, What National Finals involves.
    • Do Nats+ Save a baseline of users, Administrators members, services, tasks, Run keys and listening ports and diff it every 15 minutes. Red team changes show up as new entries. See Read-only recon report, Watch for the red team.
    • Do Nats+ Raise Security, System and PowerShell log sizes and enable Success auditing for Process Creation, Security Group Management, Security System Extension and Other Object Access. These produce and keep the events that reveal new users, services and tasks. See Set advanced audit policy in secpol, Find answers in Event Viewer.
    • Do Nats+ Poll the Security log with Get-WinEvent for 4720, 4722, 4724, 4728, 4732 and 4738 and undo unauthorized user or group changes at once. New users and admin grants are the red team's first moves. See Watch for the red team, Users, SIDs and groups.
    • Do Nats+ Watch for System 7045 and Security 4697 (new service) and 4698 (new task) and remove anything you did not create. Services and tasks are the main Windows persistence. See Services and scheduled tasks, Watch for the red team.
    • Do Nats+ Watch 4625 failures, 4624 logon types 3 and 10 and pfirewall.log, then log off unknown sessions and block attacking IPs. Shows password spraying and remote logins. See Logons, Turn on firewall logging, Block a port or a program.
    • Do Nats+ If competition rules allow outside tools, install Sysmon with a known config to log process, network and registry Run key events. Sysmon gives far better visibility than default logs. See Resources, scripts and AI, Watch for the red team.
    • Do Nats+ Watch the Defender Operational log for 1116, 1117 and 5001 and turn protection back on immediately. Attackers disable real-time protection before dropping tools. See Turn on protection with PowerShell, Watch for the red team.
    • Do Nats+ Re-run the persistence sweep (Run keys, tasks, services, WMI, IFEO, Startup) every hour. Red team re-plants persistence after you clean it. See Check WMI event subscriptions, Check scheduled tasks, Image File Execution Options debugger backdoor.
    • Do Nats+ Check every required service in a loop, set recovery to restart on failure and keep the lockout threshold at 10 so spraying cannot lock out service accounts. Service uptime is scored throughout the finals. See Keep services up, Keep README-required services healthy.
    • Do Nats+ Answer business injects on time in a short professional memo format. Injects are scored at National Finals. See Write business injects.

    #Windows 11

    • Do R1+ Work the Windows 11 image in the walkthrough order: forensics, users, policy, security options, firewall and Defender, services, software, malware. Windows 11 has been the Round 1 and Round 2 client image in CP-18 and CP-19. See Windows 11, Windows 11 master checklist.

    #Windows 10

    • Check R1+ Run winver to confirm Windows 10 and use the Windows 10 Settings paths, which differ from Windows 11. Windows 10 keys (K2, K4) use older menu locations. See Tell which version you are on, Settings paths that differ, Windows 10.
    • Check R2+ On Windows 10, expect SMB1, PowerShell 2.0 and Internet Explorer to be present by default and handle them. Windows 10 defaults differ from Windows 11. See Defaults that differ.
    • Do State+ On Windows 10, enable the Internet Explorer SmartScreen Filter and Enhanced Protected Mode in Internet Options. IE SmartScreen and Enhanced Protected Mode appear in H1. See Internet Explorer settings on Windows 10.

    #README requires Remote Desktop

    • Don't R1+ Do not turn off Remote Desktop or stop TermService. (Windows 11 and 10) Disabling required RDP cost 5 to 10 points in K7, G2 and G4. See A required service was stopped, Decide whether Remote Desktop is required.
    • Do R1+ Keep Remote Desktop on and require Network Level Authentication (UserAuthentication=1). (Windows 11 and 10) RDP NLA was scored in K4, R1, SR1 and G2. See Harden Remote Desktop when the README requires it.
    • Do R2+ Make Remote Desktop Users contain exactly the users the README allows to connect. (Windows 11 and 10) Updated Remote Desktop Users group was scored in R1. See Remove users from Remote Desktop Users.
    • Do R2+ Keep an inbound allow rule for each README service port (3389, 445, 21, 80 and 443, 5985, and 3306 or 1433 only when other hosts must reach the database) after the firewall is on. (Windows 11 and 10) A blocked required service counts as a stopped service. See Common ports and services, Block a port or a program.
    • Do R2+ Set the RDP security layer to SSL (SecurityLayer=2), encryption to High (MinEncryptionLevel=3) and Require secure RPC communication (fEncryptRPCTraffic=1). (Windows 11 and 10) SSL layer was scored in K4 and secure RPC in G2. See Set the Remote Desktop policies in the registry, Harden Remote Desktop (only when the README requires it).
    • Do R2+ Test each README service locally (open the site, connect to the share, check the port listens) before you finish. (Windows 11 and 10) A broken required service is a penalty. See Keep README-required services healthy, A required service was stopped.
    • Do State+ Set Allow log on through Remote Desktop Services to Administrators and Remote Desktop Users only, and do not add those groups to the deny right. (Windows 11 and 10) Keeps required RDP working while limiting who can use it. See User rights assignment, Harden Remote Desktop when the README requires it.
    • Do State+ Disable drive, clipboard and Plug and Play device redirection, always prompt for a password and set session time limits. (Windows 11 and 10) PnP redirection was scored in H1. See Set the Remote Desktop policies in the registry, Set session time limits.
    • Check Semis+ Check sethc.exe, utilman.exe and osk.exe for IFEO debuggers or replaced binaries, since they run at the RDP sign-in screen. (Windows 11 and 10) Accessibility backdoors give SYSTEM through an open RDP port. See Image File Execution Options debugger backdoor.
    • Do Nats+ Keep TermService up, watch 4624 type 10 logons and remove any new Remote Desktop Users members. (Windows 11 and 10) RDP is the main red-team entry on Windows clients. See Keep services up, Remove users from Remote Desktop Users.

    #README requires SSH

    • Do R2+ Keep the OpenSSH Server service (sshd) running and Automatic, then in C:\ProgramData\ssh\sshd_config set PermitEmptyPasswords no, PasswordAuthentication per the README and remove unknown keys from administrators_authorized_keys. (Windows 11 and 10) README-required SSH on Windows must stay up; administrators_authorized_keys is a common backdoor. See OpenSSH Server.

    #README requires Windows file shares

    • Don't R1+ Do not remove the README share, its business files or the Server (LanmanServer) service. (Windows 11 and 10) Removing the share or its files cost 5 points in K7 and G3. See A share or business file was removed, A share is required.
    • Do R2+ Replace Everyone Full Control on the required share with only the README users or groups. (Windows 11 and 10) Share permissions are Application Security Settings. See Fix permissions on a share the README requires.
    • Do R2+ Delete plaintext password files from the share while keeping the share folder. (Windows 11 and 10) G3 scored removing C:\Share\secret.txt and required the folder to remain. See Find plaintext password files, A share or business file was removed.
    • Do State+ Check NTFS permissions on the share with icacls and remove Everyone or Users write access. (Windows 11 and 10) Share and NTFS permissions both apply. See Check NTFS permissions with icacls, Find folders where Everyone or Users can write.
    • Do State+ Enable Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always), and turn on access-based enumeration on the required share. (Windows 11 and 10) Server signing was scored in G3 and H1. See Require SMB signing on the client and server, Turn on access-based enumeration, Harden the SMB server configuration.
    • Do Nats+ Watch Get-SmbSession and Get-SmbOpenFile, close unknown sessions and keep a copy of share data. (Windows 11 and 10) Shares are a common target for tampering. See Check open files and sessions, Keep services up.

    #README requires an FTP server

    • Don't R1+ Do not stop ftpsvc or FileZilla Server or remove the IIS FTP Server feature. (Windows 11 and 10) Stopping a critical service is a penalty. See A required service was stopped, A web or FTP server is required.
    • Do R1+ Disable anonymous FTP authentication and enable Basic authentication for README users. (Windows 11 and 10) Anonymous authentication disabled was scored in P2. See Turn off anonymous FTP and turn on basic authentication, Find the FTP site settings.
    • Do R2+ Require SSL on the FTP control and data channels. (Windows 11 and 10) Require SSL connections was scored in P2. See Require SSL (FTPS).
    • Do R2+ In FileZilla Server, set minimum TLS to 1.3, disable anonymous users and protect the admin interface with a password on localhost only. (Windows 11 and 10) FileZilla minimum TLS 1.3 was scored in P1. See FileZilla Server, Harden FileZilla Server when the README requires it.
    • Do State+ Turn on FTP user isolation, limit authorization rules to README users, remove Everyone write on the FTP root and enable FTP logging and logon attempt restrictions. (Windows 11 and 10) FTP logon restrictions were scored in P2. See Turn on user isolation, Tighten authorization rules, Logging, logon attempt limits and IP restrictions.
    • Do Nats+ Watch FTP logs for brute force and block attacking IPs while keeping the service running. (Windows 11 and 10) Keeps FTP up under attack. See IIS and FTP logs, Keep services up.

    #README requires a web server

    • Don't R1+ Do not stop W3SVC, WAS or the Apache service, or remove IIS. (Windows 11 and 10) Stopping the web server is a critical service penalty (G1). See A required service was stopped, A web or FTP server is required.
    • Do R1+ Delete phpinfo.php, info.php and test pages from the web root, keeping the site files. (Windows 11 and 10) Removed phpinfo file was scored in G1 and H2. See Remove web files such as phpinfo.
    • Do R2+ Turn off IIS directory browsing and detailed errors, and check web.config does not turn them back on. (Windows 11 and 10) IIS detailed errors disabled appears in H1. See Turn off directory browsing, Turn off debug and detailed errors in web.config, Check web.config does not turn it back on.
    • Do R2+ If the web server is Apache, set ServerTokens Prod, TraceEnable Off and Options -Indexes in httpd.conf. (Windows 11 and 10) Apache tokens and TRACE were scored in H1. See Harden Apache, PHP and MariaDB when the README requires them, Apache, XAMPP and PHP on Windows.
    • Do State+ Add an HTTPS binding and turn on Require SSL in IIS. (Windows 11 and 10) IIS requires SSL was scored in H2. See Add an HTTPS binding, Require SSL.
    • Do State+ Turn off unused IIS authentication methods, remove WebDAV publishing and stop unused sites. (Windows 11 and 10) Extra auth methods, WebDAV and stray sites give upload paths. See Review authentication, Remove WebDAV, Stop or remove unused sites.
    • Do State+ Give IUSR read only on C:\inetpub\wwwroot and turn on IIS logging. (Windows 11 and 10) Writable web roots let attackers drop shells. See Fix permissions on C:\inetpub\wwwroot, Turn on logging.
    • Do Semis+ Hide Server and X-Powered-By headers, set request filtering, disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1 and run app pools as ApplicationPoolIdentity. (Windows 11 and 10) Subtle app config expected at Semifinals. See Hide the Server and X-Powered-By headers, Disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1, Set the application pool identity.
    • Do Semis+ Hunt the web root for web shells (.aspx or .php files using eval, cmd or base64) and delete them without touching site files. (Windows 11 and 10) PHP web shell r57.php was scored in G1. See Hunt for web shells, Remove phpinfo files and web shells.
    • Do Nats+ Back up the web root and config early and compare file hashes regularly to catch new web shells. (Windows 11 and 10) Lets you restore the site fast after defacement. See Hunt for web shells, Keep services up.

    #README requires PHP

    • Don't R1+ Do not uninstall PHP or break the IIS or Apache PHP handler mapping. (Windows 11 and 10) Removing PHP is a critical service penalty (G1). See A required service was stopped.
    • Do R2+ In the php.ini the server actually loads, set display_errors = Off, expose_php = Off and log_errors = On. (Windows 11 and 10) PHP display errors and expose_php were scored in H2 and G1. See Find the php.ini the web server uses, Harden Apache, PHP and MariaDB when the README requires them.
    • Do State+ Set allow_url_include = Off, allow_url_fopen = Off and disable_functions for exec, shell_exec, system and passthru, and update PHP in its existing folder. Leave allow_url_fopen On if WordPress or a required app updates itself or fetches remote content. (Windows 11 and 10) PHP has been updated was scored in G1 and H1. See Set the scored PHP options, Update without changing the install folder.

    #README requires WordPress or a CMS

    • Don't R1+ Do not delete wp-login.php or other WordPress core files while removing bad files. (Windows 11 and 10) G1 removal items required wp-login.php to remain. See Rules the engine follows, Remove phpinfo files and web shells.
    • Do R2+ Remove unauthorized WordPress administrators, set strong passwords and update core, plugins and themes. (Windows 11 and 10) WordPress has been updated was scored in G1. See Remove unauthorized WordPress administrators, Check the version and update WordPress.
    • Do State+ In wp-config.php set DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT to true and WP_DEBUG to false, and restrict who can read the file. (Windows 11 and 10) wp-config holds the database password. See Lock down wp-config.php, Harden WordPress.
    • Check Semis+ Check plugins, mu-plugins and wp-content/uploads for unknown PHP files and remove them. (Windows 11 and 10) Uploads and mu-plugins hide persistent shells. See Harden WordPress, Hunt for web shells.

    #README requires MySQL or MariaDB

    • Don't R1+ Do not stop or disable the MySQL or MariaDB service. (Windows 11 and 10) Stopping MySQL is a critical service penalty (G1). See A required service was stopped.
    • Do R2+ Set bind-address = 127.0.0.1 in my.ini (unless the README says other hosts connect), set a root password, and drop anonymous users, the test database and remote root. (Windows 11 and 10) MySQL remote access disabled was scored in G1. See Set MySQL and MariaDB server options, Check MySQL and MariaDB accounts.
    • Do State+ Set local_infile=0 and secure_file_priv, and give the app user only its own database. (Windows 11 and 10) Blocks file read and write through SQL. See Set MySQL and MariaDB server options.
    • Do Nats+ Back up the database early and change the app's database password only after updating the app config. (Windows 11 and 10) A mismatched password takes the app down. See Keep services up, Check MySQL and MariaDB accounts.

    #README requires SQL Server

    • Don't R1+ Do not stop the SQL Server instance service (MSSQLSERVER or SQLEXPRESS). (Windows 11 and 10) A stopped critical service is a penalty. See A required service was stopped.
    • Do R2+ Use Windows authentication mode, disable sa or give it a strong password, and turn off xp_cmdshell. (Windows 11 and 10) Core SQL Server hardening. See Harden SQL Server when the README requires it.
    • Do State+ Remove unauthorized sysadmin logins, audit failed and successful logins and disable SQL Browser if not needed. (Windows 11 and 10) App-level user auditing for SQL Server. See Harden SQL Server when the README requires it, SQL Server Express.
    • Check Semis+ Check SQL Agent jobs, startup procedures, CLR and Ole Automation Procedures for persistence. (Windows 11 and 10) Database-side persistence survives OS cleanup. See Harden SQL Server when the README requires it.

    #README requires printing

    • Don't R1+ Do not disable the Print Spooler when printing is required. (Windows 11 and 10) A stopped critical service is a penalty. See Harden printing when the README requires it, A required service was stopped.
    • Do State+ Set Point and Print restrictions and RestrictDriverInstallationToAdministrators=1, and limit printer share permissions. (Windows 11 and 10) Keeps printing while blocking driver attacks. See Restrict printer driver installation, Harden printing when the README requires it.
    • Do Nats+ Watch the PrintService logs for new drivers or ports and remove ones you did not add. (Windows 11 and 10) Print drivers are a known SYSTEM-level attack path. See Harden printing when the README requires it, Watch for the red team.

    #README allows a remote access tool

    • Don't R1+ Do not uninstall the remote tool the README allows. (Windows 11 and 10) Removing required software is a penalty. See Wireshark or TeamViewer when required, Required software removed or moved.
    • Do R2+ Update the allowed remote tool, set a strong access password and turn off unattended access for unknown accounts. (Windows 11 and 10) The allowed tool is still an entry point. See Wireshark or TeamViewer when required.
    • Check State+ Remove any other remote tool besides the one the README allows. (Windows 11 and 10) Only the named tool is authorized. See Remote access tools.
    • Do Nats+ Review the allowed remote tool's connection log and access list for unknown IDs and change its password. (Windows 11 and 10) A required remote tool is a ready-made backdoor. See Wireshark or TeamViewer when required, Watch for the red team.

    #README requires WinRM

    • Don't R2+ Do not stop WinRM or run Disable-PSRemoting when the README needs remoting. (Windows 11 and 10) A stopped critical service is a penalty. See A required service was stopped.
    • Do R2+ Keep WinRM Automatic, disable Basic auth, clear TrustedHosts and limit Remote Management Users to README users. (Windows 11 and 10) Hardens the required service without breaking it. See Harden WinRM and PowerShell remoting, Check TrustedHosts.
    • Do Semis+ Move WinRM to an HTTPS listener, disable CredSSP and scope the firewall rule to known hosts. (Windows 11 and 10) Semifinals images reward app-level depth. See Fix: WinRM hardened, Harden WinRM and PowerShell remoting.
    • Do Nats+ Watch the WinRM Operational log and Remote Management Users, and scope the WinRM firewall rule to known hosts. (Windows 11 and 10) Remoting is a quiet way for the red team to run commands. See Check TrustedHosts, Watch for the red team.

    #README requires an IIS application

    • Don't R1+ Do not remove ASP.NET, .NET Framework features or the application pool the app needs. (Windows 11 and 10) Breaking the app is a critical service penalty. See A required service was stopped, A web or FTP server is required.
    • Do State+ In web.config set compilation debug=false, customErrors to RemoteOnly and cookies to httpOnly and requireSSL. (Windows 11 and 10) App-specific settings appear at State and later. See Turn off debug and detailed errors in web.config, Check web.config does not turn it back on.
    • Check State+ Remove Web Deploy and the IIS Management Service unless the README needs remote publishing. (Windows 11 and 10) Remote management is a second way in. See Web Deploy and IIS remote management, Remove Web Deploy cleanly.

    #README requires a game or chat server

    • Don't R1+ Do not remove or stop the game or chat server the README requires, or block its port. (Windows 11 and 10) A stopped critical service is a penalty. See A required service was stopped, Common ports and services.
    • Do State+ Update the game server, limit its admin or operator list to README users and set a server password. (Windows 11 and 10) Server admin lists are app-level user auditing. See Keep README-required services healthy, Check every app's version and install folder.
    • Do Nats+ Watch the game server log for new operator or admin grants and keep its process running. (Windows 11 and 10) Keeps the scored service up and controlled. See Keep services up.
    PreviousStudy plan to State and SemifinalsNextPlanner rules for Windows Server
    GO

    Planner rules for Windows Server

    jump:start-plan-server

    Every rule the Image planner can show, grouped by what triggers it. Level tags show the first round where the rule matters: R1, R2, State, Semis, Nats.

    #Windows Server 2019 and 2022

    • Don't R1+ Do not set the lockout threshold below 5 on local or domain policy unless the README gives a lower value. K7 and G3 penalized thresholds of 1 to 4. See Penalties seen in past keys, Set the lockout policy.
    • Don't R1+ Do not disable Windows Update, BITS or the Windows Event Log service. Keys score these services running, and updates fail without them. See Keep the update services running.
    • Don't R1+ Do not stop, disable or uninstall any service or role the README lists as critical. Critical service removed cost 5 points in K3, K6 and G1. See Server changes that break critical services, A required service was stopped.
    • Don't R1+ Do not uninstall or move required software out of its default folder when updating it. Required software removed or moved cost 5 points on K7 and G3. See Required software removed or moved, Update without changing the install folder.
    • Do R1+ Read the whole README and write down authorized users and admins, critical services, required software, required shares and whether the server is a domain controller. Every keep, harden or remove decision on a Server image depends on the README. See First 10 minutes on the server, Critical services.
    • Do R1+ Turn on Windows Defender Firewall for Domain, Private and Public profiles. Firewall protection has been enabled was scored on K5. See Turn on all three profiles, Updates, Defender and firewall.
    • Do R1+ Check Get-MpComputerStatus and turn real-time, behavior and cloud protection back on. Antivirus protection enabled was scored on H1. See Check Defender status on Server, Turn Defender protections back on.
    • Do R1+ Remove planted Defender exclusions from Get-MpPreference and set the exclusion policies to Not configured. Defender exclusions removed was scored on K7 Server 2022. See Remove Defender exclusions.
    • Do R1+ Install Windows updates from Settings or sconfig option 6, reboot and repeat until none remain. (not: Updates restricted or version pinned) Most Windows updates installed was scored on K7. See Install updates from Settings, Install updates with sconfig.
    • Do R1+ Set Configure Automatic Updates with option 4, Auto download and schedule the install (AUOptions=4). Windows automatically checks for updates was scored on K5 and G3. See Set the Configure Automatic Updates policy.
    • Do R1+ Disable SMB1 with Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB1Protocol $false and remove the FS-SMB1 feature. SMB1 removed was scored on K7 and H1. See Harden the SMB server configuration, Turn off SMBv1 in the SMB server.
    • Do R1+ List installed roles with Get-WindowsFeature | Where-Object Installed and mark each as README-required or not. Unneeded roles are Service Auditing items and attack surface. See List installed roles and features, Roles and features.
    • Do R1+ Stop and disable Simple TCP/IP, Telnet, SNMP, SNMP Trap, Net.Tcp Port Sharing, Remote Registry and WebClient unless the README needs them, and remove the SNMP-Service feature. These were scored on K7, G3 and H1. See Services to disable unless the README requires them, Disable a service.
    • Do R1+ Turn off Remote Desktop by setting fDenyTSConnections to 1 when the README does not require RDP. (not: README requires Remote Desktop) Remote desktop sharing turned off was scored on R2. See Turn off Remote Desktop when not required, Fix: Remote Desktop off (README does not require RDP).
    • Do R1+ Turn off Remote Assistance by setting fAllowToGetHelp to 0. Remote Assistance disabled was scored on R1. See Turn off Remote Assistance.
    • Do R1+ List shares with Get-SmbShare and remove unauthorized ones such as a C share or USERS$, keeping ADMIN$, C$, IPC$, README shares and, on a domain controller, NETLOGON and SYSVOL. USERS$ and C share removal were scored on K7, G3 and H1. See List shares and who can access them, Remove an unauthorized share.
    • Do R1+ Stop and disable the Microsoft FTP Service or remove Web-Ftp-Server when the README does not require FTP. (not: README requires an FTP server) FTP service stopped and disabled was scored on K5 and H1. See Remove FTP when it is not required.
    • Do R1+ Uninstall FileZilla Server, Open TFTP Server and other FTP servers when FTP is not required. (not: README requires an FTP server) Removed Open TFTP server was scored on K4. See Remove FileZilla Server cleanly, Third-party software.
    • Do R1+ Uninstall TeamViewer, AnyDesk, VNC and similar tools the README does not allow. (not: README allows a remote access tool) Removed AnyDesk and TeamViewer were scored on H1 and K4. See Check for third-party remote access tools, Other remote tools and servers.
    • Do R1+ Uninstall unwanted programs the README does not require, such as Adaware Web Companion, CleanMyPC, Driver Booster and games. These were scored on K5, G3 and H1. See Unwanted software, Commonly planted unwanted software.
    • Do R1+ Uninstall Wireshark, Nmap and other hacking tools when the README does not allow them. (not: README allows security tools) Removed Wireshark and Nmap were scored on K5 and H1. See Unwanted software, Uninstall a program.
    • Do R1+ Uninstall torrent and P2P clients. (not: README requires a P2P client) Removed BitTorrent was scored on K5. See Unwanted software.
    • Do R1+ Update Firefox, Chrome, Notepad++ and other listed apps with their official installers into the same folder (Server 2019 has no winget). (not: Updates restricted or version pinned) App updates were scored on K5, K7, G3 and H1. See Update third-party apps without winget, Check every app's version and install folder.
    • Do R1+ Find and delete plaintext password files on the server. Plaintext password file removed was scored on G3. See Find plaintext password files.
    • Do R1+ Find backdoors with netstat -abn -p tcp, end the process, delete the binary, remove its service, task or Run key, then run a Defender full scan. The bd, netcat and Tini backdoors were scored on K7 and H1. See Malware, Find listening ports and their programs, Scan with Defender after cleanup.
    • Do R1+ Uninstall media and streaming apps such as Nexus Radio, TVexe TV HD and Plex Media Server. (not: README requires media apps) These were scored on G3 and H1. See Unwanted software.
    • Check R1+ Confirm the server role with (Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem).DomainRole (4 or 5 means domain controller) and Get-WindowsFeature | Where-Object Installed. A DC uses AD and Group Policy instead of local users and secpol, so the whole plan changes. See Check if the server is a domain controller, Decide: standalone server or domain controller.
    • Check R1+ Check the scoring report after each batch of changes and undo the last change if the score drops or a penalty appears. Fast reversal limits penalties. See Score dropped after a change, Recover from a penalty, Score went down.
    • Check R1+ Confirm every README service is running and reachable with Get-Service and Test-NetConnection before time runs out. Critical service checks run until the image closes. See Final pass.
    • Do R2+ Run the read-only Server recon script and save its output to the desktop before making changes. One snapshot of users, groups, shares, roles, services and ports speeds every later step. See Read-only recon script.
    • Do R2+ Turn on UAC Admin Approval Mode for the built-in Administrator and prompt on the secure desktop. UAC options were scored on G2 and P1. See User Account Control options, Admin Approval Mode for the built-in Administrator.
    • Do R2+ Delete DisableAntiSpyware and DisableRealtimeMonitoring policy values under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender. Policy values keep turning protection off after you enable it. See Remove policies that disable Defender.
    • Do R2+ Remove NoAutoUpdate and bogus WUServer values under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate. A fake WSUS server silently blocks all updates. See Remove policies that block updates.
    • Do R2+ Turn IE Enhanced Security Configuration back on for Administrators and Users in Server Manager > Local Server. IE ESC enabled was scored on H1 Server 2019. See Turn IE Enhanced Security Configuration back on, Fix: turn on IE Enhanced Security Configuration.
    • Do R2+ Disable insecure guest logons (Lanman Workstation AllowInsecureGuestAuth 0). Insecure guest logons disabled was scored on P1. See Turn off insecure guest SMB access.
    • Do R2+ Set WinRM Client and Service Allow unencrypted traffic to Disabled by policy. WinRM does not allow unencrypted traffic was scored on K1. See Block unencrypted WinRM traffic by policy.
    • Do R2+ Turn off AutoPlay for all drives in Group Policy. AutoPlay disabled was scored on K4 and H2. See Turn off AutoPlay and autorun.
    • Do R2+ Remove features nobody needs such as Simple-TCPIP, Telnet-Client, TFTP-Client, SNMP-Service, FS-SMB1 and PowerShell-V2. Removing the feature keeps the service from coming back. See Usually unneeded features and their exact names, Fix: remove common unneeded features.
    • Do R2+ Remove the DNS Server role with Uninstall-WindowsFeature DNS when the server is not a DC and the README does not need DNS. (not: Domain controller and not: README requires DNS) An unneeded DNS server is an open resolver and Service Auditing item. See Remove a role or feature.
    • Do R2+ Remove the DHCP role with Uninstall-WindowsFeature DHCP when the README does not require it. (not: README requires DHCP) An unneeded DHCP server can hand out rogue settings. See Remove DHCP cleanly.
    • Do R2+ Run Disable-PSRemoting -Force and stop and disable the WinRM service when the README does not require remoting. (not: README requires WinRM) Unused remoting is an easy lateral movement path. See Turn WinRM off completely.
    • Do R2+ Stop and disable W3SVC, or remove the Web-Server role (keep it if IIS FTP is required), Web Deploy and Tomcat when no README service needs a web server and no required role such as WSUS depends on IIS. (not: README requires a web server and not: README requires an IIS application and not: README requires WordPress or a CMS and not: README requires PHP) World Wide Web Publishing stopped was scored on R2 and G2. See Remove a role or feature, Remove Web Deploy cleanly, Remove Tomcat cleanly.
    • Do R2+ Uninstall XAMPP, PHP and their Apache and MariaDB services when no README service needs them. (not: README requires PHP and not: README requires WordPress or a CMS and not: README requires a web server and not: README requires MySQL or MariaDB) Unrequired servers are Unwanted Software items. See Remove XAMPP cleanly.
    • Do R2+ Uninstall MySQL or MariaDB when no README service needs a database. (not: README requires MySQL or MariaDB and not: README requires WordPress or a CMS) Unrequired database servers are Unwanted Software. See Third-party software, Remove XAMPP cleanly.
    • Do R2+ Uninstall SQL Server Express when the README does not require it. (not: README requires SQL Server) Unrequired servers are Unwanted Software. See Remove SQL Server Express cleanly.
    • Do R2+ Remove the SMTP-Server feature and hMailServer when the README does not require mail. (not: README requires mail) Unrequired servers are Unwanted Software. See Remove SMTP cleanly, Remove hMailServer cleanly.
    • Do R2+ Remove the Print Server role when the README does not require printing. (not: README requires printing) Unneeded roles are Service Auditing items. See Remove the print server role cleanly.
    • Do R2+ Remove OpenSSH Server when the README does not require SSH. (not: README requires SSH) An unrequired remote shell is a Service Auditing item. See Remove OpenSSH Server cleanly.
    • Do R2+ Turn on Enable Enhanced Protected Mode in Internet Options > Advanced. Scored on H1 Server 2019. See Application security settings.
    • Do R2+ Check Run and RunOnce keys, startup folders, scheduled tasks and services for malware persistence. Backdoors return after reboot without this. See Check Run and RunOnce keys, Check scheduled tasks, Startup folders.
    • Check R2+ Review inbound allow rules and remove ones for programs or ports no README service needs. Planted allow rules keep backdoors reachable. See Find suspicious inbound allow rules, Disable or remove a rule.
    • Check R2+ Check Programs and Features for third-party servers not in the README such as Home Web Server or Open TFTP and remove them. Removed Home Web Server and Open TFTP were scored on G4, H1 and K4. See Third-party software.
    • Do State+ Turn on LSA protection (RunAsPPL 1) and set WDigest UseLogonCredential to 0. Stops credential dumping tools reading plaintext passwords. See Turn on LSA protection, Turn off WDigest plaintext credentials.
    • Do State+ Turn on PowerShell script block logging and module logging. Captures attacker PowerShell for detection. See Turn on PowerShell script block logging without gpedit, Turn on PowerShell module logging and transcription.
    • Do State+ Remove Remote Desktop Services roles when the README does not require RDP. (not: README requires Remote Desktop) Leftover RDS roles keep remote access open. See Remove RDS cleanly.
    • Do State+ Remove Docker and the Containers feature when the README does not require them. (not: README requires Docker) Unneeded features are attack surface. See Usually unneeded features and their exact names.
    • Check State+ Check Image File Execution Options for Debugger values on sethc.exe, utilman.exe and other binaries. Sticky keys backdoors give SYSTEM at the logon screen. See Image File Execution Options debugger backdoor.
    • Check State+ Check Winlogon Shell and Userinit values are the defaults. Modified values run attacker code at every logon. See Check Winlogon Shell, Userinit and other boot values.
    • Check State+ When stuck, compare found items with the usual Server category counts and hunt the weakest category. A Server image has about 31 items spread across all categories. See Hunt hidden items when stuck, How many items a Server image has.
    • Check Semis+ If AD Certificate Services is installed, remove it when not required or check templates for enrollee-supplied subjects and broad enroll rights. Misconfigured certificate templates give domain admin. See Harden the certificate authority, Remove AD CS cleanly.
    • Check Semis+ Check WMI event subscriptions for planted consumers. WMI persistence survives reboots and hides from Task Scheduler. See Check WMI event subscriptions.
