    • Check Semis+ Check LSA Security Packages, Authentication Packages and Notification Packages for unknown DLLs. Password filters and SSPs capture every password change. See LSA packages, password filters and Skeleton Key.
    • Don't Nats+ Do not shut down scored services, unplug the network or block the scoring engine to stop attackers. Downtime loses more points than the attack. See Keep services up.
    • Do Nats+ Split the team so one person owns AD, one owns web and DNS uptime, one watches logs and one handles injects. Finals reward parallel defense and on-time injects. See Split the work.
    • Do Nats+ Run a loop that tests the README service ports and restarts any service that stops. Service uptime under attack is scored at Nationals. See Keep services up.
    • Do Nats+ Rotate all user and admin passwords when compromise is suspected, except passwords the README fixes. (not: README gives or protects passwords) Stolen credentials are the red team's easiest way back in. See Reset every user's password at once, Set passwords and password flags.
    • Do Nats+ Complete business injects on time, such as creating a user, opening a port or writing a report, and record what you changed. Injects are scored and can conflict with earlier hardening. See Write business injects.

    #Server 2022

    • Check R2+ Use sconfig on Server 2022 for updates (6), remote management (4) and Remote Desktop (7) when the GUI is slow. sconfig is the quickest way to confirm these settings on Server. See sconfig menu on Server 2022.

    #Server 2019

    • Check Semis+ On Server 2019 plan downloads around IE ESC and the missing winget by adding trusted sites or using the official installers you need. Server 2019 returns at Semifinals and lacks the 2022 conveniences. See Download tools on Server 2019 with IE ESC on, What changes between the versions.
    • Check Semis+ On Server 2019 install updates through sconfig option 6 and its text prompts, since the menu differs from 2022. Server 2019 returns at Semifinals and its update path is different. See Install updates with sconfig on each version.
    • Check Semis+ On Server 2019 disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1 and do not expect TLS 1.3, which Server 2019 does not support. TLS settings differ by version and a wrong change can break HTTPS or RDP. See TLS settings by version.

    #Standalone server

    • Do R1+ Delete or disable every local user not listed in the README with lusrmgr.msc or Remove-LocalUser. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Removed unauthorized user was scored on K5, K7 and H1; G3 accepted disabling. See Remove or demote local users, Remove an unauthorized user.
    • Do R1+ Remove users who are not README administrators from the local Administrators group. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) User is not an administrator was scored on K7 and G3. See Remove or demote local users, Demote an unauthorized administrator.
    • Do R1+ Set a strong password on every local account that has a blank or weak password, except passwords the README says to keep. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Changed insecure password and user has a password were scored on K5, K7 and G3. See Set passwords and password flags, Set a strong password on every account.
    • Do R1+ Disable the local Guest account with net user guest /active:no. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Guest account is not enabled was scored on G3 and H1. See Disable the Guest account.
    • Do R1+ In secpol.msc set minimum length 10, history 5, maximum age 90, minimum age 1, complexity Enabled and reversible encryption Disabled. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022 and not: README states password policy values) Password age and length items were scored on K5, K7, G3 and H1. See Set the local password and lockout policy, Recommended values.
    • Do R1+ Set account lockout threshold 10, lockout duration 30 minutes and reset counter after 30 minutes. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022 and not: README states password policy values) Lockout threshold and observation window were scored on K5, G3 and H1. See Set the local password and lockout policy, Set the lockout policy.
    • Do R1+ Turn on auditing with auditpol /set /category:* /success:enable /failure:enable. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Audit Logoff and logon items were scored on H1 and client keys. See Turn on all auditing with auditpol.
    • Do R1+ Set the scored Security Options: limit blank passwords to console, Do not require CTRL+ALT+DEL Disabled, SMB client and server sign always, no anonymous SAM enumeration, recovery console auto logon Disabled, shutdown without logon Disabled, restrict CD-ROM to local user, prevent users installing printer drivers. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) These exact options were scored on K5, G3 and H1. See Set the server security options, Scored security options one by one.
    • Do R2+ Clear Password never expires and Password not required on every local user. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Password expires items were scored on client keys and appear on Server too. See Set passwords and password flags, Fix password never expires and password not required.
    • Do R2+ Unlock authorized users that are locked out in lusrmgr.msc. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) User is not locked out was scored twice on G3. See Clear a local account lockout.
    • Do R2+ Add Guest to Deny access to this computer from the network. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Scored on H1 Server 2019. See Deny network logon to Guest.
    • Do R2+ Require SMB signing on the server and client with RequireSecuritySignature set to 1. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) SMB server signing was scored on G3 and H1. See Fix: SMB hardening (any server), Require SMB signing on the client and server.
    • Do R2+ When the README needs no file sharing, remove every non-default share the README does not describe and unneeded file server extras such as FSRM, but keep the Server service and ADMIN$, C$ and IPC$. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022 and not: README requires Windows file shares) Extra shares were scored on K7, G3 and H1, and stopping the Server service breaks remote management. See Remove an unauthorized share, Remove FSRM cleanly.
    • Check R2+ Look for hidden local users under Winlogon\SpecialAccounts\UserList and names ending in $ or lookalikes of built-in names. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Removed hidden user and lookalike Guest accounts were scored on SR1. See Find hidden users, Account names ending in $.
    • Check R2+ Remove users and Everyone from Act as part of the operating system, Debug programs, Replace a process level token, Manage auditing and security log and Log on as a service. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Planted user rights were scored on P1 and H2. See Find planted user rights, User rights assignment.
    • Do State+ Set LmCompatibilityLevel to 5 and NoLMHash to 1. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Stops LM and NTLMv1 hashes that crack in seconds. See Fix: LM and NTLMv1 off (standalone server).
    • Check State+ Look for admins hidden through nested local groups or Backup Operators membership. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Hidden privilege is a common planted User Auditing item. See Check privileged groups.
    • Do Nats+ Watch events 4624, 4625, 4720, 4732, 4698 and 7045 for attacker logons, new accounts, tasks and services. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Early detection lets you evict the red team before it spreads. See Watch for the red team, Verify auditing.

    #Domain controller

    • Don't R1+ Do not set account policy in secpol.msc on a DC because domain GPOs overwrite it at the next refresh. The change looks applied and then silently reverts. See Why secpol.msc changes do not stick on a DC.
    • Don't R1+ Do not delete built-in AD groups, the domain Administrator you use, or disable, delete or reset krbtgt during normal hardening. These deletions break AD and every service that depends on it. See How not to break AD, Leave krbtgt alone, The domain Administrator account.
    • Don't R1+ Do not block the DC ports 53, 88, 135, 389, 445, 464, 636 and 3268 or disable the AD and DNS firewall rule groups. Blocking them breaks logons, DNS and Group Policy. See Ports a domain controller needs open.
    • Don't R1+ Do not stop or disable NTDS, DNS, Netlogon, Kerberos KDC, DFS Replication, ADWS, W32Time, Server, Workstation or RPC on a DC. AD and the scoring engine's checks stop working without them. See Services that must stay on a domain controller, How not to break AD.
    • Don't R1+ Do not remove the AD DS or DNS role or demote the DC. Removing them breaks the domain and every domain service. See Server changes that break critical services, What changes on a DC.
    • Don't R1+ Do not remove the NETLOGON or SYSVOL shares, even when the README lists no file sharing. Group Policy and logon scripts need them. See Shares you must keep, SYSVOL or NETLOGON share missing.
    • Do R1+ List users with Get-ADUser -Filter * and disable or remove every account the README does not list. Removed unauthorized user is the most common User Auditing item. See Compare AD users to the README, Disable or remove an unauthorized user.
    • Do R1+ Remove unauthorized members from Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, Schema Admins, Administrators, Account Operators, Server Operators, Backup Operators and Print Operators. User is not an administrator was scored on K7 and G3. See Check privileged group membership, Remove a user from a privileged group.
    • Do R1+ Disable the domain Guest account with Disable-ADAccount Guest. Guest account is not enabled was scored on G3 and H1. See Disable the domain Guest account.
    • Do R1+ Reset blank or weak domain user passwords with Set-ADAccountPassword -Reset, except passwords the README says to keep. Changed insecure password was scored on K5, K7 and G3. See Reset a user's password.
    • Do R1+ Set the password policy in the Default Domain Policy GPO (not the DC policy or an OU GPO): length 10, history 5, maximum age 90, minimum age 1, complexity Enabled, reversible encryption Disabled. (not: README states password policy values) Only the domain-linked GPO sets password policy for domain accounts. See Set the domain password policy, Which GPO holds which setting.
    • Do R1+ Set lockout threshold 10, duration 30 and reset 30 minutes in the Default Domain Policy. (not: README states password policy values) Lockout items were scored on K5, G3 and H1. See Set the domain lockout policy.
    • Do R1+ Run gpupdate /force after every GPO change and confirm with gpresult /r. Scoring reads the applied value, not the GPO you edited. See Run gpupdate, gpresult and rsop.
    • Check R1+ Manage users in Active Directory Users and Computers or ADAC because a DC has no local users and lusrmgr.msc does not work. Users fixed in the wrong place are never scored. See No local users on a domain controller, Open the ADUC and ADAC consoles.
    • Do R2+ Clear PasswordNeverExpires, PasswordNotRequired, AllowReversiblePasswordEncryption, DoesNotRequirePreAuth and TrustedForDelegation on user accounts. Risky account flags are a common planted User Auditing item. See Fix dangerous account flags, Fix: clear risky AD user flags (DC).
    • Do R2+ Use Search-ADAccount -LockedOut, -PasswordNeverExpires and -AccountDisabled, then unlock authorized users with Unlock-ADAccount. User is not locked out was scored on G3. See Search-ADAccount quick finds.
    • Do R2+ Remove unauthorized members from DnsAdmins and Group Policy Creator Owners. Both groups can be used to take over a DC. See Check privileged group membership, Check DnsAdmins and the DNS plugin DLL.
    • Do R2+ Set advanced audit policy in the Default Domain Controllers Policy for Account Logon, Account Management, DS Access including Directory Service Changes, Logon/Logoff and Policy Change. On a DC auditpol settings are overwritten by GPO. See Audit policy for domain controllers, Audit directory service access.
    • Do R2+ Set the same Security Options, including SMB signing, in the Default Domain Controllers Policy instead of secpol.msc or the registry. Security Options set locally on a DC are overwritten by the DC GPO. See Security options for domain controllers, Signing on a DC comes from the GPO, Security options for domain controllers.
    • Do R2+ Stop and disable the Print Spooler on the DC. (not: README requires printing) Spooler on a DC enables PrintNightmare and coercion attacks. See Disable the print spooler on DCs, Fix: Print Spooler off (DC without printing).
    • Check R2+ Read every user's Description and logon script fields for passwords or hints. Planted passwords and forensics clues often sit in the Description field. See Read the description and logon script fields.
    • Do State+ Back up every GPO with Backup-GPO -All -Path C:\GPOBackup before editing domain policy. A bad GPO edit can lock everyone out or break scoring; a backup restores it in seconds. See Back up and restore GPOs.
    • Do State+ Remove Everyone and Anonymous Logon from Pre-Windows 2000 Compatible Access. It lets anonymous users read the directory. See Clean up the Pre-Windows 2000 group.
    • Do State+ Reset every non-admin domain user to a strong team password in one pass when many users have weak passwords. (not: README gives or protects passwords) Bulk reset clears weak password items fast without missing any. See Reset every user's password at once.
    • Do State+ Set Send NTLMv2 response only, refuse LM and NTLM and Do not store LAN Manager hash in the Default Domain Controllers Policy. LM and NTLMv1 on a DC expose every domain hash. See Disable NTLMv1 and LM hashes.
    • Do State+ Require LDAP server signing and verify the DC security option registry values after gpupdate. Unsigned LDAP allows relay attacks against the DC. See Security options for domain controllers, Verify the registry values.
    • Do State+ Set ms-DS-MachineAccountQuota to 0 on the domain. Stops normal users creating computer accounts for attacks. See Set MachineAccountQuota to 0, Fix: MachineAccountQuota and Recycle Bin (DC).
    • Do State+ Enable the AD Recycle Bin with Enable-ADOptionalFeature. Lets you restore a user deleted by mistake. See Enable the AD Recycle Bin.
    • Do State+ Search SYSVOL for cpassword in Groups.xml and other GPP files and remove the stored passwords. GPP passwords decrypt with a public key. See Search SYSVOL for GPP passwords (cpassword).
    • Do State+ Run dcdiag /q, nltest /dsgetdc and net share to confirm AD, DNS, ADWS, SYSVOL and NETLOGON are healthy after your changes. A silent AD break can cost many points at once. See SYSVOL or NETLOGON share missing, DNS or AD broken, ADWS not running.
    • Check State+ Find users whose primaryGroupID is 512 or 519 because they do not show in Domain Admins member lists. Primary group membership hides admins from the usual checks. See Find users hidden through primary group.
    • Check State+ Run Get-ADFineGrainedPasswordPolicy -Filter * and remove or fix weak password settings objects. A weak PSO overrides the domain password policy for its targets. See Find and fix fine-grained password policies.
    • Check State+ Check FullSecureChannelProtection is 1 and no vulnerable Netlogon allow list exists. Zerologon gives instant domain admin. See Check Zerologon protection.
    • Check State+ Check SYSVOL and NETLOGON permissions so only admins and SYSTEM can write. Writable SYSVOL lets anyone push scripts to every machine. See Check SYSVOL and NETLOGON permissions.
    • Check State+ List all GPOs and links with Get-GPO -All, investigate any GPO the README does not explain, and unlink or disable a bad one before deleting it. Unknown GPOs often push bad settings that override your fixes. See Find suspicious GPOs, What to look for in an unknown GPO, Disable, unlink or delete a bad GPO.
    • Do Semis+ Add README domain admins to Protected Users and mark them Account is sensitive and cannot be delegated, but leave service accounts out. Never add the account you are logged in as or service accounts, because Protected Users blocks NTLM, cached logons and delegation. Protected Users blocks NTLM, delegation and cached credentials for admins. See Add admins to Protected Users, Mark admin accounts as sensitive.
    • Do Semis+ Run the AD backdoor sweep and work through each finding. Semifinal Server images hide AD persistence beyond group membership. See Run the AD backdoor sweep.
    • Do Semis+ Remove non-default entries from the AdminSDHolder ACL and force SDProp to re-run. A planted AdminSDHolder ACE re-grants control of every admin hourly. See Clean AdminSDHolder and force SDProp, Check AdminSDHolder permissions.
    • Do Semis+ Remove Replicating Directory Changes and Replicating Directory Changes All rights on the domain root from anyone but DCs and built-in admin groups. DCSync rights let a normal user dump every password hash. See DCSync rights on the domain.
    • Do Semis+ Remove unconstrained, constrained and resource-based delegation from accounts that are not DCs or README services. Delegation backdoors let attackers impersonate admins. See Delegation backdoors, Find unconstrained delegation.
    • Do Semis+ Clear Do not require Kerberos preauthentication and remove SPNs that no README service needs from user accounts. AS-REP and Kerberoastable accounts give offline password cracking. See Kerberoastable and AS-REP roastable accounts, Find accounts with SPNs (Kerberoastable).
    • Do Semis+ Inspect GPOs for scheduled tasks, startup scripts, restricted groups and user rights that add attacker access. GPO persistence reapplies backdoors to every machine. See GPO-based persistence.
    • Do Semis+ Review every script in NETLOGON and SYSVOL Policies folders and every user scriptPath for malicious commands. Logon scripts run attacker code for every user. See Malicious logon scripts in SYSVOL and NETLOGON.
    • Check Semis+ Run Get-ADGroupMember -Recursive on every privileged group to find rogue admins added through nested groups. Nested membership hides admins from a flat group view. See Rogue admins through nested groups.
    • Check Semis+ Check every account for SIDHistory values containing privileged SIDs and clear them. SID history injection grants admin rights invisibly. See SID history injection.
    • Check Semis+ Check msDS-KeyCredentialLink on admin and DC accounts for unexpected values. Shadow credentials let attackers log on without a password. See Shadow credentials.
    • Check Semis+ Check DsrmAdminLogonBehavior is not 2, set a strong DSRM password, and check the krbtgt pwdLastSet date for golden ticket signs. These give persistent domain admin after cleanup. See DSRM, krbtgt and Golden Tickets, Secure the DSRM administrator.
    • Do Nats+ Save a baseline of privileged group members, GPOs, AdminSDHolder ACL and services to files right after hardening. Diffing against a baseline shows red team changes in seconds. See Run the AD backdoor sweep, Watch for the red team.
    • Do Nats+ Watch DC events 4720, 4728, 4732, 4756, 4662, 5136, 4698 and 7045 for new users, group adds, DCSync, AD changes, tasks and services. These are the red team's fingerprints on a DC. See Security events on a domain controller, Watch for the red team.
    • Do Nats+ Re-run the AD baseline diff every 15 minutes, sort Get-GPO -All by ModificationTime, and revert any new admin, GPO or ACL change. Red teams re-add persistence after you clean it. See Run the AD backdoor sweep, List GPOs and their links.
    • Check Nats+ If golden tickets are suspected, reset krbtgt twice with replication time between resets. Only a double reset invalidates forged tickets. See DSRM, krbtgt and Golden Tickets, Leave krbtgt alone.

    #Domain member server

    • Do R2+ Enable Domain member: Digitally encrypt or sign secure channel data (always). (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Scored on H1 Server 2019. See Sign or encrypt the secure channel.
    • Check R2+ On a member server run gpresult /r to see which domain GPOs set password and lockout policy, and fix local accounts locally. Domain policy overrides local policy for domain accounts, so local fixes may not show. See Member server differences.
    • Check Semis+ Run gpresult /h on the member server to find domain GPOs pushing local admins, scripts or tasks. Local fixes are reverted if a domain GPO re-applies the backdoor. See Member server differences, Run gpupdate, gpresult and rsop.

    #README requires Remote Desktop

    • Don't R1+ Do not turn off Remote Desktop, stop TermService or block TCP 3389 when the README requires RDP. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Disabling required RDP cost 5 to 10 points on K7, G2 and G4. See Penalties seen in past keys, Harden Remote Desktop when it is required.
    • Do R1+ Require Network Level Authentication by setting UserAuthentication to 1. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) RDP NLA enabled was scored on K7 Server 2022. See Harden Remote Desktop when it is required.
    • Do R2+ Make Remote Desktop Users membership match the README exactly. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Updated Remote Desktop Users group was scored on R1. See Limit which users can connect by RDP.
    • Do R2+ Set the RDP security layer to SSL (SecurityLayer 2), encryption level High and fEncryptRPCTraffic to 1. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) RDP security layer and secure RPC were scored on K4 and H1. See Fix: Remote Desktop hardened (README requires RDP), Harden Remote Desktop when it is required.
    • Do State+ Turn on Do not allow supported Plug and Play device redirection and drive redirection. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Plug and Play redirection was scored on H1. See Harden Remote Desktop when it is required.
    • Do State+ Set the RDP hardening on a DC in the Default Domain Controllers Policy so it is not overwritten. (Domain controller) Registry edits on a DC are reverted by GPO. See RDP settings by GPO on a DC.
    • Check Nats+ Monitor RDP logons with event 4624 logon type 10 and TerminalServices-LocalSessionManager events 21 and 25. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) RDP is the red team's favourite way back in when it must stay on. See Limit which users can connect by RDP, Watch for the red team.

    #README requires SSH

    • Do R2+ Keep the OpenSSH Server service (sshd) running and Automatic, harden C:\ProgramData\ssh\sshd_config (no empty passwords, no unknown AllowUsers) and review administrators_authorized_keys. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) README-required SSH must stay up; keys in administrators_authorized_keys give silent admin access. See OpenSSH Server.

    #README requires Windows file shares

    • Don't R1+ Do not remove the README share or delete business files inside it. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Removing the AFA share or its files cost 5 points on K7 and G3. See Shares you must keep, A share or business file was removed.
    • Do R1+ Delete plaintext password files from the share but keep the share folder itself. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) G3 scored removing C:\Share\secret.txt and required the folder to stay. See Find plaintext password files, How the scoring engine checks removal items.
    • Do R2+ Replace Everyone Full Control on the required share with the README users or groups and the least access they need. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Share permissions are an Application Security Settings item. See Tighten share permissions on a required share.
    • Do R2+ Fix NTFS permissions on the share folder with icacls so Everyone and Users cannot write. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) NTFS permissions apply even when share permissions are tight. See Fix NTFS permissions with icacls.
    • Check Semis+ On Server 2022 check Get-SmbServerConfiguration EncryptionCiphers lists AES-256-GCM and AES-128-GCM. (Server 2022) Server 2022 adds cipher settings that Server 2019 lacks. See Check SMB encryption ciphers on Server 2022.

    #README requires an FTP server

    • Don't R1+ Do not stop the FTP service or delete the FTP site and its folder when the README requires FTP. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Stopping a critical service is a 5 point penalty. See Server changes that break critical services, Find the FTP site settings.
    • Do R1+ Turn off FTP anonymous authentication and turn on basic authentication. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Anonymous authentication disabled was scored on P2. See Turn off anonymous FTP and turn on basic authentication.
    • Do R2+ Require SSL for FTP control and data channels. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) FTP require SSL connections was scored on P2. See Require SSL (FTPS).
    • Do R2+ Turn on FTP logon attempt restrictions and FTP logging. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) FTP logon restrictions enabled was scored on P2. See Logging, logon attempt limits and IP restrictions.
    • Do R2+ If FileZilla Server is the FTP server, require TLS 1.3 minimum, disable anonymous users and update it in place. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) FileZilla minimum TLS 1.3 was scored on P1. See Harden FileZilla Server when the README requires it, FileZilla Server.
    • Do State+ Turn on FTP user isolation and limit authorization rules to README users with only the permissions they need. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Stops users reading or writing other users' files. See Turn on user isolation, Tighten authorization rules.

    #README requires a web server

    • Don't R1+ Do not stop W3SVC or WAS or remove the Web-Server role when the README requires a website. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Critical web service removed was a 5 point penalty on G1. See Server changes that break critical services.
    • Do R1+ Turn off directory browsing on every IIS site. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) A basic IIS hardening check that leaks file lists when on. See Turn off directory browsing.
    • Do R1+ Delete phpinfo.php, info.php and test pages from the web root while keeping the site files. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Removed phpinfo file was scored on H2. See Remove web files such as phpinfo.
    • Do R2+ Set IIS error pages to custom errors so detailed errors are not shown to remote users. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) IIS detailed errors disabled was scored on H1. See Turn off debug and detailed errors in web.config.
    • Do R2+ Add an HTTPS binding and turn on Require SSL for the site. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) IIS requires SSL connections was scored on H2. See Add an HTTPS binding, Require SSL.
    • Do R2+ Remove WebDAV publishing unless the README needs it. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) WebDAV allows file uploads to the web root. See Remove WebDAV.
    • Do State+ Hide the Server and X-Powered-By headers, turn on request filtering and turn on IIS logging for every site. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Reduces fingerprinting and blocks common exploit requests. See Hide the Server and X-Powered-By headers, Request filtering, Turn on logging.
    • Do State+ Set application pools to ApplicationPoolIdentity instead of LocalSystem or an admin account. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) A compromised site then cannot run as SYSTEM. See Set the application pool identity.
    • Do State+ Make C:\inetpub\wwwroot read-only for IIS_IUSRS and IUSR, remove Everyone write and disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Writable web roots let attackers drop web shells. See Fix permissions on C:\inetpub\wwwroot, Disable TLS 1.0 and 1.1.
    • Do State+ Hunt web shells in web roots and upload folders by looking for recently changed .aspx, .asp and .php files with eval or cmd calls. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Web shells are the most common web persistence. See Hunt for web shells.
    • Do Nats+ Back up the web root and IIS config with appcmd add backup so you can restore a defaced or broken site fast. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Web uptime and content checks are scored under attack. See Hunt for web shells, Keep services up.

    #README requires PHP

    • Do R2+ In php.ini set display_errors Off, expose_php Off and allow_url_include Off. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) PHP display errors disabled was scored on H2. See Harden Apache, PHP and MariaDB when the README requires them.

    #README requires WordPress or a CMS

    • Don't R1+ Do not delete or move the WordPress folder, wp-login.php or wp-config.php while cleaning web files. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Web-file items check WordPress stays intact; G1 penalized breaking it. See How the scoring engine checks removal items.
    • Do R2+ Remove unauthorized WordPress admin users, update core and plugins and protect wp-config.php from web access. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) CMS admin users and versions are Application Security items. See Harden Apache, PHP and MariaDB when the README requires them, Apache, XAMPP and PHP on Windows.

    #README requires MySQL or MariaDB

    • Don't R1+ Do not stop or uninstall MySQL or MariaDB when the README or WordPress needs it. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) MySQL removal was a 5 point penalty on G1. See Server changes that break critical services.
    • Do R2+ Set a strong MySQL root password, remove anonymous users and the test database, and bind to 127.0.0.1 when only local apps use it. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Default MySQL accounts are a classic planted weakness. See Harden Apache, PHP and MariaDB when the README requires them.

    #README requires SQL Server

    • Don't R1+ Do not stop or uninstall the SQL Server instance service when the README requires it. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Stopping a critical service is a 5 point penalty. See SQL Server Express.
    • Do R2+ Disable or strongly password the sa login, remove unauthorized sysadmin logins and keep xp_cmdshell off. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Weak SQL logins give attackers SYSTEM-level command execution. See Harden SQL Server when the README requires it.

    #README requires DNS

    • Don't R1+ Do not remove the DNS Server role or stop the DNS service. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) AD needs DNS and the README service check fails without it. See How not to break AD, DNS or AD broken.
    • Do R2+ Turn off zone transfers or limit them to the listed servers on every zone. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Open zone transfers leak the whole network map. See Stop zone transfers.
    • Do R2+ Set dynamic updates to Secure only on AD-integrated zones. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Nonsecure updates let anyone add or hijack records. See Set dynamic updates to Secure only, Fix: DNS zones (secure updates, no transfers).
    • Do State+ Turn on DNS logging and the global query block list with wpad and isatap. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Stops WPAD hijacking through DNS. See Turn on the global query block list, Turn on DNS logging.
    • Check State+ Look for rogue zones, records such as wpad or fake A records for business hosts, and forwarders that do not point to legitimate resolvers. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Malicious records redirect users to attacker hosts. See Find malicious DNS records and zones, Check recursion and forwarders.
    • Do Nats+ Export DNS zones with dnscmd /zoneexport and watch for added or changed records. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Restoring a zone quickly keeps AD and websites resolving. See Find malicious DNS records and zones, Keep services up.

    #README requires DHCP

    • Don't R1+ Do not stop or remove the DHCP Server service when the README requires DHCP. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) P1 required DHCP to keep running. See DHCP Server, Server changes that break critical services.
    • Do R2+ Turn on DHCP audit logging with Set-DhcpServerAuditLog -Enable $true. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Audit logs record leases for forensics. See DHCP: turn on audit logging, Harden DHCP when the README requires it.
    • Check State+ Check every scope's router (003) and DNS server (006) options point to the real hosts. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) A planted DNS option sends every client to the attacker. See DHCP: check scopes and options.

    #README requires mail

    • Don't R1+ Do not stop or uninstall hMailServer or the SMTP service when the README requires mail. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Stopping a critical service is a 5 point penalty. See hMailServer, SMTP Server.
    • Do R2+ Block open relay, require SMTP authentication, turn on TLS and set a strong mail admin password. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Open relay and weak admin passwords are the main mail weaknesses. See Harden hMailServer when the README requires it, Harden SMTP when the README requires it.

    #README requires printing

    • Don't R1+ Do not disable the Print Spooler or remove the Print Server role when the README requires printing, even on a DC. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Stopping a critical service is a 5 point penalty. See Print Server.
    • Do R2+ Restrict printer driver installation to administrators and set Point and Print restrictions. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Prevent users from installing printer drivers was scored on H1. See Harden printing when the README requires it, Restrict printer driver installation.

    #README requires Docker

    • Don't R2+ Do not remove the Containers or Hyper-V feature or stop the docker service when the README requires Docker. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Containers stop and the critical service fails. See Services each role needs, Hyper-V.
    • Do State+ Make sure the Docker daemon is not listening on TCP 2375 without TLS and remove containers and images the README does not mention. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) An exposed Docker API is full remote control of the host. See Find listening ports and their programs, Services each role needs.

    #README allows a remote access tool

    • Don't R1+ Do not uninstall the remote access tool the README allows or move it from its install folder. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Required software removed is a 5 point penalty. See Other remote tools and servers, Wireshark or TeamViewer when required.
    • Do R2+ Update the allowed remote tool, set a strong password and limit unattended access to README users. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Default remote tool settings give attackers easy access. See Other remote tools and servers.

    #README requires WinRM

    • Don't R1+ Do not disable PowerShell remoting or the WinRM service when the README requires it. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Stopping a required service is a 5 point penalty. See Server changes that break critical services.
    • Do R2+ Set WinRM AllowUnencrypted false and Basic auth false for client and service. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Unencrypted WinRM was scored on K1. See Harden WinRM and PowerShell remoting, Fix: WinRM hardened.
    • Check State+ Check TrustedHosts is not * and that Remote Management Users holds only README users. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) A wildcard lets the server connect to and trust any host. See Check TrustedHosts.

    #README requires an IIS application

    • Do R2+ In the ASP.NET web.config set compilation debug false, customErrors On and trace disabled. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Debug and trace leak code and secrets. See Turn off debug and detailed errors in web.config.
    PreviousPlanner rules for Windows 11 and 10NextPlanner rules for Linux and BSD
    GO

    Planner rules for Linux and BSD

    jump:start-plan-linux

    Every rule the Image planner can show, grouped by what triggers it. Level tags show the first round where the rule matters: R1, R2, State, Semis, Nats.

    #Any Linux or BSD image

    • Don't R1+ Do not edit PAM or sudoers without a second root terminal open, and test sudo before closing it. A broken PAM or sudoers file locks every user out of the image. See Locked out by a PAM change, Edit sudoers safely with visudo.
    • Don't R1+ Do not purge the LibreOffice suite that ships with the distribution just because the README does not list it. (not: README requires office apps) It is part of the stock desktop, not planted software, and removing it scores nothing. See Avoid the common Linux penalties, Common planted packages.
    • Don't R1+ Do not purge python3 or perl on Linux even when the README does not mention them. The package manager and desktop depend on them. See Avoid the common Linux penalties, apt or dpkg is locked or interrupted.
    • Don't R1+ Don't delete root, any README user or an authorized user's home directory. Penalties of 5 to 10 points in K2, G1 and G4. See Penalties seen on Linux and similar images, Avoid the common Linux penalties.
    • Don't R1+ Don't edit any file in /etc/pam.d without a backup and a root shell already open in another terminal. One typo in common-auth stops sudo and every login. See Locked out by a PAM change, Back up a file before you edit it.
    • Don't R1+ Don't edit /etc/sudoers or files in /etc/sudoers.d with a plain editor; always use visudo (visudo -f for drop-ins). A syntax error breaks sudo for everyone. See Edit sudoers safely with visudo, sudo is broken.
    • Don't R1+ Don't set ufw default deny outgoing, a firewalld drop zone or 'block out all' in pf. It cuts off apt, DNS and the scoring engine, so updates and score reporting stop. See No network or apt cannot resolve hosts, Check outbound traffic is allowed.
    • Don't R1+ Don't stop, disable, mask or purge a README critical service or its dependencies; harden it instead. Critical service stopped or removed cost 5 points in K3, K6 and G1. See Penalties seen on Linux and similar images, Avoid the common Linux penalties.
    • Don't R1+ Don't remove required software (Firefox, Thunderbird, LibreOffice, Perl and others the README names) and read the package manager's list of packages to be removed before confirming any purge. Removing required software cost 5 points each in K1 to K7 and G2 to G3. See Penalties seen on Linux and similar images, Avoid the common Linux penalties.
    • Don't R1+ Don't delete the Music folder or home directory that holds prohibited files; delete only the files. Removal items check that the parent folder still exists. See Avoid the common Linux penalties, Find prohibited media files.
    • Do R1+ Run the read-only Linux recon script and save its report before fixing anything. A baseline of users, sudoers, ports, cron and packages shows what changed later and what is planted. See Read-only recon script, First 10 minutes.
    • Do R1+ Search /home and other data folders for media files with find -iname and delete the files, keeping the folders. Prohibited MP3 files are removed is on most Linux keys. See Find prohibited media files.
    • Do R1+ Purge nmap, wireshark, kismet, ophcrack, john and similar tools when the README does not require them. (not: README allows security tools) Prohibited software removed lines named these packages. See Common planted packages, Snippet to preview removing hacking tools.
    • Do R1+ Walk the Linux checklist final pass and confirm every critical service is active with systemctl status (service <name> status on FreeBSD). A stopped critical service is a penalty. See Final pass, Avoid the common Linux penalties.
    • Do R1+ Read the whole README and write down authorized users, admins, critical services, required software and any 'do not change' lines before touching the image. Every penalty seen in past keys came from breaking something the README protected. See Read the README first, First 10 minutes.
    • Do R1+ Open a second terminal with a root shell (sudo -i, or su - on Debian) and keep it open for the whole round. A spare root shell is how you undo a bad PAM, sudoers or SSH edit without a lockout. See Use sudo or a root shell, Locked out by a PAM change.
    • Do R1+ Copy every config file before you edit it (sudo cp file file.bak) so any change can be reverted in seconds. Undoing a penalty is fast only when the original file still exists. See Back up a file before you edit it, Undo a penalty.
    • Do R1+ Give every human user a strong password with sudo passwd <user> or chpasswd, except passwords the README says to keep. Changed insecure password was scored in K6, R2, SR2 and G1. See Set passwords for every user, Snippet to set passwords from a list.
    • Do R1+ Find accounts other than root with UID 0 (awk -F: '$3==0' /etc/passwd) and delete them or give them a normal UID (FreeBSD's toor is expected but must stay locked). An extra UID 0 account is a full root backdoor. See Remove extra UID 0 accounts, Read /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow and /etc/group.
    • Do R1+ Set PASS_MAX_DAYS 90, PASS_MIN_DAYS 1 and PASS_WARN_AGE 7 in /etc/login.defs. (not: FreeBSD and not: README states password policy values) Default minimum and maximum password age were scored in K3, R1, SR2, G1, H1 and H2. See Set password aging in login.defs, Snippet to set login.defs aging values.
    • Do R1+ Allow every README service port before enabling the firewall (ufw allow, firewall-cmd --add-service, pass rules in pf.conf). A blocked critical service is scored as down and costs points. See Allow README-required services, Common ports and services.
    • Do R1+ Set net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies=1 and net.ipv4.ip_forward=0 (skip forwarding when Docker is required) in /etc/sysctl.d/99-cp.conf and run sudo sysctl --system. (not: FreeBSD) SYN cookies were scored in K3, R2, G1, H1 and H2; IPv4 forwarding in K3. See Write the sysctl hardening file, Snippet to write the sysctl hardening file.
    • Do R1+ Set /etc/shadow and /etc/gshadow to 640 root:shadow (000 root:root on Fedora) and /etc/passwd and /etc/group to 644 root:root. (not: FreeBSD) Insecure permissions on shadow were scored in K3, H1 and H2. See Correct permissions for system files, Snippet to fix permissions on account files.
    • Do R1+ List listening ports with sudo ss -tulpn and running services with systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running. (not: FreeBSD) Service Auditing items are found by comparing this list to the README. See List listening ports and services, Read ss output.
    • Do R1+ Stop and disable services the README does not need with sudo systemctl disable --now <svc>, then purge the package. (not: FreeBSD) The engine accepts a stopped and disabled service or a removed package. See Stop, disable, mask or purge a service, Commonly planted services.
    • Do R1+ When the README does not list SSH, stop and disable it and purge openssh-server (sysrc sshd_enable=NO and service sshd stop on FreeBSD). (not: README requires SSH) OpenSSH service disabled or removed was scored in R2. See Remove SSH when it is not required, Disable services in rc.conf.
    • Do R1+ When Samba is not required, disable smbd and nmbd (smb and nmb on Fedora) and purge samba. (not: README requires Samba) Samba (smbd) disabled was scored in G1. See Remove Samba when not required.
    • Do R1+ When FTP is not required, disable and purge vsftpd, pure-ftpd and proftpd. (not: README requires an FTP server) FTP service disabled or removed was scored in K3, K6 and H1. See Remove an FTP server that is not required.
    • Do R1+ When no web server is required, disable and purge apache2 (httpd on Fedora, apache24 on FreeBSD), nginx and lighttpd. (not: README requires a web server and not: README requires WordPress or a CMS) Apache2 disabled or removed was scored in R1, SR2 and H2. See Remove Apache, nginx or PHP when not required, Decide whether the web server is required.
    • Do R1+ When no database is required, disable and purge mysql-server or mariadb-server. (not: README requires MySQL or MariaDB and not: README requires WordPress or a CMS) Unneeded database servers are Service Auditing items. See Remove a database server that is not required.
    • Do R1+ When PostgreSQL is not required, disable and purge it. (not: README requires PostgreSQL) PostgreSQL disabled was scored in G1. See Remove a database server that is not required.
    • Do R1+ When DNS is not required, disable and purge bind9 (named). (not: README requires DNS) DNS service disabled or removed was scored in H2. See Remove a daemon the README does not need.
    • Do R1+ When mail is not required, disable and purge postfix, dovecot and exim4 (check that the package manager is not removing a required package). (not: README requires mail) POP3 and SMTP services disabled were scored in H1 and H2. See Remove a daemon the README does not need, Harden Dovecot or remove POP3.
    • Do R1+ When no remote tool is allowed, remove VNC servers (x11vnc, tigervnc, vino), xrdp (unless the README requires Remote Desktop), TeamViewer and AnyDesk. (not: README allows a remote access tool) Remote-administration tools count as malware or unwanted software. See Common planted packages, Commonly planted services.
    • Do R1+ When no game or chat server is required, remove minetest-server and IRC daemons (ngircd, inspircd, unrealircd). (not: README requires a game or chat server) IRC daemon and Minetest service removal were scored in H1 and H2. See Remove the Minetest server, Remove IRC servers.
    • Do R1+ Purge hacking tools such as john, hydra, nmap, zenmap, wireshark, ophcrack, nikto, kismet, aircrack-ng, dsniff and fcrackzip. (not: README allows security tools) Prohibited software removed is scored on every Linux key (R1, R2, SR2, G1, H1, H2). See Common planted packages, Snippet to preview removing hacking tools.
    • Do R1+ Purge games and game cheats such as aisleriot, gnome-mines, freeciv, zangband, manaplus and gameconqueror unless the README allows them. Games were scored as unwanted software in K6, R1, R2 and SR2. See Common planted packages.
    • Do R1+ Purge P2P clients such as amule, transmission, qbittorrent, deluge and frostwire. (not: README requires a P2P client) aMule was scored in R2. See Common planted packages.
    • Do R1+ Update Firefox and Thunderbird (apt, snap refresh on Ubuntu, dnf on Fedora). (not: FreeBSD) Firefox and Thunderbird updates were scored in K3, SR2 and H2. See Update Firefox.
    • Do R1+ Find prohibited media with find /home -iname '.mp3' -o -iname '.mp4' -o -iname '*.ogg' and similar, and delete the files. Prohibited MP3 files removed was scored in K3, K6, R1, R2, SR2 and G1. See Find prohibited media files.
    • Do R1+ Check sudo ss -tulpn (sockstat -46l on FreeBSD) for unknown listeners (nc on port 1, python on 1337), kill the process and delete the binary and what starts it. Netcat and python backdoors were scored in K3, K8, H1 and H2. See Find listening backdoors and odd processes, Remove a netcat backdoor started from cron.
    • Do R1+ Check /etc/crontab, /etc/cron.d, the cron.* folders and crontab -l -u <user> for every user, and remove backdoor lines. The K3 netcat backdoor was started from /etc/crontab. See Check system cron, Check user crontabs.
    • Do R1+ Run the final-pass checklist: users, admin groups, firewall status, required services, updates and the scoring report. Late changes often undo earlier fixes. See Final pass.
    • Do R1+ When the score drops, undo the last change from its .bak file right away. The score report updates within minutes, so the last change is almost always the cause. See Score dropped after a change, Undo a penalty, Find which change broke things.
    • Check R1+ Run cat /etc/os-release (freebsd-version on FreeBSD) to confirm the distro and version before following distro-specific steps. Paths for updates, PAM, firewall and the login screen differ between Mint, Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora and FreeBSD. See Tell which distro and version you are on, Differences table.
    • Check R1+ Confirm each README service is active and listening (systemctl is-active or service <name> status on FreeBSD, ss -tlnp, curl localhost) before time runs out. A dead critical service costs points even if you did not notice. See Config files and test commands, Score dropped after a change.
    • Don't R2+ Don't remove nullok while any account you need (including yours) has an empty password; set passwords first. Those accounts can no longer log in or use sudo, which can lock the team out. See Remove nullok, Locked out by a PAM change.
    • Don't R2+ Don't set the lockout threshold below 5 (unless the README gives a lower value) or use unlock_time=0. Thresholds of 1 to 4 were penalized in K1, K2, G2 and G3, and a permanent lock can lock out the team. See Avoid the common Linux penalties, Clear a locked account.
    • Don't R2+ Don't add noexec to /tmp or /var/tmp in /etc/fstab, and test any fstab edit with sudo mount -a before rebooting. noexec /tmp breaks apt and installer scripts, and a bad fstab line can stop boot. See Secure /tmp and /dev/shm mount options, Boot into recovery mode.
    • Don't R2+ Don't reboot or log out after PAM, fstab, GRUB or display manager changes until you have tested a new login in a second session. A broken boot or login costs the rest of the round. See Locked out by a PAM change, Boot into recovery mode.
    • Do R2+ Run the read-only recon script and save its report to see users, sudoers, ports, cron and services in one pass. A read-only sweep finds most planted items in minutes without changing anything. See Read-only recon script, Read the recon report.
    • Do R2+ Look in /etc/passwd for accounts under UID 1000 with a real login shell and remove the ones that are not system accounts. Removed hidden user was scored in K8, H1 and H2. See Find hidden users, Read /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow and /etc/group.
    • Do R2+ Apply aging to existing human users with sudo chage -m 1 -M 90 -W 7 <user>, since login.defs only affects new accounts. (not: FreeBSD and not: README states password policy values) Per-user minimum and maximum password age were scored in H1 and H2. See Apply aging to existing users with chage, Snippet to age passwords of all human users.
    • Do R2+ Set ucredit=-1 lcredit=-1 dcredit=-1 ocredit=-1 dictcheck=1 usercheck=1 in /etc/security/pwquality.conf. (not: FreeBSD) Dictionary based strength checks were scored in H1 and H2. See Turn on password complexity with pwquality.
    • Do R2+ Remove NOPASSWD lines, 'ALL ALL=(ALL)' grants and unknown users from /etc/sudoers and every file in /etc/sudoers.d. Insecure sudo configuration was scored in G1 (/etc/sudoers.d/apollo) and H2. See Remove dangerous sudoers entries, Check the files in /etc/sudoers.d.
    • Do R2+ Add net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects=0, net.ipv4.conf.all.send_redirects=0, net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_source_route=0, net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter=1, net.ipv4.conf.all.log_martians=1, net.ipv4.icmp_echo_ignore_broadcasts=1, net.ipv4.icmp_ignore_bogus_error_responses=1 and net.ipv4.tcp_rfc1337=1 (repeat the conf.all lines for conf.default). (not: FreeBSD) These were scored in G1, H1 and H2. See What each setting does, Write the sysctl hardening file.
    • Do R2+ Set each home directory to 750 (or 700) owned by its user. World-readable homes expose other users' files and keys. See Fix home directory permissions, Snippet to fix home directory permissions.
    • Do R2+ Find world-writable files with find / -xdev -type f -perm -0002 and remove the write bit; add the sticky bit to shared world-writable folders. World-writable scripts and configs let any user run code as root. See Fix world-writable files and folders.
    • Do R2+ Turn on the screen lock after 5 minutes idle (Cinnamon Screensaver settings, or gsettings org.gnome.desktop.screensaver lock-enabled true on GNOME). (not: FreeBSD) Screen locking is listed under Uncategorized OS Settings. See Lock the screen in Cinnamon, Lock the screen in GNOME.
    • Do R2+ After every change to a required service run its config test, restart it, check systemctl status (service <name> status on FreeBSD) and connect to it locally. A typo in a config keeps the service down and costs points. See Config files and test commands, A service will not start.
    • Do R2+ Remove telnetd, rsh-server, tftpd, xinetd, nis, snmpd, squid and avahi-daemon unless the README needs them. These are classic unwanted network services on CyberPatriot images. See Commonly planted services, Harden or remove SNMP, Lock down the Squid proxy.
    • Do R2+ When no PHP application is required, purge php and libapache2-mod-php packages. (not: README requires PHP and not: README requires WordPress or a CMS) Unneeded PHP is attack surface on a web server. See Remove Apache, nginx or PHP when not required.
    • Do R2+ When a DHCP server is not required, disable and purge isc-dhcp-server or kea, but keep the DHCP client. (not: README requires DHCP) A rogue DHCP server is an unwanted network service. See Other network daemons, Commonly planted services.
    • Do R2+ When printing is not required, disable cups and cups-browsed. (not: FreeBSD and not: README requires printing) CUPS listening on the network is an unneeded service. See Lock down CUPS printing.
    • Do R2+ When NFS is not required, disable nfs-kernel-server and rpcbind. (not: README requires NFS) An NFS export can hand out home folders to anyone. See Decide which file services are required, Other network daemons.
    • Do R2+ When Docker is not required, stop running containers, then disable and purge docker. (not: README requires Docker) Docker access equals root on the host. See Secure Docker.
    • Do R2+ Find and remove plaintext password files (grep -ril password /home) that are not README business files. Plaintext credentials are an easy foothold. See Find files containing plaintext passwords.
    • Check R2+ Check user and system crontabs, systemd units and timers, rc.local and shell startup files. A netcat listener started from /etc/crontab was a scored malware item. See Check user crontabs, Check systemd units and timers.
    • Check R2+ List enabled services and find units not owned by any package. Round 2 images add hidden services and attacker-made units. See Find services added by an attacker, List listening ports and services.
    • Check R2+ Check /etc/shadow (/etc/master.passwd on FreeBSD) for empty password fields and weak $1$ hashes, then set real passwords for those users. Empty passwords let anyone log in and block safe nullok removal. See Find empty or weak password hashes.
    • Check R2+ Check /etc/hosts, /etc/resolv.conf and /etc/nsswitch.conf for entries redirecting update or security sites. A hosts redirect breaks updates or sends users to a fake site. See Check /etc/hosts for tampering.
    • Check R2+ List systemctl list-timers and check /etc/systemd/system and ~/.config/systemd/user for units you cannot explain. (not: FreeBSD) Systemd units and timers are the modern cron for backdoors. See Check systemd units and timers.
    • Do State+ Set system accounts that have shells (irc, bin, games, news) to /usr/sbin/nologin with usermod -s and lock them with passwd -l (pw usermod -s and pw lock on FreeBSD). Disabled shell login for irc and password login for bin were scored in H1 and H2. See Fix system accounts with login shells, Disable login for system accounts.
    • Do State+ Add Defaults use_pty and Defaults logfile=/var/log/sudo.log, and remove !authenticate, !env_reset and long timestamp_timeout values. Logging and re-authentication make sudo abuse visible and harder. See Add hardening Defaults, What a clean Mint 21 sudoers file looks like.
    • Do State+ Add kernel.sysrq=0, kernel.dmesg_restrict=1, kernel.kptr_restrict=2, kernel.randomize_va_space=2, fs.protected_hardlinks=1, fs.protected_symlinks=1 and fs.suid_dumpable=0. (not: FreeBSD) Magic SysRq (G1) and dmesg restriction (H2) were scored. See What each setting does.
    • Do State+ Set grub.cfg to 600 root:root (/boot/grub/grub.cfg, /boot/grub2/grub.cfg on Fedora). (not: FreeBSD) GRUB configuration not world readable was scored in H2. See Protect grub.cfg.
    • Do State+ Add 'tmpfs /dev/shm tmpfs defaults,noexec,nosuid,nodev 0 0' to /etc/fstab and run sudo mount -o remount /dev/shm. (not: FreeBSD) Shared memory secured was scored in G1. See Secure /tmp and /dev/shm mount options.
    • Do State+ Install and enable auditd and add watch rules for /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/sudoers and /etc/ssh/sshd_config in /etc/audit/rules.d. (not: FreeBSD) Audit logging is a standard Local Policy item and records tampering. See Turn on auditd, Add audit rules.
    • Check State+ List SUID and SGID files with find / -perm /6000 -type f and remove the bit from copies of shells, interpreters and editors. A SUID bash or find copy is an instant root shell. See Find SUID and SGID programs, Find SUID shell copies.
    • Check State+ Check dpkg -l descriptions (rpm -qa or pkg info elsewhere), snap list and flatpak list for renamed or unusual tools. Harder images rename hacking tools to blend in. See Catch renamed or unusual tools, Find software by other means.
    • Check State+ Check .bashrc, .profile, /etc/profile.d and /etc/bash.bashrc for aliases or commands that hijack sudo, ls or ssh. Shell startup files run on every login. See Check shell startup files and aliases, Check motd, login and shell startup scripts.
    • Do Semis+ Add kernel.yama.ptrace_scope=1, kernel.unprivileged_bpf_disabled=1, net.core.bpf_jit_harden=2, kernel.perf_event_paranoid=3, fs.protected_fifos=2, fs.protected_regular=2 and IPv6 accept_redirects=0 and accept_ra=0. (not: FreeBSD) Semifinal keys go beyond the common network items. See What each setting does, Other checks top teams make.
    • Do Semis+ Block usb-storage and unused filesystems and protocols (cramfs, freevxfs, dccp, sctp, rds) with 'install <mod> /bin/false' in /etc/modprobe.d. (not: FreeBSD) Common hardening items on harder images. See Disable USB storage, Blacklist kernel modules including usb-storage.
    • Do Semis+ Run getcap -r / 2>/dev/null and remove cap_setuid, cap_dac_override or cap_sys_admin from interpreters and shells with setcap -r. (not: FreeBSD) File capabilities give root without a SUID bit, so SUID sweeps miss them. See Find dangerous file capabilities.
    • Do Semis+ Create /etc/cron.allow and /etc/at.allow (/var/cron/allow and /var/at/at.allow on FreeBSD) listing only root and README admins, and set /etc/crontab to 600. Stops ordinary users from scheduling persistence. See Restrict cron and at with allow files.
    • Do Semis+ Make sure /etc/ld.so.preload does not exist or is empty, and look for LD_PRELOAD in /etc/environment and profile files. (not: FreeBSD) A preload library hides files and processes from every tool. See Check /etc/ld.so.preload, Check LD_PRELOAD and ld.so.preload.
    • Do Semis+ Run rkhunter --check and chkrootkit (and clamscan on home and web roots), then verify each finding by hand. Scanners point to hidden files fast, though they report false positives. See Run rkhunter and chkrootkit, Run rootkit and malware scanners.
    • Do Semis+ Check systemd generators, *.service.d override files with ExecStartPre, path units, user units and loginctl lingering users. (not: FreeBSD) Semifinal persistence hides in systemd features beyond plain unit files. See Check systemd generators, timers and user units, Harden systemd.
    • Do Semis+ Work through the full persistence sweep list (cron, at, systemd, rc, shell files, SSH, PAM, preload, modules, udev, apt hooks). Planted backdoors on hard images use more than one location. See Sweep the persistence locations, Other persistence spots.
    • Check Semis+ Sweep PAM modules, /etc/ld.so.preload, package manager hooks (apt or dnf), udev rules, MOTD scripts and authorized_keys for persistence. Semifinal images hide persistence in less common locations. See Sweep the persistence locations, Check the PAM stack for backdoor lines.
    • Check Semis+ Work through the advanced Linux list (GRUB password, /tmp and /dev/shm options, cron.allow, TMOUT, umask, module blacklists). Semifinal images add obscure settings beyond the basic hardening. See Advanced hardening for later rounds (PAM, sudo, boot, mounts, kernel), Other checks top teams make.
    • Check Semis+ Check root-equivalent groups (sudo, wheel, adm, docker, lxd, disk, shadow, root) for any user who should not be there. Membership in docker, lxd or disk gives root without touching sudoers. See Find root-equivalent group memberships.
    • Check Semis+ Look for sudo rules that allow shell escapes (vim, less, find, python, tee, bash), extra #includedir paths and Defaults !authenticate. Semifinal images hide root access in harmless-looking sudo grants. See Find insecure sudo configurations, Remove dangerous sudoers entries.
    • Check Semis+ Check /etc/polkit-1/rules.d and localauthority for rules that return polkit.Result.YES for non-admins. (not: FreeBSD) A polkit rule gives admin actions without sudo. See Check polkit rules.
    • Check Semis+ Check passwd, shadow, sudoers, crontabs and authorized_keys with lsattr (chflags on FreeBSD) and clear planted +i or +a flags. Immutable flags make your fixes fail with Operation not permitted. See Remove immutable and append-only flags, Find and clear immutable files, Operation not permitted even as root.
    • Check Semis+ Set a GRUB superuser password with grub-mkpasswd-pbkdf2 in /etc/grub.d/40_custom, mark normal entries --unrestricted, run update-grub (grub2-mkconfig -o /boot/grub2/grub.cfg on Fedora) and record the password. (not: FreeBSD) Stops single-user boot to a root shell without blocking normal boot. See Set a GRUB password.
    • Check Semis+ Compare lsmod with packaged modules, check /etc/modules-load.d and /proc/sys/kernel/tainted for unknown modules. (not: FreeBSD) Kernel rootkits load as modules. See Check kernel modules, Check kernel modules and kernel taint.
    • Check Semis+ Compare ps output with /proc, list dot folders in /dev, /tmp, /var/tmp and /dev/shm, and check ls -l /proc/*/exe for deleted binaries. Rootkits hide processes and run binaries that were deleted from disk. See Find hidden processes and files, Recover deleted and deleted-but-open files.
    • Don't Nats+ Don't block the scoring engine or gray team addresses, or deny whole subnets, when blocking attackers. Services the scorer cannot reach count as down. See Keep services up, ufw blocks SSH or a required service.
    • Don't Nats+ Don't plan on running prewritten hardening scripts at Finals; practice typing the commands from the guide. Scripts are reported as banned at National Finals. See Practice for Finals, Resources, scripts and AI.
    • Do Nats+ Diff /etc/passwd, /etc/group and /etc/sudoers.d every 15 minutes and investigate any new account, admin or sudo rule. The red team adds accounts and sudo rules to keep access. See Watch for the red team, Read /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow and /etc/group.
    • Do Nats+ Compare ss -tunap (sockstat on FreeBSD) and ps auxf against your baseline regularly and kill new unknown listeners and connections. Red team implants show up as new processes and outbound connections. See Watch for the red team, Find listening backdoors and odd processes.
    • Do Nats+ Assign one person to watch service uptime and the red team, one to hardening and one to injects. National Finals score uptime, injects and red team defense at the same time. See Split the work, What National Finals involves.
    • Do Nats+ Back up every critical service config, the web root and a database dump (mysqldump or pg_dump) before hardening. Fast restores keep services up after red team defacement or deletion. See Keep services up, Back up a file before you edit it.
    • Do Nats+ Rotate passwords for every account the scoring engine does not use, early and again mid-round. (not: README gives or protects passwords) The red team starts with known or default credentials. See Watch for the red team, Set passwords for every user.
    • Do Nats+ Run a loop that checks every critical service every 30 seconds (watch -n 30 'systemctl is-active <svc>; ss -tlnp') and restart anything that drops (service <name> status on FreeBSD). Service uptime is scored continuously at Finals. See Keep services up, Config files and test commands.
    • Do Nats+ Watch logins live with tail -F on /var/log/auth.log (/var/log/secure on Fedora) or journalctl -f, and check who, last and lastb regularly. New sessions and sudo use show the red team as it arrives. See Read authentication logs and the journal, Services and logs on Fedora, Watch for the red team.
    • Do Nats+ Watch established connections (watch -n 5 'ss -tunap state established', sockstat -c on FreeBSD) and new processes (ps -eo pid,ppid,user,lstart,cmd --sort=start_time | tail). Red team shells show up as new connections and child processes. See Find listening backdoors and odd processes, Watch for the red team.
    • Do Nats+ When you find an attacker session, kill it (pkill -KILL -t pts/N), lock or re-password the account, remove planted keys and deny the source IP. Removing access quickly limits what the red team can break. See Watch for the red team, Remove or deny rules.
    • Do Nats+ Add auditd watch rules with keys on passwd, shadow, sudoers, sshd_config, crontabs and the web root, and check ausearch -k <key> -ts recent often. (not: FreeBSD) Audit keys show exactly which file the red team touched and when. See Add audit rules, Logs to know.
    • Do Nats+ Re-check cron, systemd timers, authorized_keys, sudoers and /etc/passwd every 30 minutes. The red team re-plants persistence after you remove it. See Sweep the persistence locations, Watch for the red team.
    • Do Nats+ Treat each inject as scored work: assign an owner, do exactly what it asks and submit in the requested format before the deadline. Injects are part of the Network Security Master Challenge score. See Write business injects, Split the work.
    • Check Nats+ If an inject asks for a service or user you removed, add it back and harden it rather than refusing. Business requests outrank earlier cleanup decisions. See Write business injects, Config files and test commands.

    #Mint, Ubuntu and Debian

    • Do R1+ Install libpam-pwquality and set minlen=10 (or the README value) on the pam_pwquality.so line in /etc/pam.d/common-password. Minimum password length was scored in K3, R2, H1, H2 and N1. See Turn on password complexity with pwquality.
    • Do R1+ Turn on the firewall with sudo ufw default deny incoming and sudo ufw enable (apt install ufw first on Debian). Firewall protection enabled is scored on almost every Linux key (K3, K6, R1, R2, SR2, G1, H1, H2). See Turn on the firewall, Snippet to enable ufw.
    • Do R1+ Start sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y early in a spare terminal (after apt-mark hold on any package the README pins) and let it run. Bash, systemd, APT, sudo, Firefox and service updates were scored in SR2, R2, H1 and H2. See Install updates.
    • Do R1+ Check apt sources for the security repository and remove unknown PPAs or third-party repos. Install updates from important security updates was scored in R1, R2, G1 and H2. See Check repositories for bad sources.
    • Don't R2+ Don't disable systemd-resolved or remove dnsmasq-base just because something listens on port 53 at 127.0.0.53. That is the local resolver; removing it breaks DNS for apt and scoring. See Read ss output, No network or apt cannot resolve hosts.
    • Do R2+ Lock the root password with sudo passwd -l root once a sudo admin account is confirmed working. A root password is a direct login target; sudo admins do not need it. See Lock the root account, Snippet to lock root.
    • Do R2+ Enforce password history with remember=5 (or the README value) on the pam_unix.so line or a pam_pwhistory.so line in common-password. Password history was one of G1's exact tests. See Set password history.
    • Do R2+ Remove nullok from the pam_unix.so line in /etc/pam.d/common-auth. Null passwords do not authenticate was scored in H2. See Remove nullok, Snippet to remove nullok.
    • Do R2+ Set deny=10, unlock_time=1800 and fail_interval=1800 in /etc/security/faillock.conf (or the README values). Account lockout policy was scored in K3 and H1; N1 used deny=5, and keys accept 5 to 10. See Set the lockout values in faillock.conf.
    • Do R2+ Add pam_faillock through a /usr/share/pam-configs/faillock profile and pam-auth-update (preauth, authfail and account lines). faillock.conf does nothing until pam_faillock is in the auth and account stacks. See Add faillock with a pam-auth-update profile, Add pam_faillock to common-auth, Add pam_faillock to common-account.
    • Do R2+ Turn on firewall logging with sudo ufw logging on (medium on later rounds). Logs show scans and blocked backdoor traffic. See Turn on logging.
    • Do R2+ If a full upgrade will not finish, update the scored packages directly with sudo apt install --only-upgrade bash sudo openssh-server systemd apt firefox. Individual package updates were scored in SR2, R2, H1 and H2. See Update specific packages and the kernel.
    • Check R2+ Test PAM changes with su - <user> or sudo -k in a new terminal, and clear locks with faillock --user <user> --reset. Testing before logout catches a broken stack while the root shell is still open. See Test the lockout without logging out, Clear a locked account.
    • Check R2+ Run sudo ufw status numbered and delete allow rules for ports no README service needs (4444, 1337, 31337, 6667). Planted allow rules keep backdoor ports reachable even with the firewall on. See Remove or deny rules.
    • Check R2+ Run sudo aa-status, keep AppArmor enabled with systemctl enable --now apparmor, and set profiles left in complain mode back to enforce. Disabling AppArmor is a common planted weakness. See Check AppArmor.
    • Do State+ Make sure pam_unix.so in common-password uses yescrypt or sha512 and ENCRYPT_METHOD matches in login.defs, then reset weak users' passwords. Password hashed with a secure algorithm was scored in H2. See Check the hashing algorithm, Use a secure password hash algorithm.
    • Check State+ Re-check nullok, remember and minlen after running pam-auth-update, because it rewrites the common-* files. Hand edits silently disappear and the points drop. See Avoid pam-auth-update overwrites.
    • Check State+ Check /etc/default/ufw, /etc/ufw/before.rules and user.rules for planted ACCEPT lines or DEFAULT_INPUT_POLICY=ACCEPT, and ufw reset if needed. A sabotaged ufw shows 'active' while letting everything in. See Reset a sabotaged firewall.
    • Check State+ Also fix the same values in /etc/ufw/sysctl.conf, which ufw applies on start and can undo your file. A planted ufw sysctl file silently reverts scored settings. See Fix the ufw sysctl file.
    • Do Semis+ Audit /etc/pam.d for pam_permit.so in auth lines, pam_exec.so calls and unknown modules, and verify modules with dpkg -V libpam-modules. A PAM backdoor accepts any password and survives user cleanup. See Audit PAM for backdoors, Check the PAM stack for backdoor lines, Find modified system files and PAM backdoors.
    • Do Semis+ Run sudo dpkg -V (or debsums -c) and reinstall any package whose binaries or PAM modules changed. Replaced system binaries are how rootkits hide. See Verify package files with debsums and dpkg, Find modified system files and PAM backdoors.
    • Check Semis+ Look in /etc/apt/apt.conf.d for APT::Update::Pre-Invoke or DPkg::Post-Invoke lines that run unknown commands. An apt hook re-runs a backdoor every time you update. See Check apt hooks.

    #Linux Mint 21

    • Do R1+ In Update Manager > Edit > Preferences > Automation, turn on automatic refresh of the update list and automatic upgrades. The Mint refresh and automatic install items were scored in R1 and R2. See Turn on Update Manager automation.
    • Do R1+ Set allow-guest=false under [Seat:*] in /etc/lightdm/lightdm.conf and check /usr/share/lightdm/lightdm.conf.d for files that turn it back on. Guest account disabled was scored in R2, SR2 and G1. See Set the login options, Where LightDM reads its settings, Snippet to turn off LightDM guest and autologin.
    • Do R1+ Remove autologin-user lines from LightDM files and turn off automatic login in Login Window settings. Automatic login gives anyone at the console a session. See Block passwordless and root logins at the greeter, Set the login options.
    • Don't R2+ Don't log out or restart LightDM after editing its config until lightdm --show-config parses cleanly. A broken greeter leaves you at a black screen with the clock running. See Check the effective LightDM config, Desktop froze or you logged out by accident.
    • Do R2+ Set greeter-hide-users=true, greeter-show-manual-login=true and xserver-allow-tcp=false for LightDM. Greeter user enumeration (H1) and X TCP connections (H2) were scored. See Hide the user list at the greeter, Stop the X server from accepting TCP connections.

    #Ubuntu 22.04

    • Do R1+ In Software & Updates > Updates tick the security source, set daily checks and automatic install of security updates, and confirm APT::Periodic lines in /etc/apt/apt.conf.d/20auto-upgrades. Automatic daily update checks were scored in K3, K6 and SR2. See Set automatic updates in Software & Updates, Configure unattended-upgrades.
    • Do R1+ Set AutomaticLoginEnable=false and remove TimedLoginEnable in /etc/gdm3/custom.conf (/etc/gdm/custom.conf on Fedora). GDM3 replaces LightDM on Ubuntu, so the Mint fix does nothing there. See Turn off automatic login in custom.conf, Harden the GDM3 login screen.
    • Do R2+ Run sudo snap refresh and check snap list, since Firefox is a snap on Ubuntu. apt upgrade does not update snap Firefox. See Update and check snaps.
    • Do R2+ Hide the GDM user list with disable-user-list=true in a dconf file under /etc/dconf/db/gdm.d, then run sudo dconf update. The GDM equivalent of the scored greeter-hide-users item. See Hide the user list.

    #Ubuntu 24.04

    • Do State+ On Ubuntu 24.04 disable both ssh.socket and ssh.service (or purge openssh-server) when SSH is not required. (not: README requires SSH) The socket restarts sshd on the next connection if only the service is disabled. See Ubuntu 24.04 starts SSH from a socket, Remove SSH when it is not required.
    • Check State+ Check /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ubuntu.sources includes noble-security in Suites, since sources.list is empty on 24.04. Ubuntu 24.04 uses deb822 sources, so old sources.list checks miss it. See Read deb822 sources on Ubuntu 24.04.
    • Check State+ Confirm kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1 is still set on Ubuntu 24.04. It is a 24.04 default that blocks namespace privilege escalation, and attackers turn it off. See Check AppArmor and user namespaces on Ubuntu.

    #Debian

    • Don't R1+ Don't lock root or remove su on Debian until sudo is installed and your admin user is in the sudo group. Without sudo, locking root leaves no way to administer the image. See Get sudo working on Debian, sudo is broken.
    • Do R1+ Install unattended-upgrades, run dpkg-reconfigure -plow unattended-upgrades and make sure security.debian.org is in sources.list. Debian has no Software & Updates automation by default. See Turn on automatic updates on Debian, Check Debian apt sources.
    • Check R1+ On Debian check whether sudo is installed and your user is in the sudo group; if not, use su - to get root and apt install sudo. Debian images often ship with root enabled and no sudo, so Ubuntu commands fail. See Get sudo working on Debian, Root shell on Debian without sudo.
    • Check R1+ Check /etc/X11/default-display-manager to see whether Debian uses LightDM or GDM3 and apply that display manager's rules. Debian can ship either greeter. See Debian login screens.

    #Fedora and RHEL

    • Do R1+ Run sudo systemctl enable --now firewalld, check firewall-cmd --list-all and remove unneeded services with --permanent --remove-service then --reload. Fedora uses firewalld; ufw is not the scored firewall there. See Turn on firewalld.
    • Do R1+ Run sudo dnf upgrade --refresh (after dnf versionlock on any README-pinned package), install dnf-automatic, set apply_updates=yes in automatic.conf and enable dnf-automatic.timer. Fedora updates and auto-updates use dnf, not apt. See Install updates with dnf, Turn on automatic updates with dnf-automatic.
    • Do R1+ Check getenforce returns Enforcing and SELINUX=enforcing is set in /etc/selinux/config. SELinux is Fedora's main defense and is often set to permissive on purpose. See Keep SELinux enforcing.
    • Don't R2+ Don't run setenforce 0 to make a service work; fix it with setsebool, semanage port or restorecon. Permissive mode undoes a scored setting and opens the whole system. See Keep SELinux enforcing.
    • Do R2+ Use authselect enable-feature with-faillock and edit /etc/security/faillock.conf and pwquality.conf instead of hand-editing system-auth. authselect overwrites hand edits in /etc/pam.d on Fedora. See Set password policy and lockout with authselect.
    • Do Semis+ Run sudo rpm -Va and reinstall packages with changed binaries (5 or M flags on files in /usr/bin or /usr/lib64/security). The Fedora equivalent of dpkg -V. See Find modified packages with rpm -Va.

    #FreeBSD

    • Do R1+ Write /etc/pf.conf with 'block in all', 'pass out all keep state' and pass rules for README ports, then sysrc pf_enable=YES and service pf start. pf is the usual FreeBSD firewall and is off by default. See Turn on the pf firewall.
    • Do R1+ Run freebsd-update fetch install, pkg update && pkg upgrade (after pkg lock on any README-pinned package) and pkg audit -F. Base system and packages update separately on FreeBSD. See Install updates on FreeBSD.
    • Do R1+ List listeners with sockstat -46l and enabled services with service -e, then disable extras with sysrc <name>_enable=NO. FreeBSD services are switched on in rc.conf, not systemd. See Disable services in rc.conf.
    • Do R2+ Set passwd_format=sha512, minpasswordlen=10 and passwordtime=90d in the default class of /etc/login.conf, then run cap_mkdb /etc/login.conf. FreeBSD keeps password policy in login.conf, not PAM pwquality. See Set password policy on FreeBSD.
    • Do R2+ Set security.bsd.see_other_uids=0, see_other_gids=0, unprivileged_read_msgbuf=0, unprivileged_proc_debug=0, net.inet.tcp.blackhole=2 and net.inet.udp.blackhole=1 in /etc/sysctl.conf. These are the FreeBSD equivalents of the Linux sysctl items. See Set security sysctls and securelevel.
    • Check R2+ Check that the default toor account (UID 0) still has a locked * password and that no other UID 0 user exists. toor is a second root account by design and a common backdoor if given a password. See Manage users with pw, Remove extra UID 0 accounts.
    • Check R2+ Check /etc/rc.conf, /etc/rc.local, /usr/local/etc/rc.d, /etc/crontab, /etc/periodic and /etc/rc.conf.local for persistence. FreeBSD persistence lives in different paths than Linux. See Hunt persistence on FreeBSD.

    #README requires Remote Desktop

    • Don't R2+ Do not purge xrdp when the README requires Remote Desktop; keep xrdp running and allow 3389/tcp only from where the README says. (Any Linux or BSD image) Removing a README-required remote service is a critical-service penalty. See Services and open ports.

    #README requires SSH

    • Don't R1+ Don't enable ufw, firewalld or pf before allowing SSH (22/tcp) when SSH is a critical service. (Any Linux or BSD image) SSH is scored as down the moment the firewall comes up. See ufw blocks SSH or a required service, Allow README-required services.
    • Do R1+ Set PermitRootLogin no in /etc/ssh/sshd_config. (Any Linux or BSD image) SSH root login disabled was scored in K3, K6, R1, SR2, H1 and N1. See Recommended sshd_config settings, Snippet to turn off SSH root login.
    • Do R1+ Run sudo sshd -t before restarting SSH (systemctl restart ssh on Debian family, sshd on Fedora, service sshd restart on FreeBSD). (Any Linux or BSD image) A bad sshd_config stops SSH, a scored critical service. See Test and restart SSH.
    • Don't R2+ Don't set PasswordAuthentication no, change the port or add AllowUsers that leaves out README users unless the README asks. (Any Linux or BSD image) Authorized users and the scoring check must still be able to log in. See Recommended sshd_config settings, Avoid the common Linux penalties.
