    • Do R2+ Set PermitEmptyPasswords no, MaxAuthTries 3, X11Forwarding no, HostbasedAuthentication no, IgnoreRhosts yes, LoginGraceTime 60 and ClientAliveInterval 300. (Any Linux or BSD image) Standard sshd items in Application Security Settings. See Recommended sshd_config settings.
    • Do R2+ Update the SSH server with sudo apt install --only-upgrade openssh-server. (Mint, Ubuntu and Debian) OpenSSH has been updated was scored in R1 and SR2. See Update specific packages and the kernel.
    • Do R2+ On Fedora edit sshd_config and /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/50-redhat.conf, restart sshd, and label any non-standard port with semanage port -a -t ssh_port_t. (Fedora and RHEL) SELinux blocks sshd on unlabeled ports. See Harden SSH on Fedora.
    • Do R2+ On FreeBSD set PermitRootLogin no in /etc/ssh/sshd_config, keep sshd_enable=YES and run service sshd restart. (FreeBSD) FreeBSD uses rc.conf and the service command for sshd. See Harden SSH on FreeBSD.
    • Check R2+ Check /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf, which is read first and wins over the main file, and confirm with sudo sshd -T | grep -i permitroot. (Mint, Ubuntu and Debian) A drop-in can quietly re-enable root or password logins. See Check drop-in files in sshd_config.d.
    • Check R2+ Review ~/.ssh/authorized_keys for every user and root and delete keys nobody can explain. (Any Linux or BSD image) A planted key is a login that survives password changes. See Review authorized_keys.
    • Do State+ On Ubuntu 24.04 apply sshd changes with sudo systemctl daemon-reload and sudo systemctl restart ssh.socket, and keep ssh.socket enabled. (Ubuntu 24.04) 24.04 starts SSH from a socket, so restarting only ssh.service can leave old settings or a dead listener. See Ubuntu 24.04 starts SSH from a socket.
    • Do Semis+ Install fail2ban and enable the sshd jail (or ufw limit ssh on Ubuntu, sshguard on FreeBSD). (Any Linux or BSD image) Brute-force protection on the one service attackers always try. See Set up fail2ban for SSH, Rate-limit SSH.
    • Check Semis+ Check sshd for AuthorizedKeysFile or AuthorizedKeysCommand changes, PermitUserEnvironment, ForceCommand, ~/.ssh/rc and /etc/ssh/sshrc. (Any Linux or BSD image) Semifinal persistence hides in SSH settings, not just in keys. See Check other SSH files, Check SSH keys and sshd settings used for persistence.
    • Do Nats+ Restrict SSH with AllowUsers listing every README user and watch authorized_keys files for new keys. (Any Linux or BSD image) SSH is the red team's usual way back in. See Review authorized_keys, Watch for the red team.

    #README requires Samba

    • Don't R1+ Don't delete the README share, its folder or business files inside it. (Any Linux or BSD image) Removing an authorized share or its files cost 5 points in K7 and G3. See Avoid the common Linux penalties, Decide which file services are required.
    • Do R2+ In smb.conf set server min protocol = SMB2, smb encrypt = required, restrict anonymous = 2 and map to guest = never, then run testparm. (Any Linux or BSD image) Samba SMB1 disabled and encryption required were scored in H2. See Harden Samba, Harden Samba completely.
    • Check R2+ Remove shares the README does not mention, set guest ok = no, and remove unauthorized Samba users found with sudo pdbedit -L. (Any Linux or BSD image) Extra shares and Samba-only users are planted access paths. See Remove extra shares and Samba users.
    • Do State+ Update the samba packages. (Any Linux or BSD image) Samba has been updated was scored in H1 and H2. See Update file sharing servers.

    #README requires an FTP server

    • Do R1+ Allow 21/tcp and the passive port range (pasv_min_port to pasv_max_port) through ufw. (Mint, Ubuntu and Debian) FTP data connections fail without the passive range. See Allow README-required services.
    • Don't R2+ Don't delete business files from the FTP root or change the banner a Forensics Question asks about. (Any Linux or BSD image) Removing authorized files is a penalty, and R2 asked for the FTP banner. See Avoid the common Linux penalties, Harden vsftpd (FTP).
    • Do R2+ In /etc/vsftpd.conf (/etc/vsftpd/vsftpd.conf on Fedora) set anonymous_enable=NO, local_enable=YES, chroot_local_user=YES and ssl_enable=YES with the certificate lines, then restart vsftpd. With chroot_local_user=YES the user's home must not be writable by that user (or add allow_writeable_chroot=YES), or logins fail with "refusing to run with writable root". (Any Linux or BSD image) FTP users may log in with SSL was scored in R2. See Harden vsftpd (FTP), Harden vsftpd completely.
    • Do R2+ Remove world write from the FTP root (local_root or anon_root), for example chmod 755. (Any Linux or BSD image) Insecure permissions on FTP root directory was scored in R2. See Fix the FTP root directory permissions, Fix permissions on the FTP root directory.
    • Do R2+ Update the FTP server package (vsftpd, proftpd or pure-ftpd). (Any Linux or BSD image) Vsftpd has been updated was scored in R2. See Update file sharing servers.
    • Do State+ If the required server is proftpd or pure-ftpd, turn off anonymous login, require TLS and jail users in their config. (Any Linux or BSD image) Same hardening, different config files. See Harden ProFTPD, Harden Pure-FTPd.

    #README requires a web server

    • Do R2+ Set ServerTokens Prod, ServerSignature Off, TraceEnable Off and Options -Indexes in Apache, then run apache2ctl configtest (apachectl configtest on Fedora and FreeBSD). (Any Linux or BSD image) Apache server tokens and trace requests were scored in H1. See Harden Apache2, Harden Apache beyond the basics.
    • Do R2+ If nginx is the web server set server_tokens off and autoindex off, then run sudo nginx -t. (Any Linux or BSD image) The nginx equivalents of the scored Apache items. See Harden nginx, Harden nginx beyond the basics.
    • Do R2+ Delete phpinfo pages and obviously named web shells (info.php, r57.php, c99.php, shell.php) from the web root. (Any Linux or BSD image) phpinfo file removed and PHP web shell removed were scored in G1. See Remove phpinfo files and web shells, Clean up the web root.
    • Do R2+ Update apache2 or nginx and the PHP packages. (Any Linux or BSD image) Apache and PHP updates were scored in G1 and H1. See Update the web stack.
    • Do Semis+ Hunt web shells with grep -rlE 'eval(|base64_decode|shell_exec|passthru|system(' in the web root and look for PHP files in uploads folders or recently modified. (Any Linux or BSD image) Semifinal shells are renamed or hidden inside plugins. See Find web shells, Remove phpinfo files and web shells.
    • Do Nats+ Watch the web root for new or changed PHP files and restore from your backup at once if the site is defaced. (Any Linux or BSD image) A defaced or broken site loses uptime points every check. See Find web shells, Keep services up.

    #README requires PHP

    • Do R2+ In the php.ini the web server uses set expose_php = Off, display_errors = Off and allow_url_include = Off, then restart the web server. (Any Linux or BSD image) PHP expose_php (G1) and display_errors (H1) were scored. See Find the php.ini the web server uses, Set the scored PHP options, Harden PHP.
    • Do State+ Add disable_functions = exec,shell_exec,system,passthru,proc_open,popen and set session.cookie_httponly = 1 in php.ini. (Any Linux or BSD image) Stops most web shells from running commands. See Harden PHP.

    #README requires WordPress or a CMS

    • Don't R1+ Don't delete wp-login.php or other WordPress core files while removing phpinfo pages or web shells. (Any Linux or BSD image) Web-file items check that WordPress is still intact. See Remove phpinfo files and web shells.
    • Don't R1+ Don't remove Apache or nginx, PHP or MySQL/MariaDB when WordPress is required, even if the README names only WordPress. (Any Linux or BSD image) WordPress needs the whole LAMP stack; G1 penalized stopping any of it. See Find the WordPress install and its database, Avoid the common Linux penalties.
    • Don't R2+ Don't drop or re-password the database user in wp-config.php without updating wp-config.php to match. (Any Linux or BSD image) The site shows a database error and is scored as down. See Find the WordPress install and its database.
    • Do State+ Update WordPress core from the dashboard and confirm $wp_version in wp-includes/version.php. (Any Linux or BSD image) WordPress has been updated was scored in G1. See Check the version and update WordPress.
    • Do State+ Remove WordPress administrators the README does not list and reset weak WordPress passwords. (Any Linux or BSD image) WordPress users are a separate account list from Linux users. See Remove unauthorized WordPress administrators.
    • Do State+ Set wp-config.php to 640 and add define('DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT', true) with WP_DEBUG false. (Any Linux or BSD image) The dashboard file editor is the easiest way to plant a shell. See Lock down wp-config.php.
    • Check State+ Remove file-manager, unknown or abandoned plugins and themes. (Any Linux or BSD image) Vulnerable plugins are the usual WordPress entry point. See Remove risky plugins and themes.

    #README requires MySQL or MariaDB

    • Do R2+ Set bind-address = 127.0.0.1 (unless the README says other hosts connect) and local-infile = 0 in the MySQL/MariaDB server config, then restart it. (Any Linux or BSD image) MySQL remote access disabled was scored in G1. See Set MySQL and MariaDB server options, Set the server options.
    • Do R2+ List SELECT user,host FROM mysql.user; drop anonymous users and root@'%', and set a root password. (Any Linux or BSD image) Database accounts are Application Security items. See Check MySQL and MariaDB accounts, Check database accounts by hand.
    • Do State+ Update the MySQL or MariaDB server packages. (Any Linux or BSD image) MySQL has been updated was scored in G1 and H1. See Update the database server.
    • Check State+ Remove phpMyAdmin unless required, or restrict it to localhost and require login. (Any Linux or BSD image) An open phpMyAdmin gives database admin to anyone. See Lock down phpMyAdmin.
    • Check Nats+ Re-list database users and grants during the round and restore from your dump if tables are dropped. (Any Linux or BSD image) Attackers add database users and wipe data. See Check MySQL and MariaDB accounts, Review PostgreSQL roles.

    #README requires PostgreSQL

    • Do R2+ Replace every trust entry in pg_hba.conf with scram-sha-256 (keep peer on the local postgres line), after making sure app roles have passwords, then reload PostgreSQL. (Any Linux or BSD image) PostgreSQL requires authentication for all connections was scored in H2. See Require authentication in pg_hba.conf, Harden PostgreSQL.
    • Do State+ Remove pg_ident.conf maps that map any system user to postgres. (Any Linux or BSD image) Does not map any user to postgres was scored in H2. See Remove user maps to the postgres account.
    • Do State+ Set the files in /etc/postgresql to owner postgres and mode 640 (no world access). (Any Linux or BSD image) Insecure permissions on PostgreSQL configuration files was scored in H2. See Fix permissions on PostgreSQL configuration files.
    • Do State+ In postgresql.conf set listen_addresses = 'localhost' (unless remote clients are required), ssl = on, password_encryption = scram-sha-256 and log_connections = on. (Any Linux or BSD image) Server options in postgresql.conf are Application Security items. See Set the server options in postgresql.conf.
    • Do State+ Update the PostgreSQL packages. (Any Linux or BSD image) PostgreSQL has been updated was scored in H1 and H2. See Update the database server.
    • Check State+ Run \du in psql and remove superuser or login rights from roles the README does not authorize. (Any Linux or BSD image) Extra superuser roles are a database backdoor. See Review PostgreSQL roles.

    #README requires DNS

    • Do R2+ In named.conf.options set allow-transfer { none; } (or the listed secondaries), limit recursion to local networks and set version "none", then run named-checkconf. (Any Linux or BSD image) Open zone transfers and open recursion are the classic BIND weaknesses. See Harden the BIND9 DNS server.

    #README requires DHCP

    • Check State+ Check dhcpd.conf scopes, gateways and DNS options match the README, limit INTERFACESv4 and allow 67/udp in the firewall. (Any Linux or BSD image) A tampered scope sends clients to an attacker gateway. See Other network daemons, Allow README-required services.

    #README requires mail

    • Do R2+ In Postfix limit mynetworks to 127.0.0.0/8, set smtpd_relay_restrictions to reject unauthenticated relay, disable_vrfy_command = yes and a banner without version. (Any Linux or BSD image) An open relay is the main Postfix weakness. See Harden Postfix, Harden the Postfix and Dovecot mail servers.
    • Do State+ In Dovecot set disable_plaintext_auth = yes and ssl = required, and drop pop3 from protocols if only IMAP is needed. (Any Linux or BSD image) Plaintext POP3 was a scored service in H1 and H2. See Harden Dovecot or remove POP3.

    #README requires printing

    • Do R2+ In cupsd.conf listen on localhost:631 unless sharing is required, restrict /admin to admins and turn off cups-browsed browsing. (Any Linux or BSD image) Keeps printing up while removing remote admin access. See Lock down CUPS printing.

    #README requires NFS

    • Do R2+ In /etc/exports remove no_root_squash and '*' clients, use ro where possible, then run sudo exportfs -ra. (Any Linux or BSD image) no_root_squash gives remote root on the export. See Lock down NFS exports.

    #README requires Docker

    • Don't R2+ Don't set net.ipv4.ip_forward=0 on a host running required Docker containers. (Any Linux or BSD image) Docker networking needs forwarding, so published containers go down. See Secure Docker.
    • Do State+ Remove any -H tcp:// (port 2375) listener, keep /var/run/docker.sock 660 root:docker, and check docker ps and docker inspect for privileged containers or host mounts. (Any Linux or BSD image) An open Docker API or privileged container gives root to anyone. See Secure Docker.
    • Do State+ Keep only README admins in the docker group. (Any Linux or BSD image) docker group membership is root-equivalent. See Secure Docker, Find root-equivalent group memberships.

    #README allows a remote access tool

    • Do R2+ Keep only the README remote tool, give it a strong password, disable unattended access you do not need and allow only its port in the firewall. (Any Linux or BSD image) The allowed tool must stay up but should not be an open door. See Other network daemons, Allow README-required services.

    #README requires a game or chat server

    • Do State+ Keep the required game or chat server running as its own non-root user, set its admin or oper password, allow only its port and update it. (Any Linux or BSD image) The service must stay up, so harden it instead of removing it. See Other network daemons, Allow README-required services.
    PreviousPlanner rules for Windows ServerNextPlanner rules by README scenario and service
    GO

    Planner rules by README scenario and service

    jump:start-plan-scenario

    Every rule the Image planner can show, grouped by what triggers it. Level tags show the first round where the rule matters: R1, R2, State, Semis, Nats.

    #README allows security tools

    • Don't R1+ Do not uninstall or move Wireshark, Nmap or any security tool the README requires. Removing required Wireshark was a 5-point penalty. See Wireshark or TeamViewer when required, Required software removed or moved.
    • Don't R1+ Don't remove Wireshark, nmap or other security tools the README requires. (Any Linux or BSD image) Removing required software cost 5 points each in past keys. See Avoid the common Linux penalties.
    • Don't R1+ Do not uninstall the required Wireshark or Nmap; update it in place. (Windows 11 and 10) Removing required Wireshark was a penalty in K1 and K7. See Wireshark or TeamViewer when required, Required software removed or moved.
    • Don't R1+ Do not uninstall or move Wireshark or Nmap when the README requires them; update them in place. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Required software removed is a 5 point penalty. See Wireshark or TeamViewer when required, Required software removed or moved.
    • Do R1+ Still remove hacking tools the README does not name (password crackers such as john, hydra or ophcrack, keyloggers, sniffers other than the listed one). Only the named tools are required; the rest stay unwanted software. See Network tools, Common planted packages.
    • Do R2+ Update the required security tool from its official source without changing its install folder. (not: Updates restricted or version pinned) Required apps earn Application Updates points and must stay at the default path. See Update without changing the install folder, Update specific packages and the kernel.
    • Check State+ Keep Npcap for Wireshark but still remove hacking tools the README does not list, such as password crackers. (Windows 11 and 10) Only named tools are authorized. See Network tools, Wireshark or TeamViewer when required.

    #README requires browsers

    • Don't R1+ Do not uninstall, reinstall to a new path or move the required browser. Required Firefox or Chrome removed or moved from its default path was a 5-point penalty. See Required software removed or moved, Avoid the common Linux penalties.
    • Don't R1+ Do not uninstall a required browser or reinstall it to another folder. (Windows 11 and 10) Required browser removal cost 5 points in K1 and K2. See Required software removed or moved.
    • Do R1+ Update Firefox, Chrome and the other required browsers to the latest version in place. (not: Updates restricted or version pinned and Any Windows image) Firefox and Google Chrome has been updated appear on many keys. See Firefox and Thunderbird, Chrome and Edge.
    • Do R1+ Update Firefox and Chromium with the package manager (apt install --only-upgrade, dnf upgrade or pkg upgrade) or snap refresh on Ubuntu. (not: Updates restricted or version pinned and Any Linux or BSD image) Firefox and Chromium has been updated were scored on Linux keys. See Update Firefox.
    • Do R2+ Turn on the pop-up blocker, add-on install warnings and dangerous site blocking in each required browser. (Any Windows image) Firefox pop-up blocker and add-on warning items were scored. See Firefox settings, Chrome settings.
    • Do R2+ Turn on the pop-up blocker, add-on install warnings and deceptive content blocking in Firefox. (Any Linux or BSD image) Firefox pop-up blocker and add-on warning items were scored. See Set the privacy and security options.
    • Do R2+ Keep and update every README browser (Chrome, Chromium) and set Firefox to block pop-ups, warn on add-on installs and use HTTPS-Only Mode. (Any Linux or BSD image) Chromium updates (R1, R2) and the add-on warning (H1) were scored. See Set the privacy and security options, Update Firefox.
    • Do R2+ Turn on Enhanced Safe Browsing in Chrome and SmartScreen in Edge, and remove unknown extensions. (Windows 11 and 10) Browser security settings are Application Security Settings. See Chrome settings, Edge settings.
    • Do R2+ Set required browsers to warn on add-on installs, block dangerous sites and block pop-ups, and remove policies blocking their updates. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Firefox warning and pop-up settings were scored on H1. See Firefox settings, Remove policies that block app updates.
    • Check State+ Check browser enterprise policies and about:config for planted settings that disable updates, safe browsing or warnings, and remove bad extensions. (Any Windows image) Planted policies make the browser settings revert after you fix them. See Fix Firefox enterprise policies, Fix Chrome and Edge policies in the registry.
    • Check State+ Remove unknown extensions and check prefs.js, user.js and policies.json for planted proxies or home pages. (Any Linux or BSD image) Malicious extensions and proxy settings capture traffic. See Remove bad extensions and settings, Enforce settings with policies.json.
    • Check Semis+ Check Firefox about:config and user.js for planted proxy, safebrowsing and update values. (Windows 11 and 10) Hidden prefs survive normal settings changes. See Check Firefox about:config.

    #README requires office apps

    • Don't R1+ Do not uninstall or move the required office or mail apps (LibreOffice, Thunderbird, Adobe Reader). Required Thunderbird and Adobe Reader removed or moved were penalties. See Required software removed or moved, Avoid the common Linux penalties.
    • Don't R1+ Do not uninstall the required office or PDF apps. (Windows 11 and 10) Removing required Adobe Reader or LibreOffice is a penalty (G2). See Required software removed or moved.
    • Do R1+ Update LibreOffice, Thunderbird and Adobe Reader to the latest version. (not: Updates restricted or version pinned) LibreOffice, Thunderbird and Adobe Reader DC has been updated were scored. See LibreOffice, Adobe Acrobat Reader updates and settings.
    • Do R2+ Keep LibreOffice, update it and set macro security to High (Tools > Options > Security). (Any Linux or BSD image) LibreOffice has been updated was scored in SR2, G1 and H1. See Update specific packages and the kernel.
    • Do R2+ Update LibreOffice, Office and Adobe Reader in place. (Windows 11 and 10 and not: Updates restricted or version pinned) LibreOffice and Adobe Reader updates were scored in R2 and G2. See LibreOffice, Adobe Acrobat Reader updates and settings.
    • Do R2+ Update the required office suite in place and set macro security to disable unsigned macros. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) LibreOffice updates were scored on client keys. See LibreOffice.
    • Do State+ Set macro security to High in LibreOffice and turn off JavaScript in Adobe Reader. State keys add application security settings for required apps. See LibreOffice, Adobe Acrobat Reader updates and settings.
    • Do State+ Set macro security to High or block macros, and turn off JavaScript and turn on Protected Mode in Adobe Reader. (Windows 11 and 10) App-specific settings appear from State on. See LibreOffice, Adobe Acrobat Reader updates and settings.

    #README requires developer tools

    • Don't R1+ Do not uninstall or move the required developer tools (VS Code, Git, Python, Perl, compilers). Removing required Perl was a penalty on an Ubuntu key. See Required software removed or moved, Avoid the common Linux penalties.
    • Don't R1+ Do not uninstall VS Code, Python, Git or compilers the README requires, or remove them from PATH. (Windows 11 and 10) Removing required software is a penalty. See Required software removed or moved.
    • Don't R2+ Don't purge python3, perl, gcc, git or VS Code when the README requires developer tools. (Any Linux or BSD image) They are required software, and removing python3 breaks the desktop too. See Avoid the common Linux penalties, Check for portable tools and scripts.
    • Do R2+ Update VS Code and the other required developer tools in place. (not: Updates restricted or version pinned) Visual Studio Code has been updated was a scored item. See Visual Studio Code updates and settings, Update specific packages and the kernel.
    • Do R2+ Update VS Code, Notepad++, Git and Python in place. (Windows 11 and 10 and not: Updates restricted or version pinned) Visual Studio Code and Notepad++ updates were scored in H1 and R1. See Visual Studio Code updates and settings, Notepad++.
    • Do R2+ Update the required developer tools such as VS Code in place and keep their folders. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Visual Studio Code has been updated was scored on H1 Server 2019. See Visual Studio Code updates and settings.
    • Do State+ Keep VS Code Workspace Trust on, remove unknown extensions and check Git hooks and Python startup files for backdoors. (Windows 11 and 10) Developer tooling hides auto-run code. See Visual Studio Code updates and settings, Find portable and hidden programs.
    • Check State+ Check project and script folders for listeners and reverse shells written in Python or Perl. Python and Perl backdoors were scored malware items and hide among dev files. See Check for portable tools and scripts, Unknown backdoor on a port.

    #README requires media apps

    • Don't R1+ Do not uninstall or move the required media player. Required software removed or moved is a 5-point penalty. See Required software removed or moved, Avoid the common Linux penalties.
    • Don't R1+ Don't remove VLC or the media player the README requires, but still delete prohibited media files. (Any Linux or BSD image) Removing required software is a penalty while media files stay scored. See Avoid the common Linux penalties, Find prohibited media files.
    • Don't R1+ Do not uninstall the required media player. (Windows 11 and 10) Removing required software is a penalty. See Required software removed or moved.
    • Don't R1+ Do not uninstall the required media player, but still delete prohibited media files. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Required software removed is a 5 point penalty. See Required software removed or moved.
    • Check R1+ A required media player does not make media files allowed; still delete prohibited media files. MP3 removal was scored on images that also had a media player. See Find media files in user folders, Find prohibited media files.

    #README requires a P2P client

    • Don't R1+ Do not uninstall or move the P2P client the README requires. Required software removed is a 5-point penalty. See Required software removed or moved, Avoid the common Linux penalties.
    • Don't R1+ Don't remove the required P2P or torrent client; limit it to the README's use instead. (Any Linux or BSD image) Removing required software is a penalty. See Avoid the common Linux penalties.
    • Don't R1+ Do not uninstall the required P2P client. (Windows 11 and 10) Removing required software is a penalty. See Required software removed or moved, P2P and download tools.
    • Don't R1+ Do not uninstall the P2P client the README requires; update it and still remove any other P2P apps. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Required software removed is a 5 point penalty. See Required software removed or moved.
    • Do State+ Update the required P2P client and turn off its remote web interface and any open ports beyond what it needs. A remote web UI is a remote control point on the machine. See P2P and download tools, Common ports and services.
    • Do State+ Update the required P2P client and turn off UPnP or NAT-PMP port forwarding and run at startup. (Windows 11 and 10) Limits exposure from a required P2P app. See P2P and download tools, Update without changing the install folder.

    #README lists users and admins

    • Don't R1+ Do not delete built-in accounts (Administrator, Guest, DefaultAccount, WDAGUtilityAccount) because they are not in the README; disable them instead. (Any Windows image) Built-in accounts are not README users and deleting them breaks the system. See Leave DefaultAccount and WDAGUtilityAccount disabled, Disable the Guest account.
    • Don't R1+ Do not delete root or system accounts below UID 1000 that have nologin shells; only remove a system account that has a real login shell and no package owner. (Any Linux or BSD image) Deleting root was a penalty and system accounts run services. See Fix system accounts with login shells, Find hidden users.
    • Don't R1+ Don't remove admin rights from a README administrator, including the account you are logged in as. (Any Linux or BSD image) Demoting authorized admins cost 5 points in G2 and G3. See Avoid the common Linux penalties.
    • Don't R1+ Do not delete or demote any user or administrator the README lists, and do not delete their profile folder. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Deleting or demoting authorized users cost 5 to 10 points in G2, G3 and G4. See Penalties seen in past keys, An authorized user was deleted or demoted.
    • Do R1+ Compare every local account with the README list and delete accounts that are not listed. (Any Windows image and not: Domain controller) Removed unauthorized user is on nearly every Windows key. See Compare the README with the system in one paste, Remove an unauthorized user.
    • Do R1+ Compare every human account (UID 1000 and up, plus any account with a login shell) with the README list and delete unlisted ones (deluser on the Debian family, userdel -r on Fedora, pw userdel on FreeBSD). (Any Linux or BSD image) Removed unauthorized user is on nearly every Linux key. See List users and admins, Delete an unauthorized user.
    • Do R1+ Remove every user from Administrators who is not listed as an administrator, and add listed administrators who are missing. (Any Windows image) User is not an administrator items appear on almost every key. See Demote an unauthorized administrator, Promote a README administrator.
    • Do R1+ Remove unlisted users from the sudo, admin and adm groups (wheel on Fedora and FreeBSD) and add listed administrators who are missing. (Any Linux or BSD image) Keys test the sudo line in /etc/group for each named user. See Add or remove an administrator, Remove a user's sudo rights.
    • Do R1+ Delete every human account not in the README with sudo deluser <name> (add --remove-home once forensics are done). (Mint, Ubuntu and Debian) Removed unauthorized user is scored on nearly every Linux key (K3, K6, K8, R1, R2, G1). See Delete an unauthorized user, List users and admins.
    • Do R1+ Delete unauthorized accounts with sudo userdel -r <name> on Fedora, or pw userdel <name> -r on FreeBSD (list them with pw usershow -a). (os:fed|os:bsd) User auditing is the most scored Linux category, and deluser does not exist on these systems. See Manage users and the wheel group, Manage users with pw.
    • Do R1+ Remove non-admin users from the sudo, adm and admin groups with sudo gpasswd -d <user> sudo. (Mint, Ubuntu and Debian) User is not an administrator is scored in K8, R1, R2, SR2, G1 and H1. See Add or remove an administrator, Remove a user's sudo rights.
    • Do R1+ Remove non-admins from wheel (gpasswd -d <user> wheel on Fedora, pw groupmod wheel -d <user> on FreeBSD) and check sudoers. (os:fed|os:bsd) Fedora and FreeBSD grant admin rights through wheel, not a sudo group. See Manage users and the wheel group, Manage users with pw.
    • Do R1+ Delete every local user that is not in the README with lusrmgr.msc or net user <name> /delete. (Windows 11 and 10) Removed unauthorized user appears on nearly every Windows key (K1, K4, R1, R2). See Remove an unauthorized user, Compare the README with the system in one paste.
    • Do R1+ Make the Administrators group contain exactly the README administrators: remove everyone else and add any listed admin who is missing. (Windows 11 and 10) User is not an administrator is scored in K1, K4, R1, R2 and G2; demoting a listed admin was a penalty in G2 and G3. See Demote an unauthorized administrator, Promote a README administrator.
    • Do R2+ Compare every domain user and Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins and Schema Admins membership with the README list in ADUC or PowerShell. (Domain controller) On a domain controller the users live in AD, not in local users. See Compare AD users to the README, Check privileged group membership.
    • Do R2+ Force a password change at next login with sudo chage -d 0 <user> for users the README flags. (Any Linux or BSD image and not: FreeBSD) Must change password at next login appeared in R1 and R2. See Force a password change at next login.
    • Check R2+ Look for users hidden from the sign-in screen, names ending in $ and lookalike names such as guest_. (Any Windows image and not: Domain controller) Removed hidden user and lookalike Guest items appeared on real reports. See Find hidden users, Lookalike account names.
    • Check R2+ Check /etc/passwd for extra UID 0 accounts and for users below UID 1000 with a login shell. (Any Linux or BSD image) Removed hidden user items were UIDs under 1000 that the GUI did not show. See Remove extra UID 0 accounts, Find hidden users.
    • Check R2+ Make Remote Desktop Users, Backup Operators, Event Log Readers and other privileged groups match the README. (Any Windows image) Updated Remote Desktop Users group and privileged group removals were scored. See Check privileged groups.
    • Check R2+ When an account might be a misspelled authorized user, disable it rather than deleting it until you confirm. Engine configs accepted a disabled account for removal items, and disabling is reversible. See Rules the engine follows, User lists.

    #README asks to create users or groups

    • Do R1+ Create each user the README asks for with the exact spelling and give it the team password. (Any Windows image and not: Domain controller) Created user account items are scored on exact names. See Create a missing user.
    • Do R1+ Create each user the README asks for with adduser using the exact spelling, and set a strong password. (Any Linux or BSD image) Created user account items are scored on exact names. See Add a user or group.
    • Do R1+ Create each group the README names and add exactly the listed members (lusrmgr on Windows, ADUC on a domain controller, groupadd and gpasswd -a on Linux). Added user to group and group membership items check the exact member list. See Create a group and add members, Add a user or group.
    • Do R1+ Create the users and groups the README asks for with the exact spelling (adduser or useradd, groupadd, gpasswd -a user group; pw useradd and pw groupmod -m on FreeBSD). (Any Linux or BSD image) Created user and added to group were scored in K3, K6, R1 and SR2. See Add a user or group.
    • Do R1+ Create the users and groups the README asks for and add the listed members. (Windows 11 and 10) Create user account for user and Added user to group are scored (K1, R1, K3). See Create a missing user, Create a group and add members.
    • Do R1+ Create the users and groups the README asks for with New-LocalUser, New-LocalGroup and Add-LocalGroupMember. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022 and role:standalone|role:member) Created user account items appear in past keys. See Create a missing user, Create a group and add members.
    • Do R1+ Create the AD users and groups the README asks for with New-ADUser, New-ADGroup and Add-ADGroupMember. (Domain controller) Created user and group membership items appear in past keys. See Create users and groups the README asks for, Add a README-required admin.
    • Do R2+ Create the requested domain users and groups in the OU the README names, not as local accounts. (Domain controller) On a domain controller the scored objects are AD objects. See Create users and groups the README asks for.
    • Do R2+ When the README asks for a new administrator, create the user and also add it to the admin group (Administrators or Domain Admins on Windows, sudo or wheel on Linux). Created new administrator account items need both the account and the group. See Promote a README administrator, Add or remove an administrator.
    • Do R2+ If the README says a user must change the password at next login, run chage -d 0 for that user. (Any Linux or BSD image and not: FreeBSD) User must change password at next login was scored in Rounds 1 and 2. See Force a password change at next login.
    • Do R2+ Give a newly created README admin sudo rights with sudo usermod -aG sudo <name> (usermod -aG wheel on Fedora, pw groupmod wheel -m <name> on FreeBSD). (Any Linux or BSD image) Created new administrator account was scored in R2. See Add or remove an administrator, Add a user or group.

    #README gives or protects passwords

    • Don't R1+ Do not change any password the README gives or says to keep, including your own logged-in account. Changing a kept password can lock you out or break a service that uses it. See Do-not lines and policy lines, Password rules for the team.
    • Don't R1+ Don't change your own login password or any password the README lists as fixed. (Any Linux or BSD image) Changing it can lock you out and break the README scenario. See Password rules for the team, Set passwords for every user.
    • Don't R1+ Do not change your own password or any password the README says to keep. (Windows 11 and 10) A changed auto-login or scoring password can lock the team out. See Traps that cause penalties, Stop penalties before they happen.
    • Don't R1+ Do not change passwords the README gives or says to keep, including the account you are signed in with. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Changing them can lock you out or break a scored service login. See Do-not lines and policy lines.
    • Do R1+ Still set the team password on every other authorized user that has a weak or blank password. Changed insecure password and user has a password items stay scored. See Set a strong password on every account, Set passwords for every user.
    • Check R2+ After setting a maximum password age, confirm the kept accounts are not already past it so they are not forced to change at next sign-in. (Any Windows image) An immediately expired password breaks the account the README told you to keep. See Set the password policy, Fix password never expires and password not required.
    • Check R2+ Before applying chage -M to all users, check chage -l on the kept accounts so the last-change date does not expire them at once. (Any Linux or BSD image and not: FreeBSD) An expired password on a kept account counts as changing it. See Apply aging to existing users with chage.
    • Don't State+ Do not change passwords of database, web application or service accounts that a critical service logs in with unless you also update the service config. The service stops authenticating and the critical service penalty follows. See Check database accounts by hand, Critical services.

    #README states password policy values

    • Do R1+ Set password length, age, history and lockout to the exact values the README states instead of the guide defaults. (Any Windows image) The engine tests the README values, not the defaults. See Set the password policy, Set the lockout policy.
    • Do R1+ Put the README values in /etc/login.defs (PASS_MAX_DAYS, PASS_MIN_DAYS), pwquality minlen, pwhistory remember and faillock deny (login.conf on FreeBSD). (Any Linux or BSD image) The engine tests the README values, not the defaults. See Set password aging in login.defs, Turn on password complexity with pwquality.
    • Do R1+ Use the README's password policy numbers (length, age, history, lockout) in place of the guide defaults. (Any Linux or BSD image) The scoring tests match the README values when it gives them. See Password policy (login.defs, pwquality, history), Set password aging in login.defs.
    • Do R1+ Use the exact password and lockout values the README states instead of the guide defaults. (Windows 11 and 10) The README values are what the engine checks. See Recommended values, Do-not lines and policy lines.
    • Do R1+ Use the password and lockout values the README states instead of the default recommendations. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) The scoring checks match the README values on those images. See Do-not lines and policy lines, Set the domain password policy.
    • Do R2+ Apply the README aging values to existing users with chage, because login.defs only affects new accounts. (Any Linux or BSD image and not: FreeBSD) User has a minimum or maximum password age items test each user. See Apply aging to existing users with chage.
    • Do R2+ Set the README password and lockout values in the Default Domain Policy GPO and run gpupdate /force. (Domain controller) secpol changes do not stick on a domain controller. See Set the domain password policy, Set the domain lockout policy.
    • Check R2+ Verify the policy took effect with net accounts or secedit export on Windows and by testing pwquality and faillock on Linux (login.conf on FreeBSD). A policy written to the wrong file or GPO scores nothing. See Verify the policy, Test the lockout without logging out.

    #README forbids media, games or hacking tools

    • Do R1+ Uninstall games and unapproved apps, including Store apps, that the README does not require. (Any Windows image) Removed TicTacToe and Tetris were scored items. See Games and unapproved apps, Remove Microsoft Store games and apps.
    • Do R1+ Purge game packages the README does not require (aisleriot, freeciv, manaplus, zangband, gameconqueror, minetest). (Any Linux or BSD image) Prohibited software lines named these games on past Linux keys. See Common planted packages.
    • Do R1+ Search /home, /root, /opt, /srv, /var/www and /tmp, including hidden folders and archives, for every category the README bans. (Any Linux or BSD image) Prohibited files can be any type the README names, not just MP3s. See Find prohibited media files, Find files by name, content, owner and time.
    • Do R1+ Search all drives for media files such as .mp3 and .mp4 and delete the files, not their parent folders. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Prohibited files was a scored category on CP17 State Server 2019. See Prohibited files, Search the whole C: drive for media.
    • Don't R2+ Do not delete media or documents the README describes as business files, such as training videos or a share's product images. Deleting a critical business file was a penalty. See A share or business file was removed, Traps that cause penalties.
    • Do R2+ Search for plaintext password and credit card files (passwords.txt, secret.txt, users.csv) and delete them while keeping their folders. Plaintext password file removed was scored and the folder had to remain. See Find plaintext password files, Find files containing plaintext passwords.
    • Do R2+ Remove any app the README policy forbids even when it looks harmless. (Windows 11 and 10) R2 scored removing Cursor, an app the README did not authorize. See Games and unapproved apps, Do-not lines and policy lines.
    • Do R2+ Apply the README file policy to every non-work file type it names, such as videos, images or ebooks. (Windows 11 and 10) The policy line defines what counts as prohibited. See Search the whole C: drive for media, Do-not lines and policy lines.
    • Do R2+ Search for hacking tool files such as mimikatz, nc.exe and password dumpers and delete them. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) netcat removal was scored on K4 and G2. See Find hacking-related files.
    • Check State+ Check for prohibited files hidden by renamed extensions, hidden attributes, dot names or alternate data streams by checking file type, not only names. Harder rounds hide the same items more deeply. See Real file type and polyglot files, Find hidden files and alternate data streams.

    #Forensics Questions present

    • Don't R1+ Do not delete or move the files a question asks about (pcaps, images, encoded text, suspicious programs) until it is answered. The question becomes unanswerable once the evidence is gone. See Question types seen in past answer keys.
    • Don't R1+ Don't delete MP3s, backdoors, users or Wireshark until any Forensics Question about their path, port, UID or a pcap is answered. (Any Linux or BSD image) Past questions asked the MP3 folder path (K3, K6, R1), the backdoor port (K8, H1) and pcap contents (K8). See Common Forensics Question types, Match the question to a technique.
    • Do R1+ Open and answer every Forensics Question before changing the image. Keys warn that fixes can destroy the evidence a question needs. See Forensics questions playbook (any OS), First 15 minutes on any image.
    • Do R1+ Type only the answer after ANSWER: in the question file, keep the file name and location, and save. A wrong format or a moved file scores zero. See How to write the answer.
    • Do R1+ Use the Windows forensics playbook commands (Get-FileHash, net localgroup, netstat -abno, Get-Item -Stream) to answer the questions. (Any Windows image) Hashes, group members and backdoor ports were the most common Windows questions. See Question types seen in past keys, Forensics commands.
    • Do R1+ Use the Linux forensics playbook commands (sha256sum, id, ss -tlnp or sockstat, find, base64 -d) to answer the questions. (Any Linux or BSD image) UIDs, MP3 paths, listener paths and decoded text were the most common Linux questions. See Match the question to a technique, Answer the Forensics questions.
    • Do R1+ Answer every Forensics Question first and type only the answer after 'ANSWER:' before saving the file. (Any Linux or BSD image) Keys K5 and K6 warn that fixes destroy the evidence the questions ask about. See Answer the Forensics questions, How to write the answer.
    • Do R1+ Answer every Forensics Question before making changes, and do not delete a backdoor, share or file until questions about its path, port or hash are answered. (Windows 11 and 10) K5 and K6 warn that fixes destroy evidence; K7 asked for a backdoor's port and path. See Answer a forensics question, How to write the answer, Paths of shares and programs.
    • Do R1+ Answer every Forensics Question before changing anything, typing only the answer after ANSWER: and saving the file. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) Server keys K5 and K7 warn that fixes can destroy the evidence a question asks for. See Server forensics questions, How to write the answer.
    • Check R1+ Treat each question as a hint: a backdoor port, hidden user or MP3 path question points to a scored removal item. Past forensics questions asked for backdoor ports and MP3 paths that were also scored items. See Question types seen in past answer keys.
    • Check R1+ Confirm every Forensics Question shows as correct on the report, or retry the unanswered ones. Forensics questions are worth several points each. See How to write the answer, Reading the scoring report.
    • Do R2+ For pcap questions use Wireshark Follow TCP Stream or tshark -z follow,tcp,ascii and grep for USER/PASS. (Any Linux or BSD image) K8 asked for FTP passwords recovered from a capture on the Desktop. See Read a packet capture, Find files and evidence.
    • Check R2+ Expect pcap, registry, scheduled task, deleted user and service description questions; solve pcaps in Wireshark before any Wireshark removal. (Windows 11 and 10) K1 asked for an attacker IP from a pcap; P1 and P3 asked about a service description and a task. See Question types seen in past keys, Packet captures, Registry.
    • Check R2+ Expect Server forensics on share paths (Get-SmbShare), SHA256 hashes (Get-FileHash) and backdoor ports and paths (netstat -abn -p tcp). (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) K5 asked a share path and a SHA256 hash; K7 asked a backdoor port and executable path. See Path of a share, Hash of a file, Port and path of a backdoor.
    • Do State+ If you install a tool such as Wireshark or steghide to answer a question on an image that forbids hacking tools, uninstall it once the answer is saved. (README forbids media, games or hacking tools) An installed tool the README forbids is an unwanted software item. See Network captures (pcap files), Do-not lines and policy lines.
    • Check State+ Expect multi-step questions (base64 to steghide passphrase to hash, pcap to credentials, XOR or one-time pad) and record each step. Training keys chained base64, steghide and md5 in one question. See Extract a message hidden with steghide, Decrypt a one-time pad or XOR message.
    • Check State+ For who/when questions read auth.log or journalctl, shell history files, dpkg.log (dnf history on Fedora) and cron logs. (Any Linux or BSD image) Higher-round forensics ask about logins, installs and what a job ran. See Read authentication logs and the journal, Read shell and application history, Find when a package was installed.
    • Check State+ Answer database questions with psql (\du, \l, \s) or mysql SELECT queries before changing roles or passwords. (Any Linux or BSD image and svc:postgres|svc:mysql|svc:wordpress) H2 asked for PostgreSQL users and history. See Query application databases.
    • Check State+ Answer AD forensics (group members, when an attribute changed, deleted objects) with Get-ADGroupMember, repadmin /showobjmeta and Get-ADObject -IncludeDeletedObjects before cleaning users. (Domain controller) Removing users or memberships first erases the answer. See AD user and group questions, When a membership or attribute changed, Deleted users and objects.

    #Internet-facing or public server

    • Do R1+ List every listening port with netstat -abno and match each one to a README service; investigate anything else first. (Any Windows image) An internet-facing machine is attacked through its open ports. See Find listening ports and their programs, Common ports and services.
    • Do R1+ List every listening port with ss -tulnp (sockstat -46l on FreeBSD) and match each one to a README service; investigate anything else first. (Any Linux or BSD image) An internet-facing machine is attacked through its open ports. See List listening ports and services, Common ports and services.
    • Do R2+ Allow inbound only the README service ports in Windows Defender Firewall and remove other inbound allow rules. (Any Windows image) Planted inbound allow rules expose backdoors on public servers. See Find suspicious inbound allow rules, Block a port or a program.
    • Do R2+ Set the firewall to deny incoming by default and allow only the README service ports. (Any Linux or BSD image) Firewall enabled is scored and the allow list keeps critical services reachable. See Allow README-required services, Remove or deny rules.
    • Do R2+ Harden the exposed services before internal settings: require TLS, disable anonymous access, hide version banners and turn off directory listing and error details. Application security items for SSL, anonymous FTP, server tokens and display errors were scored. See Config files and test commands, IIS web server hardening.
    • Do R2+ Remove phpinfo pages and web shells from the web root while keeping the site's own files. (README requires a web server) Removed phpinfo file and PHP web shell removed were scored, and the CMS had to stay intact. See Find web shells, Remove web files such as phpinfo.
    • Do R2+ On an internet-facing server expose only README ports, rate-limit logins and turn on fail2ban and firewall logging. (Any Linux or BSD image) Public services take the most attack traffic. See Rate-limit SSH, Set up fail2ban for SSH.
    • Do State+ Limit inbound firewall rules to the exact public service ports and require encryption on each. (Windows 11 and 10) Internet-facing services need tighter exposure. See Common ports and services, Block a port or a program.
    • Do State+ Allow inbound only the ports README services need and block everything else on the Public profile. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) An internet-facing server should expose nothing extra. See Block a port or a program, Ports a domain controller needs open.
    • Check Semis+ Read the service and authentication logs for signs of past compromise (logins from unknown IPs, uploads, new admin users). Semifinal images hide persistence that only the logs reveal. See Read authentication logs and the journal, IIS and FTP logs.

    #Personal or employee workstation

    • Do R1+ Remove server software and features the README does not need (IIS, FTP, Home Web Server, OpenTFTP, Plex). (Any Windows image) A workstation needs no server roles, and keys scored removing each one. See Servers nobody asked for, Windows optional features.
    • Do R1+ Stop and purge server packages the README does not need (apache2, nginx, vsftpd, bind9, postfix, dovecot, samba, IRC daemons such as ngircd or inspircd, minetest-server). (Any Linux or BSD image) A workstation needs no server roles, and keys scored removing each one. See Commonly planted services, Stop, disable, mask or purge a service.
    • Do R1+ Uninstall remote access tools (TeamViewer, AnyDesk, VNC servers) the README does not allow. (not: README allows a remote access tool) Removed TeamViewer and AnyDesk were scored items. See Remote access tools, Common planted packages.
    • Do R1+ On a workstation image remove server daemons the README does not list (Apache, FTP, Samba, SSH, databases). (Any Linux or BSD image) Server software on a personal workstation is usually a scored unwanted service. See Commonly planted services, Stop, disable, mask or purge a service.
    • Do R2+ On a workstation, remove every server role or app (IIS, FTP, SQL, game servers) the README does not name. (Windows 11 and 10) Workstation images plant servers nobody asked for. See Servers nobody asked for.

    #Shared folders or departments

    • Don't R1+ Do not remove the share or the business files the README describes; harden permissions instead. Disabling the authorized share or deleting its business file cost 5 points. See A share or business file was removed, Shares you must keep.
    • Don't R2+ Don't delete business files in shared folders while cleaning up prohibited content. (Any Linux or BSD image) Deleting a critical business file cost 5 points in K7 and G3. See Avoid the common Linux penalties.
    • Do R2+ Give each department group access only to its own folder and remove Everyone or Users write access on the share and NTFS permissions. (Any Windows image) Application permissions are part of the Application Security category. See Fix permissions on a share the README requires, Find folders where Everyone or Users can write.
    • Do R2+ Set group ownership and 770 or 750 modes on department folders and remove world-writable bits. (Any Linux or BSD image) World-writable shared folders let any user plant files. See Fix world-writable files and folders, Harden Samba.
    • Do R2+ Remove shares the README does not describe (USERS$, a C drive share) but keep C$, ADMIN$ and IPC$. (Any Windows image) USERS$ hidden share disabled and C drive share removed were scored. See Remove a share that is not required, Hidden and custom drive shares.
    • Do R2+ Give each department folder access only to its README department group. (Windows 11 and 10) Shared-folder scenarios score correct group access. See Fix permissions on a share the README requires, Create a group and add members.
    • Do R2+ Give each department folder only its README group access and remove cross-department access. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022 and README requires Windows file shares) Shared-folder scenarios score correct group permissions. See Tighten share permissions on a required share, Fix permissions on a share the README requires.
    • Check R2+ Check that each department group contains exactly the users the README places in that department. Group membership drives share access and is a User Auditing item. See Create a group and add members, Add a user or group.

    #Updates restricted or version pinned

    • Don't R1+ Do not upgrade the application or version the README says must stay. Upgrading a pinned version breaks what the README protects and can be a penalty. See Do-not lines and policy lines, Check every app's version and install folder.
    • Don't R1+ Don't upgrade the package or version the README pins; hold it with apt-mark hold (dnf versionlock, pkg lock) and update everything else. (Any Linux or BSD image) Breaking a README instruction is a penalty and can stop a required service. See Update specific packages and the kernel, Avoid the common Linux penalties.
    • Don't R1+ Do not upgrade the program or Windows version the README pins; update everything else. (Windows 11 and 10) The README restriction overrides the usual update items. See Do-not lines and policy lines, Windows Update and app updates.
    • Don't R1+ Do not install the updates or upgrade the versions the README says must stay. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) README restrictions override the update items. See Do-not lines and policy lines.
    • Do R1+ Run apt-mark hold on the pinned package (dnf versionlock on Fedora, pkg lock on FreeBSD) before a full upgrade, then update everything else. (Any Linux or BSD image) OS and other app update items stay scored even when one app is pinned. See Update specific packages and the kernel, Install updates.
    • Do R1+ Update the other applications one by one instead of winget upgrade --all so the pinned one is skipped. (Any Windows image) Bulk upgrades silently update the pinned application. See Update third-party apps with winget, Update apps with their own updater.
    • Check R2+ Decide whether the restriction covers the whole OS or one app; if only one app, still turn on automatic update checks and install OS updates. Automatic update checking and OS updates are scored on most images. See Configure unattended-upgrades, Set the Configure Automatic Updates policy.

    #README protects a named setting

    • Don't R1+ Do not change the setting or service the README says to leave alone, even if it looks insecure. The README overrides the guide and the change is penalized or breaks the scenario. See Do-not lines and policy lines, Traps that cause penalties.
    • Don't R1+ Don't change a setting or service the README says to leave alone, even if a checklist line says to harden it. (Any Linux or BSD image) The README overrides every generic checklist and the scoring engine follows it. See Avoid the common Linux penalties, Read the README first.
    • Don't R1+ Do not change any setting or service the README says to leave alone, even if a checklist says to harden it. (Windows 11 and 10) Changing a locked item is a penalty or breaks a scored service. See Do-not lines and policy lines, Traps that cause penalties.
    • Don't R1+ Do not change any setting or service the README says to leave alone, even if a checklist says to harden it. (Windows Server 2019 and 2022) README do-not lines override general hardening and cause penalties. See Do-not lines and policy lines.
    • Check R2+ Remove the locked setting from any secedit template or registry batch before applying it. (Any Windows image) A secedit import overwrites every value in the template. See Set everything with secedit, Apply security options with reg add.
    • Check R2+ Remove the locked setting from any sysctl, sshd or PAM file you paste in before applying it. (Any Linux or BSD image) A pasted config file overwrites every line it contains. See How to run a snippet, Snippet to write the sysctl hardening file.

    #All images

    • Don't R1+ Do not delete or demote any user the README authorizes, and never delete an authorized user's home folder. Keys penalized deleted users, deleted home folders and demoted admins by 5 to 10 points. See Traps that cause penalties, An authorized user was deleted or demoted.
    • Don't R1+ Do not set the account lockout threshold below 5 attempts; keep it between 5 and 10 unless the README gives a value. A threshold of 1 to 4 was a penalty on several keys. See Penalties to avoid, Recommended values.
    • Don't R1+ Do not stop, disable, uninstall or firewall off any service the README lists as critical; harden it instead. Stopping a critical service cost 5 to 10 points on past keys. See Critical services, Penalties to avoid.
    • Don't R1+ Do not delete a whole user folder, share folder or program folder to remove one bad file; delete only the file. Removal items check that the parent folder still exists and a deleted home folder is a penalty. See Rules the engine follows, Penalties to avoid.
    • Don't R1+ Do not run a large hardening script you have not read line by line against this README. Mass scripts remove required users, software and services and cause penalties you cannot trace. See Resources, scripts and AI, Penalties to avoid.
    • Don't R1+ Do not make risky changes (PAM, firewall, policy imports, service removal) in the last 10 minutes. A late penalty may not be noticed or undone before time ends. See 4-hour timeline, Score went down.
    • Do R1+ Enter the team Unique Identifier in the CyberPatriot setup prompt as soon as the image boots, then confirm the scoring report shows your team ID. An image without the right UID is not scored for your team. See First 15 minutes on any image, Time and images.
    • Do R1+ Read the whole README twice before changing anything and highlight every sentence that names a user, group, service, program, file or setting. Almost every README sentence maps to a scored item or a penalty. See Parts of a README, First 15 minutes on any image.
    • Do R1+ Copy the authorized users, administrators, critical services, required software and every do-not line into the README summary template before you start fixing. A written list stops teammates from deleting a required user or service under time pressure. See README summary template, User lists.
    • Do R1+ Start a change log with the time, what you changed and the old value for every change, so any penalty can be undone in seconds. Penalties appear on the report without saying which change caused them. See Keep a change log, Score went down.
    • Do R1+ Assign one owner per image and one person to the Cisco quiz and Packet Tracer, and agree that only the owner changes an image. Two people changing the same image cause undetected penalties and duplicate work. See Work as a team without stepping on each other, Cisco quiz and Packet Tracer.
    • Do R1+ Use the agreed team password for every password you set and write it in the change log. A known strong password avoids lockouts and satisfies insecure password items. See Password rules for the team.
    • Do R1+ Refresh the scoring report after each small batch of changes and undo the last batch at once if a penalty or a lost item appears. Catching a penalty right away tells you exactly which change caused it. See Score went down, Reading the scoring report.
    • Do R1+ With no README values, use minimum length 10, maximum age 90, minimum age 1, history 5, lockout threshold 10, lockout duration 30 minutes and reset counter after 30 minutes. (not: README states password policy values) These values passed every past key's thresholds. See Recommended values, Set password aging in login.defs.
    • Do R1+ Remove media servers, radio and video downloaders (Plex Media Server, Nexus Radio, Helium, SpeedBit Video Downloader) the README does not require. (not: README requires media apps) Each of these was a scored unwanted software item. See P2P and download tools, Common planted packages.
    • Do R1+ Uninstall torrent and P2P clients (BitTorrent, BitComet, uTorrent, qBittorrent, aMule, Transmission) the README does not require. (not: README requires a P2P client) Removed BitTorrent, BitComet and aMule were scored. See P2P and download tools, Common planted packages.
    • Do R1+ Re-read the README summary and tick every user, service, software and policy line against the system. The final pass catches items skipped under time pressure. See README summary template, First 15 minutes on any image.
    • Check R1+ Open the Scoring Report shortcut on the desktop, note the starting score and confirm it refreshes within a few minutes. If scoring does not update you lose feedback on every fix and on penalties. See Reading the scoring report, Score is not updating.
    • Check R1+ List every do-not and policy line in the README (do not change, must stay, only approved firewall, prohibited files) and keep it visible while you work. Keys penalize changes the README forbade, and policy lines define what removal is scored. See Do-not lines and policy lines, Traps that cause penalties.
    • Check R1+ Note the time the 4-hour window started and set checkpoints for forensics done, basics done and final pass. The round is one consecutive 4-hour block and time is the main limit on points. See 4-hour timeline, Time and images.
    • Check R1+ Check that the scoring report shows no penalties and the latest score before time ends. Penalties found at the end can still be reversed. See Reading the scoring report, Penalties to avoid.
    • Do R2+ Remove extra or adware browsers the README does not mention but keep the OS default browser. (not: README requires browsers) Removed WebDiscover browser was a scored unwanted software item. See Cleaners, driver updaters and adware, Common planted packages.
    • Check R2+ Map the README and recon findings to the official categories (User Auditing, Account Policy, Local Policy, Defensive Countermeasures, Service Auditing, Updates, Prohibited Files, Unwanted Software, Malware, Application Security) to plan the order of work. Every image spreads its items across these categories, so an empty category means items still to find. See Official categories and where to look, Scoring-report lines by category.
    • Check R2+ Re-read the README sentence by sentence and confirm each one maps to a change you made or a reason you did not. Unused README sentences are the most common source of missed items. See Parts of a README, Hunt hidden items when stuck.
    • Check R2+ Compare your found item count per category with the typical spread (about 30 items on State images) to see which categories still hide items. State keys held about 31 items across 13 categories. See How many items each category holds, How many items to expect per image.
    • Check R2+ Search for files modified around the image build time in system and user folders to find planted items. Planted files share timestamps close to the other vulnerabilities. See Find files by name, content, owner and time, Created and modified time.
    • Do State+ Plan for about 30 items per image and leave time for application settings after the basics. State images held about 31 items each across all categories. See Where the points are in each round, How many items each category holds.
    • Check State+ Open the settings of every required application and critical service and fix insecure options, not just versions. State images add application security settings for required apps and services. See Official categories and where to look, Config files and test commands.
    • Check State+ Reboot once mid-round and re-check the report; any fix that reverts reveals a persistence mechanism. Planted tasks and policies re-apply bad settings after a restart. See Hunt hidden items when stuck, A service keeps coming back.
    • Do Semis+ Set a per-image time box with a checkpoint every hour and move people to the image with the most remaining points. Semifinals add a third image and the Web-Based Challenge in the same window. See 4-hour timeline, Where the points are in each round.
    • Do Semis+ Keep one shared tracker of items found, penalties and open leads for every image so the team can coordinate. Multiple images under time pressure need one view of progress. See What live mode gives the team, Work as a team without stepping on each other.
    • Do Semis+ Assign one or two members to the Web-Based Challenge (80 points for Platinum and Gold) with a fixed time slice. The Web-Based Challenge is worth almost as much as an image at Semifinals. See During the challenge, What it is.
    • Don't Nats+ Do not rely on prewritten hardening scripts at National Finals; prepare to do every step by hand. Scripts are reported as banned at the Finals. See Resources, scripts and AI, Practice for Finals.
    • Don't Nats+ Do not take a critical service offline or block its port to stop an attack; fix the weakness while it keeps running. Downtime costs uptime points even when it stops the red team. See Keep services up, Watch for the red team.
    • Do Nats+ Name a captain who tracks injects and uptime, and give each image a single owner for the Network Security Master Challenge. The challenge combines several images, injects and a live red team. See Split the work, What National Finals involves.
    • Do Nats+ Read every inject as soon as it arrives, write its deadline in the tracker and assign an owner. Injects have deadlines and late answers lose their points. See Write business injects.
    • Do Nats+ Write inject answers as professional business memos with a summary, the steps taken, evidence and recommendations. Injects are judged as business deliverables, not just technical fixes. See Write business injects.
    • Do Nats+ Back up each critical service config before editing, test the service from a client after every change and keep a restart command ready. Service uptime is scored throughout the round. See Keep services up.
    • Do Nats+ Re-sweep scheduled tasks, cron, services and startup entries every hour during the round. The red team re-plants persistence after you clean it. See Check scheduled tasks, Check systemd units and timers.
    • Do Nats+ Turn on full auditing and firewall logging at the start so you can see red team activity. Monitoring needs logs that exist before the attack. See Turn on all auditing with auditpol, Turn on auditd.
    • Do Nats+ Log each incident with the time, indicator, affected image, action taken and result. Incident reports are a common inject and prove what the team did. See Watch for the red team, Write business injects.
    • Do Nats+ Rotate passwords of all users and service accounts the rules allow in the first 30 minutes, updating service configs that use them. (not: README gives or protects passwords) The red team may already hold the starting credentials. See Watch for the red team, Password rules for the team.
    • Do Nats+ Tell the other image owners when you change a shared dependency such as DNS, the domain, a firewall rule or a shared password. Images depend on each other and one change can break another image's services. See Split the work, What live mode gives the team.

    W11

    Windows 11 master checklist

    jump:w11-checklist

    Work top to bottom and tick items as you go; the boxes are shared live with the team. Items that depend on the README say so. Log every change (what, where, old value) so you can undo it.

    README and Forensics Questions first

    Read the whole README and answer the Forensics Questions before you delete users, files or software. A fix can destroy the evidence a question asks about. Never touch the CyberPatriot folder, the CCS Client or the scoring report.

    #First 10 minutes

    #Users and groups

    #Password and lockout policy

    #Audit policy

    #Security options and user rights

    #Firewall

    #Defender

    #Updates

    #Services

    #Optional features

    #Shares and remote access

    #Software and files

    #Malware and persistence

    #Final pass

    PreviousPlanner rules by README scenario and serviceNextREADME and forensics questions first
    W11

    README and forensics questions first

    jump:w11-readme

    Never touch the scoring engine

    Do not stop, delete, disable or firewall anything named CyberPatriot, CCS or CCS Client. Do not delete the README, the scoring report or the forensics files. Breaking scoring can cost you the whole image.

    Fast path

    1. Open the CyberPatriot README shortcut on the desktop and read all of it, including the bottom of the page.
    2. Copy the authorized users, authorized administrators, required services and required software into your team notes.
    3. Open each Forensics Question N.txt on the desktop in Notepad and answer what you can before changing anything (how).
    4. Open the CyberPatriot Scoring Report shortcut and confirm it shows a score.
    5. Start a change log (format), then harden in checklist order.

    #Where things are on a Windows 11 image

    Item Location Notes
    README Desktop shortcut "CyberPatriot README" Opens a web page. Read every line, including the bottom.
    Forensics Questions Desktop: Forensics Question 1.txt, Forensics Question 2.txt, ... Plain text. Open with Notepad.
    Scoring Report Desktop shortcut "CyberPatriot Scoring Report" Refreshes every minute or two and needs internet.
    CyberPatriot folder C:\CyberPatriot and the CCS Client scoring service Never modify, move or delete.

    #Answer a forensics question

    1. Right-click the file > Open with > Notepad.
    2. Read the question and the example answer format.
    3. Type your answer after ANSWER: on the answer line, for example ANSWER: C:\Users\Public\notes.txt.
    4. Press Ctrl+S. Do not rename the file, change its encoding or delete the other lines.
    5. Check the scoring report a minute later.

    You can also open a question from PowerShell:

    notepad "$env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\Forensics Question 1.txt"

    Match the example format exactly

    Copy the case, path style and separators from the example. Add quotes only if the example has them. If the file has several ANSWER: lines, put one answer on each.

    #Forensics commands

    Run these in PowerShell. Most work without admin rights; reading other users' files needs an elevated window. Harder question types (event logs, browser history, registry, deleted files, pcaps) are in the Windows forensics playbook.

    #Find a user's SID

    Get-LocalUser -Name <username> | Select-Object Name, SID

    For the account you are signed in as:

    whoami /user

    #Hash a file

    SHA256 is the default. Change -Algorithm to MD5 or SHA1 if the question asks for those.

    Get-FileHash -Path "<path>" -Algorithm SHA256

    certutil -hashfile "<path>" SHA256

    #Decode Base64 text

    [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString([System.Convert]::FromBase64String('<base64-text>'))

    Save the Base64 text in in.txt first, then decode it into out.txt and print it:

    certutil -decode in.txt out.txt
type out.txt

    ROT13, Caesar and other simple ciphers

    Use CyberChef (gchq.github.io/CyberChef) in the browser if the image has internet. It runs locally in the page.

    #Find a file by name

    Get-ChildItem -Path C:\Users -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue -Filter "*<part-of-name>*"

    #Find which file contains some text

    Get-ChildItem -Path C:\Users -Recurse -Force -File -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-String -Pattern "<search-text>" -List | Select-Object Path

    #See a user's groups or a group's members

    net user <username>

    net localgroup "<groupname>"

    #Find the process that owns a listening port

    Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort <port> -State Listen | ForEach-Object { Get-Process -Id $_.OwningProcess }

    #Read hidden alternate data streams

    List the streams on a file, then read one by name:

    Get-Item "<path>" -Stream *

    Get-Content "<path>" -Stream <stream-name>

    A normal file shows only :$DATA. Any other stream name is hidden data.

    #Check file times and owner

    Get-Item "<path>" | Select-Object FullName, CreationTime, LastWriteTime
(Get-Acl "<path>").Owner

    #Keep a change log

    Keep notes in a file away from the desktop forensics files (for example Documents\changes.txt) or on paper. For each change, write the time, what you changed, the old value, the new value and the score before and after. When the score drops, the log tells you what to undo.

    10:14  Removed user "<username>" from Administrators     score 12 -> 15
10:20  Disabled service RemoteRegistry (was Manual)       score 15 -> 17
10:31  Disabled Print Spooler (was Automatic)             score 17 -> 15  UNDO (README requires printing)

    Check it worked

    Each correct forensics answer appears as a scored item on the scoring report within a few minutes. If it does not, re-read the example format.

    Why forensics come first, and how penalties work

    Forensics questions often ask about the exact user, file, program, port or setting you are about to remove. Answer every question that mentions one of those before you remove it. The read-only recon script in w11-scripts records the original state so you can still answer later questions.

    The scoring report shows penalties when you remove a required user, service or program. Undo the change and the points come back. Not every vulnerability is scored, so a fix that adds nothing is not proof it was wrong.

    PreviousWindows 11 master checklistNextUsers and groups
    W11

    Users and groups

    jump:w11-users

    The README defines who is allowed

    Never delete or demote a user the README lists as authorized, and never delete your own account. Answer forensics questions about users first.

    Fast path

    1. Open PowerShell as administrator (Start, type powershell, Run as administrator).

    2. List local users and administrators:

      Get-LocalUser | Select-Object Name, Enabled
net localgroup Administrators

    3. Delete every user the README does not list (how).

    4. Remove every administrator the README does not list as an admin (how).

    5. Disable Guest:

      Disable-LocalUser -Name Guest

    6. Set the team password on every other account (how).

    7. Check the other privileged groups (table).

    #Open the Local Users and Groups console

    • Win+R > lusrmgr.msc > Users or Groups. Home edition does not have it; use Settings or the commands below.
    • Win+R > compmgmt.msc > System Tools > Local Users and Groups opens the same view.
    • Settings > Accounts > Other users can add or remove accounts and switch a user between Administrator and Standard User.
    • Win+R > netplwiz lists users with their group.

    #List users and administrators

    Get-LocalUser | Select-Object Name, Enabled, PasswordRequired, PasswordExpires, PasswordLastSet, LastLogon, Description | Format-Table -AutoSize

    Get-LocalGroupMember -Group Administrators | Select-Object Name, ObjectClass, PrincipalSource

    net user
net localgroup Administrators

    Administrator, Guest, DefaultAccount and WDAGUtilityAccount are built in. Every other name must appear in the README.

    net user hides names ending in $

    Use Get-LocalUser for the final check. See names ending in $.

    #Compare the README with the system in one paste

    Edit the first two lines before pasting into elevated PowerShell. $authUsers holds every authorized user from the README, including admins and yourself. $authAdmins holds the authorized administrators, including yourself. Spell names exactly as the README does.

    $authUsers  = @('<user1>','<user2>','<user3>')
$authAdmins = @('<admin1>','<admin2>')
$builtin    = @('Administrator','Guest','DefaultAccount','WDAGUtilityAccount')

"--- Users NOT in README (candidates to delete) ---"
Get-LocalUser | Where-Object { $_.Name -notin $authUsers -and $_.Name -notin $builtin } | Select-Object Name, Enabled

"--- README users that do NOT exist (create them) ---"
$authUsers | Where-Object { -not (Get-LocalUser -Name $_ -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) }

"--- Admins NOT authorized (remove from Administrators) ---"
net localgroup Administrators | Select-Object -Skip 6 | Where-Object { $_ -and $_ -notmatch 'command completed' } |
  Where-Object { ($_ -split '\\')[-1].Trim() -notin $authAdmins -and ($_ -split '\\')[-1].Trim() -ne 'Administrator' }

"--- Authorized admins missing from Administrators ---"
$current = net localgroup Administrators | Select-Object -Skip 6 | ForEach-Object { ($_ -split '\\')[-1].Trim() }
$authAdmins | Where-Object { $_ -notin $current }

    Each heading line prints, followed by the names that need action. An empty list under a heading means nothing to fix.

    Why the script uses net localgroup

    Get-LocalGroupMember stops with an error if the group contains an orphaned SID from a deleted account. net localgroup always works.

    #Remove an unauthorized user

    Remove-LocalUser -Name <username>

    net user <username> /delete

    lusrmgr.msc > Users > right-click the user > Delete > Yes.
