    W11

    Browser hardening (Firefox, Chrome, Edge)

    jump:w11-browsers

    Check the README for browser requirements

    The README may name a default browser or require an add-on. Update and harden every browser that is installed, and never uninstall one the README mentions.

    Fast path

    1. Update each browser: Firefox Menu > Help > About Firefox, chrome://settings/help, edge://settings/help.
    2. Open about:policies, chrome://policy and edge://policy. Anything that turns off Safe Browsing, allows pop-ups or force-installs an extension is planted (fix).
    3. Firefox: Settings > Privacy & Security > block pop-ups, block dangerous content, HTTPS-Only Mode in all windows, stop asking to save passwords.
    4. Chrome: Safe Browsing = Enhanced protection, pop-ups blocked, Offer to save passwords off.
    5. Edge: Microsoft Defender SmartScreen and Block potentially unwanted apps On, pop-ups blocked.
    6. Remove unknown extensions: about:addons, chrome://extensions, edge://extensions.

    #Firefox settings

    Open Firefox > Menu (three lines) > Settings, or type about:preferences in the address bar.

    Section Setting Value
    General > Firefox Updates Automatically install updates Selected
    Privacy & Security > Enhanced Tracking Protection Standard or Strict Strict
    Privacy & Security > Website Privacy Preferences Tell websites not to sell or share my data On
    Privacy & Security > Passwords Ask to save passwords Off
    Privacy & Security > Passwords Saved passwords Remove all
    Privacy & Security > Passwords Use a Primary Password Optional
    Privacy & Security > Permissions Block pop-up windows Checked
    Privacy & Security > Permissions Warn you when websites try to install add-ons Checked
    Privacy & Security > Security Block dangerous and deceptive content Checked
    Privacy & Security > Security Block dangerous downloads Checked
    Privacy & Security > Security Warn you about unwanted and uncommon software Checked
    Privacy & Security > Certificates Query OCSP responder servers Checked, if shown
    Privacy & Security > HTTPS-Only Mode Enable HTTPS-Only Mode in all windows Selected
    Privacy & Security > DNS over HTTPS Increased or Max protection Optional

    Firefox 135 removed the old "Do Not Track" checkbox. The "Tell websites not to sell or share my data" switch (Global Privacy Control) took its place.

    Remove extensions at Menu > Add-ons and themes (about:addons) > Extensions. Update at Menu > Help > About Firefox.

    Verify

    Reopen about:preferences#privacy and read the settings back. about:policies should list no policy that weakens them.

    #Check Firefox about:config

    Type about:config > Accept the Risk and Continue. Search each name. Bold entries differ from the default; reset a bad one with the reset arrow, or set it:

    Preference Secure value
    browser.safebrowsing.malware.enabled true
    browser.safebrowsing.phishing.enabled true
    browser.safebrowsing.downloads.enabled true
    dom.disable_open_during_load true (pop-up blocker)
    xpinstall.signatures.required true
    xpinstall.whitelist.required true
    dom.security.https_only_mode true
    signon.rememberSignons false
    network.cookie.cookieBehavior 5 (the Standard default)
    security.tls.version.min 3 (TLS 1.2) or default

    #Fix Firefox enterprise policies

    Firefox reads C:\Program Files\Mozilla Firefox\distribution\policies.json. A planted file can turn off updates or Safe Browsing. Open it in Notepad as administrator and remove bad lines such as "DisableAppUpdate": true. A hardened file looks like this:

    {
  "policies": {
    "DisableAppUpdate": false,
    "AppAutoUpdate": true,
    "PopupBlocking": { "Default": true, "Locked": true },
    "PasswordManagerEnabled": false,
    "OfferToSaveLogins": false,
    "DisableFirefoxStudies": true,
    "DisableTelemetry": true,
    "HttpsOnlyMode": "force_enabled",
    "InstallAddonsPermission": { "Default": false }
  }
}

    Firefox can also take policies from the registry under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Mozilla\Firefox. Check that key too:

    reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Mozilla\Firefox" /s

    Restart Firefox and open about:policies to confirm what applies. When a scoring line ends in "[all users]", set the matching policy here as well as in Settings, so it applies to every profile on the machine.

    #Chrome settings

    Open chrome://settings.

    Location Setting Value
    Privacy and security > Security Safe Browsing Enhanced protection
    Privacy and security > Security Always use secure connections On
    Privacy and security > Site settings > Pop-ups and redirects Default behavior Don't allow sites to send pop-ups or use redirects
    Privacy and security > Site settings > Additional content settings > Insecure content Default behavior Blocked
    Autofill and passwords > Google Password Manager > Settings Offer to save passwords and passkeys Off
    Autofill and passwords Payment methods, Addresses Off, remove saved entries
    Extensions (chrome://extensions) Unknown extensions Remove
    About Chrome (chrome://settings/help) Update Up to date

    "Your browser is managed by your organization" at the bottom of the menu means a policy is set. Read it at chrome://policy.

    #Edge settings

    Open edge://settings.

    Location Setting Value
    Privacy, search, and services > Security Microsoft Defender SmartScreen On
    Privacy, search, and services > Security Block potentially unwanted apps On
    Privacy, search, and services > Security Website typo protection (older builds: Typosquatting Checker) On
    Privacy, search, and services > Security Enhanced security mode Balanced or Strict
    Privacy, search, and services > Tracking prevention Level Strict
    Cookies and site permissions > Pop-ups and redirects Block On
    Passwords > Settings Offer to save passwords Off
    Default browser Allow sites to be reloaded in Internet Explorer mode Don't allow, unless the README needs it
    Extensions (edge://extensions) Unknown extensions Remove
    About Microsoft Edge (edge://settings/help) Update Up to date

    #Fix Chrome and Edge policies in the registry

    Planted policies can force-install bad extensions or turn off Safe Browsing. Read them:

    reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Google\Chrome" /s
reg query "HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Google\Chrome" /s
reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge" /s
reg query "HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge" /s

    Set secure Chrome policies (elevated cmd):

    reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Google\Chrome" /v SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel /t REG_DWORD /d 2 /f
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Google\Chrome" /v DefaultPopupsSetting /t REG_DWORD /d 2 /f
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Google\Chrome" /v PasswordManagerEnabled /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f

    Edge uses the same names for pop-ups and passwords. Its Safe Browsing equivalent is SmartScreen:

    reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge" /v SmartScreenEnabled /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge" /v SmartScreenPuaEnabled /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge" /v DefaultPopupsSetting /t REG_DWORD /d 2 /f
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge" /v PasswordManagerEnabled /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f
    Policy Values
    SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel 0 no protection, 1 standard, 2 enhanced
    DefaultPopupsSetting 1 allow pop-ups, 2 block pop-ups
    PasswordManagerEnabled 0 off, 1 on
    SmartScreenEnabled, SmartScreenPuaEnabled 0 off, 1 on

    Values to delete when you find them: SafeBrowsingProtectionLevel = 0, SafeBrowsingEnabled = 0, SmartScreenEnabled = 0, DefaultPopupsSetting = 1, and any ExtensionInstallForcelist entry you do not recognize. An ExtensionInstallBlocklist containing * is a hardening setting and can stay.

    Remove a force-installed extension. The value names under the key are numbers:

    reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Google\Chrome\ExtensionInstallForcelist"

    reg delete "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Google\Chrome\ExtensionInstallForcelist" /v <number> /f

    Verify

    Restart the browser, open chrome://policy or edge://policy, click Reload policies, and read the values back.

    PreviousUAC, AutoPlay, screen lock and other settingsNextRegistry hardening values
    W11

    Registry hardening values

    jump:w11-registry

    Fast path

    1. Open cmd as administrator.

    2. Back up the key you are about to change:

      reg export "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" "%USERPROFILE%\Documents\lsa-backup.reg" /y

    3. Paste the core set.

    4. Read DefaultPassword for forensics, then turn off autologon (details).
    5. Check that Winlogon Shell is explorer.exe and Userinit is C:\Windows\system32\userinit.exe,.
    6. Read the values back with reg query (see Verify below).

    #Back up a key before changing it

    reg export "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" "%USERPROFILE%\Documents\winlogon-backup.reg" /y

    Restore it with reg import "%USERPROFILE%\Documents\winlogon-backup.reg" or by double-clicking the .reg file. In regedit, select the key > File > Export.

    Use the right hive

    HKLM is HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE (the whole computer) and HKCU is HKEY_CURRENT_USER (only the signed-in user). A value under the wrong hive does nothing. reg add takes REG_DWORD data in decimal unless you write it with 0x.

    #Hardening values table

    All values are REG_DWORD unless the Value column says otherwise. Paths are under HKLM.

    Purpose Key Value Data
    AutoRun off on all drives SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Explorer NoDriveTypeAutoRun 255
    Ignore autorun.inf SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Explorer NoAutorun 1
    No anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa RestrictAnonymous 1
    No anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa RestrictAnonymousSAM 1
    Everyone does not include anonymous users SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa EveryoneIncludesAnonymous 0
    Send NTLMv2 only, refuse LM and NTLM SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa LmCompatibilityLevel 5
    Do not store LM hashes SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa NoLMHash 1
    Blank passwords work only at the console SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa LimitBlankPasswordUse 1
    Do not store network credentials SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa DisableDomainCreds 1
    LSA protection SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa RunAsPPL 1 (or 2, see w11-uac-misc)
    NTLM client needs NTLMv2 session security and 128-bit SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0 NTLMMinClientSec 537395200
    NTLM server needs NTLMv2 session security and 128-bit SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0 NTLMMinServerSec 537395200
    No WDigest plaintext credentials SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest UseLogonCredential 0
    UAC on SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System EnableLUA 1
    UAC: consent prompt on the secure desktop SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin 2 (5 is the default)
    UAC secure desktop SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System PromptOnSecureDesktop 1
    UAC for the built-in Administrator SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System FilterAdministratorToken 1
    UAC remote restrictions for local accounts SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy 0 (or absent)
    Require Ctrl+Alt+Del SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System DisableCAD 0
    Do not show the last user name SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System DontDisplayLastUserName 1
    No shutdown from the sign-in screen SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System ShutdownWithoutLogon 0
    Lock after 15 minutes idle SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System InactivityTimeoutSecs 900
    Remote Desktop denied (if not required) SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server fDenyTSConnections 1
    Remote Desktop requires NLA (if required) SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp UserAuthentication 1
    Remote Assistance off SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Remote Assistance fAllowToGetHelp 0
    SMB server signing required SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanServer\Parameters RequireSecuritySignature 1
    SMB client signing required SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanWorkstation\Parameters RequireSecuritySignature 1
    No null session access to shares SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanServer\Parameters RestrictNullSessAccess 1
    SMBv1 server off SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanServer\Parameters SMB1 0
    No autologon SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon AutoAdminLogon (REG_SZ) 0
    Cached logons SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon CachedLogonsCount (REG_SZ) 4 or fewer (default 10)
    Correct shell SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon Shell (REG_SZ) explorer.exe
    Correct userinit SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon Userinit (REG_SZ) C:\Windows\system32\userinit.exe,
    No "always install elevated" SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer AlwaysInstallElevated 0 (set it in HKCU too)
    SmartScreen on SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\System EnableSmartScreen 1
    Defender not turned off by policy SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender DisableAntiSpyware Delete the value
    Automatic updates on SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU NoAutoUpdate 0
    Firewall on by policy SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\WindowsFirewall\StandardProfile (also DomainProfile, PublicProfile) EnableFirewall 1, or delete
    PowerShell script block logging SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ScriptBlockLogging EnableScriptBlockLogging 1
    What 537395200 means

    537395200 is hex 0x20080000: the flag for "Require NTLMv2 session security" (0x00080000) plus "Require 128-bit encryption" (0x20000000). In secpol.msc these are the two "Network security: Minimum session security for NTLM SSP" options with both boxes checked.

    #Apply the core set with reg add

    Run in elevated cmd. Each line stands alone, so a failure on one does not stop the rest.

    reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Explorer" /v NoDriveTypeAutoRun /t REG_DWORD /d 255 /f
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Explorer" /v NoAutorun /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" /v RestrictAnonymous /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" /v RestrictAnonymousSAM /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" /v EveryoneIncludesAnonymous /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" /v LmCompatibilityLevel /t REG_DWORD /d 5 /f
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" /v NoLMHash /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" /v LimitBlankPasswordUse /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" /v RunAsPPL /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0" /v NTLMMinClientSec /t REG_DWORD /d 537395200 /f
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0" /v NTLMMinServerSec /t REG_DWORD /d 537395200 /f
reg add "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest" /v UseLogonCredential /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" /v EnableLUA /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" /v ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin /t REG_DWORD /d 2 /f
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" /v PromptOnSecureDesktop /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" /v LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" /v DisableCAD /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" /v DontDisplayLastUserName /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" /v ShutdownWithoutLogon /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" /v InactivityTimeoutSecs /t REG_DWORD /d 900 /f
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /v CachedLogonsCount /t REG_SZ /d 4 /f
reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer" /v AlwaysInstallElevated /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f
reg add "HKCU\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer" /v AlwaysInstallElevated /t REG_DWORD /d 0 /f

    RunAsPPL needs a reboot

    LSA protection starts at the next boot. If a third-party security product on the image then fails to start, see w11-uac-misc for how the UEFI lock affects undoing it. Normal CyberPatriot images are not affected.

    Verify

    reg query "HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa" and reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System" show the new data. Close and reopen secpol.msc and the matching Security Options show the same values.

    #Turn off autologon and remove the stored password

    Autologon keeps a plaintext password in the registry. Read the three values:

    reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /v AutoAdminLogon
reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /v DefaultUserName
reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /v DefaultPassword

    AutoAdminLogon = 1 with a DefaultPassword means Windows signs that user in automatically. Turn it off and delete the password:

    reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /v AutoAdminLogon /t REG_SZ /d 0 /f

    reg delete "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /v DefaultPassword /f

    Read it before you delete it

    A forensics question may ask for the password in DefaultPassword. Also, if the image signed you in automatically, confirm your account's password from the README before you turn off autologon and reboot.

    Also run netplwiz and check "Users must enter a user name and password to use this computer" if the box is shown.

    #Check the Winlogon shell and userinit values

    reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /v Shell
reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon" /v Userinit

    They must be exactly explorer.exe and C:\Windows\system32\userinit.exe,. The commands to put them back are in w11-malware.

    #Search the registry for a value

    reg query HKLM /f "<text>" /s /d

    /d searches data, /v searches value names and /k searches key names. Searching all of HKLM is slow; start from a narrower key when you can.

    #Read and change values in PowerShell

    Read every value in a key:

    Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System'

    Set one DWORD value:

    Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System' -Name DontDisplayLastUserName -Value 1 -Type DWord

    Delete one value:

    Remove-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender' -Name DisableAntiSpyware

    Set-ItemProperty fails when the key does not exist. Create the key only if it is missing, then set the value. <key> is the path after HKLM\:

    $k = 'HKLM:\<key>'
if (-not (Test-Path $k)) { New-Item -Path $k -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name <value-name> -Value <number> -Type DWord

    Do not run New-Item -Force on a key that exists

    It can replace the key and wipe the values in it. reg add creates missing keys on its own and is the safer choice.

    PreviousBrowser hardening (Firefox, Chrome, Edge)NextLocal Group Policy Editor reference
    W11

    Local Group Policy Editor reference

    jump:w11-gpedit

    Fast path

    1. Win+R > gpedit.msc. Windows 11 Home does not have it; use the registry values in w11-registry there.
    2. Go to Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > All Settings and click the State column to sort.
    3. Read every Enabled or Disabled entry. Set the ones that weaken security to Not Configured or to the secure value in the table below.
    4. Repeat under User Configuration > Administrative Templates > All Settings.

    5. Apply:

      gpupdate /force

    6. Confirm with gpresult /r (details).

    #Where settings live

    Setting gpedit path Value
    Password policy Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Account Policies > Password Policy See w11-passpol
    Account lockout Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Account Policies > Account Lockout Policy See w11-passpol
    Audit policy Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > Audit Policy See w11-audit
    User Rights and Security Options Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies See w11-secopts
    Firewall Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security All profiles On
    Configure Automatic Updates Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Windows Update > Manage end user experience Enabled, 4
    Remove access to use all Windows Update features Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Windows Update > Manage end user experience Not Configured
    Turn off Microsoft Defender Antivirus Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Microsoft Defender Antivirus Not Configured or Disabled
    Turn off real-time protection Same path > Real-time Protection Not Configured or Disabled
    PUA detection Same path > Configure detection for potentially unwanted applications Enabled, Block
    Defender exclusions Same path > Exclusions Not Configured
    SmartScreen for apps and files Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Windows Defender SmartScreen > Explorer > Configure Windows Defender SmartScreen Enabled, Warn and prevent bypass
    Allow Remote Desktop connections Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Remote Desktop Services > Remote Desktop Session Host > Connections > Allow users to connect remotely by using Remote Desktop Services Disabled if RDP is not required
    Remote Desktop NLA Same path > Remote Desktop Session Host > Security > Require user authentication for remote connections by using Network Level Authentication Enabled
    Remote Desktop encryption Same path > Remote Desktop Session Host > Security > Set client connection encryption level Enabled, High Level
    Remote Assistance Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Remote Assistance > Configure Solicited Remote Assistance Disabled
    Turn off AutoPlay Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > AutoPlay Policies > Turn off Autoplay Enabled, All drives
    AutoRun default Same path > Set the default behavior for AutoRun Enabled, Do not execute any autorun commands
    Always install with elevated privileges Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Windows Installer > Always install with elevated privileges Disabled (also under User Configuration, same path)
    PowerShell script block logging Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Windows PowerShell > Turn on PowerShell Script Block Logging Enabled
    PowerShell module logging Same path > Turn on Module Logging Enabled, module names *
    PowerShell transcription Same path > Turn on PowerShell Transcription Enabled (optional)
    Command line in process creation events Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Audit Process Creation > Include command line in process creation events Enabled
    List admins when elevating Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Windows Components > Credential User Interface > Enumerate administrator accounts on elevation Disabled
    Network selection on the sign-in screen Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > System > Logon > Do not display network selection UI Enabled
    Lock screen camera Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Control Panel > Personalization > Prevent enabling lock screen camera Enabled
    Screen saver (per user) User Configuration > Administrative Templates > Control Panel > Personalization See w11-uac-misc
    Prohibit access to Control Panel User Configuration > Administrative Templates > Control Panel Not Configured (never set this)
    Insecure guest logons Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Network > Lanman Workstation > Enable insecure guest logons Disabled
    SMBv1 client driver Not in the default templates (needs the Microsoft Security Guide ADMX) Use optional features instead

    Find planted policies quickly

    "All Settings" under Administrative Templates lists every policy in one view. Sorted by State, every Enabled or Disabled entry is a change from the default. Check both Computer Configuration and User Configuration.

    #Apply and check policy

    Apply changes now:

    gpupdate /force

    Summary of what applies:

    gpresult /r

    Full HTML report on the Desktop. Run it elevated so computer settings are included:

    gpresult /h "%USERPROFILE%\Desktop\gpresult.html" /f

    rsop.msc shows the same result in a console.

    #Turn on PowerShell script block logging without gpedit

    On Home edition, set the registry value the policy uses:

    reg add "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ScriptBlockLogging" /v EnableScriptBlockLogging /t REG_DWORD /d 1 /f

    The logs appear in Event Viewer > Applications and Services Logs > Microsoft > Windows > PowerShell > Operational as Event ID 4104.

    #Reset all local policies (last resort)

    Know what you lose

    Deleting the policy folders removes every Administrative Template policy, including the good ones you set. Afterwards re-apply the Windows Update, Defender, AutoPlay and Remote Desktop policies. Only do this when many bad template policies exist.

    Delete the local policy files and reapply:

    rd /s /q "%windir%\System32\GroupPolicy"
rd /s /q "%windir%\System32\GroupPolicyUsers"
gpupdate /force

    Security Settings (password, lockout, audit, user rights, Security Options) are stored separately and survive this. To reset those to Windows defaults, which are weak, run the command below and then re-apply your hardening:

    secedit /configure /cfg %windir%\inf\defltbase.inf /db defltbase.sdb /verbose
    PreviousRegistry hardening valuesNextPowerShell helper scripts (recon and fixes)
    W11

    PowerShell helper scripts (recon and fixes)

    jump:w11-scripts

    Know what a script does before you run it

    The recon script only reads. Each fix snippet changes one area; run only the ones that match your README. Nothing here deletes users or files. Read the report and act by hand.

    Fast path

    1. Start > type powershell > right-click Windows PowerShell > Run as administrator. The title bar must say Administrator.

    2. Allow scripts in this window only:

      Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Force

    3. Copy the whole recon script and paste it into the window. It runs on its own.

    4. Wait for Notepad to open the report (1-5 minutes; the media search is the slow part).
    5. Work through the report section by section and fix by hand or with the fix snippets.
    6. Run the recon again at the end and compare the two reports.

    #Run PowerShell as administrator and allow scripts

    1. Start > type powershell > right-click Windows PowerShell > Run as administrator.

    2. Allow scripts for this window only. Nothing changes system-wide and the setting ends when the window closes:

      Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Force

    3. Paste a script into the window, or run a saved one:

      & "$env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\recon.ps1"

    Save a script as a .ps1 file

    Open Notepad, paste, then File > Save As > name it recon.ps1, Save as type: All files, Encoding: UTF-8. If Windows blocks a downloaded script, run Unblock-File "<path>".

    Use Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe), the one built into Windows 11. The LocalAccounts and Defender cmdlets are most reliable there.

    #Read-only recon report

    What the script does:

    1. Checks that the window is elevated and warns if it is not (most sections come back empty without admin rights).
    2. Writes recon_<date>_<time>.txt to your Desktop and opens it in Notepad when finished.
    3. Reports, in this order: system info; every local user with flags (ENABLED, ADMIN, NO-PASSWORD-REQUIRED, PASSWORD-NEVER-EXPIRES, CANNOT-CHANGE-PASSWORD, BUILT-IN); Administrators members; other non-empty groups; hidden users; password and lockout policy (net accounts plus complexity and reversible encryption); audit policy gaps; security registry values; firewall profiles and custom inbound allow rules; Defender status, settings and exclusions; Defender, Update and Firewall policy keys; non-default shares with their permissions; listening TCP ports with process and service names; non-Microsoft services; services running from unusual paths; the state of commonly risky services; scheduled tasks outside \Microsoft\; Run and RunOnce keys for the machine and every loaded user; Startup folders; IFEO debuggers and Winlogon values; enabled risky optional features; installed programs from the uninstall registry keys; non-comment hosts file lines; media files in C:\Users.
    4. Changes nothing. The only file it writes besides the report is a temporary policy export, which it deletes.

    How to run it: elevated Windows PowerShell, run Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Force, then paste the whole block or save it as recon.ps1 and run it.

    $report = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
$out = Join-Path ([Environment]::GetFolderPath('Desktop')) ('recon_{0}.txt' -f (Get-Date -Format 'yyyyMMdd_HHmm'))
$isAdmin = ([Security.Principal.WindowsPrincipal][Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent()).IsInRole([Security.Principal.WindowsBuiltInRole]::Administrator)
if (-not $isAdmin) { Write-Warning 'This window is not elevated. Most sections will be empty. Reopen PowerShell with Run as administrator.' }

function Add-Part {
    param([string]$Title, [scriptblock]$Body)
    Write-Host "Checking: $Title"
    $report.Add('')
    $report.Add("==================== $Title ====================")
    try { $text = (& $Body 2>&1 | Out-String -Width 300).TrimEnd() } catch { $text = "ERROR: $($_.Exception.Message)" }
    if (-not $text) { $text = '(nothing found)' }
    $report.Add($text)
}

function Get-GroupMembers {
    param([string]$Group)
    $seen = $false
    foreach ($line in (net localgroup "$Group" 2>$null)) {
        if ($line -match '^-{5,}') { $seen = $true; continue }
        if ($seen -and $line.Trim() -and $line -notmatch 'command completed') { $line.Trim() }
    }
}

$admins = @(Get-GroupMembers 'Administrators' | ForEach-Object { ($_ -split '\\')[-1] })

$services = @(Get-CimInstance Win32_Service -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object {
    $exe = $null
    if ($_.PathName -match '^\s*"([^"]+)"') { $exe = $Matches[1] }
    elseif ($_.PathName -match '^\s*(\S.*?\.(exe|com|bat|cmd|ps1|dll))(\s|$)') { $exe = $Matches[1] }
    elseif ($_.PathName) { $exe = ($_.PathName -split '\s+')[0] }
    if ($exe) { $exe = [Environment]::ExpandEnvironmentVariables($exe) }
    $company = $null
    if ($exe -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $exe -PathType Leaf)) { $company = (Get-Item -LiteralPath $exe).VersionInfo.CompanyName }
    [pscustomobject]@{ Name = $_.Name; State = $_.State; StartMode = $_.StartMode; Account = $_.StartName; Company = $company; Exe = $exe; PathName = $_.PathName; ProcessId = $_.ProcessId }
})

Add-Part 'SYSTEM' {
    Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | Select-Object Caption, Version, BuildNumber, LastBootUpTime | Format-List
    "Computer: $env:COMPUTERNAME    Running as: $(whoami)    Elevated: $isAdmin"
}

Add-Part 'LOCAL USERS (check every name against the README)' {
    Get-LocalUser | ForEach-Object {
        $u = $_
        $flags = @()
        if ($u.Enabled) { $flags += 'ENABLED' } else { $flags += 'disabled' }
        if ($admins -contains $u.Name) { $flags += 'ADMIN' }
        if (-not $u.PasswordRequired) { $flags += 'NO-PASSWORD-REQUIRED' }
        if ($null -eq $u.PasswordExpires) { $flags += 'PASSWORD-NEVER-EXPIRES' }
        if (-not $u.UserMayChangePassword) { $flags += 'CANNOT-CHANGE-PASSWORD' }
        if ($u.SID.Value -match '-(500|501|503|504)$') { $flags += 'BUILT-IN' }
        [pscustomobject]@{ Name = $u.Name; Flags = ($flags -join ' '); PasswordLastSet = $u.PasswordLastSet; LastLogon = $u.LastLogon; Description = $u.Description }
    } | Format-Table -AutoSize -Wrap
}

Add-Part 'ADMINISTRATORS GROUP MEMBERS' { Get-GroupMembers 'Administrators' }

Add-Part 'OTHER GROUPS WITH MEMBERS' {
    foreach ($g in Get-LocalGroup) {
        if ($g.Name -eq 'Administrators') { continue }
        $m = @(Get-GroupMembers $g.Name)
        if ($m.Count -gt 0) { '[{0}]  {1}' -f $g.Name, ($m -join ', ') }
    }
}

Add-Part 'HIDDEN USERS (Winlogon SpecialAccounts UserList)' {
    $k = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\SpecialAccounts\UserList'
    if (Test-Path $k) { Get-ItemProperty $k | Select-Object * -ExcludeProperty PS* | Format-List } else { 'No UserList key.' }
}

Add-Part 'PASSWORD AND LOCKOUT POLICY' {
    net accounts
    $cfg = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'recon_secpol.inf'
    secedit /export /cfg $cfg /areas SECURITYPOLICY | Out-Null
    if (Test-Path $cfg) {
        Select-String -Path $cfg -Pattern '^(PasswordComplexity|ClearTextPassword|EnableGuestAccount|EnableAdminAccount|LSAAnonymousNameLookup|NewAdministratorName|NewGuestName)' | ForEach-Object { $_.Line }
        Remove-Item $cfg -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }
}

Add-Part 'AUDIT POLICY (subcategories not set to Success and Failure)' {
    auditpol /get /category:* | Where-Object { $_ -match '(No Auditing|Success|Failure)\s*$' -and $_ -notmatch 'Success and Failure' }
}

Add-Part 'SECURITY REGISTRY VALUES' {
    $checks = @(
        @('HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa', 'LimitBlankPasswordUse'),
        @('HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa', 'RestrictAnonymous'),
        @('HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa', 'RestrictAnonymousSAM'),
        @('HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa', 'EveryoneIncludesAnonymous'),
        @('HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa', 'LmCompatibilityLevel'),
        @('HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa', 'NoLMHash'),
        @('HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa', 'RunAsPPL'),
        @('HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0', 'NTLMMinClientSec'),
        @('HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\MSV1_0', 'NTLMMinServerSec'),
        @('HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest', 'UseLogonCredential'),
        @('HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System', 'EnableLUA'),
        @('HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System', 'ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin'),
        @('HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System', 'PromptOnSecureDesktop'),
        @('HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System', 'LocalAccountTokenFilterPolicy'),
        @('HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System', 'DisableCAD'),
        @('HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System', 'DontDisplayLastUserName'),
        @('HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System', 'ShutdownWithoutLogon'),
        @('HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System', 'InactivityTimeoutSecs'),
        @('HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Explorer', 'NoDriveTypeAutoRun'),
        @('HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Explorer', 'NoAutorun'),
        @('HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server', 'fDenyTSConnections'),
        @('HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp', 'UserAuthentication'),
        @('HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Remote Assistance', 'fAllowToGetHelp'),
        @('HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon', 'AutoAdminLogon'),
        @('HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon', 'DefaultUserName'),
        @('HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon', 'DefaultPassword'),
        @('HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon', 'CachedLogonsCount'),
        @('HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon', 'Shell'),
        @('HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon', 'Userinit'),
        @('HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows', 'AppInit_DLLs'),
        @('HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer', 'AlwaysInstallElevated'),
        @('HKCU:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\Installer', 'AlwaysInstallElevated')
    )
    foreach ($c in $checks) {
        $v = (Get-ItemProperty -Path $c[0] -Name $c[1] -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).($c[1])
        if ($null -eq $v) { $v = '(not set)' }
        '{0,-30} = {1}    [{2}]' -f $c[1], $v, $c[0]
    }
}

Add-Part 'FIREWALL PROFILES' {
    Get-NetFirewallProfile | Select-Object Name, Enabled, DefaultInboundAction, DefaultOutboundAction, LogAllowed, LogBlocked | Format-Table -AutoSize
}

Add-Part 'ENABLED INBOUND ALLOW RULES WITHOUT A GROUP (likely custom)' {
    Get-NetFirewallRule -Direction Inbound -Action Allow -Enabled True | Where-Object { -not $_.DisplayGroup } | ForEach-Object {
        $pf = $_ | Get-NetFirewallPortFilter
        $af = $_ | Get-NetFirewallApplicationFilter
        '{0} | {1} {2} | {3}' -f $_.DisplayName, $pf.Protocol, ($pf.LocalPort -join ','), $af.Program
    }
}

Add-Part 'DEFENDER STATUS' {
    Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object AMServiceEnabled, AntivirusEnabled, RealTimeProtectionEnabled, BehaviorMonitorEnabled, IoavProtectionEnabled, OnAccessProtectionEnabled, IsTamperProtected, AntivirusSignatureLastUpdated | Format-List
}

Add-Part 'DEFENDER SETTINGS AND EXCLUSIONS' {
    Get-MpPreference | Select-Object DisableRealtimeMonitoring, DisableBehaviorMonitoring, DisableIOAVProtection, DisableScriptScanning, MAPSReporting, SubmitSamplesConsent, PUAProtection, EnableNetworkProtection, ExclusionPath, ExclusionExtension, ExclusionProcess, ExclusionIpAddress | Format-List
}

Add-Part 'POLICY KEYS FOR DEFENDER, WINDOWS UPDATE AND FIREWALL' {
    foreach ($p in 'HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender', 'HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate', 'HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\WindowsFirewall') {
        "-- $p"
        reg query "$p" /s 2>$null
    }
}

Add-Part 'NON-DEFAULT SHARES AND WHO CAN USE THEM' {
    Get-SmbShare | Where-Object { -not $_.Special -and $_.Name -notin 'ADMIN$', 'IPC$', 'print$' -and $_.Name -notmatch '^[A-Z]\$$' } | ForEach-Object {
        $s = $_
        '{0}    path: {1}    description: {2}' -f $s.Name, $s.Path, $s.Description
        Get-SmbShareAccess -Name $s.Name | ForEach-Object { '    {0} {1} {2}' -f $_.AccountName, $_.AccessControlType, $_.AccessRight }
    }
    'SMB1 server enabled: ' + (Get-SmbServerConfiguration).EnableSMB1Protocol
}

Add-Part 'LISTENING TCP PORTS' {
    $svcByPid = @{}
    foreach ($s in $services) { if ($s.ProcessId) { $svcByPid[[int]$s.ProcessId] = @($svcByPid[[int]$s.ProcessId]) + $s.Name } }
    Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen | Sort-Object LocalPort | ForEach-Object {
        $p = Get-Process -Id $_.OwningProcess -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        $names = (@($svcByPid[[int]$_.OwningProcess]) | Where-Object { $_ }) -join ','
        '{0,-6} {1,-16} PID {2,-6} {3,-18} {4}  {5}' -f $_.LocalPort, $_.LocalAddress, $_.OwningProcess, $p.ProcessName, $p.Path, $names
    }
}

Add-Part 'NON-MICROSOFT SERVICES' {
    $services | Where-Object { $_.Company -notmatch 'Microsoft' } | Sort-Object Name | Select-Object Name, State, StartMode, Account, Company, PathName | Format-Table -AutoSize -Wrap
}

Add-Part 'SERVICES RUNNING FROM UNUSUAL PATHS' {
    $services | Where-Object { $_.Exe -and $_.Exe -notmatch '^[a-z]:\\(Windows\\(System32|SysWOW64|servicing|Microsoft\.NET)\\|Program Files( \(x86\))?\\|ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender\\)' } |
        Sort-Object Name | Select-Object Name, State, StartMode, Account, PathName | Format-Table -AutoSize -Wrap
}

Add-Part 'RISKY SERVICES (check each against the README)' {
    Get-Service RemoteRegistry, TlntSvr, ftpsvc, W3SVC, SNMP, SSDPSRV, upnphost, SharedAccess, RemoteAccess, RasAuto, simptcp, TermService, WinRM, sshd, Spooler, Fax -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Select-Object Name, Status, StartType | Format-Table -AutoSize
}

Add-Part 'SCHEDULED TASKS OUTSIDE \Microsoft\' {
    Get-ScheduledTask | Where-Object { $_.TaskPath -notlike '\Microsoft\*' } | ForEach-Object {
        $t = $_
        $acts = ($t.Actions | ForEach-Object { ('{0} {1}' -f $_.Execute, $_.Arguments).Trim() }) -join ' ; '
        '{0}{1}  [{2}]  user: {3}  runs: {4}' -f $t.TaskPath, $t.TaskName, $t.State, $t.Principal.UserId, $acts
    }
}

Add-Part 'RUN AND RUNONCE KEYS' {
    $keys = @(
        'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run',
        'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce',
        'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run',
        'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce',
        'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Explorer\Run'
    )
    foreach ($h in Get-ChildItem Registry::HKEY_USERS -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        if ($h.PSChildName -notmatch '_Classes$') {
            $keys += "Registry::HKEY_USERS\$($h.PSChildName)\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run"
            $keys += "Registry::HKEY_USERS\$($h.PSChildName)\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce"
        }
    }
    foreach ($k in $keys) {
        if (Test-Path $k) {
            $item = Get-Item $k
            foreach ($n in $item.GetValueNames()) { '{0}  |  {1} = {2}' -f $k, $n, $item.GetValue($n) }
        }
    }
}

Add-Part 'STARTUP FOLDERS (desktop.ini hidden)' {
    Get-ChildItem -Force 'C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\StartUp', 'C:\Users\*\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Where-Object Name -ne 'desktop.ini' | ForEach-Object { $_.FullName }
}

Add-Part 'IFEO DEBUGGER VALUES (should be empty)' {
    foreach ($root in 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options', 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options') {
        Get-ChildItem $root -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | ForEach-Object {
            $d = (Get-ItemProperty $_.PSPath).Debugger
            if ($d) { '{0} : {1}' -f $_.PSChildName, $d }
        }
    }
}

Add-Part 'RISKY OPTIONAL FEATURES THAT ARE ENABLED' {
    Get-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online | Where-Object { $_.State -eq 'Enabled' -and $_.FeatureName -match 'SMB1|Telnet|TFTP|SimpleTCP|IIS|PowerShellV2|MSMQ' } | ForEach-Object { $_.FeatureName }
}

Add-Part 'INSTALLED PROGRAMS (uninstall registry keys)' {
    Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*', 'HKLM:\Software\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*', 'Registry::HKEY_USERS\*\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Where-Object DisplayName | ForEach-Object { '{0} | {1} | {2} | {3}' -f $_.DisplayName, $_.DisplayVersion, $_.Publisher, $_.InstallDate } | Sort-Object -Unique
}

Add-Part 'HOSTS FILE ENTRIES (non-comment lines)' {
    Get-Content "$env:windir\System32\drivers\etc\hosts" | Where-Object { $_ -notmatch '^\s*#' -and $_.Trim() }
}

Add-Part 'MEDIA FILES IN C:\Users (AppData skipped)' {
    $ext = '*.mp3', '*.mp4', '*.m4a', '*.m4v', '*.wav', '*.wma', '*.wmv', '*.flac', '*.aac', '*.ogg', '*.avi', '*.mov', '*.mkv', '*.flv', '*.webm', '*.mpg', '*.mpeg'
    Get-ChildItem -Path C:\Users -Recurse -Force -File -Include $ext -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
        Where-Object { $_.FullName -notmatch '\\AppData\\' } | ForEach-Object { $_.FullName }
}

$report | Set-Content -Path $out -Encoding UTF8
"Report written to $out"
notepad $out

    How to read the report:

    Section What to look for
    Local users Names the README does not list, ADMIN on someone who is not an authorized admin, NO-PASSWORD-REQUIRED, PASSWORD-NEVER-EXPIRES, an ENABLED Guest or built-in Administrator. PASSWORD-NEVER-EXPIRES shows on every user when the maximum password age is unlimited.
    Hidden users Any name with value 0 is hidden from the sign-in screen (w11-users).
    Security registry values Compare with the hardening table.
    Defender exclusions Should be empty (w11-defender).
    Listening ports, services, tasks, Run keys Anything in a user folder, Temp or ProgramData, or a name you cannot explain (w11-malware).
    Installed programs, media files Compare with the README (w11-software, w11-files).

    Compare the first and last report

    Compare-Object (Get-Content "<first-report>") (Get-Content "<last-report>") lists the lines that changed. => lines appear only in the second report and <= lines only in the first.

    #Fix snippets

    Each block below runs on its own in an elevated Windows PowerShell window after Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Force. Skip any block the README contradicts, and log what you ran.

    #Set password and lockout policy

    1. Sets history 24, maximum age 60 days, minimum age 1 day, minimum length 12.
    2. Sets lockout after 5 bad attempts for 30 minutes, with a 30-minute counter reset.
    3. Turns on password complexity and turns off reversible encryption through a secedit export and import.
    4. Prints net accounts so you can check the result.
    net accounts /uniquepw:24 /maxpwage:60 /minpwage:1 /minpwlen:12
net accounts /lockoutthreshold:5
net accounts /lockoutduration:30
net accounts /lockoutwindow:30
$cfg = Join-Path $env:TEMP 'pwpolicy.inf'
secedit /export /cfg $cfg /areas SECURITYPOLICY | Out-Null
(Get-Content $cfg) -replace '^PasswordComplexity\s*=.*', 'PasswordComplexity = 1' -replace '^ClearTextPassword\s*=.*', 'ClearTextPassword = 0' | Set-Content $cfg -Encoding Unicode
secedit /configure /db (Join-Path $env:TEMP 'pwpolicy.sdb') /cfg $cfg /areas SECURITYPOLICY
Remove-Item $cfg -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
net accounts

    #Audit success and failure for everything

    1. Turns on success and failure auditing for every subcategory.
    2. Run it in elevated PowerShell or cmd.
    auditpol /set /category:* /success:enable /failure:enable

    #Disable Guest and the built-in Administrator

    1. Finds both accounts by their well-known SID (ending 501 and 500), so it works even if they were renamed.
    2. Disables Guest.
    3. Disables the built-in Administrator unless you are signed in as that account.
    4. Prints both accounts' state.
    $guest = Get-LocalUser | Where-Object { $_.SID.Value -like '*-501' }
$admin = Get-LocalUser | Where-Object { $_.SID.Value -like '*-500' }
Disable-LocalUser -SID $guest.SID
if ([Security.Principal.WindowsIdentity]::GetCurrent().User.Value -eq $admin.SID.Value) { 'You are signed in as the built-in Administrator, so it stays enabled.' } else { Disable-LocalUser -SID $admin.SID }
Get-LocalUser -SID $guest.SID, $admin.SID | Select-Object Name, Enabled

    #Set the team password on listed users

    1. Replace <username> with the users to change; add more names separated by commas. Leave your own account out unless you mean to change it.
    2. Sets each user's password to <team-password>, makes the password expire normally and requires a password.
    3. Prints each name it changed.
    $pw = ConvertTo-SecureString '<team-password>' -AsPlainText -Force
$users = @('<username>')
foreach ($u in $users) {
    Set-LocalUser -Name $u -Password $pw -PasswordNeverExpires $false
    net user $u /passwordreq:yes | Out-Null
    "set $u"
}

    #Turn on the firewall with logging

    1. Turns on all three profiles, blocks unsolicited inbound, allows outbound and logs allowed and dropped packets.
    2. Prints the profile state.
    Set-NetFirewallProfile -Profile Domain,Private,Public -Enabled True -DefaultInboundAction Block -DefaultOutboundAction Allow -LogAllowed True -LogBlocked True
Get-NetFirewallProfile | Select-Object Name, Enabled, DefaultInboundAction, DefaultOutboundAction

    #Turn on Defender protections and remove exclusions

    1. Turns on real-time, behavior, download and script scanning, cloud protection, sample submission, PUA blocking and network protection.
    2. Removes every path, extension and process exclusion. Read the report's exclusions first if a forensics question might ask about them.
    3. Updates signatures and prints the status. Tamper Protection silently blocks some of these changes; see w11-defender.
    Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $false -DisableBehaviorMonitoring $false -DisableIOAVProtection $false -DisableScriptScanning $false -MAPSReporting Advanced -SubmitSamplesConsent SendSafeSamples -PUAProtection Enabled -EnableNetworkProtection Enabled
$p = Get-MpPreference
if ($p.ExclusionPath) { Remove-MpPreference -ExclusionPath $p.ExclusionPath }
if ($p.ExclusionExtension) { Remove-MpPreference -ExclusionExtension $p.ExclusionExtension }
if ($p.ExclusionProcess) { Remove-MpPreference -ExclusionProcess $p.ExclusionProcess }
Update-MpSignature
Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object RealTimeProtectionEnabled, AntivirusSignatureLastUpdated

    #Set security options in the registry

    1. Sets the anonymous access, LM hash, NTLM and blank password values under Lsa.
    2. Sets UAC to Always notify, requires Ctrl+Alt+Del, hides the last user name, blocks shutdown from the sign-in screen and locks after 15 minutes idle.
    3. Every key here exists on a normal Windows 11 install, so nothing is created.
    $lsa = 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa'
$sys = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System'
Set-ItemProperty -Path $lsa -Name LimitBlankPasswordUse -Value 1 -Type DWord
Set-ItemProperty -Path $lsa -Name RestrictAnonymous -Value 1 -Type DWord
Set-ItemProperty -Path $lsa -Name RestrictAnonymousSAM -Value 1 -Type DWord
Set-ItemProperty -Path $lsa -Name EveryoneIncludesAnonymous -Value 0 -Type DWord
Set-ItemProperty -Path $lsa -Name NoLMHash -Value 1 -Type DWord
Set-ItemProperty -Path $lsa -Name LmCompatibilityLevel -Value 5 -Type DWord
Set-ItemProperty -Path $sys -Name EnableLUA -Value 1 -Type DWord
Set-ItemProperty -Path $sys -Name ConsentPromptBehaviorAdmin -Value 2 -Type DWord
Set-ItemProperty -Path $sys -Name PromptOnSecureDesktop -Value 1 -Type DWord
Set-ItemProperty -Path $sys -Name DisableCAD -Value 0 -Type DWord
Set-ItemProperty -Path $sys -Name DontDisplayLastUserName -Value 1 -Type DWord
Set-ItemProperty -Path $sys -Name ShutdownWithoutLogon -Value 0 -Type DWord
Set-ItemProperty -Path $sys -Name InactivityTimeoutSecs -Value 900 -Type DWord

    #Turn off AutoPlay and autorun

    1. Creates the Explorer policies key if it is missing.
    2. Sets NoDriveTypeAutoRun to 255 and NoAutorun to 1.
    $k = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\Explorer'
if (-not (Test-Path $k)) { New-Item -Path $k -Force | Out-Null }
Set-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name NoDriveTypeAutoRun -Value 255 -Type DWord
Set-ItemProperty -Path $k -Name NoAutorun -Value 1 -Type DWord

    #Disable risky services

    1. Edit the list first: remove any service the README requires.
    2. Stops and disables each listed service that exists on the image, and skips the rest.
    3. Prints each service it disabled.
    $disable = @('RemoteRegistry', 'SSDPSRV', 'upnphost', 'SharedAccess', 'RasAuto', 'RemoteAccess', 'simptcp', 'SNMP', 'SNMPTrap', 'TlntSvr', 'Fax')
foreach ($s in $disable) {
    if (Get-Service -Name $s -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        Set-Service -Name $s -StartupType Disabled
        Stop-Service -Name $s -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        "disabled $s"
    }
}

    #Remove old protocols (SMBv1, Telnet, TFTP, Simple TCP/IP, PowerShell 2.0)

    1. Turns off the SMBv1 server protocol.
    2. Disables each listed optional feature that is enabled, without restarting. PowerShell 2.0 is already gone from current Windows 11 builds and is skipped.
    3. Prints each feature it disabled. Reboot later to finish.
    Set-SmbServerConfiguration -EnableSMB1Protocol $false -Force
foreach ($f in 'SMB1Protocol', 'TelnetClient', 'TFTP', 'SimpleTCP', 'MicrosoftWindowsPowerShellV2Root') {
    $st = Get-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName $f -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if ($st -and $st.State -eq 'Enabled') {
        Disable-WindowsOptionalFeature -Online -FeatureName $f -NoRestart | Out-Null
        "disabled $f"
    }
}

    #Turn off Remote Desktop (only when the README does not require it)

    1. Denies Remote Desktop connections and disables its firewall rules.
    2. Turns off Remote Assistance.
    3. Lists the Remote Desktop Users group so you can empty it by hand.
    Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server' -Name fDenyTSConnections -Value 1 -Type DWord
Disable-NetFirewallRule -DisplayGroup 'Remote Desktop'
Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Remote Assistance' -Name fAllowToGetHelp -Value 0 -Type DWord
net localgroup "Remote Desktop Users"

    #Harden Remote Desktop (only when the README requires it)

    1. Requires Network Level Authentication, TLS and high encryption.
    2. Turns off Remote Assistance.
    3. Leaves Remote Desktop itself on.
    $rdp = 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Terminal Server\WinStations\RDP-Tcp'
Set-ItemProperty -Path $rdp -Name UserAuthentication -Value 1 -Type DWord
Set-ItemProperty -Path $rdp -Name SecurityLayer -Value 2 -Type DWord
Set-ItemProperty -Path $rdp -Name MinEncryptionLevel -Value 3 -Type DWord
Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Remote Assistance' -Name fAllowToGetHelp -Value 0 -Type DWord

    #Turn off autologon

    1. Prints the stored DefaultPassword so you can record it for forensics.
    2. Sets AutoAdminLogon to 0 and deletes DefaultPassword.
    3. Know your own password before you reboot.
    $wl = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon'
'Old DefaultPassword: ' + (Get-ItemProperty -Path $wl -Name DefaultPassword -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).DefaultPassword
Set-ItemProperty -Path $wl -Name AutoAdminLogon -Value '0' -Type String
Remove-ItemProperty -Path $wl -Name DefaultPassword -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

    W11

    Windows troubleshooting

    jump:w11-troubleshoot

    Fast path

    1. Score went down: open your change log and undo the most recent change first.
    2. Wait 1-2 minutes and refresh the scoring report.
    3. Read the penalty line. It usually names the thing ("Critical service X stopped"); fix that exact thing (common causes).
    4. "Access denied": reopen the window with Run as administrator (details).
    5. "Running scripts is disabled": run Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Force.
    6. Report not updating: check the internet connection and the clock (details).

    #Fix a score that went down

    Undo the most recent change first and wait 1-2 minutes for the report to refresh.

    What you did Why it cost points Undo
    Deleted or demoted a README user or admin Authorized user removed Re-create the user or add them back to Administrators
    Disabled a required service (IIS, FTP, RDP, Spooler, SMB server) Critical service down Set-Service <service-name> -StartupType Automatic; Start-Service <service-name>
    Uninstalled required software Required program removed Reinstall it, for example winget install --id <package-id> -e
    Deleted a required file or company document Required file removed Restore it from the Recycle Bin (right-click > Restore)
    Removed a firewall rule a required service needs Service not reachable Re-enable the rule or rule group
    Blocked outbound traffic or broke the network Scoring cannot report Set DefaultOutboundAction to Allow and check the adapter is enabled in ncpa.cpl

    Penalties show in their own list

    The scoring report lists penalties separately from gains, and the text usually names the thing that broke. Every penalty is recoverable by undoing the change. The penalties seen in past Windows keys, with how to avoid each, are in w11-penalties.

    #Get back in when you are locked out

    • Signed out and your password fails: type the README password exactly (case and symbols) and check Caps Lock and the keyboard layout.
    • Locked out by your own lockout policy: wait the lockout duration (30 minutes with the guide's settings), or sign in as another admin and clear the lockout in lusrmgr.msc > Users > the user > Properties > uncheck "Account is locked out".
    • Removed your own admin rights: sign in as another README admin and add yourself back. If no other admin exists, there is no fix inside the image; ask your coach about restarting the image (you lose time).

    To clear a lockout from another admin's elevated PowerShell (works on Home edition too):

    $u = [ADSI]"WinNT://./<username>,user"
$u.IsAccountLocked = $false
$u.SetInfo()

    Prevent lockouts

    Never change your own password, group membership or rights without writing it down. Never add Users or Administrators to "Deny log on locally". Keep one elevated window open while you change policy.

    #Fix PowerShell errors

    Message Fix
    "running scripts is disabled on this system" Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Force, then run the script again
    "'X' is not recognized as an internal or external command" You typed a PowerShell command in cmd (prompt starts C:\>, without PS). Type powershell first
    "The term 'X' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet" You are in PowerShell. Check the spelling. If the prompt is PowerShell 7 (pwsh), switch to Windows PowerShell (powershell.exe)
    winget is not recognized Update "App Installer" in the Microsoft Store, or use the app's own updater
    sc config does nothing or writes a file In PowerShell sc means Set-Content. Type sc.exe

    #Fix access denied

    1. Check the window is elevated: the title bar must say Administrator. If not, reopen it with right-click > Run as administrator.

    2. For a file or folder, take ownership and grant Administrators full control:

      takeown /f "<path>" /r /d y

      icacls "<path>" /grant Administrators:F /t

    3. For a registry key: regedit > right-click the key > Permissions > Advanced > Owner: Change to Administrators > Apply, then give Administrators Full Control.

    4. For Defender settings, Tamper Protection blocks changes. Turn it off in Windows Security, make the change, and turn it back on.
    5. Protected services such as WinDefend, WaaSMedicSvc and RpcSs cannot be changed in services.msc. That is normal.

    #Stop a service that will not stop

    • Set the startup type to Disabled first so nothing restarts it.
    • Stop services that depend on it: sc.exe enumdepend <service-name> lists them, or use Stop-Service <service-name> -Force.
    • Stuck in "Stopping": get its PID with sc.exe queryex <service-name>, then taskkill /PID <pid> /F.
    • It keeps coming back: in services.msc > the service > Recovery, set First, Second and Subsequent failures to Take No Action, and look for a scheduled task or Run key that restarts it (w11-malware).

    #Work without gpedit or secpol on Home edition

    Windows 11 Home has no gpedit.msc, secpol.msc or lusrmgr.msc. Check the edition with winver or:

    Get-ComputerInfo -Property WindowsProductName
    Task Use instead
    Users and groups net user, net localgroup, the PowerShell LocalAccounts cmdlets, netplwiz
    Password, lockout, audit and user rights net accounts, auditpol, and the secedit export, edit and import method (w11-passpol, w11-secopts)
    Administrative Template policies Their registry values under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies (w11-registry)

    #Scoring report not updating

    • Wait 2 minutes and refresh the page (F5).

    • Test the internet connection; TcpTestSucceeded should be True:

      Test-NetConnection www.google.com -Port 443

    • Check you did not block outbound traffic and that the hosts file does not redirect scoring sites.

    • In services.msc, find the CyberPatriot scoring service and check it is Running. If it stopped, start it. Change nothing else about it.
    • Check the clock: Settings > Time & language > Date & time > Sync now. A wrong clock breaks HTTPS.
    • If it is still stuck, ask your coach. Never reinstall or modify the scoring client.

    #Find answers in Event Viewer

    Open eventvwr.msc > Windows Logs > Security (or System). Right-click the log > Filter Current Log > type the Event IDs.

    ID Log Meaning
    4624 Security Successful logon (Logon Type 2 local, 3 network, 10 Remote Desktop)
    4625 Security Failed logon
    4634, 4647 Security Logoff
    4648 Security Logon with explicit credentials (runas)
    4672 Security Admin privileges assigned at logon
    4688 Security New process created (needs process creation auditing)
    4697 Security Service installed (needs Security System Extension auditing)
    4698 Security Scheduled task created (needs Other Object Access auditing)
    4719 Security Audit policy changed
    4720 Security User account created
    4722, 4725 Security User enabled, user disabled
    4723, 4724 Security Password change attempt, password reset attempt
    4726 Security User deleted
    4732 Security Member added to a security-enabled local group, such as Administrators
    4733 Security Member removed from a security-enabled local group
    4740 Security Account locked out
    1102 Security Security log cleared
    7045 System New service installed
    7040 System Service start type changed
    104 System An event log was cleared (System or another log)
    4104 PowerShell Operational Script block logged
    1116, 1117 Defender Operational Malware detected, action taken
    5001 Defender Operational Real-time protection turned off
    5007 Defender Operational Defender configuration changed (exclusions show up here)

    Pull the common ones from PowerShell:

    Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Security'; Id=4720,4732} -MaxEvents 50 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object TimeCreated, Id, @{n='Msg';e={($_.Message -split "`n")[0]}}

    Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='System'; Id=7045} -MaxEvents 20 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Format-List TimeCreated, Message

    Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Microsoft-Windows-Windows Defender/Operational'; Id=1116,1117,5001,5007} -MaxEvents 30 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Format-List TimeCreated, Id, Message

    Logs answer forensics questions

    Event logs often answer "which user was created", "when was the backdoor service installed" or "which account logged in remotely". Read them before you change anything, and never clear them.

    #Other quick fixes

    Problem Fix
    A Settings page says "Some settings are managed by your organization" A policy is set. Find it under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies or in gpedit (All Settings sorted by State)
    A change in secpol does not show Close and reopen secpol.msc, then run gpupdate /force
    Windows Update error 0x8024402c or 0x80244022 A planted WSUS server or proxy. Delete WUServer and UseWUServer (w11-updates) and run netsh winhttp reset proxy
    Cannot delete a file that is "in use" resmon > CPU > Associated Handles > search the file name > End Process
    Explorer crashed or the screen is black Ctrl+Shift+Esc > Run new task > explorer.exe
    Restart only Explorer Stop-Process -Name explorer -Force (it restarts itself)
    Network adapter disabled ncpa.cpl > right-click the adapter > Enable

    Past answer key items (Windows 10/11)

    jump:w11-answer-key

    Fast path

    1. Open the scoring report and find the line you just earned or are hunting for.
    2. Press Ctrl+F on this page and type a few words of that line.
    3. Follow the link next to the matching item for the full fix.
    4. On a practice image, work down the list and tick each item once the report shows it.

    Every item below appeared in a real CyberPatriot answer key, scoring report or decrypted scoring config for a Windows client image (Windows 7 to 11). The code text is the scoring-report wording. Items marked (Hivestorm) come from a sister competition that uses the same scoring engine and wording; items marked (practice image) come from a team-made image. Not every item shows up on every image, and the README can turn an item around (a required RDP server is never "turned off").

    #How points were spread on a Windows image

    A CP17 State Round Platinum Windows 10 image had 31 scored items:

    Category Items Category Items
    User Auditing 4 Malware 3
    Local Policy 4 Unwanted Software 3
    Forensics 3 Account Policy 2
    Application Security 3 Application Updates 2
    Defensive Countermeasures 2 Service Auditing 2
    Uncategorized OS Settings 2 Prohibited Files 1
    OS Updates 0

    Forensics questions usually carry more points than a single fix (6 points each in one real report), so answer them first.

    Where these came from

    The list is built from official CyberPatriot training keys (CP-XI to CP18, Windows 10 and 11), round answer lists from CP18 Rounds 1 and 2, a real CP-IX state-round scoring report, decrypted CP-IX and CP-X scoring configs (Windows 7, 8 and Server 2008), a CP17 Server 2019 key, one CP19 Server 2022 training key, two Hivestorm writeups and a few team-made practice images.     W11

    README scenarios seen on Windows images

    jump:w11-readme-scenarios

    Fast path

    1. Read the README and list every service, share and program it calls required or critical.
    2. Find each one in the scenario table and follow its row.
    3. Harden required things instead of removing them.
    4. Keep required files and installers where they are, even if they look like clutter.
    5. Re-read the README once more before you uninstall anything.

    #Scenarios seen in past READMEs

    README says Keep Harden Penalty seen when broken
    Users connect with Remote Desktop TermService running, fDenyTSConnections 0, the Remote Desktop firewall group NLA, SSL security layer, high encryption, secure RPC, only README users in Remote Desktop Users (how) -5 to -10 for RDP disabled
    A named file share (for example AFA or C:\Share) The share, its folder and the business files in it Share and NTFS permissions, SMB signing, SMB1 off (how) -5 for the share disabled, -5 for a business file deleted
    The machine runs a web site on IIS (sometimes with PHP) W3SVC, the site folder, wp-login.php or other site files Web server below Expect the critical-service penalty (-5 in Linux keys)
    The machine runs an FTP server (IIS FTP or FileZilla Server) ftpsvc or the FileZilla Server service SSL required, anonymous off (IIS FTP, FileZilla Server) Expect the critical-service penalty (-5 in Linux keys)
    Staff use Wireshark for network analysis Wireshark and Npcap Update it (how) -5 for required software removed
    A list of required programs (Firefox, Thunderbird, Chrome, Notepad++, 7-Zip, Adobe Reader, LibreOffice) Each program in its original folder Update in place (w11-apps) -5 each when removed or moved
    DHCP, DNS client and Event Log must keep running Those services, Automatic Nothing to change (table) Expect the critical-service penalty (-5 in Linux keys)
    Create user X, add X to group Y Do exactly that (users)
    Non-work media is prohibited; no hacking tools, games or P2P Files, unwanted software
    Turn on automatic update checks Windows and apps

    Wireshark flips between images

    Some READMEs list Wireshark as required and some keys score removing it. Search the README for "Wireshark" before you touch it.

    #A web or FTP server is required

    1. Keep W3SVC (and ftpsvc for FTP) Running and Automatic.
    2. Delete test pages and web shells only (how).
    3. Require SSL and turn off anonymous access in IIS Manager (IIS, IIS FTP). The Server pages apply unchanged to IIS on Windows 11.

    4. If PHP is installed, find its configuration file:

      Get-ChildItem C:\ -Recurse -Filter php.ini -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object FullName

    5. Open it in Notepad as administrator and set these lines (a Hivestorm Windows 10 key scored PHP display errors disabled):

      display_errors = Off
expose_php = Off

    6. Restart IIS from elevated cmd with iisreset.

    Verify

    The site still opens at http://localhost and Get-Service W3SVC shows Running.

    #A share is required

    Keep the share and every file the README calls business data. A past key penalized deleting a "pizza" file from the AFA share, and an older one penalized deleting a Notepad++ installer kept in C:\Share. Remove only files that are clearly prohibited (media, password lists), then fix permissions (how).

    PreviousPast answer key items (Windows 10/11)NextApplication updates and settings (Firefox, Notepad++, 7-Zip, PuTTY, FileZilla, Reader)
    W11

    Application updates and settings (Firefox, Notepad++, 7-Zip, PuTTY, FileZilla, Reader)

    jump:w11-apps

    Update in place

    Past keys penalize required software that is "not installed at default location". Update over the existing install: same folder, same 32-bit or 64-bit build. Never uninstall a required app to reinstall it somewhere else, and never move its folder.

    Fast path

    1. Open PowerShell as administrator and list versions and folders (command).
    2. Remove planted policies that block app updates (how).

    3. Update each README app with its own updater (Help > About or Check for updates), or with winget:

      winget upgrade --id <package-id> -e --accept-source-agreements --accept-package-agreements

    4. Run the version command again and confirm the folder did not change.

    5. Apply the app's security settings from its section below.

    #Check every app's version and install folder

    Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*', 'HKLM:\Software\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*', 'Registry::HKEY_USERS\*\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Where-Object DisplayName | Select-Object DisplayName, DisplayVersion, InstallLocation | Sort-Object DisplayName | Format-Table -AutoSize

    The engine often reads the version stamped on the program file itself (an old config tested AcroRd32.exe). Read it the same way:

    (Get-Item "<path>").VersionInfo | Select-Object ProductVersion, FileVersion, FileName
    App Usual program file
    Firefox C:\Program Files\Mozilla Firefox\firefox.exe
    Thunderbird C:\Program Files\Mozilla Thunderbird\thunderbird.exe
    Chrome C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe
    Notepad++ C:\Program Files\Notepad++\notepad++.exe
    7-Zip C:\Program Files\7-Zip\7zFM.exe
    LibreOffice C:\Program Files\LibreOffice\program\soffice.exe
    PuTTY C:\Program Files\PuTTY\putty.exe
    FileZilla Client C:\Program Files\FileZilla FTP Client\filezilla.exe
    Adobe Acrobat Reader (32-bit) C:\Program Files (x86)\Adobe\Acrobat Reader DC\Reader\AcroRd32.exe
    Visual Studio Code (user install) C:\Users\<username>\AppData\Local\Programs\Microsoft VS Code\Code.exe

    A 32-bit build lives under C:\Program Files (x86) instead. Check which folder the image uses before you download anything.

    #Update without changing the install folder

    1. Use the app's built-in updater first. It always installs over itself.
    2. Otherwise use winget upgrade --id <package-id> -e. It upgrades the installed build in place. IDs are in w11-updates.
    3. Otherwise download the installer from the vendor's own site, pick the same architecture (x64 or 32-bit) and run it. Accept the folder it offers only if it matches the old one.
    4. Re-run the version check.

    Avoid download-site ad buttons

    Pages for Notepad++, 7-Zip and PuTTY have ads that look like download buttons and lead to bundled installers. Use only the vendor's own download link, and never install anything that offers extra software.

    No internet on the image

    Scoring needs internet, so images almost always have it. If downloads are blocked, look for an installer the README points to (sometimes in a share). Run it from where it is; deleting or moving an installer the README calls a business file was penalized in a past key.

    #Remove policies that block app updates

    Planted values can stop an app from updating. Read them:

    reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Mozilla\Firefox" /s
reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Google\Update" /s
reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\EdgeUpdate" /s
reg query "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Adobe" /s
    Where Bad value Fix
    HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Mozilla\Firefox or policies.json DisableAppUpdate = 1 or true Delete it (policies.json)
    HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Mozilla\Firefox or policies.json AppAutoUpdate = 0 or false Delete it or set 1 / true
    HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Google\Update UpdateDefault = 0, AutoUpdateCheckPeriodMinutes = 0, any Update{...} = 0 Delete the value
    HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\EdgeUpdate UpdateDefault = 0, AutoUpdateCheckPeriodMinutes = 0 Delete the value
    HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Adobe\Acrobat Reader\DC\FeatureLockDown bUpdater = 0 Delete the value
    VS Code settings.json "update.mode": "none" Delete the line
    Notepad++ Settings > Preferences > MISC. > auto-updater turned off, or the updater folder deleted Turn it on; reinstall over the old version if the folder is gone

    Delete one value in elevated cmd:

    reg delete "HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Mozilla\Firefox" /v DisableAppUpdate /f

    #Firefox and Thunderbird

    Version and update: Menu > Help > About Firefox (or About Thunderbird). It downloads the update and asks to restart. Settings that keys scored for Firefox (pop-ups, add-on install warnings, malware warnings, automatic updates) are in w11-browsers.

    For automatic updates, Firefox Settings > General > Firefox Updates > "Automatically install updates (recommended)". A Hivestorm key scored Firefox automatically checks for updates.

    Thunderbird settings worth setting (not seen in a key):

    Location Setting Value
    Settings > Privacy & Security > Mail Content Allow remote content in messages Unchecked
    Settings > Privacy & Security > Scam Detection Tell me if the message I'm reading is a suspected email scam Checked
    Settings > Privacy & Security > Antivirus Allow antivirus clients to quarantine individual incoming messages Checked
    Settings > Privacy & Security > Passwords Saved passwords Remove what the README does not need
    Settings > General > Thunderbird Updates Automatically install updates Selected

    #Chrome and Edge

    Version and update: chrome://settings/help and edge://settings/help. Both update in place. If the page says updates are disabled by your administrator, delete the values in the policy table. Security settings are in w11-browsers.

    #Notepad++

    Version: ? menu > About Notepad++. Update: ? menu > Update Notepad++, or install the current release from notepad-plus-plus.org over the old one. A Server 2022 training key mentioned version 8.8.

    Old Notepad++ updaters

    Before version 8.8.9 the built-in updater (WinGUp) did not verify the downloaded installer, and attackers redirected its traffic. If the image has a version older than 8.8.9, download the current installer from the official site instead of trusting the built-in updater.

    Remove unknown plugins in Plugins > Plugins Admin > Installed. Plugin files live in C:\Program Files\Notepad++\plugins.

    #7-Zip and PeaZip

    7-Zip version: open 7-Zip File Manager > Help > About 7-Zip. There is no updater; download the current x64 installer from 7-zip.org and run it over the old version. Versions before 24.09 do not pass the Mark-of-the-Web from an archive to the files inside, so downloaded files can skip SmartScreen.

    PeaZip: download the current Windows installer from the official PeaZip site and install over the old version. Version is under Help > About in PeaZip.

    #LibreOffice

    Version: Help > About LibreOffice. Update: Help > Check for Updates, or install the current MSI from libreoffice.org over the old one. Settings worth setting:

    Location Setting Value
    Tools > Options > LibreOffice > Security > Macro Security Security level High or Very High
    Tools > Options > LibreOffice > Online Update Check for updates automatically Checked

    #PuTTY

    Version: click the PuTTY icon at the top-left of a PuTTY window > About PuTTY, or read the file version with the command above. There is no updater; install the current 64-bit MSI from the official PuTTY download page over the old one. Versions 0.68 to 0.80 leak NIST P-521 private keys used for signatures (CVE-2024-31497), so anything older than 0.81 is a real vulnerability.

    Saved sessions sit in HKCU\Software\SimonTatham\PuTTY\Sessions, which can answer forensics questions about which hosts a user connected to.

    #FileZilla Client

    Version: Help > About. Update: Help > Check for updates, or the official installer. Settings:

    Location Setting Value
    Edit > Settings > Interface > Passwords Save passwords "Save passwords protected by a master password", or "Do not save passwords"
    Edit > Settings > Updates Check for updates automatically Daily or weekly

    Saved sites live in %APPDATA%\FileZilla\sitemanager.xml and recentservers.xml. Older versions stored the passwords there as Base64, which can be the answer to a forensics question.

    #FileZilla Server

    Only when the README requires an FTP server. A team-made practice image scored FileZilla minimum TLS set to 1.3.

    1. Open the FileZilla Server administration interface and connect.
    2. Server > Configure > Server listeners: set each listener's protocol to "Require explicit FTP over TLS". The other choice, "Explicit FTP over TLS and insecure plain FTP", allows plain-text logins.
    3. Server > Configure > FTP and FTP over TLS (FTPS) > Connection security tab: set the minimum allowed TLS version to 1.3 (or 1.2 if clients cannot do 1.3).
    4. Server > Configure > Rights management > Users: remove users the README does not list, make sure every account has a password, and turn off any anonymous or <system user> login the README does not need.
    5. Update it from the official FileZilla Server download page.

    If the README does not require it, remove it (how).

    #Adobe Acrobat Reader updates and settings
