    SRV

    Server 2019 and Server 2022 differences

    jump:srv-2019-vs-2022

    Semifinals Platinum and Gold use both versions side by side, and Server 2019 is also the Training Round image. Most hardening steps are identical. The table lists only what changes how you work.

    Fast path

    1. Find the version and build:

      Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | Select-Object Caption,Version,BuildNumber

    2. Build 17763 is Server 2019. Build 20348 is Server 2022.

    3. On Server 2019, download installers through IE 11 with a trusted site entry, or with Invoke-WebRequest (how). Leave IE ESC on.
    4. Use the matching sconfig update prompts (how).
    5. Everything else in the Server sections applies to both versions.

    #What changes between the versions

    Area Server 2019 Server 2022
    Build and version 10.0.17763 (version 1809) 10.0.20348 (version 21H2)
    Browser Internet Explorer 11 only. No Edge unless someone installed it Microsoft Edge preinstalled, plus Internet Explorer 11
    Effect of IE ESC Blocks almost every download in the only browser Affects only IE; Edge downloads normally
    sconfig Older script; update prompts use letters PowerShell-based; update option has a numbered sub-menu
    TLS 1.3 Not available Available and on by default
    SMB encryption ciphers AES-128-GCM and AES-128-CCM Adds AES-256-GCM and AES-256-CCM
    DNS over HTTPS client No Yes
    Highest domain and forest functional level Windows Server 2016 Windows Server 2016 (2022 added no new level)
    .NET Framework in the box 4.7.2 4.8
    Settings app Windows 10 1809 layout Windows 10 21H2 layout
    Things that are the same, so do not hunt for differences

    Feature names (FS-SMB1, PowerShell-V2, Simple-TCPIP, Web-Ftp-Server, Windows-Defender), AD and Group Policy cmdlets, IIS 10 and its WebAdministration module, secpol.msc and GPO paths, Defender cmdlets, the Windows Security app, Get-LocalUser, OpenSSH as an optional capability, Server Manager and Remote Desktop settings are the same on both. Neither version supports winget. Windows LAPS is built into both after the April 2023 cumulative update. Telnet Server does not exist on either.

    #Download tools on Server 2019 with IE ESC on

    IE Enhanced Security Configuration is scored when on (why), so do not turn it off to download. Use one of these.

    Download straight to the desktop from an elevated PowerShell window. -UseBasicParsing avoids the IE engine:

    Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "<url>" -OutFile "$env:USERPROFILE\Desktop\<file>" -UseBasicParsing

    If it fails with "Could not create SSL/TLS secure channel", force TLS 1.2 in that window and try again:

    [Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12

    IE 11 > gear icon > Internet options > Security > Trusted sites > Sites > add the vendor's https:// address > Close. Downloads from that site then work while ESC stays on. Remove the entry when done.

    On Server 2022, use Edge.

    #Install updates with sconfig on each version

    1. Run sconfig in an elevated PowerShell window.
    2. Option 5 > A sets automatic download and install.
    3. Option 6 > 1 (All quality updates) or 2 (Recommended quality updates only).
    4. At the list, type A to install all of them, N for none or S for one.
    1. Run sconfig in an elevated PowerShell or cmd window.
    2. Option 5 > A sets automatic download and install (D is download only, M is manual).
    3. Option 6 > A searches for all updates (R searches recommended only).
    4. At the list, type A to install all, N for none or S for a single update.

    Both versions also work from Settings > Update & Security > Windows Update > Check for updates. Reboot when asked, then check again; one pass rarely installs everything.

    #Update third-party apps without winget

    Neither Server version ships winget. Update each app with its own updater or the vendor's installer, run over the existing install so it stays in its default folder.

    App How
    Firefox Menu > Help > About Firefox, or the full installer from mozilla.org
    Google Chrome Menu > Help > About Google Chrome, or the enterprise MSI from google.com/chrome
    Notepad++ ? menu > Update Notepad++, or the installer from notepad-plus-plus.org
    7-Zip, PeaZip, FileZilla Client, VS Code Installer from the vendor's site
    Adobe Reader DC Help > Check for updates

    Check the installed version afterwards:

    Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*','HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*' | Where-Object DisplayName | Select-Object DisplayName,DisplayVersion,InstallLocation | Sort-Object DisplayName

    Download pages have ad buttons

    The real download link on some vendor pages sits next to advertising buttons that install other software. Download from the vendor domain only and read the file name before running it.

    #TLS settings by version

    Server 2022 already offers TLS 1.3 and still allows TLS 1.0 and 1.1. Server 2019 tops out at TLS 1.2. The SCHANNEL script turning off TLS 1.0 and 1.1 works on both. An app setting such as FileZilla Server's minimum TLS 1.3 only works where the app itself supports 1.3; FileZilla Server 1.x ships its own TLS library, so it can on both versions.

    #Check SMB encryption ciphers on Server 2022

    Server 2022 can prefer AES-256. This is optional hardening and never seen in a key:

    Get-SmbServerConfiguration | Select-Object EncryptionCiphers

    On Server 2019 the property does not exist, which is normal.

    PreviousServer items scored in past answer keysNextStandalone server users and local policy
    SRV

    Standalone server users and local policy

    jump:srv-standalone

    Both CyberPatriot Server training keys (K5 on Server 2019, K7 on Server 2022) were standalone servers fixed with lusrmgr.msc and secpol.msc. Use this page when the domain role is 2. Most steps are the same as on Windows 11 users and password policy; the differences and the Server-only scored settings are below.

    Keep the account you are logged in with

    On Server the built-in Administrator is usually enabled and is often the logon account. Do not disable, rename or delete it unless the README says so, and know its password before you change any policy.

    Fast path

    1. Open PowerShell as administrator and confirm the role is 2 (standalone):

      (Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem).DomainRole

    2. List local users and the Administrators group, and compare with the README:

      Get-LocalUser | Format-Table Name,Enabled,PasswordRequired,PasswordExpires,LastLogon -AutoSize
Get-LocalGroupMember Administrators

    3. Remove unauthorized users and admins (how).

    4. Set the password and lockout policy:

      net accounts /minpwlen:10 /maxpwage:90 /minpwage:1 /uniquepw:24 /lockoutthreshold:10 /lockoutduration:30 /lockoutwindow:30

    5. Apply the Server security options (table and script).

    6. Turn on auditing with auditpol /set /category:* /success:enable /failure:enable.

    #Remove or demote local users

    Remove a user the README does not list:

    Remove-LocalUser -Name <username>

    Take a user out of Administrators (they stay a normal user):

    Remove-LocalGroupMember -Group Administrators -Member <username>

    GUI: lusrmgr.msc > Users > right-click > Delete, or Groups > Administrators > select the user > Remove. This is how both Server training keys did it.

    Check Remote Desktop Users, Backup Operators and Remote Management Users too:

    foreach ($g in 'Administrators','Remote Desktop Users','Backup Operators','Remote Management Users','Event Log Readers') { "=== $g ==="; Get-LocalGroupMember -Group $g -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name }

    #Set passwords and password flags

    Set the team password on one user:

    Set-LocalUser -Name <username> -Password (ConvertTo-SecureString '<team-password>' -AsPlainText -Force)

    Make the password expire and require a password:

    Set-LocalUser -Name <username> -PasswordNeverExpires $false
net user <username> /passwordreq:yes

    Get-LocalUser shows PasswordRequired False for accounts that can have a blank password. Setting a password fixes the "User X has a password" item; /passwordreq:yes stops it going blank again.

    #Clear a local account lockout

    GUI: lusrmgr.msc > Users > double-click the user > clear Account is locked out > OK. This is how the official config tested it (LockedOut false).

    PowerShell through the WinNT provider:

    $u = [ADSI]"WinNT://./<username>,user"
$u.IsAccountLocked = $false
$u.SetInfo()

    #Set the local password and lockout policy

    net accounts /minpwlen:10 /maxpwage:90 /minpwage:1 /uniquepw:24 /lockoutthreshold:10 /lockoutduration:30 /lockoutwindow:30
net accounts
    Setting Value Past key
    Minimum password length 10 or more K7, H1
    Maximum password age 90 (30-90) K5, H1
    Minimum password age 1 G3, H1
    Password history 24 Client
    Lockout threshold 10 (never below 5) K5, H1; below 5 was a K7 penalty
    Lockout duration 30 Client
    Reset counter after 30 (no longer than the duration) G3, H1

    Complexity and reversible encryption need secpol.msc or secedit (how). If net accounts reports "The parameter is incorrect", see the fix.

    #Set the server security options

    These are the security options seen on Server keys. Path: secpol.msc > Local Policies > Security Options.

    Policy Value Registry value Seen in
    Accounts: Limit local account use of blank passwords to console logon only Enabled HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa LimitBlankPasswordUse = 1 K5
    Interactive logon: Do not require CTRL+ALT+DEL Disabled HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System DisableCAD = 0 G3
    Microsoft network server: Digitally sign communications (always) Enabled HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanServer\Parameters RequireSecuritySignature = 1 G3, H1
    Microsoft network client: Digitally sign communications (always) Enabled HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanWorkstation\Parameters RequireSecuritySignature = 1 H1
    Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts Enabled ...\Control\Lsa RestrictAnonymousSAM = 1 Client
    Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares Enabled ...\Control\Lsa RestrictAnonymous = 1 H1
    Recovery console: Allow automatic administrative logon Disabled HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Setup\RecoveryConsole SecurityLevel = 0 H1
    Shutdown: Allow system to be shut down without having to log on Disabled ...\Policies\System ShutdownWithoutLogon = 0 H1
    Devices: Restrict CD-ROM access to locally logged-on user only Enabled HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon AllocateCDRoms = "1" (a string) H1
    Devices: Prevent users from installing printer drivers Enabled HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Print\Providers\LanMan Print Services\Servers AddPrinterDrivers = 1 H1
    Domain member: Digitally encrypt or sign secure channel data (always) Enabled HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Netlogon\Parameters RequireSignOrSeal = 1 Client

    The script sets every row in one paste from an elevated PowerShell window. It does three things: 1. defines a helper that creates the key if needed and writes one value, 2. writes the ten DWORD values, 3. writes AllocateCDRoms as a string.

    function SetReg($path, $name, $value, $type = 'DWord') {
  if (-not (Test-Path $path)) { New-Item -Path $path -Force | Out-Null }
  New-ItemProperty -Path $path -Name $name -Value $value -PropertyType $type -Force | Out-Null
}
$lsa = 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa'
$sys = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System'
SetReg $lsa LimitBlankPasswordUse 1
SetReg $lsa RestrictAnonymousSAM 1
SetReg $lsa RestrictAnonymous 1
SetReg $sys DisableCAD 0
SetReg $sys ShutdownWithoutLogon 0
SetReg 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanServer\Parameters' RequireSecuritySignature 1
SetReg 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\LanmanWorkstation\Parameters' RequireSecuritySignature 1
SetReg 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Setup\RecoveryConsole' SecurityLevel 0
SetReg 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Print\Providers\LanMan Print Services\Servers' AddPrinterDrivers 1
SetReg 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\Netlogon\Parameters' RequireSignOrSeal 1
SetReg 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon' AllocateCDRoms '1' 'String'

    Verify

    Close and reopen secpol.msc and read the rows above, or check one value:

    Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa' | Select-Object LimitBlankPasswordUse,RestrictAnonymous,RestrictAnonymousSAM

    The rest of the commonly scored options (UAC, LAN Manager level, anonymous access, last user name) are in Windows 11 security options and apply to Server unchanged.

    #Deny network logon to Guest

    secpol.msc > Local Policies > User Rights Assignment > Deny access to this computer from the network > Add User or Group > Guest > OK. The secedit method is in Windows 11 user rights. Never add Administrators or your own account to a Deny right.

    #Member server differences

    A member server (domain role 3) still has local users, but domain GPOs override local policy. Fix password and lockout policy in the domain's Default Domain Policy on the DC, and use gpresult /h C:\gp.html on the member to see which GPO set each value (GPO).

    PreviousServer 2019 and Server 2022 differencesNextOther roles and server apps (harden or remove)
    SRV

    Other roles and server apps (harden or remove)

    jump:srv-roles-more

    For each role or app the README requires, harden it and keep its service running. For each one it does not mention, remove it cleanly so no service or listening port is left. IIS, FTP, DNS, DHCP, SMB and RDP have their own pages: IIS, FTP, DNS and DHCP, SMB, RDP.

    Required means keep it running

    Stopping or removing a service the README lists cost 5 to 10 points in past keys. When the README says "this server hosts the company mail" or "the web app must stay up", harden it and test that it still answers.

    Fast path

    1. Open PowerShell as administrator and list installed roles, then third-party programs:

      Get-WindowsFeature | Where-Object Installed | Format-Table Name,DisplayName -AutoSize
Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*','HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\*' | Where-Object DisplayName | Select-Object DisplayName,DisplayVersion | Sort-Object DisplayName

    2. List what is listening, with the process name:

      Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen | Sort-Object LocalPort | Select-Object LocalPort,OwningProcess,@{n='Process';e={(Get-Process -Id $_.OwningProcess).ProcessName}}

    3. Find each role or app in the table below and mark it required or not from the README.

    4. Required: follow its Harden subsection. Not required: follow its Remove subsection.
    5. Run step 2 again. Ports of removed apps should be gone and required ones still listening.

    #Spot the role or app

    Role or app Feature name or installer Service names Ports
    DHCP Server DHCP DHCPServer 67 UDP
    Print Server Print-Services, Print-Server, Print-Internet, Print-LPD-Service Spooler, LPDSVC 515 (LPD), 80 (Internet Printing)
    Remote Desktop Services RDS-RD-Server, RDS-Licensing, RDS-Connection-Broker, RDS-Web-Access, RDS-Gateway TermService, TermServLicensing, Tssdis, TSGateway 3389, 443
    WSUS UpdateServices, UpdateServices-WidDB, UpdateServices-Services WsusService, W3SVC 8530, 8531
    AD Certificate Services ADCS-Cert-Authority, ADCS-Web-Enrollment CertSvc 135, 80/443 for web enrollment
    Hyper-V Hyper-V vmms none by default
    SQL Server Express Installer "Microsoft SQL Server 20xx" MSSQL$SQLEXPRESS, SQLBrowser 1433 or dynamic, 1434 UDP
    File Server Resource Manager FS-Resource-Manager SrmSvc none
    Network Policy Server NPAS IAS 1812, 1813 UDP
    Web Deploy Installer "Microsoft Web Deploy" plus Web-Mgmt-Service MsDepSvc, WMSVC 80 (/MsDeployAgentService), 8172
    SMTP Server SMTP-Server SMTPSVC 25
    SNMP SNMP-Service, SNMP-WMI-Provider SNMP, SNMPTRAP 161, 162 UDP
    OpenSSH Server Capability OpenSSH.Server~~~~0.0.1.0 sshd 22
    FileZilla Server Installer "FileZilla Server" filezilla-server (1.x) or FileZilla Server (0.9.x) 21, 990, 14148 or 14147 (admin)
    XAMPP (Apache, MariaDB, PHP) C:\xampp Apache2.4, mysql 80, 443, 3306
    Apache Tomcat Installer "Apache Tomcat" Tomcat9 (or Tomcat10) 8080, 8005, 8009
    hMailServer Installer "hMailServer" hMailServer 25, 110, 143, 587

    #DHCP Server

    #Harden DHCP when the README requires it

    Authorize the server, turn on audit logging, check scope options for a rogue DNS server or gateway and remove a WPAD option. All steps are on the DNS and DHCP page. Keep DHCPServer at Automatic; one team-made key listed DHCP, DNS and Event Log as services that had to stay running.

    #Remove DHCP cleanly

    On a domain member or DC, take it out of AD first, then remove the role:

    Remove-DhcpServerInDC -DnsName "<hostname>" -IPAddress <ip-address>
Uninstall-WindowsFeature DHCP -IncludeManagementTools

    On a standalone server skip the first line. Check with Get-Service DHCPServer, which should then error with "Cannot find any service".

    #Print Server

    #Harden printing when the README requires it

    1. Keep Spooler running and Automatic.

    2. Let only admins install printer drivers (Point and Print fix for PrintNightmare) from an elevated PowerShell window:

      $k = 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Printers\PointAndPrint'
if (-not (Test-Path $k)) { New-Item $k -Force | Out-Null }
New-ItemProperty $k -Name RestrictDriverInstallationToAdministrators -Value 1 -PropertyType DWord -Force | Out-Null

    3. If NoWarningNoElevationOnInstall or UpdatePromptSettings exist in that key with value 1, set them to 0. A 1 there allows silent driver installs by any user.

    4. Enable the security option Devices: Prevent users from installing printer drivers (table), scored in a Hivestorm Server key.

    5. Review shared printers, drivers and ports. A port that points at a file path or script is suspicious:

      Get-Printer | Select-Object Name,ShareName,Shared,DriverName,PortName
Get-PrinterPort | Select-Object Name,Description,PrinterHostAddress

    6. Remove Internet Printing and LPD unless the README names them: Uninstall-WindowsFeature Print-Internet,Print-LPD-Service.

    #Remove the print server role cleanly

    Uninstall-WindowsFeature Print-Services
Stop-Service Spooler -Force
Set-Service Spooler -StartupType Disabled

    Disable Spooler only when nothing on the server needs to print. The print$ share disappears with the role.

    #Remote Desktop Services

    Remote Desktop for administration (TermService, port 3389) works without this role. The role adds a Session Host for many users, a Gateway, Web Access and Licensing. RDP hardening itself is on the RDP page.

    #Harden RDS when the README requires it

    • RD Web Access is an IIS site at /RDWeb. Keep it HTTPS only (IIS SSL).
    • RD Gateway: run tsgateway.msc (RD Gateway Manager). In the connection authorization policy (CAP) and resource authorization policy (RAP), allow only the README groups.
    • Session collections: Server Manager > Remote Desktop Services > Collections > Tasks > Edit Properties > User Groups lists who may connect. Remove Domain Users or Everyone if the README names a smaller group.
    • Under Security in the same dialog, set Security Layer to SSL and require NLA.

    #Remove RDS cleanly

    Remove only the role services that are installed, then reboot:

    Get-WindowsFeature RDS-* | Where-Object Installed | Uninstall-WindowsFeature

    This does not turn off admin RDP. If RDP itself is not required, also follow Turn off Remote Desktop.

    #WSUS

    #Harden WSUS when the README requires it

    • WSUS Administrators (local group, or domain group on a DC) should hold only README admins.
    • The WSUS Administration IIS site listens on 8530 (HTTP) and 8531 (HTTPS). The README may ask for SSL; that needs a certificate on the site and wsusutil configuressl <hostname> from C:\Program Files\Update Services\Tools.
    • Clients find WSUS through the WUServer policy. If that points anywhere other than this server, it is planted (update policies).

    #Remove WSUS cleanly

    Get-WindowsFeature UpdateServices* | Where-Object Installed | Uninstall-WindowsFeature
Uninstall-WindowsFeature Windows-Internal-Database

    Reboot, then confirm the WSUS Administration site is gone with Get-Website. Removing WSUS leaves any WUServer policy in place, so check the update policies afterwards.

    #AD Certificate Services

    Removing a CA on a DC can break LDAPS and smart cards

    If the README does not mention certificates, prefer hardening over removal unless the role is clearly planted. Certificates the CA already issued stop validating once it is gone.

    #Harden the certificate authority

    1. Check the dangerous EditFlags setting (ESC6). If the output lists EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2, any requester can put any name in a certificate:

      certutil -getreg policy\EditFlags

    2. Turn it off and restart the CA:

      certutil -setreg policy\EditFlags -EDITF_ATTRIBUTESUBJECTALTNAME2
net stop certsvc
net start certsvc

    3. On a DC, list templates where the requester supplies the subject name (ESC1). A template on this list that is also published, allows Client Authentication and gives Domain Users enroll rights is a domain takeover:

      $cfg = (Get-ADRootDSE).configurationNamingContext
Get-ADObject -SearchBase "CN=Certificate Templates,CN=Public Key Services,CN=Services,$cfg" -Filter * -Properties msPKI-Certificate-Name-Flag,pKIExtendedKeyUsage | Where-Object { $_.'msPKI-Certificate-Name-Flag' -band 1 } | Select-Object Name,@{n='EKU';e={$_.pKIExtendedKeyUsage -join ', '}}

    4. List the templates the CA publishes:

      certutil -CATemplates

    5. Stop publishing a template the README does not need:

      certutil -SetCATemplates -<template-name>

    6. In certsrv.msc > right-click the CA > Properties > Security, only Administrators, Domain Admins and Enterprise Admins should have Manage CA or Issue and Manage Certificates.

    7. If Web Enrollment (/certsrv) is installed and not required, remove it (ESC8 relay target): Uninstall-AdcsWebEnrollment -Force, then Uninstall-WindowsFeature ADCS-Web-Enrollment.

    Client Authentication shows in the EKU column as 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.2. Template enrollment rights are on certtmpl.msc > template > Properties > Security.

    #Remove AD CS cleanly

    Unconfigure the CA, then remove the features:

    Uninstall-AdcsCertificationAuthority -Force
Get-WindowsFeature ADCS-* | Where-Object Installed | Uninstall-WindowsFeature

    #Hyper-V

    #Harden Hyper-V when the README requires it

    • Hyper-V Administrators (Builtin) should be empty or hold README admins only. Members control every VM.
    • List VMs and their state with Get-VM. A VM the README does not mention may be planted, but answer any Forensics Question about it first.
    • Virtual switches: Get-VMSwitch. An External switch bridges VMs to the real network.

    #Remove Hyper-V cleanly

    Uninstall-WindowsFeature Hyper-V,Hyper-V-PowerShell,Hyper-V-Tools

    It needs a reboot. On a competition VM the role usually cannot run anyway, so an installed but unused Hyper-V is a removal candidate when the README does not mention it.

    #SQL Server Express

    Find the instance name first. The service is MSSQL$<sql-instance>, usually MSSQL$SQLEXPRESS:

    Get-Service *SQL* | Format-Table Name,DisplayName,Status,StartType -AutoSize

    #Harden SQL Server when the README requires it

    All commands use Windows authentication (-E) from an elevated PowerShell window. Replace <sql-instance> with the instance name (for example SQLEXPRESS).

    1. List SQL logins, whether they are disabled and whether the password policy applies:

      sqlcmd -S .\<sql-instance> -E -Q "SELECT name, is_disabled, is_policy_checked, is_expiration_checked FROM sys.sql_logins"

    2. List members of the sysadmin role:

      sqlcmd -S .\<sql-instance> -E -Q "SELECT p.name FROM sys.server_role_members m JOIN sys.server_principals r ON m.role_principal_id = r.principal_id JOIN sys.server_principals p ON m.member_principal_id = p.principal_id WHERE r.name = 'sysadmin'"

    3. Remove a login the README does not authorize from sysadmin:

      sqlcmd -S .\<sql-instance> -E -Q "ALTER SERVER ROLE sysadmin DROP MEMBER [<sql-login>]"

    4. Disable sa (unless the README app logs in as sa; then give it a strong password instead):

      sqlcmd -S .\<sql-instance> -E -Q "ALTER LOGIN [sa] DISABLE"

    5. Set a strong password with the Windows policy enforced on a SQL login:

      sqlcmd -S .\<sql-instance> -E -Q "ALTER LOGIN [<sql-login>] WITH PASSWORD = '<team-password>', CHECK_POLICY = ON"

    6. Turn off xp_cmdshell, which runs operating system commands from SQL:

      sqlcmd -S .\<sql-instance> -E -Q "EXEC sp_configure 'show advanced options', 1; RECONFIGURE; EXEC sp_configure 'xp_cmdshell', 0; RECONFIGURE;"

    7. If only local apps use the database, disable the TCP/IP protocol in SQL Server Configuration Manager > SQL Server Network Configuration and stop SQL Server Browser:

      Stop-Service SQLBrowser
Set-Service SQLBrowser -StartupType Disabled

    Windows-only authentication is stronger than mixed mode. The value is LoginMode (1 Windows only, 2 mixed) under HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Microsoft SQL Server\<instance-id>\MSSQLServer, where <instance-id> looks like MSSQL15.SQLEXPRESS. Find it with:

    Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Microsoft SQL Server\Instance Names\SQL'

    Change it only if no README app logs in with a SQL login, then restart with Restart-Service 'MSSQL$<sql-instance>'.

    #Remove SQL Server Express cleanly

    appwiz.cpl > Microsoft SQL Server 20xx (64-bit) > Uninstall/Change > Remove > pick the instance > select all features > Remove. Stop the services first if the wizard complains. Leave the "Microsoft ODBC Driver" and "Visual C++" entries; other apps share them.

    #File Server Resource Manager

    #Harden FSRM when the README requires it

    • File screens: Get-FsrmFileScreen | Select-Object Path,Template,Active. Active False means a passive screen that only warns. Set a README-required screen to active with Set-FsrmFileScreen -Path "<path>" -Active.

    • Command notifications run a program as LocalSystem whenever a quota or screen fires, which makes them a quiet persistence spot. List them:

      Get-FsrmFileScreen | ForEach-Object { $_.Notification } | Where-Object Type -eq 'Command' | Select-Object Command,CommandParameters,SecurityLevel
Get-FsrmQuota | ForEach-Object { $_.Threshold.Action } | Where-Object Type -eq 'Command' | Select-Object Command,CommandParameters

    • A README file screen, for example blocking audio and video in a share, is in SMB file screens.

    #Remove FSRM cleanly

    Uninstall-WindowsFeature FS-Resource-Manager

    #Network Policy Server

    #Harden NPS when the README requires it

    1. Run nps.msc. Under RADIUS Clients and Servers > RADIUS Clients, remove clients the README does not list and set long shared secrets.
    2. Under Policies > Network Policies, look for a policy at the top that grants access to everyone, or one that allows PAP or CHAP (Constraints > Authentication Methods). Disable it or remove the weak methods.
    3. Turn on logging: Accounting > Configure Accounting.

    List clients from PowerShell:

    Get-NpsRadiusClient | Select-Object Name,Address,Enabled

    #Remove NPS cleanly

    Uninstall-WindowsFeature NPAS -IncludeManagementTools

    #Web Deploy and IIS remote management

    Web Deploy publishes code to IIS from another machine. It installs the Web Deployment Agent Service (MsDepSvc) and often uses the IIS Web Management Service (WMSVC) on port 8172.

    #Harden Web Deploy when the README requires it

    • In inetmgr > server node > Management Service, allow only Windows credentials, keep the SSL certificate on port 8172, and add IP restrictions to the README's admin addresses.
    • In IIS Manager Permissions on each site, list only README users.
    • Keep MsDepSvc stopped if publishing goes through WMSVC.

    #Remove Web Deploy cleanly

    Stop-Service MsDepSvc,WMSVC -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Set-Service MsDepSvc -StartupType Disabled -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Uninstall-WindowsFeature Web-Mgmt-Service

    Then appwiz.cpl > Microsoft Web Deploy > Uninstall.

    #SMTP Server

    #Harden SMTP when the README requires it

    Open Internet Information Services (IIS) 6.0 Manager > SMTP Virtual Server > Properties:

    • Access > Relay: Only the list below, with the list empty or only README hosts. Leave Allow all computers which successfully authenticate to relay checked only if the README needs authenticated relay.
    • Access > Authentication: clear Anonymous access if only internal users send mail.
    • Access > Connection: restrict to README subnets if given.
    • General > Enable logging.

    #Remove SMTP cleanly

    Stop-Service SMTPSVC -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Uninstall-WindowsFeature SMTP-Server

    #SNMP service

    Scored in a Hivestorm Server key as "SNMP service has been stopped and disabled" and "SNMP Trap service has been stopped and disabled".

    #Harden SNMP when the README requires it

    List community strings and rights (4 read only, 8 read write, 16 read create):

    Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\SNMP\Parameters\ValidCommunities'
Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\SNMP\Parameters\PermittedManagers'

    Remove the default public and any write community, then restart:

    Remove-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\SNMP\Parameters\ValidCommunities' -Name public -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Restart-Service SNMP

    GUI: services.msc > SNMP Service > Properties > Security tab: community names READ ONLY, and Accept SNMP packets from these hosts with only the README manager.

    #Remove SNMP cleanly

    Stop-Service SNMP,SNMPTRAP -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Set-Service SNMPTRAP -StartupType Disabled -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Uninstall-WindowsFeature SNMP-Service,SNMP-WMI-Provider

    #Small services seen in past keys

    Scoring wording Service name Feature to remove Seen in
    Simple TCP/IP Services has been stopped and disabled simptcp Simple-TCPIP K7, Client
    Net.Tcp Port Sharing Service has been stopped and disabled NetTcpPortSharing Leave the .NET feature; disable the service H1, Client
    World Wide Web Publishing service has been stopped and disabled W3SVC Web-Server if no site is required Client
    FTP service has been stopped and disabled ftpsvc Web-Ftp-Server K5, H1
    Telnet service stopped and disabled TlntSvr Not on 2019 or 2022; uninstall the third-party server G3
    Remote Registry service has been stopped and disabled RemoteRegistry none Client
    SNMP Trap service has been stopped and disabled SNMPTRAP SNMP-Service H1

    Stop and disable each one the README does not need in one paste. Edit the list first:

    $svc = 'simptcp','NetTcpPortSharing','RemoteRegistry','SNMPTRAP','TlntSvr'
foreach ($s in $svc) { if (Get-Service $s -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { Stop-Service $s -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; Set-Service $s -StartupType Disabled; Get-Service $s | Select-Object Name,Status,StartType } }

    The scoring check passes on Stopped plus Disabled. Removing the feature also passes.

    #OpenSSH Server

    #Harden OpenSSH when the README requires it

    The config is C:\ProgramData\ssh\sshd_config. Set or add these lines (keep PasswordAuthentication yes if README users log in with passwords):

    PermitEmptyPasswords no
MaxAuthTries 4
LoginGraceTime 60
AllowGroups administrators

    Replace administrators in AllowGroups with the README group, or leave the line out if every user may connect. Keys for admins are read from C:\ProgramData\ssh\administrators_authorized_keys (the Match Group administrators block at the end of the file). A key in that file, or in a user's C:\Users\<username>\.ssh\authorized_keys, that the README does not explain is a backdoor:

    Get-Content C:\ProgramData\ssh\administrators_authorized_keys -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Get-ChildItem C:\Users\*\.ssh\authorized_keys -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object FullName,LastWriteTime

    Restart to apply: Restart-Service sshd.

    #Remove OpenSSH Server cleanly

    Stop-Service sshd -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Remove-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Server~~~~0.0.1.0

    If C:\Program Files\OpenSSH exists with its own sshd.exe, it was installed from the GitHub package; run uninstall-sshd.ps1 in that folder, then delete it.

    #FileZilla Server

    Two versions exist. FileZilla Server 1.x (current) runs the service filezilla-server, keeps its config in C:\ProgramData\filezilla-server (settings.xml, users.xml, groups.xml) and has its admin interface on port 14148. FileZilla Server 0.9.x runs the service FileZilla Server, keeps FileZilla Server.xml in its install folder and uses admin port 14147.

    #Harden FileZilla Server when the README requires it

    Open the FileZilla Server administration interface (Start > FileZilla Server, connect to localhost).

    1. Server > Configure > Rights management > Users: delete or disable the anonymous user and every user the README does not list. Each remaining user needs a password (Authentication: Require a password to log in).
    2. Each user's Mount points: only the folders the README names, with write access only where uploads are required.
    3. Server > Configure > Server listeners: set the Protocol of every listener to Require explicit FTP over TLS.
    4. Server > Configure > Protocols settings > FTP and FTP over TLS (FTPS) > Connection security: set the minimum allowed TLS version to 1.3 (a team-made practice key scored exactly this).
    5. Server > Configure > Protocols settings > Autobanner: enable it, for example ban for 1 hour after 5 failed logins within 100 seconds.
    6. Server > Configure > Administration: set a strong admin password and keep the admin interface bound to 127.0.0.1 only.
    7. Server > Configure > Logging: include more detail and log to a file.

    Check the update item too: Help > Check for updates, or reinstall the newest version over the old one.

    #Remove FileZilla Server cleanly

    Stop the service, then uninstall from appwiz.cpl > FileZilla Server:

    Get-Service *filezilla* | Stop-Service -Force

    Delete the leftover C:\ProgramData\filezilla-server folder only after any Forensics Question about FTP users is answered.

    #Apache, XAMPP and PHP on Windows

    XAMPP installs Apache, MariaDB and PHP under C:\xampp, controlled by C:\xampp\xampp-control.exe. Services exist only if someone ticked Service in the control panel (Apache2.4 and mysql).

    #Harden Apache, PHP and MariaDB when the README requires them

    1. Find where the server version settings are set; the last line read wins:

      Select-String -Path C:\xampp\apache\conf\httpd.conf,C:\xampp\apache\conf\extra\*.conf -Pattern '^\s*(ServerTokens|ServerSignature|TraceEnable|Options)'

    2. In C:\xampp\apache\conf\extra\httpd-default.conf (and anywhere step 1 found a weaker value) set:

      ServerTokens Prod
ServerSignature Off
TraceEnable Off

    3. In httpd.conf, in the <Directory "C:/xampp/htdocs"> block, remove Indexes from the Options line so folders are not listed.

    4. In C:\xampp\apache\conf\extra\httpd-xampp.conf, the block for phpmyadmin and the XAMPP pages must say Require local. Require all granted there exposes the database admin page.

    5. In C:\xampp\php\php.ini set:

      expose_php = Off
display_errors = Off
display_startup_errors = Off
log_errors = On
allow_url_include = Off
disable_functions = exec,passthru,shell_exec,system,proc_open,popen

    6. Give the database root user a password. In a fresh XAMPP it has none. From cmd:

      C:\xampp\mysql\bin\mysql.exe -u root -p -e "ALTER USER 'root'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY '<team-password>';"

      Press Enter at the password prompt if it was blank. 7. Make phpMyAdmin ask for a login. In C:\xampp\phpMyAdmin\config.inc.php change the auth type line and delete the stored password line:

      $cfg['Servers'][$i]['auth_type'] = 'cookie';

    7. Delete phpinfo.php, info.php and test pages in C:\xampp\htdocs, and hunt PHP web shells with the IIS web shell search pointed at C:\xampp\htdocs.

    8. Restart Apache and MySQL from the XAMPP Control Panel (or Restart-Service Apache2.4,mysql if they run as services) and load the site to confirm it works.

    PHP on IIS uses the same php.ini settings. Find the file IIS loads through the FastCGI path:

    Get-WebConfiguration -PSPath 'MACHINE/WEBROOT/APPHOST' -Filter system.webServer/fastCgi/application | Select-Object fullPath

    php.ini sits in the same folder as that php-cgi.exe. Run iisreset after editing.

    #Remove XAMPP cleanly

    Stop everything in the XAMPP Control Panel (or stop the services), then run C:\xampp\uninstall.exe. Confirm nothing listens on 80, 443 or 3306 afterwards. If the README needs IIS on port 80, a leftover Apache blocks it.

    #Apache Tomcat

    Default folder: C:\Program Files\Apache Software Foundation\Tomcat 9.0 (the number follows the version). Service: Tomcat9.

    #Harden Tomcat when the README requires it

    1. Open conf\tomcat-users.xml. Remove users the README does not list, and any user with a weak password and the manager-gui, manager-script or admin-gui role. A remaining admin line looks like:

      <user username="<username>" password="<team-password>" roles="manager-gui"/>

    2. If nobody needs the web manager, delete or move the webapps\manager and webapps\host-manager folders. If it is needed, keep the RemoteAddrValve in webapps\manager\META-INF\context.xml that limits it to 127.0.0.1.

    3. In conf\server.xml, disable the shutdown port by setting port="-1" on the <Server> element:

      <Server port="-1" shutdown="SHUTDOWN">

    4. In the same file, remove or comment out any <Connector protocol="AJP/1.3" ...> that is active. It is off by default since 9.0.31.

    5. In conf\web.xml, the DefaultServlet listings parameter must be false.
    6. Delete the webapps\examples and webapps\docs folders.
    7. Restart: Restart-Service Tomcat9.

    #Remove Tomcat cleanly

    Stop the service, then run Uninstall.exe in the Tomcat folder (or appwiz.cpl > Apache Tomcat). Check that nothing listens on 8080, 8005 or 8009.

    #hMailServer

    #Harden hMailServer when the README requires it

    Open hMailServer Administrator and connect to localhost.

    1. Settings > Advanced > IP Ranges > Internet: clear External to external e-mail addresses under Allow deliveries from, and require SMTP authentication for Local to external and External to external. This closes an open relay.
    2. Settings > Advanced > Auto-ban: Enabled.
    3. Settings > Protocols: turn off POP3 or IMAP if the README does not use them.
    4. Settings > Advanced > SSL certificates and TCP/IP ports: add SSL or STARTTLS on the ports the README uses.
    5. Domains > the domain > Accounts: remove accounts for users the README does not list and set strong passwords.
    6. Change the administrator password (Settings > Advanced). The hash is stored as AdministratorPassword in hMailServer.ini in the program's Bin folder.
    7. Turn on logging: Settings > Logging.

    #Remove hMailServer cleanly

    Stop-Service hMailServer -Force

    Then appwiz.cpl > hMailServer > Uninstall. Check that ports 25, 110 and 143 are closed.

    #Other remote tools and servers

    VNC servers (TightVNC, UltraVNC, RealVNC), TeamViewer, AnyDesk, Plex Media Server, OpenTFTP and Home Web Server are third-party programs. Remove them from appwiz.cpl unless the README needs them, then confirm their service and port are gone (remote tools, software).

    PreviousStandalone server users and local policyNextAD backdoors and persistence hunting
    SRV

    AD backdoors and persistence hunting

    jump:srv-ad-attacks

    These are the tricks a hard image uses to keep admin access after you clean the obvious users. None was named in a past CyberPatriot key, so treat them as nationals-level extras: do the AD users, GPO and AD hardening pages first.

    Answer AD Forensics Questions before removing anything

    A question may ask which account has replication rights, what a logon script downloads or which GPO creates a task. Read and record first, then fix. Never remove rights from built-in principals (Domain Controllers, Enterprise Domain Controllers, Administrators, SYSTEM).

    Fast path

    1. Open PowerShell as administrator on the DC.
    2. Paste the read-only sweep. It writes ad_backdoors.txt to the desktop and opens it.
    3. For each non-empty header, follow the matching section below.

    4. Remove a planted right with dsacls (example for the domain root):

      dsacls (Get-ADDomain).DistinguishedName /R "<domain-netbios>\<username>"

    5. After cleaning AdminSDHolder, force SDProp so admin objects get the clean permissions (how).

    6. Run dcdiag /q to confirm nothing broke.

    #Run the AD backdoor sweep

    The script changes nothing. It does this, in order:

    1. Creates ad_backdoors.txt on the desktop and a helper T that writes one check under a ===== header, catching errors so every check runs.
    2. Defines $ok, the built-in principals that normally hold rights, and a helper Risky that lists other principals with write, owner, permission or extended rights on one AD object.
    3. Lists who holds replication (DCSync) rights on the domain.
    4. Lists unexpected rights on the domain root, AdminSDHolder, Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, Builtin Administrators, the Administrator account and the Domain Controllers OU.
    5. Lists groups nested in privileged groups, SID history, every kind of delegation, SPNs, preauth and password-not-required flags, shadow credentials, the newest and most recently changed accounts, and krbtgt's password age.
    6. Lists trusts, GPO edit rights held by non-admins, GPO preference and script files in SYSVOL, NETLOGON scripts, and the LSA registry values.
    Import-Module ActiveDirectory
$out = Join-Path ([Environment]::GetFolderPath('Desktop')) 'ad_backdoors.txt'
"AD backdoor sweep $(Get-Date)" | Out-File $out -Encoding utf8
function T([string]$name, [scriptblock]$sb) { "`r`n===== $name =====" | Out-File $out -Append -Encoding utf8; try { & $sb 2>&1 | Format-Table -AutoSize -Wrap | Out-String -Width 4096 | Out-File $out -Append -Encoding utf8 } catch { "ERROR: $($_.Exception.Message)" | Out-File $out -Append -Encoding utf8 } }
$dom = Get-ADDomain
$dn = $dom.DistinguishedName
$ok = 'NT AUTHORITY\\|BUILTIN\\|\\(Domain Admins|Enterprise Admins|Schema Admins|Domain Controllers|Enterprise Read-only Domain Controllers|Read-only Domain Controllers|Cloneable Domain Controllers|Key Admins|Enterprise Key Admins|Cert Publishers)$|^Everyone$|^CREATOR OWNER$'
function Risky([string]$path) { (Get-Acl "AD:$path").Access | Where-Object { $_.AccessControlType -eq 'Allow' -and $_.IdentityReference.Value -notmatch $ok -and $_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericAll|GenericWrite|WriteDacl|WriteOwner|WriteProperty|ExtendedRight' } | Select-Object @{n='Object';e={$path.Split(',')[0]}},IdentityReference,ActiveDirectoryRights,ObjectType }
$rep = '1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2','1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2','89e95b76-444d-4c62-991a-0facbeda640c'
T 'DCSync rights on the domain' { (Get-Acl "AD:$dn").Access | Where-Object { $rep -contains $_.ObjectType.ToString() } | Select-Object IdentityReference,ObjectType }
T 'Unexpected rights on sensitive objects' { foreach ($o in @($dn, "CN=AdminSDHolder,CN=System,$dn", (Get-ADGroup 'Domain Admins').DistinguishedName, (Get-ADGroup 'Enterprise Admins').DistinguishedName, (Get-ADGroup 'Administrators').DistinguishedName, (Get-ADUser 'Administrator').DistinguishedName, $dom.DomainControllersContainer)) { Risky $o } }
T 'Groups nested in privileged groups' { foreach ($g in 'Domain Admins','Enterprise Admins','Schema Admins','Administrators','Account Operators','Backup Operators','Server Operators','Print Operators','DnsAdmins','Group Policy Creator Owners') { Get-ADGroupMember $g -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object objectClass -eq 'group' | Select-Object @{n='Parent';e={$g}},SamAccountName } }
T 'SID history' { Get-ADObject -LDAPFilter '(sIDHistory=*)' -Properties sIDHistory,samAccountName | ForEach-Object { foreach ($s in $_.sIDHistory) { [pscustomobject]@{Account=$_.samAccountName; SidHistory=$s.Value; SameDomain=$s.Value.StartsWith($dom.DomainSID.Value)} } } }
T 'Unconstrained delegation (DCs are normal)' { Get-ADObject -LDAPFilter '(userAccountControl:1.2.840.113556.1.4.803:=524288)' | Select-Object Name,ObjectClass }
T 'Constrained delegation targets' { Get-ADObject -LDAPFilter '(msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo=*)' -Properties msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo | Select-Object Name,ObjectClass,@{n='DelegatesTo';e={$_.'msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo' -join '; '}} }
T 'Protocol transition (TrustedToAuthForDelegation)' { Get-ADObject -LDAPFilter '(userAccountControl:1.2.840.113556.1.4.803:=16777216)' | Select-Object Name,ObjectClass }
T 'Resource-based delegation' { Get-ADComputer -Filter * -Properties PrincipalsAllowedToDelegateToAccount | Where-Object PrincipalsAllowedToDelegateToAccount | Select-Object Name,@{n='Allowed';e={$_.PrincipalsAllowedToDelegateToAccount -join '; '}} }
T 'Users with SPNs (krbtgt is normal)' { Get-ADUser -LDAPFilter '(servicePrincipalName=*)' -Properties servicePrincipalName,adminCount | Select-Object SamAccountName,adminCount,@{n='SPN';e={$_.servicePrincipalName -join '; '}} }
T 'Kerberos preauth not required (AS-REP)' { Get-ADUser -LDAPFilter '(userAccountControl:1.2.840.113556.1.4.803:=4194304)' | Select-Object SamAccountName,Enabled }
T 'Password not required' { Get-ADUser -LDAPFilter '(userAccountControl:1.2.840.113556.1.4.803:=32)' | Select-Object SamAccountName,Enabled }
T 'Shadow credentials (msDS-KeyCredentialLink)' { Get-ADObject -LDAPFilter '(msDS-KeyCredentialLink=*)' | Select-Object Name,ObjectClass }
T 'Newest 15 users and groups' { Get-ADObject -LDAPFilter '(|(objectClass=user)(objectClass=group))' -Properties whenCreated,samAccountName | Sort-Object whenCreated -Descending | Select-Object -First 15 samAccountName,ObjectClass,whenCreated }
T 'Most recently changed 25 objects' { Get-ADObject -Filter * -Properties whenChanged | Sort-Object whenChanged -Descending | Select-Object -First 25 Name,ObjectClass,whenChanged }
T 'krbtgt password last set' { Get-ADUser krbtgt -Properties PasswordLastSet | Select-Object Name,PasswordLastSet }
T 'Trusts' { Get-ADTrust -Filter * | Select-Object Name,Direction,TrustType,SIDFilteringQuarantined }
T 'GPO edit rights outside the defaults' { Get-GPO -All | ForEach-Object { $g = $_.DisplayName; Get-GPPermission -Guid $_.Id -All | Where-Object { $_.Permission -in 'GpoEdit','GpoEditDeleteModifySecurity','GpoCustom' -and $_.Trustee.Name -notin 'Domain Admins','Enterprise Admins','SYSTEM','ENTERPRISE DOMAIN CONTROLLERS','CREATOR OWNER' } | Select-Object @{n='GPO';e={$g}},@{n='Trustee';e={$_.Trustee.Name}},Permission } }
$pol = "C:\Windows\SYSVOL\sysvol\$($dom.DNSRoot)\Policies"
T 'GPO preference, script and security template files' { Get-ChildItem $pol -Recurse -File -Force -Include ScheduledTasks.xml,Groups.xml,Registry.xml,Services.xml,Files.xml,scripts.ini,psscripts.ini,GptTmpl.inf -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object FullName,LastWriteTime }
T 'GPO script folders with files' { Get-ChildItem $pol -Recurse -File -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.DirectoryName -match '\\Scripts\\(Startup|Shutdown|Logon|Logoff)$' } | Select-Object FullName,LastWriteTime }
T 'NETLOGON scripts' { Get-ChildItem "C:\Windows\SYSVOL\sysvol\$($dom.DNSRoot)\scripts" -Recurse -File -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object FullName,Length,LastWriteTime }
T 'Users with a logon script' { Get-ADUser -LDAPFilter '(scriptPath=*)' -Properties scriptPath | Select-Object SamAccountName,scriptPath }
T 'LSA packages and DSRM' { Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa' | Select-Object 'Authentication Packages','Notification Packages','Security Packages',RunAsPPL,DsrmAdminLogonBehavior }
T 'LSA OSConfig security packages' { Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\OSConfig' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object 'Security Packages' }
"`r`nDone." | Out-File $out -Append -Encoding utf8
notepad $out

    Reading the output

    An empty header means nothing suspicious was found. The ObjectType column under Unexpected rights is a GUID: 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 means every property or right, which is the worst case.

    #Rogue admins through nested groups

    Get-ADGroupMember -Recursive shows every user who ends up in a group, but not the group that carries them. Find groups placed inside privileged groups:

    Get-ADGroupMember "Domain Admins" | Select-Object SamAccountName,objectClass
Get-ADGroupMember "Administrators" | Select-Object SamAccountName,objectClass

    On a fresh domain, Builtin Administrators holds Administrator, Domain Admins and Enterprise Admins, and Domain Admins holds only users. Any other group in those lists makes all its members admins. Remove the nested group, not its members:

    Remove-ADGroupMember -Identity "Domain Admins" -Members "<groupname>" -Confirm:$false

    A second way in is a permission instead of membership: a user with GenericAll, GenericWrite or WriteProperty on the Domain Admins group can add themselves at any time. The sweep lists these under Unexpected rights. Remove every right that one user holds on the group:

    dsacls (Get-ADGroup "Domain Admins").DistinguishedName /R "<domain-netbios>\<username>"

    Domain Admins is protected by AdminSDHolder, so also clean AdminSDHolder or the right comes back within the hour.

    #Clean AdminSDHolder and force SDProp

    Every 60 minutes, SDProp on the PDC emulator copies the permissions of CN=AdminSDHolder,CN=System,<domain-dn> onto every protected account and group (Administrators, Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, Schema Admins, Account, Backup, Server and Print Operators, Administrator, krbtgt and others). A right planted there turns back on by itself. Find it with the sweep or the AdminSDHolder check.

    1. Remove every right the planted user or group holds on AdminSDHolder:

      dsacls "CN=AdminSDHolder,CN=System,$((Get-ADDomain).DistinguishedName)" /R "<domain-netbios>\<username>"

    2. Make SDProp run now instead of within the hour:

      $root = [ADSI]'LDAP://RootDSE'
$root.Put('runProtectAdminGroupsTask', 1)
$root.SetInfo()

    3. After a minute, run the sweep again. The user should be gone from AdminSDHolder, Domain Admins and Administrator.

    GUI: dsa.msc with View > Advanced Features > System > AdminSDHolder > Properties > Security > Advanced > select the entry > Remove.

    #DCSync rights on the domain

    An account with both Replicating Directory Changes and Replicating Directory Changes All on the domain object can pull every password hash, including krbtgt, from anywhere on the network. The three rights have fixed GUIDs:

    Right GUID
    Replicating Directory Changes 1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2
    Replicating Directory Changes All 1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2
    Replicating Directory Changes In Filtered Set 89e95b76-444d-4c62-991a-0facbeda640c

    Expected holders: BUILTIN\Administrators, Domain Controllers, ENTERPRISE DOMAIN CONTROLLERS, Enterprise Read-only Domain Controllers and Read-only Domain Controllers. A named user, Domain Users or Everyone is a backdoor, and so is anyone holding GenericAll or WriteDacl on the domain root (they can grant themselves DCSync). Check:

    $dn = (Get-ADDomain).DistinguishedName
(Get-Acl "AD:$dn").Access | Where-Object { $_.ObjectType.ToString() -in '1131f6aa-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2','1131f6ad-9c07-11d1-f79f-00c04fc2dcd2','89e95b76-444d-4c62-991a-0facbeda640c' } | Select-Object IdentityReference,ObjectType

    Remove all rights of that principal on the domain root:

    dsacls (Get-ADDomain).DistinguishedName /R "<domain-netbios>\<username>"

    dsacls /R removes everything that principal holds on the object

    Use it only for a principal that should have no explicit rights there (a planted user or group). Never run it for Administrators, Domain Controllers or ENTERPRISE DOMAIN CONTROLLERS.

    Security event 4662 with one of these GUIDs from an account that is not a DC means DCSync actually ran (events).

    #SID history injection

    SID history allows a migrated account to keep its old SID. A user whose SID history holds a Domain Admins SID (ending in -512), Enterprise Admins (-519) or Administrator (-500) is an admin everywhere while appearing in no group. In a lab domain with no migrations, any SID history is planted, and SID history from the same domain is always malicious.

    $domSid = (Get-ADDomain).DomainSID.Value
Get-ADObject -LDAPFilter '(sIDHistory=*)' -Properties sIDHistory,samAccountName | ForEach-Object { foreach ($s in $_.sIDHistory) { [pscustomobject]@{Account=$_.samAccountName; SidHistory=$s.Value; SameDomain=$s.Value.StartsWith($domSid)} } }

    Remove one value (copy the SID from the output):

    Set-ADUser <username> -Remove @{sIDHistory='<sid>'}

    Remove all SID history from one user:

    Get-ADUser <username> -Properties sIDHistory | ForEach-Object { Set-ADUser $_ -Remove @{sIDHistory=$_.sIDHistory.Value} }

    #Delegation backdoors

    Kind How to spot Normal Fix
    Unconstrained userAccountControl flag 524288 (TrustedForDelegation) DCs only Set-ADAccountControl <username> -TrustedForDelegation $false
    Constrained msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo has values Nothing in a lab Set-ADUser <username> -Clear msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo (use Set-ADComputer for a computer)
    Protocol transition flag 16777216 (TrustedToAuthForDelegation) Nothing in a lab Set-ADAccountControl <username> -TrustedToAuthForDelegation $false
    Resource-based PrincipalsAllowedToDelegateToAccount on a computer Nothing in a lab Set-ADComputer <hostname> -PrincipalsAllowedToDelegateToAccount $null

    Constrained delegation to ldap/, cifs/ or host/ on the DC allows that account to impersonate a Domain Admin to the DC. Resource-based delegation set on the DC's own computer object does the same. The sweep lists all four. Unconstrained delegation on the DC itself is required; never clear it there (details).

    #Kerberoastable and AS-REP roastable accounts

    • A user with an SPN can have a service ticket requested by any domain user and cracked offline. An SPN on an admin account (adminCount 1 in the sweep) is the worst case: remove the SPN unless the README names that service (how), and give every remaining service account a long password.
    • A user with Do not require Kerberos preauthentication can be attacked the same way without any credentials. Clear the flag (how).

    List SPNs on accounts that are or were admins:

    Get-ADUser -LDAPFilter '(&(servicePrincipalName=*)(adminCount=1))' -Properties servicePrincipalName | Where-Object SamAccountName -ne 'krbtgt' | Select-Object SamAccountName,@{n='SPN';e={$_.servicePrincipalName -join '; '}}

    #Shadow credentials

    An attacker who can write msDS-KeyCredentialLink on an account adds a key and then logs on as that account with a certificate, without its password. In a lab without Windows Hello for Business the attribute should be empty everywhere. Clear it on a user:

    Set-ADUser <username> -Clear msDS-KeyCredentialLink

    On a computer object use Set-ADComputer <hostname> -Clear msDS-KeyCredentialLink. Then find who could write it (Unexpected rights in the sweep) and remove that right.

    #GPO-based persistence

    A GPO can create a scheduled task, run a startup or logon script, add a user to Administrators or grant a privilege on every computer it applies to, including the DC. The sweep lists the files that carry these. Map a policy folder name (a GUID in braces) to its GPO name:

    Get-GPO -Guid <gpo-guid> | Select-Object DisplayName,GpoStatus,ModificationTime
    File under the GPO folder What it does Read it with
    Machine\Preferences\ScheduledTasks\ScheduledTasks.xml (or User\...) Creates scheduled tasks, often "Immediate" ones that run once as SYSTEM Get-Content and look at Command, Arguments, runAs
    Machine\Scripts\scripts.ini, psscripts.ini (hidden files) Startup and shutdown scripts; User\Scripts\... for logon and logoff Get-Content -Force, then open the script it names
    Machine\Preferences\Groups\Groups.xml Adds users to local groups such as Administrators Get-Content
    Machine\Microsoft\Windows NT\SecEdit\GptTmpl.inf Restricted groups ([Group Membership]), user rights ([Privilege Rights]), security options Get-Content
    Machine\Preferences\Registry\Registry.xml Writes registry values, for example Run keys Get-Content
    Machine\Preferences\Services\Services.xml, Files\Files.xml Changes services, copies files Get-Content

    Search every GPO's security template for group membership and powerful rights:

    $pol = "C:\Windows\SYSVOL\sysvol\$((Get-ADDomain).DNSRoot)\Policies"
Get-ChildItem $pol -Recurse -Filter GptTmpl.inf -Force | Select-String -Pattern '__Members|__Memberof|SeDebugPrivilege|SeTcbPrivilege|SeBackupPrivilege|SeImpersonatePrivilege|SeLoadDriverPrivilege' | Select-Object Path,Line

    Fix, from safest to strongest:

    1. Answer any Forensics Question about it.
    2. In gpmc.msc, edit the GPO and delete the preference item, script or restricted group entry. If the whole GPO is planted, disable its link (how).
    3. Run gpupdate /force.
    4. Remove what it already created on the DC: the scheduled task (Get-ScheduledTask outside \Microsoft\), the added group member, the dropped file (malware).

    Non-admins with edit rights on a GPO can push any of the above. The sweep lists them under GPO edit rights. Remove the right:

    Set-GPPermission -Name "<gpo-name>" -TargetName "<username>" -TargetType User -PermissionLevel None -Replace

    If that errors, use gpmc.msc > the GPO > Delegation tab > select the user > Remove. For a group use -TargetType Group.

    #Malicious logon scripts in SYSVOL and NETLOGON

    Logon scripts run as each user who logs on. NETLOGON is the scripts folder of SYSVOL. List scripts, then search them for download and account-changing commands:

    $scripts = "C:\Windows\SYSVOL\sysvol\$((Get-ADDomain).DNSRoot)\scripts"
Get-ChildItem $scripts -Recurse -File -Force | Select-Object FullName,LastWriteTime
Get-ChildItem $scripts -Recurse -File -Force | Select-String -Pattern 'IEX|Invoke-Expression|DownloadString|DownloadFile|Invoke-WebRequest|FromBase64String|-enc|net user|net localgroup|nc\.exe|bitsadmin|certutil' | Select-Object Path,LineNumber,Line

    Then:

    • Clear a planted scriptPath on a user: Set-ADUser <username> -Clear scriptPath.
    • Delete a planted script after the Forensics Questions are answered. Keep scripts the README describes (drive mappings, printers).
    • Fix write permissions on the folder so normal users cannot plant new ones (SYSVOL permissions).

    #LSA packages, password filters and Skeleton Key

    Three LSA registry values load DLLs into LSASS, which sees every password. An extra DLL there is a credential stealer or a password filter that logs every new password.

    Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa' | Select-Object 'Authentication Packages','Notification Packages','Security Packages',RunAsPPL
Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa\OSConfig' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object 'Security Packages'
    Value Normal content
    Authentication Packages msv1_0
    Notification Packages scecli (plus rassfm when RRAS or NPS is installed)
    Security Packages (Lsa) Empty ("")
    Security Packages (Lsa\OSConfig) Microsoft names such as kerberos, msv1_0, schannel, wdigest, tspkg, pku2u, cloudap

    A name like mimilib, kdcsvc in the wrong place or anything you cannot match to a Microsoft DLL in C:\Windows\System32 is planted. Put the normal value back, delete the DLL, and reboot:

    Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa' -Name 'Notification Packages' -Value @('scecli') -Type MultiString

    Skeleton Key is an in-memory patch of LSASS on a DC (mimikatz misc::skeleton) that makes one master password work for every account. It survives until reboot and leaves few traces:

    • Mimikatz files, or a driver service named mimidrv, on disk; System event 7045 for a new service.
    • Any account accepts the password mimikatz in addition to its real one.
    • LSASS is not running as a protected process (RunAsPPL not 1).

    Remove the tool and whatever re-runs it (task, service, Run key), turn on LSA protection (how) and reboot the DC to clear the patch.

    #DSRM, krbtgt and Golden Tickets

    • DsrmAdminLogonBehavior set to 2 allows the DSRM account to log on over the network (fix).
    • A Golden Ticket is forged with the krbtgt hash and stays valid until krbtgt is reset twice. The sweep shows when krbtgt last changed. Resetting it is the correct real-world fix after a compromise, but in competition leave krbtgt alone unless the README says otherwise (why).

    #Other AD backdoor quick checks

    Check Command Bad sign
    OUs that block GPO inheritance (Get-ADOrganizationalUnit -Filter *).DistinguishedName, then Get-GPInheritance -Target "<ou-dn>" on each (GpoInheritanceBlocked) An OU holding admin or rogue accounts out of the hardened GPOs
    Rogue computer accounts Get-ADComputer -Filter * -Properties whenCreated,mS-DS-CreatorSID (a creator SID means a user created it) A computer created by a user, often used for resource-based delegation
    DnsAdmins plugin ServerLevelPluginDll Any value
    Trusts Get-ADTrust -Filter * A trust the README does not mention; remove it in domain.msc
    Accounts protected from deletion Get-ADObject -LDAPFilter '(objectClass=user)' -Properties ProtectedFromAccidentalDeletion and read the True rows A rogue user protected so your delete fails
    Certificate templates AD CS hardening A template where any user supplies the subject name
    Primary group trick Primary group check PrimaryGroupID 512 on a normal user
    PreviousOther roles and server apps (harden or remove)NextServer forensics questions
    SRV

    Server forensics questions

    jump:srv-forensics

    Answer every question before you change the image; fixes destroy evidence. Server questions seen in past keys: the folder path of a named share and the SHA256 of a file (K5, Server 2019), and the port a backdoor listens on plus the full path of an executable (K7, Server 2022). A Hivestorm Server 2019 image asked for a banned user inside a MediaWiki app. The answer format and generic decoding are on the forensics playbook.

    Fast path

    1. Open the question file on the desktop and decide what it asks about: a share, a file, a process or port, an AD object, a log, a DNS record, a GPO.
    2. Open PowerShell as administrator. Change nothing yet.
    3. Run the matching recipe below and copy the value exactly (case, slashes, full path).
    4. Type it after ANSWER: in the file and save with Ctrl+S.
    5. Check the scoring report for "Forensics Question N correct" before moving on.

    #Path of a share

    Get-SmbShare | Format-Table Name,Path,Description -AutoSize
Get-SmbShare -Name "<share-name>" | Select-Object Path

    GUI: fsmgmt.msc > Shares, Shared Path column. Give the local path (C:\...) unless the question asks for the UNC path (\\<hostname>\<share-name>).

    #Hash of a file

    Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 "<path>"

    Use -Algorithm MD5 or SHA1 when asked. To find the file first: Get-ChildItem C:\ -Recurse -Force -Filter "<file>" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object FullName.

    #Port and path of a backdoor

    netstat -abn -p tcp

    The line after each [name.exe] block shows the port. In PowerShell, list listeners with their program path:

    Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen | Select-Object LocalPort,OwningProcess,@{n='Path';e={(Get-Process -Id $_.OwningProcess -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Path}} | Sort-Object LocalPort

    Full command line of one process:

    Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "ProcessId=<pid>" | Select-Object Name,ExecutablePath,CommandLine

    For a program that is running but not listening (K7 asked for GooseDesktop.exe): Task Manager > Details > right-click > Open file location, then Shift+right-click the file > Copy as path.

    #AD user and group questions

    Question Command
    SID of a user (Get-ADUser <username>).SID.Value
    When it was created or last changed Get-ADUser <username> -Properties whenCreated,whenChanged
    Which OU it is in (Get-ADUser <username>).DistinguishedName
    Groups it belongs to (Get-ADPrincipalGroupMembership <username>).Name
    Members of a group, nested included (Get-ADGroupMember "<groupname>" -Recursive).SamAccountName
    Last logon and password change Get-ADUser <username> -Properties LastLogonDate,PasswordLastSet
    Text hidden in a description Get-ADUser -Filter 'Description -like "*"' -Properties Description
    Every attribute Get-ADUser <username> -Properties *

    On a standalone server use Get-LocalUser <username> | Select-Object * and Get-LocalGroupMember "<groupname>" instead.

    #When a membership or attribute changed

    AD records when every attribute value was written. This shows when each member was added to a group, even with no audit log:

    Get-ADReplicationAttributeMetadata -Object (Get-ADGroup "Domain Admins").DistinguishedName -Server $env:COMPUTERNAME -ShowAllLinkedValues | Where-Object AttributeName -eq 'member' | Select-Object AttributeValue,FirstOriginatingCreateTime,LastOriginatingChangeTime

    For a user's attributes (for example when scriptPath or userAccountControl changed), drop -ShowAllLinkedValues and use the user's distinguished name.

    #Deleted users and objects

    Get-ADObject -Filter 'isDeleted -eq $true' -IncludeDeletedObjects -Properties samAccountName,whenChanged,lastKnownParent | Select-Object samAccountName,whenChanged,lastKnownParent

    On a standalone server, a deleted user's profile folder name stays in HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\ProfileList\<SID>\ProfileImagePath (seen on a Hivestorm Windows key):

    Get-ChildItem 'HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\ProfileList' | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{SID=$_.PSChildName; Path=(Get-ItemProperty $_.PSPath).ProfileImagePath} }

    #Security events on a domain controller

    Event Meaning
    4720 User account created
    4722, 4725 User account enabled, disabled
    4724 Password reset by someone else
    4726 User account deleted
    4728, 4732, 4756 Member added to a global, local (or Builtin), universal security group
    4729, 4733, 4757 Member removed from those groups
    4738 User account changed (flags such as Password not required)
    4740 Account locked out
    4741 Computer account created
    4624, 4625 Logon succeeded, failed
    4672 Logon with special privileges (an admin logon)
    4768 Kerberos TGT requested (Pre-Authentication Type 0 means preauth was off)
    4769 Kerberos service ticket requested (Ticket Encryption Type 0x17 is RC4, typical of Kerberoasting)
    4662 Operation on an AD object (with replication GUIDs, a DCSync)
    5136 Directory object modified (needs Audit Directory Service Changes)
    4765 SID history added to an account
    4794 Attempt to set the DSRM administrator password
    4698 Scheduled task created
    4697, and System 7045 Service installed
    4719 Audit policy changed
    1102 Security log cleared

    Read the newest matching events with their full text:

    Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Security'; Id=4720,4726,4728,4732,4756} -MaxEvents 50 | Format-List TimeCreated,Id,Message

    Narrow to one name:

    Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Security'; Id=4728,4732,4756} | Where-Object Message -match '<username>' | Format-List TimeCreated,Id,Message

    Service installs are in the System log:

    Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='System'; Id=7045} | Format-List TimeCreated,Message

    Other logs worth opening in eventvwr.msc on a DC: Applications and Services Logs > Directory Service, DNS Server, DFS Replication, Microsoft > Windows > PowerShell > Operational (event 4104 holds script block text) and TaskScheduler > Operational.

    #IIS and FTP logs

    Log Folder
    Web site C:\inetpub\logs\LogFiles\W3SVC<site-id>\u_exYYMMDD.log
    FTP site C:\inetpub\logs\LogFiles\FTPSVC<site-id>\u_exYYMMDD.log
    Requests IIS rejected before the site C:\Windows\System32\LogFiles\HTTPERR

    The site ID is the ID column of Get-Website. Times are UTC. Find requests to a page, for example a web shell:

    Get-ChildItem C:\inetpub\logs\LogFiles -Recurse -Filter *.log | Select-String -Pattern '<file>' | Select-Object -Last 20 Line

    Count requests per client IP for one site. The script reads the #Fields line to find the c-ip column:

    $lines = Get-ChildItem C:\inetpub\logs\LogFiles\W3SVC1 -Filter *.log | Get-Content
$fields = ($lines | Where-Object { $_ -like '#Fields:*' } | Select-Object -First 1).Substring(9).Split(' ')
$ip = [array]::IndexOf($fields, 'c-ip')
$lines | Where-Object { $_ -notlike '#*' } | ForEach-Object { $_.Split(' ')[$ip] } | Group-Object | Sort-Object Count -Descending | Select-Object -First 10 Count,Name

    In FTP logs, cs-method shows the command: USER (name tried), STOR (upload), RETR (download), DELE (delete). The file name is in cs-uri-stem. Passwords are not logged.

    #DNS records and zones

    Get-DnsServerResourceRecord -ZoneName "<zone-name>" -Name "<hostname>"
Get-DnsServerResourceRecord -ZoneName "<zone-name>" -RRType Txt | Select-Object HostName,@{n='Text';e={$_.RecordData.DescriptiveText}}
Resolve-DnsName "<hostname>" -Server 127.0.0.1

    File-backed zones are text files in C:\Windows\System32\dns\<zone-name>.dns. AD-integrated zones live in AD; use the cmdlets.

    #GPO contents

    Which GPO contains a setting or a word:

    Get-GPOReport -All -ReportType Xml -Path C:\gpos.xml
Select-String -Path C:\gpos.xml -Pattern '<search-text>' -Context 5,5

    <search-text> is the word you are looking for, such as a script name or a setting name. Name, creation and change time of a GPO from its folder GUID:

    Get-GPO -Guid <gpo-guid> | Select-Object DisplayName,CreationTime,ModificationTime,Owner

    What applied to this server and from where: gpresult /h C:\gp.html, then open the file.

    #Other Server answers

    Question Command
    Computer name or domain hostname, (Get-ADDomain).DNSRoot
    MAC or IP of a DHCP client Get-DhcpServerv4Lease -ScopeId <scope-id> (ClientId is the MAC)
    Certificate subject or thumbprint Get-ChildItem Cert:\LocalMachine\My
    Message in a service description sc.exe qdescription <service-name>
    Who created a scheduled task schtasks /query /fo LIST /v (Author line), or Task Scheduler > task > General tab
    Version of an installed program Installed program version
    User in a web app database (MediaWiki, WordPress) The app's admin pages, or the database tool (SQL, MariaDB)

    SRV

    Server penalties and how to avoid them

    jump:srv-penalties

    A penalty shows in the scoring report with a negative value. Undoing the change usually gives the points back. The first table is every penalty seen in past keys that applies to Server; the second lists Server changes that break critical services even though no key named them.

    Fast path

    1. Before removing a role, service, share, user or program, search the README for its name.
    2. Change one thing at a time and refresh the scoring report after each group of changes.
    3. If the score drops, undo the last change at once (recover).
    4. On a DC, run dcdiag /q after AD, DNS or GPO changes and undo anything that adds errors.

    #Penalties seen in past keys

    Penalty Points Seen in How to avoid
    Account lockout threshold set below 5 -2 to -4 K7 (Server 2022), G3, client keys Use 10 (anything from 5 to 50)
    Remote Desktop disabled when the README requires RDP -5 to -10 K7 Harden RDP instead (how)
    Authorized SMB share disabled (AFA in K7, C:\Share in G3) -5 K7, G3 Tighten the share, never remove it (how)
    Business file deleted from the share (a "pizza" file in K7, a Notepad++ installer in G3) -5 K7, G3 Delete only password files and media the README prohibits
    Required software removed or moved from its default path (Chrome, Notepad++, 7-Zip, Wireshark, Firefox) -5 each K7, G3, client keys Update in place with the vendor installer
    Authorized administrator demoted -5 G3 Compare admins with the README before removing anyone from Administrators
    Authorized user deleted, or their home folder deleted -5 to -10 client keys, G1 Delete only users missing from the README; delete files, not profile folders
    Critical service stopped, disabled or removed -5 Linux keys Search the README for the service before disabling it
    VirtualBox used instead of VMware 0 (warning) K7 Use the supported VMware player; problems on other hypervisors cannot be appealed

    #Server changes that break critical services

    No key named these as penalties, but each one takes down AD, DNS or a README service that the scoring engine checks.

    Do not What breaks Fix
    Remove AD-Domain-Services or DNS on a DC Demotes the DC or kills name resolution for the domain Never on a DC. Reinstall DNS with Install-WindowsFeature DNS -IncludeManagementTools
    Delete or unshare SYSVOL or NETLOGON Group Policy and domain logons Restore the shares
    Set the AD zones to DynamicUpdate None DC SRV records stop registering Set Secure (how)
    Change the DC's own DNS client address AD cannot find itself Point it back at 127.0.0.1 or its own IP
    Disable NTDS, Netlogon, Kdc, DNS, DFSR, W32Time or ADWS Logons, GPOs, AD PowerShell Services that must stay
    Put Administrators, Authenticated Users or Everyone in a Deny logon right, or remove Authenticated Users from Access this computer from the network Locks admins out, breaks Group Policy Locked out
    Add your own account to Protected Users NTLM and cached logons for you stop working Add only other admin accounts
    Delete, rename or enable krbtgt Kerberos for the whole domain Leave it alone
    Set EnableSMB2Protocol to False All file sharing, SYSVOL included Only ever turn SMB1 off
    Require FTPS when the README client uses plain FTP FTP looks down to the checker Undo if the score drops (FTPS)
    Turn off anonymous authentication on a public website Visitors get a password prompt Keep anonymous on with IUSR
    Remove the IIS site the README names, or Default Web Site when it is that site The required website Stop only unused sites
    Use Uninstall-WindowsFeature -Remove Payload deleted, cannot reinstall without media Plain Uninstall-WindowsFeature
    Block outbound traffic, or delete the AD DS, DNS or role firewall rule groups Scoring upload, domain traffic Never block outbound
    Turn off WinRM on a DC Server Manager management Harden WinRM instead
    Change the password or name of the account the README says to keep Your own logon, auto-logon checks Follow the README
    Touch the CyberPatriot folder, CCS Client or scoring service Scoring itself Leave them alone

    #How the scoring engine checks removal items

    From the decrypted official configs:

    • A removal item for a file also checks that its parent folder still exists. Deleting a whole folder or profile to get rid of one file scores nothing and triggers the penalty.
    • The share items in G3 checked that C:\Share still existed while secret.txt was gone.
    • Service items pass on Stopped plus Disabled (Start greater than 2) or a removed service.
    • Unauthorized-user items often accept a disabled account as well as a deleted one.

    #Recover from a penalty

    1. Undo the last change and refresh the report. If the penalty clears, that item was required.
    2. A removed role: Install-WindowsFeature <feature-name> -IncludeManagementTools, then restore its configuration (how).
    3. A disabled service: Set-Service <service-name> -StartupType Automatic and Start-Service <service-name>.
    4. A deleted share: recreate it with the same name and path, New-SmbShare -Name "<share-name>" -Path "<path>" -FullAccess "<domain-netbios>\<groupname>", then match the old permissions from the README.
    5. A deleted AD user: restore it from the Recycle Bin if it was enabled (how); otherwise recreate it with the exact name.
    6. A removed program: reinstall it to its default folder from the official installer.

    More troubleshooting is in Server troubleshooting and Windows troubleshooting.

    LNX

    Linux master checklist (Mint, Ubuntu, Debian)

    jump:lin-checklist

    Work top to bottom and tick items as you go (the ticks are shared with the team). Each item names the command; the link goes to the section that explains it. Keep a root terminal open the whole round and write every change in your changelog so you can undo it.

    The commands are written for Linux Mint 21 and work the same on Ubuntu 22.04, Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 11/12 unless an item names a distro. The distro differences table shows what changes (login screen, update tool, SSH unit, sudo). For Fedora or FreeBSD use Fedora and FreeBSD instead.

    README and Forensics first

    The README on the desktop decides which users, admins, services and programs are authorized. Answer the Forensics Questions before you delete users, files or packages, because the fix can destroy the evidence. Never touch the CyberPatriot folder, the scoring report shortcut, or anything named CCS.

    #First 10 minutes

    #Users and groups

    #sudo and admin rights
