    NET

    SRWE flashcards for modules 18 to 23

    jump:net-srwe-flashcards

    Click a card to reveal the answer. These are original practice items written for this guide, not real quiz questions.

    #Basic device and switching flashcards

    Q: What does a Layer 2 switch need so it can be managed from another subnet?

    An IP address on an SVI and an ip default-gateway.

    Q: In what order does a switch start up?

    POST, boot loader from ROM, CPU initialization, flash file system initialization, then the IOS image is loaded.

    Q: Which environment variable tells a switch which IOS image to load?

    BOOT, set with boot system.

    Q: Which prompt shows the switch is in the boot loader?

    switch:

    Q: Which counter rises when frames shorter than 64 bytes arrive?

    Runts.

    Q: Late collisions on a link usually point to what?

    A duplex mismatch (or a cable that is too long).

    Q: What must be true for auto-MDIX to work?

    Speed and duplex are both set to auto.

    Q: Which command deletes the RSA keys and so disables SSH?

    crypto key zeroize rsa

    Q: Which forwarding method checks the CRC before sending a frame?

    Store-and-forward.

    Q: Which cut-through variant waits for the first 64 bytes?

    Fragment-free.

    Q: A router with three active interfaces has how many broadcast domains?

    Three, one per interface.

    #VLAN and inter-VLAN flashcards

    Q: Which VLAN carries untagged traffic on an 802.1Q trunk?

    The native VLAN.

    Q: Which VLANs cannot be deleted?

    VLAN 1 and VLANs 1002-1005.

    Q: Where are normal-range VLANs stored?

    In vlan.dat in flash.

    Q: How large is the 802.1Q tag and how many bits hold the VLAN ID?

    4 bytes; 12 bits.

    Q: A port you configured is missing from show vlan brief. Why might that be?

    It is a trunk port. Trunks are not listed there; use show interfaces trunk.

    Q: Two 2960 switches are connected with default port settings. Do they form a trunk?

    No. Both are dynamic auto, so the link stays an access link.

    Q: Which command stops a port from sending DTP frames?

    switchport nonegotiate

    Q: Which command allows a port to carry both a data VLAN and IP phone traffic?

    switchport voice vlan <vlan-id> along with switchport access vlan <vlan-id>.

    Q: Which interface command assigns a router subinterface to VLAN 30?

    encapsulation dot1Q 30

    Q: Which global command must be entered before a Layer 3 switch routes between SVIs?

    ip routing

    Q: Which command turns a Layer 3 switch port into a routed port?

    no switchport

    Q: Which inter-VLAN method uses one router interface per VLAN?

    Legacy inter-VLAN routing.

    #STP flashcards

    Q: What problems does a Layer 2 loop cause?

    Broadcast storms, MAC table instability and duplicate frames.

    Q: Which switch becomes the root bridge?

    The one with the lowest bridge ID: lowest priority, then lowest MAC address.

    Q: A switch shows bridge priority 32778. Which VLAN is this?

    VLAN 10 (32768 + 10).

    Q: In what increments can the bridge priority be set?

    4096.

    Q: What is the 802.1D cost of a FastEthernet (100 Mbps) port?

    19.

    Q: What role do all active ports on the root bridge have?

    Designated.

    Q: Two paths to the root have equal cost. What breaks the tie first?

    The lowest sender bridge ID, then sender port priority, then sender port ID.

    Q: In which 802.1D state does a port learn MAC addresses but not forward data?

    Learning.

    Q: What are the default STP hello, forward delay and max age timers?

    2, 15 and 20 seconds.

    Q: Which three RSTP port states exist?

    Discarding, learning and forwarding.

    Q: Which STP version is the default on Cisco Catalyst switches?

    PVST+.

    Q: Which IEEE standard is RSTP?

    802.1w.

    Q: Which command makes a switch the root for VLAN 1 automatically?

    spanning-tree vlan 1 root primary

    Q: What does Altn BLK mean in show spanning-tree?

    Alternate port in the blocking state.

    #EtherChannel flashcards

    Q: Which EtherChannel protocol is an IEEE standard?

    LACP (802.3ad).

    Q: Which LACP mode actively starts negotiation?

    Active.

    Q: Will an EtherChannel form with passive on one side and passive on the other?

    No. At least one side must be active.

    Q: Will an EtherChannel form with desirable on one side and auto on the other?

    Yes.

    Q: Which mode forces a channel without PAgP or LACP?

    on

    Q: How many ports can be active in one EtherChannel?

    Eight.

    Q: Where should trunk settings for an EtherChannel be configured?

    On the interface port-channel interface.

    Q: What do the flags SU and P mean in show etherchannel summary?

    SU: Layer 2 port channel in use. P: member bundled.

    #DHCP flashcards

    Q: What are the four DHCPv4 messages in order?

    Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledgment (DORA).

    Q: Why is the DHCPREQUEST broadcast?

    So any other server that made an offer knows it was not chosen.

    Q: Which UDP port does a DHCPv4 server listen on?

    67.

    Q: Which command keeps the router's own address out of a DHCP pool?

    ip dhcp excluded-address

    Q: Which pool command sets the default gateway handed to clients?

    default-router

    Q: Which interface command forwards DHCP broadcasts to a server on another subnet?

    ip helper-address <server-ip>

    Q: Which command makes a router interface get its address from the ISP?

    ip address dhcp

    Q: Which command lists leased addresses on a Cisco DHCP server?

    show ip dhcp binding

    Q: How do you turn the DHCP service off on a Cisco router?

    no service dhcp

    #SLAAC and DHCPv6 flashcards

    Q: Which RA flag values mean stateless DHCPv6?

    A = 1, O = 1, M = 0.

    Q: Which interface command sets the M flag?

    ipv6 nd managed-config-flag

    Q: Which interface command sets the O flag?

    ipv6 nd other-config-flag

    Q: Where does an IPv6 host always get its default gateway?

    From the source (link-local) address of the RA.

    Q: To which address does a DHCPv6 client send SOLICIT?

    FF02::1:2, all DHCPv6 servers and relays.

    Q: Which message does a stateless DHCPv6 client send in place of REQUEST?

    INFORMATION-REQUEST.

    Q: How is an EUI-64 interface ID built?

    Insert FFFE in the middle of the MAC and flip the seventh bit.

    Q: Which global command must be on for a Cisco router to send RAs?

    ipv6 unicast-routing

    Q: How does a host check that its new IPv6 address is unique?

    Duplicate Address Detection: it sends a Neighbor Solicitation for its own address and waits for no reply.

    #HSRP flashcards

    Q: What is the default HSRP priority?

    100.

    Q: Is HSRP preemption enabled by default?

    No.

    Q: Two HSRP routers have the same priority. Which becomes active?

    The one with the highest IPv4 address.

    Q: What default gateway do hosts use with HSRP?

    The virtual IP address.

    Q: What are the default HSRP hello and hold timers?

    3 and 10 seconds.

    Q: Which FHRP is an open standard that supports IPv4 and IPv6?

    VRRPv3.

    Q: Which Cisco FHRP load balances across routers?

    GLBP.

    Q: Which command shows the active and standby HSRP routers?

    show standby brief

    #LAN and switch security flashcards

    Q: Which feature stops MAC address table flooding?

    Port security.

    Q: Which feature stops a rogue DHCP server?

    DHCP snooping.

    Q: Which feature stops ARP poisoning and what must be enabled first?

    Dynamic ARP Inspection; DHCP snooping must be on first.

    Q: Which tool name is linked to DHCP starvation in SRWE?

    Gobbler.

    Q: A double-tagging attack only works when the attacker is on which VLAN?

    The native VLAN of the trunk.

    Q: What is the default port security violation mode?

    Shutdown.

    Q: Which violation mode drops traffic and logs it but keeps the port up?

    Restrict.

    Q: Which violation mode drops traffic with no log message?

    Protect.

    Q: Which port security option saves learned MACs to the running config?

    switchport port-security mac-address sticky

    Q: How do you bring an err-disabled port back after removing the bad device?

    shutdown then no shutdown on the interface.

    Q: Port security is rejected with a dynamic port message. What is missing?

    switchport mode access.

    Q: Which ports should be DHCP snooping trusted?

    Uplinks and ports toward the real DHCP server.

    Q: What happens when a BPDU arrives on a port with BPDU guard?

    The port goes err-disabled.

    Q: Which AAA part records what a user did?

    Accounting.

    Q: Which AAA protocol uses TCP 49 and encrypts the whole body?

    TACACS+.

    Q: In 802.1X, what is the switch called?

    The authenticator.

    Q: Which Cisco appliance watches SMTP traffic for threats?

    The ESA (Email Security Appliance).

    #Wireless flashcards

    Q: Which 802.11 standard is called Wi-Fi 6?

    802.11ax.

    Q: Which standards use only the 5 GHz band?

    802.11a and 802.11ac.

    Q: Which three 2.4 GHz channels do not overlap?

    1, 6 and 11.

    Q: Which access method do WLANs use?

    CSMA/CA.

    Q: In which mode do wireless clients connect without an AP?

    Ad hoc (IBSS).

    Q: What identifies a BSS?

    The BSSID, the AP's MAC address.

    Q: What do you call two or more BSSs linked by a wired distribution system?

    An ESS.

    Q: Which client discovery mode uses probe requests?

    Active mode.

    Q: Which protocol do lightweight APs use to talk to a WLC, and on which ports?

    CAPWAP, UDP 5246 and 5247.

    Q: In split MAC, who sends beacons: the AP or the WLC?

    The AP.

    Q: Which encryption does WPA2 use?

    AES with CCMP.

    Q: Which WPA3 feature replaces the pre-shared key handshake?

    SAE (Simultaneous Authentication of Equals).

    Q: Which wireless mode authenticates each user through a RADIUS server?

    Enterprise (802.1X/EAP).

    Q: Why are SSID cloaking and MAC filtering weak?

    The SSID can still be discovered and MAC addresses can be spoofed.

    Q: What is an evil twin?

    A fake AP with the same SSID that lures clients for a man-in-the-middle attack.

    #Routing and static route flashcards

    Q: Which route does a router use when several match the destination?

    The longest prefix match.

    Q: Which forwarding mechanism is the default and fastest on Cisco routers?

    CEF.

    Q: What does the code L mean in the routing table?

    A local route: the router's own interface address.

    Q: In [110/20], what do the two numbers mean?

    Administrative distance 110 (OSPF) and metric 20.

    Q: What is the AD of a static route?

    1.

    Q: Which is preferred: an internal EIGRP route or an OSPF route to the same network?

    Internal EIGRP (AD 90 beats 110).

    Q: Which metric does RIP use?

    Hop count, maximum 15.

    Q: What is the syntax of an IPv4 default static route?

    ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 <next-hop-ip> (or an exit interface).

    Q: What makes a static route floating?

    An AD higher than the primary route's AD, so it is used only when the primary fails.

    Q: What prefix length is an IPv4 host route?

    /32 (IPv6: /128).

    Q: Which static route needs a recursive lookup?

    A next-hop static route.

    Q: When must an IPv6 static route include the exit interface?

    When the next hop is a link-local address.

    Q: What does Gateway of last resort is not set mean?

    The router has no default route.

    Q: Ping works one way but replies never come back. What is the likely static routing problem?

    A missing return route on the far router.

    #ACL, NAT, OSPF and VPN flashcards

    Q: Which numbers identify a standard IPv4 ACL?

    1-99 and 1300-1999.

    Q: Where should a standard ACL be placed?

    As close to the destination as possible.

    Q: What is the wildcard mask for 255.255.255.224?

    0.0.0.31.

    Q: What is at the end of every ACL?

    An implicit deny any.

    Q: Which command applies an ACL to the vty lines?

    access-class <acl-number> in

    Q: Which keyword turns dynamic NAT into PAT?

    overload

    Q: What is the inside global address?

    The public address that represents an inside host.

    Q: How is the OSPF router ID chosen without a router-id command?

    Highest loopback IPv4 address, then highest active interface IPv4 address.

    Q: Which OSPF area is the backbone?

    Area 0.

    Q: Which IPsec protocol provides encryption?

    ESP.

    Q: Which tunnel protocol carries multicast but does not encrypt?

    GRE.
