    PT

    Packet Tracer challenge strategy

    jump:pt-strategy

    Fast path

    1. Read every page of the instructions window (Next/Previous) before you touch a device.
    2. Copy every exact value into a scratch text file: hostnames, passwords, banner text, IPs, masks, gateways, SSIDs, passphrases, usernames, domain name, descriptions.
    3. Hover over each device and write down its model. Interface names depend on the model (table).
    4. Do cabling, modules and power first (which cable).
    5. Configure one device at a time, using a template where one fits, and check the completion percentage after each device.

    6. Save every router and switch before you leave it:

      write memory

    7. Save the activity file and submit the way the round instructions say.

    The Packet Tracer (PT) activity is graded automatically by comparing your devices against a hidden answer network. Points come from exact matches: a hostname of s1 when the task says S1 earns nothing. Read carefully once, then type from your list.

    Exact spelling and case are graded

    Hostnames, passwords, usernames, SSIDs, passphrases, banner text and domain names are case-sensitive and checked character by character. Copy them from the instructions instead of retyping from memory. An extra space, a missing period or a wrong capital letter in a banner can cost the item.

    #What each round's Packet Tracer covers

    The Packet Tracer exercise is cumulative: each round can use anything from earlier rounds. CyberPatriot numbers the modules by its own NetAcad Content Course. Modules 1-17 match ITN v7; modules 18-23 are not published and most likely come from SRWE (switching, routing, wireless). The topic columns for 18-23, and for 21-22, are an informed guess, so confirm against the Content Course titles on the Coach Dashboard.

    Round (CP-19 dates) PT modules PT points (HS) What to be fast at
    Round 1 (Oct 22-25, 2026) 1-7 20 Initial switch config, passwords and SSH, PC addressing, cabling, Simulation mode questions
    Round 2 (Nov 12-15, 2026) 1-11 and 21-22 20 Everything above, plus router interfaces, default gateways, subnetting and VLSM, ARP; 21-22 likely DHCPv4 and wireless
    State (Dec 10-13, 2026) 1-17 70 Everything above, plus IPv6 and dual stack, ping and traceroute, device hardening (checklist), troubleshooting a small network
    Semifinals (Jan 21-23, 2027) 1-23 168 Platinum, 70 Gold and Silver Everything above, plus likely VLANs, trunks, inter-VLAN routing, STP, EtherChannel, switch security, static routes, WLC wireless
    • Practice files: the ITN v7 activities 2.9.1, 10.4.3, 11.10.1, 12.9.1, 16.5.1, 17.8.2 and 17.8.3, and the SRWE v7 activities 3.6.1, 4.5.1, 6.4.1, 7.4.1, 11.6.1, 13.5.1 and 15.6.1 are the closest matches to a scored exercise.
    • Past seasons put the team number in the PT file name and in the activity itself; a file without it has scored zero. Follow the round instructions for where it goes.
    • From Round 2 on, the exercise may run in the browser-based Online Packet Tracer. The CLI and GUI tabs work the same way.
    • Full templates for the later rounds are in the advanced template gallery and the advanced checklist.

    #Workflow checklist for the activity

    #Do not change things the task did not ask for

    The grader may also check items you were never told about: existing IPs, existing VLAN membership, existing cables. Do not "clean up" devices, rename display labels, delete devices, move cables or re-address anything outside the instructions.

    Never click Reset Activity

    Reset Activity reloads the original file and wipes all of your work.

    #How grading and Check Results work

    • A .pka activity contains an answer network. Each graded item (for example S1 > Hostname or S1 > Ports > Vlan1 > IP Address) is compared against your network.
    • If the author left feedback on, the bottom of the instructions window shows a completion percentage and a Check Results button. Check Results opens a window with an Assessment Items tab (a tree of items marked correct or incorrect) and sometimes a Connectivity Tests tab (pings the grader runs).
    • The author can hide feedback. If you see only a percentage, or nothing, verify each requirement yourself with show commands.
    • Some activities compare the saved startup-config, so save every device.
    • Some activities show a countdown timer in the instructions window. The CyberPatriot round rules set the overall time window; read them before the round.

    Use the percentage as a tripwire

    Check the percentage after every device. If it did not move after you finished a requirement, re-read that requirement while it is fresh. A typo in a value, the wrong interface or the wrong device are the usual causes (why the score is stuck).

    #Time management

    Phase Share of time What to do
    Read and plan 10% Read every instruction page, copy all values, note device models
    Physical and cabling 10% Add modules, connect cables, power on
    Device configuration 55% One device at a time, save each
    Verification 15% Pings, show commands, Check Results
    Buffer 10% Fix red items, final save, submit
    • Do the items you are sure of first. Park anything confusing and come back after the easy points are banked.
    • Do not spend more than a few minutes stuck on one item.
    • Build configs in a text editor (Notepad, or a PC's Desktop > Text Editor), fill in the values, then paste.

    #Paste configs into the CLI tab

    1. Write the commands in a plain text editor with the exact values filled in, or start from a template.
    2. Copy them.
    3. In PT, open the device, click the CLI tab, click in the console window and press Enter until you see a prompt.
    4. Get to the prompt the block expects (usually Switch# or Router#, after enable).
    5. Click the Paste button below the console window. Keyboard paste also works in most versions.
    6. Scroll back and read every line that starts with %, then verify with show running-config.

    Pasted commands that ask a question

    A command that prompts for input takes the next pasted line as its answer. Keep these out of pasted blocks, or put them last:

    • copy running-config startup-config asks Destination filename [startup-config]?. Use write memory in pasted blocks.
    • crypto key generate rsa with no options asks for the modulus. Use crypto key generate rsa general-keys modulus 1024.
    • If RSA keys already exist, even the full command asks Do you really want to replace them? [yes/no]:. Check first with show ip ssh; if SSH is already enabled, type the command by hand and answer yes.
    • reload and erase startup-config ask for confirmation. Never paste them.

    To run a show command or save without leaving configuration mode, put do in front of it (details).

    #Verify each requirement as you go

    Requirement type Verify with
    Hostname, passwords, banner, lines show running-config
    Interface IP and up/down state show ip interface brief
    IPv6 addresses show ipv6 interface brief
    SSH show ip ssh, then ssh -l <admin-username> <ip-address> from a PC
    Default gateway on a switch show running-config, look for ip default-gateway
    PC addressing PC > Desktop > Command Prompt > ipconfig /all
    End-to-end connectivity ping from the PC Command Prompt, or Add Simple PDU
    Saved config show startup-config matches show running-config

    Done means

    The completion percentage stops rising only on items you cannot do, every device shows the required config in show running-config, the required pings succeed, and every router and switch has been saved.

    PreviousSRWE flashcards for modules 18 to 23NextPacket Tracer interface tour
    PT

    Packet Tracer interface tour

    jump:pt-interface

    Fast path

    1. Click a device to open its window. Routers and switches: CLI tab. PCs and servers: Desktop tab.
    2. Hover over a device to see its model, ports, IPs and link state.
    3. Pick cables from the Connections category by their tooltip name (which cable).
    4. Stay in Realtime mode for configuration. Switch to Simulation only when a task asks you to watch packets.
    5. Click Fast Forward Time (bottom bar, next to the clock) to speed up Spanning Tree and DHCP.

    #Logical and physical workspace

    Workspace What it shows When you need it
    Logical (default) Devices and cables as a topology diagram Almost all configuration and cabling
    Physical Intercity, City, Building, Wiring Closet, racks; wireless ranges; cable lengths Tasks that say "move the device to a closet or rack", or wireless range problems

    Switch with the Logical and Physical buttons near the top-left of the workspace. Most ITN 1-7 activities stay in Logical view.

    #Device and connection selection box

    The bottom-left panel has two parts: a box of device categories and a box with the models in the selected category.

    Category Contains
    Network Devices Routers, Switches, Hubs, Wireless Devices (for example WRT300N, HomeRouter-PT-AC, AccessPoint-PT), Security (ASA), WAN Emulation (Cloud, DSL and cable modems)
    End Devices PC, Laptop, Server, Printer, IP Phone, Tablet, Smartphone, TV, IoT items
    Components IoT sensors and actuators
    Connections All cable types
    Miscellaneous, Multiuser Prebuilt groups, multiuser connection

    To add a device, click the category, click the model, then click in the workspace (or drag it).

    #Cable types in the Connections box

    Hover over each cable icon to read its name. Pick by name; the icons are small and look alike.

    Tooltip name Use
    Automatically Choose Connection Type PT picks the cable and the first free port. Avoid it when the task names ports
    Console PC RS 232 port to a router or switch Console port (then PC > Desktop > Terminal)
    Copper Straight-Through Unlike devices: PC to switch, switch to router, PC to hub
    Copper Cross-Over Like devices: switch to switch, router to router, PC to PC, PC to router Ethernet
    Fiber Fiber port to fiber port only (FX, SFP or fiber Gigabit modules)
    Phone DSL modem to the cloud's modem port
    Coaxial Cable modem to the cloud's coaxial port
    Serial DCE Router serial to router serial; the end you click first is DCE (sets the clock rate)
    Serial DTE Router serial to router serial; the end you click first is DTE
    Octal Async module to many console ports
    IoT Custom Cable, USB IoT components, USB console

    To connect: click the cable type, click the first device, pick the port from the pop-up list, click the second device, pick the port. Pick the exact port the task names (for example FastEthernet0/1 or GigabitEthernet0/0).

    See port names on the diagram

    In Options > Preferences, tick Always Show Port Labels in Logical Workspace to show the port name at each cable end. Hovering over a device also lists its ports, IPs and link state.

    #Link lights and what the colors mean

    Light at the cable end Meaning Typical fix
    Green triangle Physical link up (blinking means traffic) Nothing
    Amber circle Switch port is up but Spanning Tree is still in listening/learning (about 30 seconds after connecting), or blocking a redundant link Wait, or click Fast Forward Time
    Red triangle Link down Interface shut down (routers default to shutdown), wrong cable, device off, wrong port type
    No light No connection Connect the cable

    Router interfaces are shut down by default, so a new link to a router stays red until you run no shutdown on the router interface (router interfaces).

    #Device window tabs

    Tab Found on What it does
    Physical All devices Picture of the chassis, power switch, module list for adding and removing modules
    Config All devices GUI forms for hostname, interfaces, IPs, routing, VLANs; Cisco devices show Equivalent IOS Commands at the bottom
    CLI Routers, switches The IOS command line (same as a console session), with Copy and Paste buttons
    Desktop PCs, laptops, servers, tablets IP Configuration, Command Prompt, Web Browser, Terminal, PC Wireless, Text Editor, Email, Firewall and more
    Services Servers HTTP, DHCP, DHCPv6, TFTP, DNS, SYSLOG, AAA, NTP, EMAIL, FTP, IoT, VM Management
    GUI Wireless routers (WRT300N, HomeRouter-PT-AC) Linksys-style web pages: Setup, Wireless, Security, Access Restrictions, Administration, Status
    Attributes Many devices Informational properties such as cost; rarely needed

    Display Name is not the hostname

    On a router or switch, the Config tab has both Display Name (the label under the icon) and Hostname (the IOS hostname). The grader checks the IOS hostname. Set it in the CLI with hostname <hostname>.

    Learn syntax from the Config tab

    When you change a setting in the Config tab of a router or switch, the matching IOS command appears in the Equivalent IOS Commands box. Some activities disable the Config tab, so know the CLI too.

    #Add or remove a module in the Physical tab

    Power off reloads from startup-config

    Turning a router or switch off and on reloads it from startup-config, so anything unsaved is lost. Run write memory first. PCs keep their IP settings.

    1. Open the device and click the Physical tab.
    2. Click the power switch on the chassis picture to turn the device off (the green light goes dark).
    3. If replacing a module, drag the old one out of its slot back onto the module list.
    4. Drag the new module from the list into the empty slot. Click a module name to see its description and picture.
    5. Turn the power on again.

    PT refuses to add or remove a module while the device is on.

    Catalyst 3650 starts without a power supply

    The 3650-24PS is placed with an empty power bay and stays off. In the Physical tab, drag the AC power supply module from the module list into the empty bay, and it boots.

    #Desktop tab apps on PCs, laptops and servers

    App Use
    IP Configuration Static or DHCP IPv4, subnet mask, gateway, DNS; IPv6 settings
    Command Prompt ipconfig, ping, tracert, arp -a, nslookup, ssh -l, telnet (full list)
    Terminal Console session to a router or switch over a Console cable (9600 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, no flow control)
    Web Browser Browse to a server, or to a wireless router's web pages (for example http://192.168.0.1)
    PC Wireless Join an SSID (only when a wireless card is installed)
    Text Editor Scratch pad for building configs to paste
    Email Mail client exercises
    Firewall, IPv6 Firewall Host firewall rules that can block pings and web traffic

    #Realtime and Simulation mode

    The bottom-right corner has Realtime and Simulation tabs.

    • Realtime: the network runs normally and pings complete in seconds. Do all configuration and graded work here.
    • Simulation: time stops and you step through every packet. Use it when a task asks you to observe PDUs or identify protocols, layers or headers.

    #Watch PDUs in Simulation mode

    1. Click Simulation. The Simulation Panel opens with the Event List and Play Controls.
    2. Click Edit Filters (or Show All/None) and select only the protocols you care about, for example ICMP and ARP, or HTTP, DNS and TCP.
    3. Create traffic: Add Simple PDU, ping from a PC Command Prompt, or open a web page in a PC's Web Browser.
    4. Click Capture/Forward to move one event at a time, or Play to run automatically. Back steps backwards. The slider sets play speed.
    5. Click an envelope on the topology, or the colored square in the Event List Info column, to open PDU Information.
    6. On the OSI Model tab, In Layers and Out Layers show what each layer did at this device. The Inbound and Outbound PDU Details tabs show header fields (Ethernet II MACs, IP addresses, TTL, TCP/UDP ports, ICMP type).
    7. Click Reset Simulation to clear events, then return to Realtime.

    Envelopes are color-coded by protocol (set in Edit Filters). A green check on an envelope means it arrived; a red X means it was dropped at that device.

    #OSI and TCP/IP layers for Simulation tasks

    OSI layer TCP/IP layer PDU name Examples seen in PT
    7 Application Application Data HTTP, HTTPS, DNS, DHCP, FTP, SMTP, POP3, Telnet, SSH
    6 Presentation Application Data Encoding, encryption, compression
    5 Session Application Data Session setup and teardown
    4 Transport Transport Segment (TCP), datagram (UDP) TCP, UDP, source and destination ports
    3 Network Internet Packet IPv4, IPv6, ICMP
    2 Data Link Network Access Frame Ethernet II, 802.11; ARP resolves IPv4 to MAC here
    1 Physical Network Access Bits Copper, fiber, wireless signal

    #Common protocol ports

    Protocol Transport Port
    FTP TCP 20 (data), 21 (control)
    SSH TCP 22
    Telnet TCP 23
    SMTP TCP 25
    DNS UDP (and TCP) 53
    DHCP UDP 67 server, 68 client
    HTTP TCP 80
    POP3 TCP 110
    IMAP TCP 143
    HTTPS TCP 443

    #Send a test with Add Simple PDU

    1. Click the closed-envelope Add Simple PDU button in the toolbar.
    2. Click the source device, then the destination device. PT sends one ICMP echo.
    3. Read the result in the PDU list (bottom-right): Last Status shows Successful or Failed, with source, destination, type and time.
    4. Double-click (delete) on a row to remove it. Double-click the Fire column to send it again.

    The first attempt often fails

    In Realtime, the first PDU or ping between two devices often fails or times out while ARP resolves the MAC address. Send it again before troubleshooting.

    #Other toolbar tools

    Hover over any toolbar button to see its name and keyboard shortcut.

    Tool How to use Use for
    Select (arrow) Click it, or press Esc Return to normal clicking
    Inspect (magnifying glass) Click it, then a device; pick a table View the ARP, MAC address or routing table without the CLI
    Delete (X) Click it, then a device or cable Remove a wrong cable. Do not delete devices the activity provided
    Place Note Click it, then the workspace Notes; not graded
    Draw, Resize Shapes and resizing Cosmetic
    Zoom in, out, reset Toolbar magnifier buttons Read small labels
    Fast Forward Time Bottom bar, next to the Realtime clock Skips ahead so STP ports turn green and DHCP clients get addresses sooner
    Power Cycle Devices Bottom bar, next to Fast Forward Time Reboots every device

    Power Cycle Devices reloads everything

    Every router and switch reboots from its startup-config, and anything unsaved is gone. Do not click it unless every device is saved.

    PreviousPacket Tracer challenge strategyNextIOS CLI basics and modes
    PT

    IOS CLI basics and modes

    jump:pt-ios-basics

    Fast path

    1. Open the device, click the CLI tab, click in the window and press Enter. If asked Would you like to enter the initial configuration dialog? [yes/no]:, type no.

    2. From the > prompt, enter privileged EXEC (type the enable password if one is set):

      enable

    3. Enter global configuration mode:

      configure terminal

    4. Stop mistyped commands from hanging on DNS lookups:

      no ip domain-lookup

    5. Configure what the task asks, then return to privileged EXEC and save:

      end
write memory

    #IOS command modes

    Mode Prompt How to enter What you can do
    User EXEC S1> Log in, or press Enter at the console Limited show, ping, enable
    Privileged EXEC S1# enable (then the enable secret if set) All show, copy, write, reload, debug, configure terminal
    Global configuration S1(config)# configure terminal Device-wide settings: hostname, passwords, banner, routes, SSH, users
    Interface configuration S1(config-if)# interface <interface> IP address, description, shutdown, switchport settings
    Interface range S1(config-if-range)# interface range <interface-range> Same as interface mode, many ports at once
    Line configuration S1(config-line)# line console 0 or line vty 0 15 Line passwords, login, exec-timeout, transport input
    VLAN interface (SVI) S1(config-if)# interface vlan 1 Switch management IP
    VLAN configuration S1(config-vlan)# vlan <vlan-id> VLAN name
    Router DHCP pool R1(dhcp-config)# ip dhcp pool <pool-name> DHCP pool settings

    #Move between modes

    Command or key From Goes to
    enable User EXEC (>) Privileged EXEC (#)
    disable Privileged EXEC User EXEC
    configure terminal (conf t) Privileged EXEC Global configuration
    interface g0/1, line vty 0 15 Global configuration or another sub-mode That sub-mode
    exit Any sub-mode One level up (sub-mode to global, global to privileged EXEC)
    end or Ctrl+Z Any configuration mode Straight to privileged EXEC
    exit or logout EXEC Ends the session

    Jump straight to another interface

    From (config-if)# you can type interface g0/1 to move to another interface without exit. The same works for line from (config-line)#.

    #Help, completion and abbreviations

    Technique Example Result
    ? alone ? at S1(config)# Lists every command available in this mode
    Partial word and ? (no space) sh? Lists commands starting with "sh"
    Command, space, ? show ip ? Lists the next keyword or argument options
    Tab conf then Tab Completes to configure
    Abbreviate conf t, sh run, sh ip int br, int g0/1, no shut, wr Any unique prefix works
    Short Full
    en enable
    conf t configure terminal
    sh run show running-config
    sh start show startup-config
    sh ip int br show ip interface brief
    int g0/1, int fa0/1, int s0/0/0 interface GigabitEthernet0/1, FastEthernet0/1, Serial0/0/0
    int ra fa0/1 - 24 interface range FastEthernet0/1 - 24
    no shut no shutdown
    wr write memory
    copy run start copy running-config startup-config

    Abbreviate commands, never values

    Shorten commands and keywords freely, but type hostnames, passwords, banner text, IP addresses and domain names in full.

    #IOS hotkeys

    Key Action
    Up arrow or Ctrl+P Previous command in history
    Down arrow or Ctrl+N Next command in history
    Tab Complete the current keyword
    Ctrl+A Cursor to start of line
    Ctrl+E Cursor to end of line
    Ctrl+Z Leave configuration mode, go to privileged EXEC
    Ctrl+C Abort the current command or leave configuration mode
    Ctrl+Shift+6 Break a running ping, traceroute or DNS lookup
    Space at --More-- Next page of output
    Enter at --More-- Next line of output
    Q or any other key at --More-- Stop the output

    #Stop the Translating delay on typos

    Press Ctrl+Shift+6 to break out of the lookup. Then, in global configuration mode, turn lookups off:

    no ip domain-lookup

    In EXEC mode, IOS treats an unknown word as a hostname and tries to resolve it with DNS. The delay looks like this:

    S1#shwo run
Translating "shwo"...domain server (255.255.255.255)
% Unknown command or computer name, or unable to find computer address

    no ip domain-lookup is standard in ITN labs and does not affect SSH. If the task configures a DNS server on the router or switch (ip name-server), check whether it also expects lookups to stay on.

    #Undo a command with no

    Put no in front of almost any configuration command to remove it. Run each in the mode where the original command was entered.

    Mode Command Removes
    (config)# no banner motd The MOTD banner
    (config)# no username <username> A local user account
    (config)# no enable password The plaintext enable password (keeps enable secret)
    (config-if)# no ip address The interface IP
    (config-if)# no shutdown The shutdown state (turns the interface on)
    (config-line)# no password The line password

    #Run EXEC commands from config mode with do

    In any configuration mode, put do in front of an EXEC command to run it without leaving configuration mode:

    do show ip interface brief

    do show running-config

    do write memory

    #IOS error messages and what they mean

    Message Meaning Fix
    % Invalid input detected at '^' marker. The command is wrong at the caret, you are in the wrong mode, or PT does not support it Check spelling at the ^; check the prompt ((config)# or #?); try do; try ?
    % Incomplete command. A required keyword or value is missing Press Up arrow, add a space and ?
    % Ambiguous command: "s" The abbreviation matches more than one command Type more letters
    % Unknown command or computer name... Typo in EXEC mode, treated as a hostname Retype; set no ip domain-lookup
    % Please define a hostname other than Switch. RSA key generation needs a non-default hostname hostname <hostname>
    % Please define a domain-name first. RSA key generation needs a domain name ip domain-name <domain-name>
    % Password too short - must be at least N characters. security passwords min-length is set Use a longer password, or recheck the instructions
    % Login invalid Wrong username or password with login local Check case; check the username line in show running-config
    % Bad passwords Three wrong enable or line passwords Retry; check case

    #Questions IOS may ask

    Prompt Answer
    Would you like to enter the initial configuration dialog? [yes/no]: no
    Would you like to terminate autoinstall? [yes]: Press Enter
    Press RETURN to get started! Click in the CLI window and press Enter
    Destination filename [startup-config]? Press Enter
    Proceed with reload? [confirm] Press Enter only if you mean it
    System configuration has been modified. Save? [yes/no]: yes to keep your changes, no if you are deliberately starting over
    PreviousPacket Tracer interface tourNextInitial switch configuration
    PT

    Initial switch configuration

    jump:pt-basic-switch

    Fast path

    1. From the Switch> prompt, enter global configuration mode:

      enable
configure terminal

    2. Set the hostname, stop DNS lookups and set the privileged EXEC password:

      hostname <hostname>
no ip domain-lookup
enable secret <enable-secret>

    3. Set the console and vty passwords:

      line console 0
password <console-password>
login
line vty 0 15
password <vty-password>
login
exit

    4. Encrypt plaintext passwords and add the banner:

      service password-encryption
banner motd #<banner-text>#

    5. Give the switch its management IP and default gateway:

      interface vlan 1
ip address <ip-address> <subnet-mask>
no shutdown
exit
ip default-gateway <default-gateway>

    6. Return to privileged EXEC and save:

      end
write memory

    This is the ITN Module 2 sequence. The same lines as one pasteable block are in the simple passwords template. For SSH, local users and other hardening, see securing device access.

    #Set the hostname

    In global configuration mode:

    hostname <hostname>

    The prompt changes immediately (for example S1(config)#). Hostnames start with a letter, contain no spaces, and are graded case-sensitively.

    #Choose enable secret or enable password

    Command Stored as Notes
    enable secret <enable-secret> Hashed (enable secret 5 $1$... in PT) Preferred. Wins if both are configured
    enable password <password> Plaintext, or type 7 after service password-encryption Legacy. Configure only if the task says "enable password"

    Use the one the task names

    "Encrypted privileged EXEC password" or "enable secret" means enable secret. "Enable password" means enable password. If both are asked, configure both with the given values. IOS warns when the two are identical, so check show running-config that both lines are there.

    To remove an insecure plaintext enable password while keeping the secret, in global configuration mode:

    no enable password

    #Set console and vty line passwords

    In global configuration mode:

    line console 0
password <console-password>
login
line vty 0 15
password <vty-password>
login
end
    • login makes the line ask for the password. A password without login is not enforced.
    • 2960 switches have vty lines 0 to 15, and line vty 0 15 configures all of them. Routers usually show line vty 0 4 (router differences).
    • If the task asks for usernames instead of line passwords, use login local with a username (local users).

    #Encrypt plaintext passwords

    In global configuration mode:

    service password-encryption

    This encrypts every current and future plaintext password in the config (console, vty, enable password, username ... password) with weak type 7. enable secret and username ... secret are already hashed and are unaffected.

    Verify

    show running-config shows password 7 0822455D0A16 style lines under line con 0 and line vty 0 4, and enable secret 5 $1$....

    #Set the MOTD banner and pick a delimiter

    In global configuration mode:

    banner motd #<banner-text>#
    • The first character after motd is the delimiter. Everything up to the next copy of that character is the banner.
    • The banner text cannot contain the delimiter. If the text has a #, use a character that is not in the text, such as $, % or ^:
    banner motd $<banner-text>$
    • For a multi-line banner, type the delimiter, press Enter, type the lines, then end with the delimiter on its own line. The session looks like this:
    S1(config)#banner motd #
Enter TEXT message.  End with the character '#'.
Authorized Access Only!
Violators will be prosecuted.
#
    • show running-config displays the banner as banner motd ^CAuthorized Access Only!^C. The ^C is how IOS stores the delimiter, whatever character you typed.
    • Remove a banner with no banner motd.

    Banner text must match exactly

    Do not put spaces between the delimiter and the text unless the instructions show them; # Text # stores the leading and trailing spaces. If the instructions put the banner in quotation marks, the quotes usually only mark the text, so leave them out unless the task clearly includes them.

    #Set the switch management IP on interface vlan 1

    In global configuration mode:

    interface vlan 1
ip address <ip-address> <subnet-mask>
no shutdown
exit
    • A Layer 2 switch has one management IP, on a switch virtual interface (SVI). Physical switch ports such as Fa0/1 do not get IP addresses.
    • interface vlan 1 is administratively down by default, so no shutdown is required.
    • The SVI becomes up/up only when at least one port in VLAN 1 is connected and up. On a switch with no cables it stays up/down, which is expected.
    • If the task names another management VLAN (for example VLAN 99), use interface vlan 99. That VLAN must exist and have an active port.

    #Set the default gateway on a switch

    In global configuration mode (not interface mode):

    ip default-gateway <default-gateway>

    The switch needs this to answer devices on other networks (remote SSH or Telnet, pings from another subnet). Use the router interface IP in the same subnet as the SVI. It does not affect traffic passing through the switch.

    On a Layer 3 switch (3650) with ip routing turned on, IOS ignores ip default-gateway; that switch needs a default route instead (static routes).

    #Add interface descriptions

    In global configuration mode, for each interface the task names:

    interface <interface>
description <description>
exit

    Descriptions are free text and are graded exactly as typed when the task asks for them.

    #Shut down unused ports

    In global configuration mode:

    interface range <interface-range>
shutdown

    Check which ports are in use first with show interfaces status (status connected). Never shut a port a cable uses. Range syntax and port security are in securing device access.

    #Save the configuration

    In privileged EXEC mode:

    write memory

    copy running-config startup-config does the same but asks for a filename first. Typed by hand, it looks like this (press Enter at the question):

    S1#copy running-config startup-config
Destination filename [startup-config]?
Building configuration...
[OK]

    From configuration mode, use do write memory.

    Config Where Survives reload?
    running-config RAM No
    startup-config NVRAM Yes

    Unsaved means lost

    A reload, power cycle, module change or Power Cycle Devices wipes anything not saved, and some graded items check startup-config. Save every device before you leave it.

    #Verify the switch

    In privileged EXEC mode:

    show ip interface brief

    show running-config

    show startup-config

    What correct looks like

    show ip interface brief shows a line like Vlan1 192.168.1.2 YES manual up up. show running-config shows hostname, enable secret 5 ..., banner motd ^C...^C, line con 0 with password 7 ... and login, ip default-gateway, and service password-encryption. A PC in the same subnet can ping the SVI address.

    #Reset a switch to start over

    Only do this if the task allows it and the config is beyond repair. Fixing individual lines with no commands is usually faster. Type these by hand in privileged EXEC mode, one at a time:

    erase startup-config

    reload

    Press Enter at each [confirm]. If asked System configuration has been modified. Save? [yes/no]:, answer no, or the bad config is saved again. VLANs are stored separately in flash:vlan.dat; to remove them too, run delete flash:vlan.dat before reload.

    PreviousIOS CLI basics and modesNextSecuring device access and SSH
    PT

    Securing device access and SSH

    jump:pt-security

    Create the username before login local

    login local on the console with no username configured locks you out of the console as soon as you log out. Create the user first.

    Fast path

    1. From privileged EXEC, enter global configuration mode and set the minimum password length before any other password:

      configure terminal
security passwords min-length <min-length>

    2. Set the enable secret and encrypt plaintext passwords:

      enable secret <enable-secret>
service password-encryption

    3. Create the local admin account:

      username <admin-username> secret <admin-password>

    4. Generate RSA keys and turn on SSH version 2 (hostname must already be set):

      ip domain-name <domain-name>
crypto key generate rsa general-keys modulus 1024
ip ssh version 2

    5. Allow only SSH on the vty lines with local login (use 0 4 on a router if 0 15 is rejected):

      line vty 0 15
transport input ssh
login local
exec-timeout <timeout-minutes> 0
exit

    6. Add the idle timeout on the console and block brute-force logins:

      line console 0
exec-timeout <timeout-minutes> 0
exit
login block-for <block-seconds> attempts <attempts> within <within-seconds>

    7. Save and check SSH:

      end
write memory
show ip ssh

    The same steps as pasteable blocks are in the secure switch template and the secure router template. For a list of everything CyberPatriot tends to score on Cisco devices, see the hardening checklist.

    #Set a minimum password length

    In global configuration mode:

    security passwords min-length <min-length>
    • Any new password shorter than the value is rejected with % Password too short. This applies to the enable secret, line passwords and usernames.
    • Passwords already configured are not checked, so set this first.
    • The accepted range is 0 to 16.

    #Block brute-force logins with login block-for

    In global configuration mode:

    login block-for <block-seconds> attempts <attempts> within <within-seconds>

    Example: login block-for 120 attempts 3 within 60 means "if 3 logins fail within 60 seconds, block all Telnet and SSH logins for 120 seconds". Read the three numbers from the task carefully; the order is block time, attempts, window.

    If a 2960 in your PT version rejects the command with % Invalid input, that model does not support it. Skip it unless the task explicitly requires it on that switch.

    Verify

    show running-config | include login block shows the line. show login also shows the settings and whether the device is in quiet mode, on versions that support it.

    #Set exec-timeout and logging synchronous

    In global configuration mode:

    line console 0
exec-timeout <timeout-minutes> 0
logging synchronous
line vty 0 15
exec-timeout <timeout-minutes> 0
exit
    • exec-timeout <minutes> <seconds> logs out an idle session. 5 0 is 5 minutes. 0 0 disables the timeout and is insecure; never set it unless told to.
    • logging synchronous stops console log messages from breaking up what you are typing. It is not a security setting, but tasks often list it.

    #Use local usernames with login local

    In global configuration mode:

    username <admin-username> secret <admin-password>
line vty 0 15
login local
exit
    Line command Authenticates with
    login The line's own password
    login local A username and secret from the local database
    login with no password set vty refuses connections (Password required, but none set)
    no login Nothing at all (insecure; never configure unless told)
    • username <admin-username> secret <admin-password> stores a hash. username ... password ... stores plaintext (type 7 after service password-encryption). Use secret unless told otherwise.
    • username <admin-username> privilege 15 secret <admin-password> logs the user straight into privileged EXEC. Add privilege 15 only if the task asks.
    • Remove an unauthorized or default account with no username <username>.

    #Configure SSH step by step

    Every step is required. Missing any one makes SSH fail.

    Step Command Why
    1 hostname <hostname> RSA keys need a hostname other than the default Router or Switch
    2 ip domain-name <domain-name> The key name is built from hostname and domain
    3 crypto key generate rsa general-keys modulus 1024 Creates the keys and enables SSH
    4 ip ssh version 2 Allows only SSH version 2 (needs a key of at least 768 bits)
    5 username <admin-username> secret <admin-password> The account to log in with
    6 line vty 0 15, transport input ssh, login local Allow only SSH, authenticate with the local account

    In global configuration mode:

    hostname <hostname>
ip domain-name <domain-name>
crypto key generate rsa general-keys modulus 1024
ip ssh version 2
username <admin-username> secret <admin-password>
line vty 0 15
transport input ssh
login local
end
write memory

    Key generation prints something like this (example names R1 and ccna-lab.com):

    The name for the keys will be: R1.ccna-lab.com
% The key modulus size is 1024 bits
% Generating 1024 bit RSA keys, keys will be non-exportable...[OK]
%SSH-5-ENABLED: SSH 1.99 has been enabled
    • If you type only crypto key generate rsa, IOS asks How many bits in the modulus [512]:. Type 1024, or 2048 if the task says so. A 512-bit key does not allow SSH version 2.
    • Use line vty 0 4 on a router whose vty range ends at 4. Check the range with line vty 0 ?.
    • Some tasks also list ip ssh time-out 60 and ip ssh authentication-retries 2 (global configuration).
    • A switch needs a working management IP (SVI up, plus ip default-gateway for remote subnets) before SSH can reach it.

    #Choose the transport input setting

    Command Allows
    transport input ssh SSH only (the usual requirement; this disables Telnet)
    transport input telnet Telnet only
    transport input telnet ssh Both
    transport input all All protocols
    transport input none No remote access on these lines

    #Verify SSH

    In privileged EXEC mode:

    show ip ssh

    You should see:

    SSH Enabled - version 2.0
Authentication timeout: 120 secs; Authentication retries: 3

    version 1.99 means keys exist but ip ssh version 2 is missing. SSH Disabled means no keys.

    Check the vty lines:

    show running-config | begin line vty

    Then test from a PC (Desktop > Command Prompt):

    ssh -l <admin-username> <ip-address>

    Enter the password when prompted. You should land at R1> (or R1# with privilege 15); type exit to close. Then try telnet <ip-address>. With transport input ssh it must be refused.

    Pipe section is unreliable in Packet Tracer

    show running-config | section line vty is rejected on some PT models and versions. Use | begin line vty or | include instead, or read the full show running-config.

    #Configure port security on access ports

    Fast path

    1. From privileged EXEC, select the port and make it a static access port:

      configure terminal
interface <interface>
switchport mode access

    2. Turn on port security and set the limits the task gives:

      switchport port-security
switchport port-security maximum <max-macs>
switchport port-security mac-address sticky
switchport port-security violation <violation-mode>
end

    3. Ping from the attached PC so the sticky MAC is learned, then save:

      write memory
    • switchport mode access must come first. On a port still in the default dynamic mode, IOS rejects port security with Command rejected: FastEthernet0/1 is a dynamic port.
    • switchport port-security alone turns it on with defaults: maximum 1 MAC, violation shutdown.
    • mac-address sticky learns connected MACs and writes them into the running-config. Save to keep them.
    • For a static MAC instead of sticky, use switchport port-security mac-address <mac-address> (format aaaa.bbbb.cccc; get it from the PC's ipconfig /all).
    Violation mode Drops traffic Logs and counts the violation Shuts the port (err-disabled)
    shutdown (default) Yes Yes Yes
    restrict Yes Yes No
    protect Yes No No

    Verify port security

    show port-security interface <interface> shows Port Security Enabled, Port Status Secure-up, the violation mode, maximum MAC addresses, sticky MAC count and violation count. show port-security address lists the learned MACs. Sticky MACs appear only after the PC sends traffic.

    #Recover an err-disabled port

    Remove the offending device first, or the port shuts again. Then, in global configuration mode:

    interface <interface>
shutdown
no shutdown

    #Shut down unused switch ports

    In global configuration mode (example ports; use the ones that are not in use):

    interface range fa0/2 - 4 , fa0/7 - 24 , g0/2
shutdown
    • Find used ports first: show interfaces status (connected or notconnect) or show ip interface brief.
    • Range syntax: a space on each side of the hyphen, groups separated by commas. A range cannot cross interface types; add a comma group instead.
    • Hardening tasks sometimes also move unused ports to an unused VLAN. Inside the same range, add switchport mode access and switchport access vlan <vlan-id> (create the VLAN first with vlan <vlan-id> in global configuration).

    #Disable unused services

    Command (global config unless noted) Effect Notes
    no ip http server Turns off the HTTP management server If PT rejects it, the model has no HTTP server; skip it
    no ip http secure-server Turns off HTTPS management Same
    no cdp run Disables CDP globally Only if the task says so; CDP helps verification
    no cdp enable (interface) Disables CDP on one port For example the port facing an untrusted network
    no ip domain-lookup Stops DNS lookups of typos Usability

    Do not disable what the task needs

    Turning off CDP or HTTP is good practice, but if the scenario uses CDP to discover neighbors or uses a web interface, leave it on unless instructed.

    #Pick the right banner type

    Banner Shown Typical use
    banner motd #<banner-text># On connection, before the login prompt Legal warning (the ITN default)
    banner login #<banner-text># After the MOTD, before the username and password prompt Login warning
    banner exec #<banner-text># After a successful login Post-login notice

    Configure exactly the banner type the task names. With SSH, the MOTD banner may appear after authentication. Some Packet Tracer switch models may reject banner login; check with banner ? and use banner motd unless the task names the login banner.

    PreviousInitial switch configurationNextRouter basic configuration
    PT

    Router basic configuration

    jump:pt-router

    Fast path

    1. In privileged EXEC mode, list the interface names this model uses:

      show ip interface brief

    2. Enter global configuration mode and configure each LAN interface from the addressing table:

      configure terminal
interface <interface>
description <description>
ip address <ip-address> <subnet-mask>
no shutdown
exit

    3. Apply the passwords, banner and SSH the task asks for (secure router template).

    4. If the task has IPv6, turn on IPv6 routing and add the addresses (IPv6).

    5. Save:

      end
write memory

    6. Ping the router interface from a PC on that LAN.

    #Router differences from a switch

    Everything in initial switch configuration and securing device access applies to routers too (hostname, enable secret, console and vty, banner, service password-encryption, SSH, save). The differences:

    Item Switch (2960) Router (ISR)
    Where the IP goes interface vlan 1 (SVI) Each physical interface (G0/0, G0/1, ...)
    Default gateway ip default-gateway <default-gateway> Not used; routers use routes (ip route)
    Interface default state Physical ports up Every interface administratively down until no shutdown
    vty lines line vty 0 15 Often line vty 0 4 (check with line vty 0 ?)
    First prompt Switch> Router> (may ask the initial configuration dialog; answer no)

    #Interface names by router model

    Run show ip interface brief to see the exact names on the device in front of you.

    Model Built-in LAN ports Notation Serial (if a module is added)
    1841 Fa0/0, Fa0/1 slot/port S0/0/0, S0/0/1 (WIC-2T)
    1941 G0/0, G0/1 slot/port S0/0/0, S0/0/1 (HWIC-2T)
    2901 G0/0, G0/1 slot/port S0/0/0, S0/0/1
    2911 G0/0, G0/1, G0/2 slot/port S0/0/0, S0/0/1
    ISR4321 G0/0/0, G0/0/1 slot/subslot/port S0/1/0, S0/1/1 (NIM-2T)
    ISR4331 G0/0/0, G0/0/1, G0/0/2 slot/subslot/port S0/1/0, S0/1/1 (NIM-2T)

    ISR4321 and ISR4331 use three numbers

    On an ISR4321 or ISR4331, interface g0/0 gives % Invalid input; use interface g0/0/0. On a 1941, 2901 or 2911, g0/0/0 is invalid; use g0/0. Serial numbering depends on which slot holds the module, so confirm with show ip interface brief.

    #Configure a router LAN interface

    In global configuration mode:

    interface <interface>
description <description>
ip address <ip-address> <subnet-mask>
no shutdown
exit

    When the link comes up you see:

    %LINK-5-CHANGED: Interface GigabitEthernet0/0, changed state to up
%LINEPROTO-5-UPDOWN: Line protocol on Interface GigabitEthernet0/0, changed state to up
    • The router interface IP is the default gateway for every host on that LAN.
    • Each router interface must be in a different subnet. IOS rejects an overlap with % 192.168.10.0 overlaps with GigabitEthernet0/1.
    • The link goes up/up only when something powered on is cabled to it.

    Verify

    show ip interface brief shows the interface with its IP and up up. A PC on that LAN can ping the interface IP.

    #Add IPv6 to router interfaces

    In global configuration mode, turn on IPv6 routing once:

    ipv6 unicast-routing

    Then, for each interface:

    interface <interface>
ipv6 address <ipv6-address>/<prefix-length>
ipv6 address <link-local-address> link-local
no shutdown
exit
    • ipv6 unicast-routing turns on IPv6 forwarding and makes the router send Router Advertisements, which hosts set to Automatic (SLAAC) need.
    • The prefix length goes directly on the address (/64, no space). There is no mask.
    • ipv6 address fe80::1 link-local replaces the auto-generated EUI-64 link-local address with an easy one. The same link-local can go on every interface of one router, because link-locals only matter on their own link.
    • Hosts can use the router's link-local (for example fe80::1) as their IPv6 default gateway.
    • For an EUI-64 global address, if a task asks: ipv6 address 2001:db8:acad:1::/64 eui-64.

    Verify IPv6

    show ipv6 interface brief lists each interface as [up/up] with its FE80::1 link-local and global unicast address. show ipv6 route shows C and L entries. From a PC, ping the router's global address.

    IPv6 on a 2960 switch SVI

    A 2960 needs a dual-stack SDM template before interface vlan 1 accepts an IPv6 address. In global configuration mode run sdm prefer dual-ipv4-and-ipv6 default, then end, write memory and reload. Only do this if the task asks for an IPv6 address on the switch.

    #Add a loopback interface

    In global configuration mode:

    interface loopback 0
ip address <ip-address> <subnet-mask>

    Loopbacks are virtual and always up (no cable, no no shutdown needed). Labs use them to simulate networks or as a stable test address. Any mask is allowed; 255.255.255.255 is common.

    #Serial links and the DCE clock rate

    In global configuration mode (example values):

    interface s0/0/0
ip address 10.0.0.1 255.255.255.252
clock rate 128000
no shutdown
    • The router you clicked first with the Serial DCE cable is the DCE side. Only the DCE side needs clock rate.
    • Check which end is DCE with show controllers s0/0/0 (look for DCE V.35, clock rate 128000 or DTE V.35).
    • If the task does not mention serial links, you do not need this.

    #Static and default routes

    All are entered in global configuration mode. Floating routes, IPv6 next hops and verification are in static and default routes.

    Default route (send everything unknown to the next hop):

    ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 <next-hop>

    Static route to one remote network:

    ip route <network-address> <subnet-mask> <next-hop>

    IPv6 default route:

    ipv6 route ::/0 <next-hop>

    #Read show ip route

    Example output:

    R1#show ip route
Codes: L - local, C - connected, S - static, ...
Gateway of last resort is 209.165.200.226 to network 0.0.0.0

     192.168.10.0/24 is variably subnetted, 2 subnets, 2 masks
C       192.168.10.0/24 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
L       192.168.10.1/32 is directly connected, GigabitEthernet0/0
S*   0.0.0.0/0 [1/0] via 209.165.200.226
    Code Meaning
    C Directly connected network (interface is up/up with an IP)
    L The router's own interface address (/32)
    S Static route
    S* Static default route (gateway of last resort)
    O, D, R OSPF, EIGRP, RIP learned routes

    A missing C route for a LAN means that interface is not up/up or has no IP.

    #Run a DHCP server on the router

    Only if the task asks. In global configuration mode, exclude the static addresses first:

    ip dhcp excluded-address <first-excluded> <last-excluded>

    Then create the pool:

    ip dhcp pool <pool-name>
network <network-address> <subnet-mask>
default-router <default-gateway>
dns-server <dns-server>
exit

    Verify with show ip dhcp binding after a PC is set to DHCP. Relay, gotchas and expected output are in DHCPv4 on a router.

    PreviousSecuring device access and SSHNextPCs, laptops and servers
    PT

    PCs, laptops and servers

    jump:pt-end-devices

    Fast path

    1. Click the PC, laptop or server and open Desktop > IP Configuration.
    2. Select Static (or DHCP if the task says so).
    3. Type the IPv4 Address and Subnet Mask from the addressing table. Overwrite the mask PT fills in.
    4. Type the Default Gateway (the router interface on this LAN) and the DNS Server if given.
    5. Close the window. There is no Save button.

    6. Open Desktop > Command Prompt and test:

      ping <default-gateway>

    #Set a static IPv4 address

    Desktop > IP Configuration, IPv4 area:

    1. Select Static.
    2. Enter IPv4 Address, Subnet Mask, Default Gateway and DNS Server from the addressing table.
    3. Values apply as you type or leave the field. Close the window when done.

    The Config tab sets the same values: Config > Settings (gateway, DNS) and Config > FastEthernet0 (IP, mask).

    Watch the gateway field

    The default gateway is the router interface IP in the PC's own subnet. Never use the switch management IP; a Layer 2 switch does not route. With a wrong or empty gateway the PC can still ping its own subnet but no other network, which is an easy point to lose.

    PT fills in a classful mask (255.255.255.0 for 192.x, 255.0.0.0 for 10.x) when you click into the mask field. Always overwrite it with the mask from the addressing table.

    #Use DHCP on a PC

    Desktop > IP Configuration > DHCP. The PC shows DHCP request successful and fills the fields.

    If it shows DHCP failed. APIPA is being used (a 169.254.x.x address), no DHCP server answered. Check the link, the server's DHCP service or the router pool, and the wireless association. Click Static and then DHCP again (or run ipconfig /renew) to retry; Fast Forward Time helps.

    #Set IPv6 on a PC

    Desktop > IP Configuration, IPv6 Configuration area:

    Option Use
    Static Type the IPv6 address, the prefix length (64) in its own box, the IPv6 gateway (often the router's FE80::1) and the IPv6 DNS server
    Automatic SLAAC from the router's Router Advertisements (the router needs ipv6 unicast-routing)

    The link-local address is generated automatically and shown read-only. Verify in the Command Prompt: ipconfig shows the IPv6 address, link-local and gateway.

    #Add a wireless card to a PC or laptop

    1. Open the device and click the Physical tab.
    2. Click the power button on the device picture to turn it off.
    3. Drag the existing Ethernet module out of its slot onto the module list (PC: PT-HOST-NM-1CFE; laptop: PT-LAPTOP-NM-1CFE).
    4. Drag in the wireless module: WMP300N for a PC, WPC300N for a laptop (both 2.4 GHz Wireless-N). For a 5 GHz-only network, use the matching AC module from the list.
    5. Turn the power on.

    PT refuses to insert or remove modules while the device is on.

    #Connect a wireless client to an SSID

    Open the client, Config > Wireless0, and set:

    Field Value
    SSID Exact SSID (case-sensitive)
    Authentication WPA2-PSK (match the router)
    PSK Pass Phrase Exact passphrase
    Encryption Type AES
    IP Configuration DHCP (or Static per the task)

    Desktop > PC Wireless > Connect tab. Select the SSID (click Refresh if it is missing), click Connect, choose the security type, enter the pre-shared key and click Connect.

    Verify the client joined

    A wireless link line appears between the client and the wireless router or AP. Desktop > IP Configuration shows an address from the router's DHCP range (not 169.254.x.x), and ping to the router LAN IP succeeds.

    #Command Prompt commands

    Desktop > Command Prompt. Type ? to list what your PT version supports.

    Command Use
    ipconfig IPv4 and IPv6 address, mask, gateway
    ipconfig /all Adds the MAC (Physical Address), DNS server, DHCP server
    ipconfig /release, ipconfig /renew Drop and re-request a DHCP lease
    ping <ip-address> Test reachability (4 echoes)
    ping -t <ip-address> Ping until Ctrl+C
    ping -n <count> <ip-address> Ping a set number of times
    tracert <ip-address> List each router hop to the destination
    arp -a Show the PC's ARP cache (IP to MAC)
    arp -d Clear the ARP cache
    nslookup <hostname> Query DNS for a name
    ssh -l <admin-username> <ip-address> SSH to a router or switch (lowercase L)
    telnet <ip-address> Telnet to a router or switch
    ftp <ip-address> FTP to a server
    netstat Show connections

    #Console into a device from a PC

    1. Connect a Console cable from the PC's RS 232 port to the device's Console port.
    2. On the PC, open Desktop > Terminal, keep the defaults (9600 bits per second, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, no flow control) and click OK.
    3. Press Enter. You get the device CLI, the same as its CLI tab.

    Tasks that say "access the switch through the console from PC-A" usually expect this cable to exist.

    #Server services

    All of these are on the server's Services tab.

    #HTTP and HTTPS

    Services > HTTP: turn HTTP and HTTPS on or off. The File Manager lists index.html and other pages; click edit to change content. Test from a PC: Desktop > Web Browser > http:// followed by the server IP or DNS name.

    #DHCP server on a server

    Services > DHCP:

    Field Value
    Interface FastEthernet0
    Service On
    Pool Name The task's pool name (or edit the default serverPool)
    Default Gateway Router IP for that LAN
    DNS Server DNS server IP
    Start IP Address First address to hand out
    Subnet Mask LAN mask
    Maximum Number of Users How many leases

    Click Add for a new pool, or Save to update the selected pool. The server itself needs a static IP.

    Click Save or Add

    Typing values without clicking Save or Add leaves the old pool settings. Select the pool in the list, change it, then click Save.

    #DNS records

    Services > DNS > DNS Service On. Enter the Name (for example www.example.com), Type A Record and Address (server IP), then click Add. PCs need this server as their DNS Server. Verify with nslookup www.example.com on a PC, or open the name in the Web Browser.

    #FTP users

    Services > FTP > Service On. Enter Username and Password, tick the permissions (Write, Read, Delete, Rename, List) and click Add. Remove an account by selecting it and clicking Remove. A default cisco/cisco account exists; remove it only if the task says so.

    #Email

    Services > EMAIL: set the Domain Name and add users with passwords. On the PC, open Desktop > Email and configure the account with the incoming and outgoing server.

    Host firewall

    PCs and servers have Desktop > Firewall (IPv4) and IPv6 Firewall. If a server suddenly stops answering pings or web requests, check whether a rule there blocks it.

    PreviousRouter basic configurationNextWireless router and access point
    PT

    Wireless router and access point

    jump:pt-wireless

    Fast path

    1. Open the wireless router and click the GUI tab.
    2. Setup > Basic Setup: set the router IP, mask and DHCP range from the task. Click Save Settings.
    3. Wireless > Basic Wireless Settings: set the Network Name (SSID) and SSID Broadcast as asked. Click Save Settings.
    4. Wireless > Wireless Security: Security Mode WPA2 Personal, Encryption AES, the exact passphrase. Click Save Settings.
    5. Administration > Management: set the Router Password. Click Save Settings.
    6. Reconnect every wireless client with the new SSID and passphrase (connect a client).

    #Which wireless device is this

    Device What it is How to configure
    WRT300N Linksys home wireless router (router, 4-port switch, AP and DHCP server in one) GUI tab, Config tab, or a PC's Web Browser
    HomeRouter-PT-AC Newer home wireless router with 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz radios GUI tab (same layout, extra 5 GHz settings) or Config tab
    AccessPoint-PT (and -A, -N, -AC) Access point only: bridges wireless to the wired LAN; no routing, no DHCP Config tab > Port 1

    Factory defaults on the WRT300N and HomeRouter-PT-AC: LAN IP 192.168.0.1 and web login admin / admin. The default SSID is usually Default with no wireless security, and DHCP usually starts at 192.168.0.100. The activity author may have changed any of these, so read the current values in the Config tab before relying on them.

    #Configure through the GUI tab

    Click Save Settings on every page

    Each GUI page has a Save Settings button at the bottom. Leaving the page without clicking it discards your changes. Changing the router IP or wireless settings can briefly disconnect clients; that is normal.

    #Setup > Basic Setup for Internet, router IP and DHCP

    Area Field Notes
    Internet Setup Internet Connection Type Automatic Configuration - DHCP (default), Static IP (Internet IP, mask, gateway, DNS from the task), or PPPoE
    Network Setup, Router IP IP Address, Subnet Mask The LAN gateway address for wireless and wired clients
    Network Setup, DHCP Server Settings DHCP Server Enabled/Disabled Leave Enabled unless the task says otherwise
    Start IP Address Last octet of the first lease (for example 100)
    Maximum number of Users Number of leases
    Static DNS 1-3 DNS servers handed to clients

    Click Save Settings.

    #Set the SSID on the basic wireless settings page

    Field Typical task value
    Network Mode Mixed (default); Disabled turns the radio off
    Network Name (SSID) Exact SSID from the task (case-sensitive)
    Radio Band, Wide Channel, Standard Channel Change only if asked (for example channel 6)
    SSID Broadcast Enabled or Disabled as asked; disabled hides the SSID, so clients must type it

    Path: Wireless > Basic Wireless Settings. Click Save Settings. On the HomeRouter-PT-AC, set each band the task names (2.4 GHz and the 5 GHz radios).

    #Set WPA2 on the wireless security page

    Field Value
    Security Mode WPA2 Personal
    Encryption AES
    Passphrase Exact passphrase from the task (8 to 63 characters)

    Path: Wireless > Wireless Security. Click Save Settings. Avoid WEP and WPA unless the task requires them; both are weak.

    #Administration > Management for the router password

    Set Router Password and Re-enter to Confirm to the task's value, then click Save Settings. After this, the web login from a PC browser uses the new password.

    #MAC filtering and access restrictions

    • Wireless > Wireless MAC Filter: Enabled, choose Permit PCs listed below (allow list) or Prevent, enter the client MACs (from each client's ipconfig /all), Save Settings.
    • Access Restrictions: policies that block devices or times. Use only when asked.

    #Configure through the Config tab

    Open the wireless router and click Config.

    Page Settings
    INTERFACE > Internet DHCP, Static or PPPoE for the WAN side
    INTERFACE > LAN Router IP and mask
    INTERFACE > Wireless (one page per band on the HomeRouter-PT-AC) SSID, channel, Authentication (WPA2-PSK), PSK Pass Phrase (8 to 63 characters), Encryption Type (AES)

    Config-tab values and GUI-tab values are the same settings; use whichever the activity allows.

    #Configure from a PC web browser

    1. Cable a PC to a LAN port (Ethernet 1-4, not Internet) of the wireless router, or join it wirelessly, and set the PC to DHCP.
    2. On the PC, open Desktop > Web Browser and go to http://192.168.0.1 (or the router's current LAN IP).
    3. Log in with admin / admin, or the password set in Administration.
    4. Use the same pages as the GUI tab, with Save Settings on each page.

    #Configure an access point

    Open the AccessPoint-PT and go to Config > Port 1:

    Field Value
    SSID Exact value
    Channel As asked
    Authentication WPA2-PSK
    PSK Pass Phrase Exact passphrase
    Encryption Type AES

    The AP has no IP routing and no DHCP. Wireless clients get addresses from the DHCP server on the wired LAN the AP is plugged into.

    #Verify wireless clients

    Clients do not reconnect after a security change

    After you change the SSID, security mode or passphrase, reconfigure every client with the new values (Config > Wireless0 or PC Wireless). A client with the old key shows no wireless link.

    PreviousPCs, laptops and serversNextWhich cable to use
    PT

    Which cable to use

    jump:pt-cabling

    Fast path

    1. Pick the cable from the table below: unlike devices use straight-through, like devices use crossover.
    2. Click Connections, then the cable type by its tooltip name.
    3. Click the first device and choose the exact port the task names, then the second device and its port.
    4. Wait for green link lights (amber means Spanning Tree is converging; click Fast Forward Time).
    5. If a light stays red, work through why the link is red.

    #Which cable to use

    Rule of thumb: unlike devices use straight-through, like devices use crossover. PCs and routers are one group (they transmit on the same pins); switches and hubs are the other.

    From To Cable in Packet Tracer
    PC, laptop, server, printer Switch or hub Copper Straight-Through
    Switch Router (Ethernet) Copper Straight-Through
    Wireless router LAN port (Ethernet 1-4) PC or laptop Copper Straight-Through
    Wireless router LAN port (Ethernet 1-4) Switch Copper Cross-Over (PT treats these LAN ports like switch ports; if the link stays red, try the other copper type)
    Switch Switch Copper Cross-Over
    Hub Switch or hub Copper Cross-Over
    Router Router (Ethernet) Copper Cross-Over
    PC Router (Ethernet) Copper Cross-Over
    PC PC Copper Cross-Over
    PC RS 232 port Router or switch Console port Console
    Fiber port (FX, SFP, GLC modules) Fiber port Fiber
    Router serial port Router serial port Serial DCE (click the DCE router first) or Serial DTE
    Cable modem Cloud coaxial port Coaxial
    DSL modem Cloud modem port Phone

    Auto-MDIX does not save you from the grader

    Modern Cisco switches use auto-MDIX, so in a real lab either copper cable usually works. Packet Tracer may still show the wrong copper cable as a red link, and even when the link comes up, the grader can check the cable type. Use the cable from the table and the exact ports in the instructions.

    Automatic connection type

    Automatically Choose Connection Type picks the right cable but uses the first free port, which may not be the port the task requires. Use it only when the task does not name ports.

    #Port naming

    Device Ports Name in IOS
    Catalyst 2960-24TT 24 x 10/100, 2 x Gigabit FastEthernet0/1 to 0/24 (Fa0/1), GigabitEthernet0/1 to 0/2 (G0/1)
    Catalyst 3650-24PS 24 x Gigabit, 4 SFP uplinks GigabitEthernet1/0/1 to 1/0/24, GigabitEthernet1/1/1 to 1/1/4
    ISR 1941, 2901 Gigabit G0/0, G0/1
    ISR 2911 Gigabit G0/0, G0/1, G0/2
    ISR4321 Gigabit G0/0/0, G0/0/1
    ISR4331 Gigabit G0/0/0, G0/0/1, G0/0/2
    PC, laptop, server One NIC FastEthernet0 (or GigabitEthernet0), Wireless0 with a wireless card
    WRT300N wireless router LAN and WAN Ethernet 1 to 4 (LAN), Internet (WAN)

    The pattern is type slot/port or type slot/subslot/port. Abbreviations: fa, g or gi, s or se, lo, vlan.

    Use the Internet port only for the ISP side

    On a wireless router, plug the LAN (switches, PCs) into Ethernet 1-4. The Internet port is the WAN uplink. A LAN cable in the Internet port leaves clients unable to reach the rest of the network.

    #Why is the link red

    #Delete and redo a wrong cable

    Click the Delete tool (X), click the cable, then reconnect with the correct type and ports. Press Esc to return to the Select tool.

    PreviousWireless router and access pointNextVerification commands
    PT

    Verification commands

    jump:pt-verify

    Fast path

    1. In privileged EXEC mode, check every interface's IP and state:

      show ip interface brief

    2. Read the configuration and tick each requirement:

      show running-config

    3. Confirm it is saved (startup-config is not present means it is not):

      show startup-config

    4. From a PC Command Prompt, ping the gateway and every host the task names.

    #Verification command table

    Command Shows Look for
    show running-config Active configuration in RAM Every configured item: hostname, secret, lines, banner, IPs, SSH, usernames, descriptions
    show startup-config Saved configuration in NVRAM Same as running-config; if it says startup-config is not present or differs, save
    show ip interface brief One line per interface: IP, method, status, protocol up up on used interfaces; correct IP; administratively down means shutdown
    show interfaces <interface> Detailed Layer 1 and 2 status is up, line protocol is up, MAC (address is), errors, Description: line
    show interfaces status Switch ports: status, VLAN, duplex, speed connected, notconnect, disabled, err-disabled
    show vlan brief VLANs and their access ports Ports in the expected VLAN (all in VLAN 1 by default)
    show mac address-table MACs learned per port PC MACs on the right ports (after the PC sends traffic)
    show version IOS version, uptime, model, RAM, config register Model and IOS image; Configuration register is 0x2102 on routers
    show flash: Files in flash IOS image file, vlan.dat on switches
    show ip ssh SSH status SSH Enabled - version 2.0
    show ssh Active SSH sessions Your test session
    show users Who is logged in on which line con 0, vty 0 sessions
    show history Recent commands in this session Recall what you did
    show port-security Summary of secure ports MaxSecureAddr, CurrentAddr, SecurityViolation, Action
    show port-security interface <interface> Port security detail Enabled, Secure-up, violation mode, maximum, sticky count
    show port-security address Secure MACs Sticky or static MACs on each port
    show ipv6 interface brief IPv6 addresses per interface [up/up], link-local FE80::1, global unicast address
    show ip route IPv4 routing table C and L per configured interface; S* if a default route is set
    show ipv6 route IPv6 routing table C and L IPv6 routes
    show cdp neighbors Directly connected Cisco devices Neighbor name, local port, remote port; confirms cabling
    show cdp neighbors detail Adds neighbor IPs and IOS Neighbor management IP
    show clock Device time Only if the task sets the clock (clock set in privileged EXEC)
    show arp or show ip arp Router or switch ARP table IP-to-MAC mappings of hosts it talked to
    show login login block-for status (not on every PT version) Configured block-for values
    show controllers <interface> Serial cable info DCE or DTE, and the clock rate
    show ip dhcp binding Router DHCP leases Clients and their IPs
    ping <ip-address> ICMP reachability !!!!! success, . timeout, U unreachable; .!!!! is normal (ARP on the first try)
    traceroute <ip-address> Each hop to the destination Where the path stops (break with Ctrl+Shift+6)

    #Commands Packet Tracer does not support

    Support varies by device model and PT version. If one of these gives % Invalid input, use the fallback:

    • show interfaces description: use show running-config, or show interfaces <interface> and read its Description: line.
    • show running-config | section <text>: use show running-config | begin <text> or | include <text>.
    • show running-config interface <interface>: use show running-config | begin interface <interface>.
    • banner login on a switch: check banner ?; use banner motd unless the task names the login banner.

    When any command gives % Invalid input and you are sure of the mode and spelling, type the first word and ? to see what that PT model offers.

    #Filter long output

    Add a filter after the command. Filters are case-sensitive and match anywhere in the line.

    • | include <text> shows only matching lines, for example show running-config | include hostname.
    • | begin <text> starts the output at the first match, for example show running-config | begin line con.
    • | exclude <text> hides matching lines, for example show running-config | exclude !.

    #Read show ip interface brief

    Example output:

    S1#show ip interface brief
Interface              IP-Address      OK? Method Status                Protocol
FastEthernet0/1        unassigned      YES manual up                    up
FastEthernet0/2        unassigned      YES manual down                  down
FastEthernet0/3        unassigned      YES manual administratively down down
Vlan1                  192.168.1.2     YES manual up                    up
    Status and protocol Meaning Fix
    up / up Working Nothing
    down / down No cable, or the other end is down Connect the cable; check the far end
    administratively down / down shutdown is configured no shutdown
    up / down Layer 1 is fine, Layer 2 problem; for Vlan1, no active port in the VLAN Connect or enable a port in that VLAN

    #Ping from a PC or from IOS

    From Command Success looks like
    PC Command Prompt ping 192.168.1.1 Reply from 192.168.1.1: bytes=32 time<1ms TTL=255 four times, Lost = 0
    PC Command Prompt tracert 192.168.20.10 Numbered hops ending at the destination
    Router or switch ping 192.168.1.10 Success rate is 100 percent (5/5)
    Router or switch traceroute 192.168.20.10 Hop list ending at the destination
    Router (IPv6) ping 2001:db8:acad:1::10 !!!!!

    PT

    Copy-paste config templates

    jump:pt-templates

    Fast path

    1. Pick the template that matches the device and task below.
    2. Fill in the placeholders on this page (or copy the block into a text editor and replace every <...> value, angle brackets included). Delete any line the task did not ask for.
    3. On the device, open the CLI tab, press Enter and type enable (plus the enable password if one is set) so the prompt ends in #.
    4. Click Paste below the console window.
    5. Scroll back and fix every line that starts with % by hand.
    6. Verify with show running-config and show ip interface brief.

    A leftover placeholder is a wrong value

    If you paste hostname <hostname> unfilled, IOS rejects it or stores the wrong text. Search your edited text for < before pasting. Values are case-sensitive.

    Placeholder values you type on this page fill every block that uses the same name. Update them when you move to the next device.

    #Why the templates end with write memory

    Every template starts with configure terminal (so you paste it from privileged EXEC) and ends with end and write memory. copy running-config startup-config asks Destination filename [startup-config]? and waits for an answer, so in a pasted block it would take the next pasted line as the filename. write memory saves to startup-config without asking anything. If you type copy run start by hand, press Enter at the question.

    RSA keys that already exist

    If the device already has RSA keys, crypto key generate rsa general-keys modulus 1024 asks Do you really want to replace them? [yes/no]: and swallows the next pasted line. Run show ip ssh first. If SSH is already enabled, delete the crypto line from the template and type it by hand afterwards (answer yes).

    #Secure switch baseline template

    Replace these first:

    Placeholder Example Notes
    <hostname> S1 Exact hostname
    <min-length> 10 Delete the line if no minimum length is asked
    <enable-secret> class12345 Privileged EXEC password; must meet the minimum length
    <banner-text> text from the task Must not contain #; if it does, change both # delimiters to $
    <admin-username>, <admin-password> admin, Admin1Pa55 Local user for SSH; the password must meet the minimum length
    <block-seconds>, <attempts>, <within-seconds> 120, 3, 60 Delete the line if not asked. If the 2960 rejects it, skip it
    <console-password> cisco12345 Must meet the minimum length. For console local login, replace password and login with login local
    <timeout-minutes> 5 Idle timeout in minutes
    <domain-name> ccna-lab.com Required for SSH keys
    <ip-address>, <subnet-mask> 192.168.1.2, 255.255.255.0 SVI address from the addressing table
    <default-gateway> 192.168.1.1 Router LAN IP 
    configure terminal
hostname <hostname>
no ip domain-lookup
security passwords min-length <min-length>
enable secret <enable-secret>
service password-encryption
banner motd #<banner-text>#
username <admin-username> secret <admin-password>
login block-for <block-seconds> attempts <attempts> within <within-seconds>
line console 0
password <console-password>
login
exec-timeout <timeout-minutes> 0
logging synchronous
exit
ip domain-name <domain-name>
crypto key generate rsa general-keys modulus 1024
ip ssh version 2
line vty 0 15
transport input ssh
login local
exec-timeout <timeout-minutes> 0
exit
interface vlan 1
ip address <ip-address> <subnet-mask>
no shutdown
exit
ip default-gateway <default-gateway>
end
write memory

    If the task wants plain vty passwords instead of SSH, replace transport input ssh and login local under line vty 0 15 with password <vty-password> and login.

    #Secure router baseline template

    Replace these first (the rest are as in the switch template):

    Placeholder Example Notes

    <interface>, <interface-2> g0/0, g0/1 g0/0, g0/1 on 1941/2901/2911; g0/0/0, g0/0/1 on ISR4321/4331
    <description>, <description-2> Link to LAN-A Exact text; delete the line if not asked
    <ip-address>, <subnet-mask> 192.168.10.1, 255.255.255.0 First interface, from the addressing table
    <ip-address-2>, <subnet-mask-2> 192.168.20.1, 255.255.255.0 Second interface 
    configure terminal

    configure terminal

    #Shut down unused switch ports template

    Placeholder Example Notes
    <interface-range> fa0/2 - 4 , fa0/7 - 24 , g0/2 Only ports NOT in use; check show interfaces status first (anything connected stays up)
