    PT

    Device models and port names for later rounds

    jump:pt-adv-models

    Fast path

    1. Hover over each device and write down the model.

    2. On every router and switch, list the real interface names before you type any interface command:

      show ip interface brief

    3. On a 3650 that is powered off, add the power supply in the Physical tab (how).

    4. Check how many vty lines exist before configuring them:

      configure terminal
line vty 0 ?

    #Model cheat sheet

    Model Role Ports in PT vty lines Notes
    2960-24TT Layer 2 access switch Fa0/1-24, G0/1-2 0-15 No ip routing. Management IP on one SVI plus ip default-gateway
    3650-24PS Layer 3 switch G1/0/1-24, G1/1/1-4 0-15 Ships with an empty power bay. Needs ip routing to route between VLANs
    3560-24PS Layer 3 switch (older labs) Fa0/1-24, G0/1-2 0-15 Needs switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q before switchport mode trunk
    1941 Router G0/0, G0/1 0-4 (some versions 0-15) Add an HWIC-2T for serial S0/0/0-1
    2911 Router G0/0, G0/1, G0/2 0-4 (some versions 0-15) Serial modules in slot 0 give S0/0/0
    ISR4321 Router G0/0/0, G0/0/1 0-4 Three-number names. NIM-2T gives S0/1/0-1
    ISR4331 Router G0/0/0, G0/0/1, G0/0/2 0-4 Three-number names. NIM-2T gives S0/1/0-1
    WLC-2504, WLC-3504 Wireless LAN controller Gigabit ports, hover to read n/a Configured from a PC web browser over HTTPS (WLC)
    LAP (3702i) Lightweight access point G0 n/a Gets an IP by DHCP and joins the WLC with CAPWAP
    WRT300N, HomeRouter-PT-AC Home wireless router Internet, Ethernet 1-4 n/a GUI tab (wireless router)

    Interface names are the top cause of Invalid input

    interface g0/0 fails on an ISR4331 and interface g0/0/0 fails on a 2911. On a 3650 the ports are g1/0/1 and up. Copy names from show ip interface brief, not from memory.

    #Feature support by model in Packet Tracer

    What usually works in PT. Versions differ, so test an unsure keyword with ? before building a plan around it.

    Feature 2960 3650 ISR routers
    VLANs, trunks, port security, STP, EtherChannel Yes Yes No (802.1Q subinterfaces for router-on-a-stick only)
    DHCP snooping Yes (may not score reliably) Yes No
    Dynamic ARP Inspection Test with ip arp inspection ? Test with ip arp inspection ? No
    ip routing, routed ports (no switchport) No Yes Always routing
    DHCP server pool Test with ip dhcp ? Yes Yes
    OSPF, HSRP No Yes Yes
    NAT No No Yes
    ACL on vty lines (access-class) Yes Yes Yes
    login block-for Depends on PT version Yes Yes

    When a command fails with % Invalid input and the syntax is right, run ? at that point. If the keyword is missing, that model or PT version does not have it; move on and do the rest of the task.

    PreviousIPv4 quick refresher for Packet TracerNextRouter interface addressing and IPv6
    PT

    Router interface addressing and IPv6

    jump:pt-adv-ipv6

    Fast path

    1. Find the interface names with show ip interface brief.

    2. Turn on IPv6 routing and address each interface (IPv4, IPv6 global, link-local):

      configure terminal
ipv6 unicast-routing
interface <interface>
description <description>
ip address <ip-address> <subnet-mask>
ipv6 address <ipv6-address>/<prefix-length>
ipv6 address <link-local-address> link-local
no shutdown
end
write memory

    3. Check both stacks:

      show ip interface brief
show ipv6 interface brief

    4. From a PC, ping the router's IPv4 address and its IPv6 global address.

    Basic router interface steps are in router basic configuration. This section adds dual stack, link-local and EUI-64 detail.

    #Configure a dual-stack router interface

    In privileged EXEC mode, paste one block per interface:

    configure terminal
ipv6 unicast-routing
interface <interface>
ip address <ip-address> <subnet-mask>
ipv6 address <ipv6-address>/<prefix-length>
ipv6 address <link-local-address> link-local
no shutdown
end
write memory

    Expected output of show ipv6 interface brief:

    GigabitEthernet0/0/0   [up/up]
    FE80::1
    2001:DB8:ACAD:1::1
GigabitEthernet0/0/1   [administratively down/down]
    unassigned
    • IOS displays IPv6 addresses in capitals with zeros compressed. The grader compares the address value, so 2001:db8:acad:1::1 and 2001:DB8:ACAD:1::1 are the same.
    • An interface may have one link-local address and several global addresses. Typing a second ipv6 address .../64 adds; it does not replace. Remove a wrong one with no ipv6 address <ipv6-address>/<prefix-length>.
    • ipv6 unicast-routing is global and needed once. Without it the router does not forward IPv6 and does not send Router Advertisements, so SLAAC hosts get no prefix or gateway.

    #Set a static link-local address

    In interface configuration mode:

    ipv6 address <link-local-address> link-local
    • The link-local keyword is required. Without it IOS treats fe80::1 as a global address and rejects it or stores it wrong.
    • The same link-local (for example FE80::1 on R1, FE80::2 on R2) can go on every interface of one router.
    • Hosts may use the router's link-local as their IPv6 default gateway. PT accepts FE80::1 in the PC's IPv6 Gateway field.

    #Use EUI-64 for the interface ID

    In interface configuration mode, give only the /64 prefix:

    ipv6 address <ipv6-prefix>/64 eui-64

    The router builds the last 64 bits from the interface MAC: split the MAC in half, insert FFFE in the middle, and flip the seventh bit of the first byte.

    Step Example
    MAC address 00E0.F7A1.2B3C
    Split and insert FFFE 00E0:F7FF:FEA1:2B3C
    Flip bit 7 of the first byte (00 becomes 02) 02E0:F7FF:FEA1:2B3C
    Global address with prefix 2001:db8:acad:1::/64 2001:DB8:ACAD:1:2E0:F7FF:FEA1:2B3C
    Auto link-local FE80::2E0:F7FF:FEA1:2B3C

    Find the MAC with show interfaces <interface> (the address is field). The first-byte flip: 00 becomes 02, 02 becomes 00, 0C becomes 0E.

    #Other ways an interface gets IPv6

    Interface command Result
    ipv6 enable Link-local only (auto EUI-64), no global address
    ipv6 address autoconfig Router takes a global address by SLAAC from another router's RA
    ipv6 address dhcp Router is a DHCPv6 client
    ipv6 address <ipv6-address>/<prefix-length> Static global; link-local is auto-generated unless you set one

    #Verify addressing on both stacks

    In privileged EXEC mode:

    show ipv6 interface brief
show ipv6 route
show ip route connected

    show ipv6 route lists a C entry for each /64 and an L entry for each address (/128). If the C line is missing, the interface is not up/up.

    Grader gotchas for addressing

    • Wrong interface: G0/0/0 and G0/0/1 swapped. Check the addressing table column, not the cable you think you see.
    • Missing no shutdown: the address is right, but the item that checks port status fails.
    • Missing link-local: tasks that list FE80::1 grade it as its own item.
    • Prefix typo: /46 instead of /64 stores without an error.
    • On a 2960 SVI, IPv6 needs sdm prefer dual-ipv4-and-ipv6 default and a reload first (note).
    PreviousDevice models and port names for later roundsNextSubnetting tasks in Packet Tracer
    PT

    Subnetting tasks in Packet Tracer

    jump:pt-adv-subnetting

    Fast path

    1. List each network the task needs, largest host count first. Count router interfaces as hosts.
    2. For each one, pick the smallest prefix whose usable hosts cover it (table below).
    3. Assign subnets in order from the start of the given block, each starting at the next free multiple of its block size.
    4. For each subnet write network, first usable, last usable and broadcast.
    5. Give addresses by the task's rule (usually the router gets the first usable, the switch SVI the last usable or the second), then fill the addressing table before touching a device.

    #Pick a prefix from a host requirement

    Usable hosts = 2^(host bits) - 2.

    Hosts needed (up to) Prefix Mask Block size (last octet)
    2 /30 255.255.255.252 4
    6 /29 255.255.255.248 8
    14 /28 255.255.255.240 16
    30 /27 255.255.255.224 32
    62 /26 255.255.255.192 64
    126 /25 255.255.255.128 128
    254 /24 255.255.255.0 256
    510 /23 255.255.254.0 2 in the third octet
    1022 /22 255.255.252.0 4 in the third octet

    A /31 is not used for hosts in these activities. Point-to-point router links use /30 unless the task says otherwise.

    #Pick a prefix from a subnet-count requirement

    Subnets created = 2^(borrowed bits). Borrow the smallest number of bits that covers the count, then check the hosts still fit.

    Subnets needed (up to) Bits borrowed from a /24 New prefix Hosts each
    2 1 /25 126
    4 2 /26 62
    8 3 /27 30
    16 4 /28 14
    32 5 /29 6
    64 6 /30 2

    #Work a VLSM example

    Block 192.168.10.0/24. Needs: LAN A 100 hosts, LAN B 50 hosts, LAN C 20 hosts, two router links.

    Network Prefix Network address First usable Last usable Broadcast
    LAN A (100) /25 192.168.10.0 192.168.10.1 192.168.10.126 192.168.10.127
    LAN B (50) /26 192.168.10.128 192.168.10.129 192.168.10.190 192.168.10.191
    LAN C (20) /27 192.168.10.192 192.168.10.193 192.168.10.222 192.168.10.223
    Link 1 /30 192.168.10.224 192.168.10.225 192.168.10.226 192.168.10.227
    Link 2 /30 192.168.10.228 192.168.10.229 192.168.10.230 192.168.10.231

    Each subnet starts where the previous one's broadcast + 1 lands, which always works when you go largest first.

    #Find the four addresses of any subnet

    1. Block size = 256 minus the mask's interesting octet (for /27: 256 - 224 = 32).
    2. Network = the largest multiple of the block size that is not above the host's octet (host .77 in a /27: multiples 0, 32, 64, 96; network .64).
    3. Broadcast = next network minus 1 (.95).
    4. First usable = network + 1 (.65). Last usable = broadcast - 1 (.94).

    Grader gotchas for subnetting tasks

    • The grader checks the exact address on each interface. If the task says "first usable", the router gets network + 1, not .254.
    • Number subnets in the order the task lists them. "Subnet 3" is the fourth block if the task counts from subnet 0, so read whether it starts at 0 or 1.
    • With a wrong mask on a PC, local pings still work but remote ones fail. Check the mask on every host.
    • PT accepts an address that is the network or broadcast address on some end devices without complaint. IOS rejects it with Bad mask or overlaps, PCs may not.

    #Subnet IPv6

    With a /48 global routing prefix such as 2001:db8:acad::/48, the fourth hextet is the subnet ID. Count it in hex.

    Subnet Prefix Router address (::1 convention)
    0 2001:db8:acad::/64 (same as 2001:db8:acad:0::/64) 2001:db8:acad::1
    1 2001:db8:acad:1::/64 2001:db8:acad:1::1
    9 2001:db8:acad:9::/64 2001:db8:acad:9::1
    10 2001:db8:acad:a::/64 2001:db8:acad:a::1
    16 2001:db8:acad:10::/64 2001:db8:acad:10::1

    Every LAN gets a /64, including point-to-point links in ITN-level activities. Subnet IDs past 9 are hex: 10 is a, 16 is 10.

    PreviousRouter interface addressing and IPv6NextDHCPv4 server and relay on a router
    PT

    DHCPv4 server and relay on a router

    jump:pt-adv-dhcpv4

    Fast path

    1. Exclude the static addresses, create the pool, and save:

      configure terminal
ip dhcp excluded-address <first-excluded> <last-excluded>
ip dhcp pool <pool-name>
network <network-address> <subnet-mask>
default-router <default-gateway>
dns-server <dns-server>
domain-name <domain-name>
end
write memory

    2. If the clients are on a different router than the server, add the relay on the clients' gateway interface (relay).

    3. Set each PC to DHCP (Desktop > IP Configuration > DHCP) and click Fast Forward Time if it shows 169.254.x.x.

    4. Check the leases:

      show ip dhcp binding

    #Create a DHCPv4 pool with excluded addresses

    Run the exclusions before the pool so no client grabs a reserved address while you type. In privileged EXEC mode:

    configure terminal
ip dhcp excluded-address <first-excluded> <last-excluded>
ip dhcp excluded-address <excluded-address>
ip dhcp pool <pool-name>
network <network-address> <subnet-mask>
default-router <default-gateway>
dns-server <dns-server>
domain-name <domain-name>
end
write memory
    • network takes the network address and a mask (or /24 prefix form on some versions). Not a host address.
    • default-router is the router interface IP in that subnet. A pool without it hands out addresses that cannot leave the LAN.
    • One pool per subnet. Pool names are graded case-sensitively.
    • Delete a line you do not need (single exclusion, domain name).

    Expected output:

    R1#show ip dhcp binding
IP address       Client-ID/              Lease expiration        Type
                 Hardware address
192.168.10.11    0001.6458.2A01           --                     Automatic
192.168.10.12    0060.2F84.4AB6           --                     Automatic

    The first lease is the first address that is not excluded. If PCs got .11 and up, the exclusion 192.168.10.1 192.168.10.10 worked.

    #Relay DHCP to another network with ip helper-address

    In privileged EXEC mode on the router that is the clients' gateway (not the DHCP server):

    configure terminal
interface <interface>
ip helper-address <dhcp-server-ip>
end
write memory
    • Put it on the interface facing the clients (for router-on-a-stick, on each subinterface).
    • <dhcp-server-ip> is an address of the DHCP server that the relay can reach by routing, usually the server router's link address or a Server-PT's IP.
    • The server needs a pool for the client subnet and a route back to it.

    #Make the router a DHCP client

    In privileged EXEC mode:

    configure terminal
interface <interface>
ip address dhcp
no shutdown
end
write memory

    show ip interface brief shows the Method column as DHCP and the leased address once the ISP side answers.

    #Verify DHCPv4

    Command Shows
    show ip dhcp binding Leases handed out (MAC and IP)
    show ip dhcp pool Pool range, leased count
    show ip dhcp conflict Addresses the router found already in use
    show running-config (the ip dhcp lines) Exclusions and pool names
    PC ipconfig /all Address, gateway, DNS received; DHCP Servers field

    On a PC, ipconfig /release then ipconfig /renew forces a new request.

    Grader gotchas for DHCPv4

    • Exclusion range covers the wrong addresses (for example .1 .9 when the task said the first 10).
    • Pool network uses a host address or the wrong mask.
    • PCs left on Static: the grader checks that the PC is set to DHCP and has a lease.
    • ip helper-address on the server-facing interface instead of the client-facing one.
    • A switch with DHCP snooping on and no trusted uplink drops the offers (DHCP snooping).
    PreviousSubnetting tasks in Packet TracerNextDHCPv6 stateless and stateful
    PT

    DHCPv6 stateless and stateful

    jump:pt-adv-dhcpv6

    Fast path

    1. Decide the mode from the task wording: "stateless" (SLAAC address plus DNS from DHCPv6, O flag) or "stateful" (address from DHCPv6, M flag).
    2. Turn on IPv6 routing and create the pool and interface settings (stateless or stateful).
    3. On each PC, open Desktop > IP Configuration and set IPv6 to Automatic.

    4. Verify:

      show ipv6 dhcp pool
    Method RA flags Address from DNS from
    SLAAC only M=0, O=0 Router's RA prefix Nothing (or RDNSS)
    Stateless DHCPv6 M=0, O=1 Router's RA prefix DHCPv6 server
    Stateful DHCPv6 M=1 DHCPv6 server DHCPv6 server

    #Configure stateless DHCPv6

    In privileged EXEC mode on the router that is the clients' gateway:

    configure terminal
ipv6 unicast-routing
ipv6 dhcp pool <pool-name>
dns-server <ipv6-dns-server>
domain-name <domain-name>
exit
interface <interface>
ipv6 nd other-config-flag
ipv6 dhcp server <pool-name>
end
write memory

    The pool has no address prefix: clients build their own address from the interface's /64 by SLAAC, so the interface must have a global /64 address.

    #Configure stateful DHCPv6

    In privileged EXEC mode:

    configure terminal
ipv6 unicast-routing
ipv6 dhcp pool <pool-name>
address prefix <ipv6-prefix>/64
dns-server <ipv6-dns-server>
domain-name <domain-name>
exit
interface <interface>
ipv6 nd managed-config-flag
ipv6 dhcp server <pool-name>
end
write memory

    Some labs also add ipv6 nd prefix default no-autoconfig on the interface so clients do not also build a SLAAC address. Add it only if the task lists it; if PT rejects it, skip it.

    #Relay DHCPv6

    In privileged EXEC mode, on the clients' gateway interface:

    configure terminal
interface <interface>
ipv6 dhcp relay destination <ipv6-dhcp-server>
end
write memory

    #Verify DHCPv6

    Command Shows
    show ipv6 dhcp pool Pool name, DNS server, domain, active clients (stateful)
    show ipv6 dhcp binding Stateful leases
    show ipv6 interface <interface> Ends with Hosts use DHCP to obtain other configuration (O flag) or Hosts use DHCP to obtain routable addresses (M flag)
    PC ipconfig /all IPv6 address, gateway (router link-local) and DNS server

    Grader gotchas for DHCPv6

    • Flag swapped: other-config-flag is stateless, managed-config-flag is stateful.
    • ipv6 dhcp server <pool-name> missing on the interface: the pool exists but nobody answers.
    • Forgot ipv6 unicast-routing: no RAs, so PCs set to Automatic get only a link-local address.
    • PCs left on Static IPv6 instead of Automatic.
    PreviousDHCPv4 server and relay on a routerNextStatic and default routes for IPv4 and IPv6
    PT

    Static and default routes for IPv4 and IPv6

    jump:pt-adv-static-routes

    Fast path

    1. For each router, list every remote network it does not have a C route for (show ip route).

    2. Add a static route to each one, or one default route toward the edge:

      configure terminal
ip route <network-address> <subnet-mask> <next-hop>
ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 <next-hop>
ipv6 route <ipv6-prefix>/<prefix-length> <ipv6-next-hop>
ipv6 route ::/0 <ipv6-next-hop>
end
write memory

    3. Check the table and ping a remote host:

      show ip route static
show ipv6 route static

    #Choose next hop, exit interface or fully specified

    Form Example Use when
    Next hop ip route 192.168.20.0 255.255.255.0 10.1.1.2 The default choice; the task gives the neighbor IP
    Exit interface ip route 192.168.20.0 255.255.255.0 s0/1/0 Point-to-point serial links; the task says "directly connected"
    Fully specified ip route 192.168.20.0 255.255.255.0 g0/0/1 10.1.1.2 Ethernet exit plus next hop; IPv6 with a link-local next hop

    The grader usually checks the exact form the task names. "Configure a directly connected static route" means the exit-interface form.

    #Configure a floating static route

    In privileged EXEC mode, add the backup route with an administrative distance higher than the primary (static default is 1):

    configure terminal
ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 <next-hop>
ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 <next-hop-2> <admin-distance>
ipv6 route ::/0 <ipv6-next-hop>
ipv6 route ::/0 <ipv6-next-hop-2> <admin-distance>
end
write memory

    The floating route is in the running-config but not in show ip route while the primary works. Verify it with show running-config | include ip route, or shut the primary link and check that the backup appears.

    #Configure IPv6 static routes

    In privileged EXEC mode (the router needs ipv6 unicast-routing):

    configure terminal
ipv6 unicast-routing
ipv6 route <ipv6-prefix>/<prefix-length> <ipv6-next-hop>
ipv6 route ::/0 <ipv6-next-hop>
end
write memory

    With a link-local next hop the exit interface is required: ipv6 route ::/0 g0/0/1 fe80::2.

    #Configure a host route

    configure terminal
ip route <ip-address> 255.255.255.255 <next-hop>
ipv6 route <ipv6-address>/128 <ipv6-next-hop>
end
write memory

    #Verify static routes

    Expected output:

    R1#show ip route static
S    192.168.20.0/24 [1/0] via 10.1.1.2
S*   0.0.0.0/0 [1/0] via 209.165.200.226

    R1#show ipv6 route static
S   2001:DB8:ACAD:2::/64 [1/0]
     via 2001:DB8:ACAD:12::2
S   ::/0 [1/0]
     via 2001:DB8:ACAD:12::2

    [1/0] is administrative distance 1, metric 0. A floating route shows [5/0] only when it is active. Use traceroute <ip-address> from IOS or tracert from a PC to see which path is used.

    Grader gotchas for static routes

    • Network address typed as a host address (192.168.20.1 instead of 192.168.20.0): IOS rejects it with Inconsistent address and mask, or a typo in the mask stores a different route.
    • Next hop is the far router's address on the shared link, not your own interface.
    • Return routes forgotten: the far router also needs a route back.
    • A static route whose next hop is unreachable does not appear in the table. Fix the link first.
    • Default route on a 2960: use ip default-gateway instead (switch gateway). A 3650 with ip routing uses ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0.
    PreviousDHCPv6 stateless and statefulNextVLANs and access ports
    PT

    VLANs and access ports

    jump:pt-adv-vlans

    Fast path

    1. Create and name every VLAN in the VLAN table, then assign the access ports:

      configure terminal
vlan <vlan-id>
name <vlan-name>
exit
interface range <interface-range>
switchport mode access
switchport access vlan <vlan-id>
end
write memory

    2. Repeat for each VLAN. Create VLANs on every switch that carries them, even switches with no ports in that VLAN.

    3. Check names and port membership:

      show vlan brief

    #Create and name VLANs

    In privileged EXEC mode:

    configure terminal
vlan <vlan-id>
name <vlan-name>
exit
end
write memory

    VLAN names are case-sensitive and graded exactly as the VLAN table shows them (Faculty is not faculty). To rename, enter vlan <vlan-id> again and type the new name.

    #Assign access ports to a VLAN

    In privileged EXEC mode:

    configure terminal
interface range <interface-range>
switchport mode access
switchport access vlan <vlan-id>
end
write memory
    • switchport mode access stops the port from negotiating a trunk. Graders often check it as its own item.
    • If the VLAN does not exist yet, switchport access vlan creates it with a default name like VLAN0010. Name it afterwards.

    #Set up a management VLAN

    In privileged EXEC mode:

    configure terminal
vlan <vlan-id>
name <vlan-name>
exit
interface vlan <vlan-id>
ip address <ip-address> <subnet-mask>
no shutdown
exit
ip default-gateway <default-gateway>
end
write memory

    The SVI stays up/down until the VLAN exists and at least one port in it (or a trunk carrying it) is up. If the task moves management off VLAN 1, it may also want interface vlan 1 and shutdown.

    #Add a voice VLAN

    In privileged EXEC mode:

    configure terminal
interface <interface>
switchport mode access
switchport access vlan <vlan-id>
mls qos trust cos
switchport voice vlan <voice-vlan-id>
end
write memory

    #Verify VLANs

    Expected output:

    S1#show vlan brief
VLAN Name                             Status    Ports
---- -------------------------------- --------- -------------------------------
1    default                          active    Fa0/3, Fa0/4, Fa0/5, Fa0/6
10   Faculty                          active    Fa0/11, Fa0/12
20   Students                         active    Fa0/18
99   Management                       active
1002 fddi-default                     act/unsup

    Trunk ports do not appear in show vlan brief. show interfaces <interface> switchport shows one port's administrative mode and access VLAN.

    Grader gotchas for VLANs

    • VLAN name spelling or case differs from the table.
    • A port left in VLAN 1 because the range missed it. Count the ports in the output against the table.
    • VLAN deleted with no vlan <vlan-id>: its ports go inactive and stay assigned to the missing VLAN.
    • VLANs live in flash:vlan.dat, not in the running-config. write memory still matters for the port settings.
    PreviousStatic and default routes for IPv4 and IPv6NextTrunks, native VLAN and DTP
    PT

    Trunks, native VLAN and DTP

    jump:pt-adv-trunks

    Fast path

    1. On both ends of each switch-to-switch link (and the switch port facing a router-on-a-stick), configure a static trunk:

      configure terminal
interface <interface>
switchport mode trunk
switchport trunk native vlan <native-vlan-id>
switchport trunk allowed vlan <allowed-vlans>
switchport nonegotiate
end
write memory

    2. Create the native VLAN on both switches first if it is not VLAN 1 (vlan <native-vlan-id>, name <vlan-name>).

    3. On a 3560, add switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q before switchport mode trunk.

    4. Check both ends match:

      show interfaces trunk

    #Configure a static trunk

    In privileged EXEC mode:

    configure terminal
interface <interface>
switchport mode trunk
end
write memory

    If you see Command rejected: An interface whose trunk encapsulation is "Auto" can not be configured to "trunk" mode., the switch supports ISL too (3560). Run switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q first, then switchport mode trunk.

    #Change the native VLAN

    In interface configuration mode, on both ends of the trunk:

    switchport trunk native vlan <native-vlan-id>

    Until both ends match, the console prints %CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH: Native VLAN mismatch discovered on GigabitEthernet0/1 (99), with S2 GigabitEthernet0/1 (1). The message stops once both sides are set. Hardening tasks use an unused VLAN as native (for example VLAN 100 named Native) to stop VLAN hopping.

    #Limit the allowed VLANs

    In interface configuration mode:

    switchport trunk allowed vlan <allowed-vlans>
    • <allowed-vlans> is a comma list without spaces, for example 10,20,99.
    • A plain list replaces the current list. To add one later use switchport trunk allowed vlan add <vlan-id>; remove takes one out.
    • Include the native VLAN and the management VLAN, or management and untagged traffic stop.

    #Turn off DTP

    In interface configuration mode, after setting the mode:

    switchport nonegotiate

    On access ports, switchport mode access already stops trunk negotiation; some tasks also want switchport nonegotiate there.

    Local mode Remote mode Result
    trunk trunk, dynamic auto, dynamic desirable Trunk (with nonegotiate on one end, only trunk on the other works)
    dynamic desirable dynamic auto or dynamic desirable Trunk
    dynamic auto dynamic auto Access (no trunk)
    access anything Access

    The 2960 default is dynamic auto, so two untouched 2960s never form a trunk.

    #Verify trunks

    Expected output:

    S1#show interfaces trunk
Port        Mode         Encapsulation  Status        Native vlan
Gig0/1      on           802.1q         trunking      99

Port        Vlans allowed on trunk
Gig0/1      10,20,99

Port        Vlans allowed and active in management domain
Gig0/1      10,20,99

Port        Vlans in spanning tree forwarding state and not pruned
Gig0/1      10,20,99

    Mode on means a static trunk. An empty output means no port is trunking. show interfaces <interface> switchport shows Negotiation of Trunking: Off after switchport nonegotiate.

    Grader gotchas for trunks

    • Configured on one end only. The grader checks both switches.
    • Native VLAN set on the trunk but the VLAN never created, so the item that checks the VLAN table fails.
    • Allowed list typed with spaces or missing a VLAN the PCs need.
    • switchport nonegotiate typed before switchport mode trunk is rejected on a dynamic port. Order: mode, native, allowed, nonegotiate.
    PreviousVLANs and access portsNextRouter-on-a-stick inter-VLAN routing
    PT

    Router-on-a-stick inter-VLAN routing

    jump:pt-adv-roas

    Fast path

    1. On the switch, make the port facing the router a trunk (trunks).

    2. On the router, create one subinterface per VLAN and turn the parent interface on:

      configure terminal
interface <interface>.<vlan-id>
description <description>
encapsulation dot1Q <vlan-id>
ip address <ip-address> <subnet-mask>
exit
interface <interface>
no shutdown
end
write memory

    3. Repeat the subinterface lines for every VLAN.

    4. Set each PC's gateway to its VLAN's subinterface IP and ping across VLANs.

    #Create the subinterfaces

    In privileged EXEC mode, one block per VLAN:

    configure terminal
interface <interface>.<vlan-id>
description <description>
encapsulation dot1Q <vlan-id>
ip address <ip-address> <subnet-mask>
end
write memory

    For the native VLAN subinterface, if the task asks for one:

    configure terminal
interface <interface>.<native-vlan-id>
encapsulation dot1Q <native-vlan-id> native
ip address <ip-address> <subnet-mask>
end
write memory

    Bring the physical interface up once:

    configure terminal
interface <interface>
no shutdown
end
write memory
    • encapsulation dot1Q must come before ip address. In the other order IOS replies % Configuring IP routing on a LAN subinterface is only allowed if that subinterface is already configured as part of an IEEE 802.10, IEEE 802.1Q, or ISL vLAN.
    • The subinterface number does not have to equal the VLAN, but use the same number unless the table says otherwise. The VLAN in encapsulation dot1Q is what matters.
    • The parent interface has no IP address. Subinterfaces need no no shutdown; they follow the parent.

    #Verify router-on-a-stick

    Expected output:

    R1#show ip interface brief
Interface              IP-Address      OK? Method Status                Protocol
GigabitEthernet0/0/1   unassigned      YES unset  up                    up
GigabitEthernet0/0/1.10 192.168.10.1   YES manual up                    up
GigabitEthernet0/0/1.20 192.168.20.1   YES manual up                    up
GigabitEthernet0/0/1.99 192.168.99.1   YES manual up                    up

    show ip route shows a C route for each VLAN subnet. If one is missing, that subinterface has no IP or a typo in the VLAN number.

    Grader gotchas for router-on-a-stick

    • Switch port toward the router left as access: only one VLAN works.
    • encapsulation dot1Q 20 on the .10 subinterface (copy and paste error).
    • Parent interface still shut down.
    • PCs pointing at the wrong gateway: each VLAN's gateway is its own subinterface IP.
    • DHCP for several VLANs needs ip helper-address on each subinterface if the server is elsewhere.
    PreviousTrunks, native VLAN and DTPNextLayer 3 switch inter-VLAN routing
    PT

    Layer 3 switch inter-VLAN routing

    jump:pt-adv-l3switch

    Fast path

    1. Power the 3650 if it is off (Physical tab, add the power supply).

    2. Turn on routing, create the VLANs and give each VLAN an SVI:

      configure terminal
ip routing
vlan <vlan-id>
name <vlan-name>
exit
interface vlan <vlan-id>
description <description>
ip address <ip-address> <subnet-mask>
no shutdown
end
write memory

    3. Make the uplink to the router a routed port and add a default route (routed port).

    4. Set each PC's gateway to its VLAN SVI address and ping across VLANs.

    #Turn on routing and create SVIs

    In privileged EXEC mode, one SVI block per VLAN:

    configure terminal
ip routing
interface vlan <vlan-id>
ip address <ip-address> <subnet-mask>
no shutdown
end
write memory

    Without ip routing the SVIs are up and each VLAN can ping its own SVI, but traffic between VLANs fails.

    #Make a routed port

    In privileged EXEC mode:

    configure terminal
interface <interface>
no switchport
ip address <ip-address> <subnet-mask>
no shutdown
exit
ip route 0.0.0.0 0.0.0.0 <next-hop>
end
write memory

    The router on the other end needs routes back to every VLAN subnet through the switch's routed-port address (or OSPF).

    #Verify Layer 3 switching

    Command Correct result
    show ip route Starts with codes, not Default gateway is ...; one C per SVI and routed port; S* default
    show ip interface brief Each Vlan<vlan-id> up/up with its IP
    show interfaces <interface> switchport Switchport: Disabled on the routed port

    Grader gotchas for Layer 3 switches

    • ip routing missing (the most common miss).
    • SVI up/down: the VLAN does not exist on this switch or no port in it is up.
    • Routed port configured on the wrong interface, or no switchport forgotten so ip address is rejected.
    • ip default-gateway used instead of a default route; it is ignored once ip routing is on.
    PreviousRouter-on-a-stick inter-VLAN routingNextSpanning Tree root bridge, PortFast and BPDU guard
    PT

    Spanning Tree root bridge, PortFast and BPDU guard

    jump:pt-adv-stp

    Fast path

    1. Set the STP mode and make the named switch the root for the named VLANs:

      configure terminal
spanning-tree mode rapid-pvst
spanning-tree vlan <vlan-list> root primary
end
write memory

    2. On the backup switch, use spanning-tree vlan <vlan-list> root secondary.

    3. On the access switch, enable PortFast and BPDU guard on the PC ports (edge ports).

    4. Confirm the root:

      show spanning-tree vlan <vlan-id>

    #Make a switch the root bridge

    In privileged EXEC mode, either use the macro:

    configure terminal
spanning-tree vlan <vlan-list> root primary
end
write memory

    or set an explicit priority (a multiple of 4096):

    configure terminal
spanning-tree vlan <vlan-list> priority <stp-priority>
end
write memory
    • root primary sets priority 24576 (or lower if another switch is already below that). root secondary sets 28672.
    • If the task gives a number, use priority with that number; the grader may check the value.
    • <vlan-list> can be 1, 10,20 or 10-30.

    #Enable PortFast and BPDU guard on access ports

    In privileged EXEC mode, per access port range:

    configure terminal
interface range <interface-range>
spanning-tree portfast
spanning-tree bpduguard enable
end
write memory

    Or as defaults for every access port on the switch:

    configure terminal
spanning-tree portfast default
spanning-tree portfast bpduguard default
end
write memory
    • IOS prints a %Warning: portfast should only be enabled on ports connected to a single host... message. That is normal.
    • Never enable PortFast on a trunk or switch-to-switch link.
    • The global defaults only apply to ports in access mode. Graders that check the interface lines want the per-port form; read which one the task says ("on all active access ports" vs "by default").

    #Recover a port shut by BPDU guard

    Remove the switch that was plugged in, then in privileged EXEC mode:

    configure terminal
interface <interface>
shutdown
no shutdown
end

    #Verify STP

    Expected output on the root:

    S1#show spanning-tree vlan 10
VLAN0010
  Spanning tree enabled protocol rstp
  Root ID    Priority    24586
             Address     0001.4209.A9C3
             This bridge is the root

    The priority shown is the configured value plus the VLAN number (24576 + 10). show spanning-tree summary shows Portfast Default and Portfast BPDU Guard Default states. show spanning-tree interface <interface> detail shows The port is in the portfast mode and Bpdu guard is enabled.

    Grader gotchas for STP

    • Root set for VLAN 1 only when the task listed several VLANs.
    • Priority not a multiple of 4096: IOS rejects it and lists the allowed values.
    • PortFast enabled on the uplink; BPDU guard then err-disables the trunk.
    PreviousLayer 3 switch inter-VLAN routingNextEtherChannel with LACP and PAgP
    PT

    EtherChannel with LACP and PAgP

    jump:pt-adv-etherchannel

    Fast path

    1. Shut the member ports, put them in the same channel group, and bring them back up:

      configure terminal
interface range <interface-range>
shutdown
channel-group <channel-number> mode active
no shutdown
exit
interface port-channel <channel-number>
switchport mode trunk
switchport trunk native vlan <native-vlan-id>
switchport trunk allowed vlan <allowed-vlans>
end
write memory

    2. Do the same on the other switch with a compatible mode (table below).

    3. Check the bundle shows SU and each port P:

      show etherchannel summary

    #Pick the channel mode

    Protocol Mode Forms a channel with
    LACP (IEEE 802.3ad) active active or passive
    LACP passive active only
    PAgP (Cisco) desirable desirable or auto
    PAgP auto desirable only
    None on on only

    Use the mode the task names on each switch. "Negotiate with LACP" with no side named usually means active on both.

    #Configure an EtherChannel trunk

    In privileged EXEC mode, on each switch:

    configure terminal
interface range <interface-range>
shutdown
channel-group <channel-number> mode <channel-mode>
no shutdown
exit
interface port-channel <channel-number>
switchport mode trunk
switchport trunk native vlan <native-vlan-id>
switchport trunk allowed vlan <allowed-vlans>
end
write memory
    • Configure trunk settings on the port-channel interface; IOS copies them to the members.
    • Member ports must match: speed, duplex, access VLAN or trunk settings, native VLAN.
    • The channel number is local to each switch, but use the number the task gives on both.

    #Verify EtherChannel

    Expected output:

    S1#show etherchannel summary
Flags:  D - down        P - in port-channel
        I - stand-alone s - suspended
        R - Layer3      S - Layer2
        U - in use      f - failed to allocate aggregator
...
Group  Port-channel  Protocol    Ports
------+-------------+-----------+----------------------------------------------
1      Po1(SU)           LACP   Fa0/1(P) Fa0/2(P)
    What you see Meaning
    Po1(SU) and ports (P) Working Layer 2 channel
    Po1(SD) Channel down: modes do not match, or other side not configured
    Port (s) suspended or (I) stand-alone That member does not match the others (speed, VLAN, trunk)

    Grader gotchas for EtherChannel

    • passive on both ends (LACP) or auto on both ends (PAgP): nothing forms.
    • Trunk configured on the members but not on interface port-channel.
    • STP shows the bundle as Po1; PortFast and BPDU guard do not belong on it.
    PreviousSpanning Tree root bridge, PortFast and BPDU guardNextHSRP first hop redundancy
    PT

    HSRP first hop redundancy

    jump:pt-adv-hsrp

    Fast path

    1. On the router that should be active, configure the group with a higher priority and preempt:

      configure terminal
interface <interface>
standby version 2
standby <hsrp-group> ip <virtual-ip>
standby <hsrp-group> priority <hsrp-priority>
standby <hsrp-group> preempt
end
write memory

    2. On the other router, the same interface with the same group and virtual IP, and no priority line (default 100).

    3. Set every PC's default gateway to the virtual IP.

    4. Check that one router is Active and the other Standby:

      show standby brief

    #Configure HSRP on both routers

    Active router, in privileged EXEC mode:

    configure terminal
interface <interface>
standby version 2
standby <hsrp-group> ip <virtual-ip>
standby <hsrp-group> priority <hsrp-priority>
standby <hsrp-group> preempt
end
write memory

    Standby router:

    configure terminal
interface <interface>
standby version 2
standby <hsrp-group> ip <virtual-ip>
end
write memory
    • The virtual IP is a third, unused address in the LAN subnet. Each router keeps its own real interface IP.
    • Higher priority wins. Default is 100; tasks usually use 150 for the active router.
    • Without preempt, a higher-priority router that boots second stays standby.
    • Version, group number and virtual IP must match on both routers.

    #Verify HSRP

    Expected output on the active router:

    R1#show standby brief
                     P indicates configured to preempt.
                     |
Interface   Grp  Pri P State    Active          Standby         Virtual IP
Gig0/1      1    150 P Active   local           192.168.1.3     192.168.1.254

    On the other router the State column says Standby and Active shows R1's real IP. Init or Listen on both means the routers cannot see each other or a value does not match.

    Grader gotchas for HSRP

    • PCs still point at a real router IP instead of the virtual IP.
    • standby version 2 on one router only: they do not talk.
    • Priority put on the wrong router, so the wrong one is Active.
    PreviousEtherChannel with LACP and PAgPNextPort security with sticky MACs and violation modes
    PT

    Port security with sticky MACs and violation modes

    jump:pt-adv-port-security

    Fast path

    1. Apply port security to every active access port the task names:

      configure terminal
interface range <interface-range>
switchport mode access
switchport port-security
switchport port-security maximum <max-macs>
switchport port-security mac-address sticky
switchport port-security violation <violation-mode>
end
write memory

    2. If one port needs a fixed MAC, add it on that port (static MAC).

    3. Ping from each PC so sticky MACs are learned, then save again with write memory.

    4. Check the table:

      show port-security

    Basics and the violation table are in port security on access ports. This section adds the SRWE-level options.

    #Match the task wording to the violation mode

    Task says Mode
    "shut down the port", "err-disable", or nothing shutdown (default)
    "drop traffic, log or send a syslog message, increment the counter, keep the port up" restrict
    "drop traffic silently, no log" protect

    #Add a static secure MAC

    Find the PC's MAC (Desktop > Command Prompt > ipconfig /all, Physical Address, shown as 0001.6458.2A01). In privileged EXEC mode:

    configure terminal
interface <interface>
switchport port-security mac-address <mac-address>
end
write memory

    Type the MAC in dotted format aaaa.bbbb.cccc. A static MAC counts toward the maximum.

    #Set port security aging

    In interface configuration mode:

    switchport port-security aging time <aging-minutes>
switchport port-security aging type inactivity

    Aging does not remove sticky addresses. If PT rejects either line, that version lacks it.

    #Recover err-disabled ports automatically

    Manual recovery is shutdown then no shutdown on the port (how). For automatic recovery, in privileged EXEC mode:

    configure terminal
errdisable recovery cause psecure-violation
errdisable recovery cause bpduguard
errdisable recovery interval <recovery-seconds>
end
write memory

    Use these only when the task asks; some PT versions do not have errdisable recovery.

    #Verify port security

    Expected output:

    S1#show port-security
Secure Port MaxSecureAddr CurrentAddr SecurityViolation Security Action
               (Count)       (Count)        (Count)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
        Fa0/1        4          1                 0         Restrict
        Fa0/2        4          1                 0         Restrict

    S1#show port-security interface fa0/1
Port Security              : Enabled
Port Status                : Secure-up
Violation Mode             : Restrict
Maximum MAC Addresses      : 4
Total MAC Addresses        : 1
Sticky MAC Addresses       : 1
Security Violation Count   : 0

    Secure-shutdown means the port is err-disabled. Sticky MACs show as switchport port-security mac-address sticky 0001.6458.2A01 lines in show running-config once learned.

    Grader gotchas for port security

    • switchport mode access missing: port security is rejected on a dynamic port.
    • Sticky MACs not saved because no traffic was sent before write memory.
    • Port security put on an unused or trunk port the task did not list.
    • Maximum left at 1 when the task said 2 or 4.
    PreviousHSRP first hop redundancyNextDHCP snooping
    PT

    DHCP snooping

    jump:pt-adv-dhcp-snooping

    Fast path

    1. Turn snooping on for the VLANs, trust the uplinks toward the real DHCP server, and rate-limit the access ports:

      configure terminal
ip dhcp snooping
ip dhcp snooping vlan <vlan-list>
no ip dhcp snooping information option
interface <interface>
ip dhcp snooping trust
exit
interface range <interface-range>
ip dhcp snooping limit rate <rate-limit>
end
write memory

    2. Renew a PC (ipconfig /renew) and confirm it still gets an address.

    3. Check the settings:

      show ip dhcp snooping

    #Configure DHCP snooping

    • Trusted ports: trunks and uplinks toward the DHCP server (router or server). Everything else stays untrusted (the default).
    • limit rate goes on untrusted access ports, in packets per second.
    • no ip dhcp snooping information option stops the switch from inserting option 82. With option 82 inserted, an IOS router acting as DHCP server can drop the requests and PCs end up with 169.254 addresses. Add it unless the task says otherwise.

    Expected output:

    S1#show ip dhcp snooping
Switch DHCP snooping is enabled
DHCP snooping is configured on following VLANs:
10,20,99
Insertion of option 82 is disabled
Interface                  Trusted    Rate limit (pps)
-----------------------    -------    ----------------
GigabitEthernet0/1         yes        unlimited
FastEthernet0/1            no         5

    show ip dhcp snooping binding lists the leases snooping has seen; DAI depends on it.

    Grader gotchas for DHCP snooping

    • Global ip dhcp snooping typed but no vlan line: nothing is snooped.
    • Uplink not trusted: every client loses DHCP.
    • The SRWE 11.6.1 activity notes that DHCP snooping may not score correctly in PT. Configure it as asked and move on.
    PreviousPort security with sticky MACs and violation modesNextDynamic ARP Inspection
    PT

    Dynamic ARP Inspection

    jump:pt-adv-dai

    Fast path

    1. Configure DHCP snooping first; DAI checks ARP against the snooping binding table.

    2. Turn on DAI for the VLANs, trust the uplinks and set validation:

      configure terminal
ip arp inspection vlan <vlan-list>
ip arp inspection validate src-mac dst-mac ip
interface <interface>
ip arp inspection trust
end
write memory

    3. Renew the PCs' DHCP leases and ping between them.

    4. Check:

      show ip arp inspection

    #Configure DAI

    • Put all three validate keywords on one line. Each new validate line replaces the previous one, so three separate lines leave only the last.
    • Trust the same uplinks you trusted for DHCP snooping.
    • Hosts with static IPs have no snooping binding, so DAI drops their ARP. Use DAI only on VLANs whose hosts use DHCP, unless the task gives an ARP ACL.
    • If ip arp inspection ? shows nothing on this model or PT version, the feature is missing. Note it and move on.

    Grader gotchas for DAI

    • DAI on before DHCP snooping bindings exist: every host loses connectivity until it renews.
    • Uplink not trusted: ARP from the router is dropped.
    PreviousDHCP snoopingNextUnused ports into a black-hole VLAN
    PT

    Unused ports into a black-hole VLAN

    jump:pt-adv-blackhole

    Fast path

    1. Find the ports in use (status connected):

      show interfaces status

    2. Create the VLAN and move every unused port into it, then shut them:

      configure terminal
vlan <blackhole-vlan>
name <vlan-name>
exit
interface range <interface-range>
switchport mode access
switchport access vlan <blackhole-vlan>
shutdown
end
write memory

    3. Confirm the ports show in the black-hole VLAN and as disabled:

      show vlan brief
show interfaces status

    #Build the unused port range

    • Range syntax: fa0/2 - 9 , fa0/11 - 23 , g0/2. A space on both sides of the hyphen and around commas, at most five groups per range command.
    • Skip trunks and every connected port. A port that is cabled but shut down in the original file may still be "in use"; check the task's port table.
    • Use the VLAN ID and name exactly as given (SRWE uses VLAN 999 BlackHole).

    Grader gotchas for black-hole VLANs

    • Ports moved to the VLAN but not shut down, or shut down but left in VLAN 1. Tasks usually grade both.
    • A port used by a PC included in the range by mistake. Ping every PC afterwards.
    PreviousDynamic ARP InspectionNextSSH, local AAA and login protection
    PT

    SSH, local AAA and login protection

    jump:pt-adv-ssh-aaa

    Fast path

    1. Do the SSH basics first (SSH step by step).

    2. Add local AAA so the console and vty lines use the local database:

      configure terminal
username <admin-username> privilege 15 secret <admin-password>
aaa new-model
aaa authentication login default local
line console 0
login authentication default
exit
line vty 0 4
login authentication default
transport input ssh
end
write memory

    3. Add login protection if asked (login options).

    4. Test from a PC with ssh -l <admin-username> <ip-address>.

    #Configure local AAA authentication

    • Create the user before aaa new-model. Once AAA is on, the console asks for a username at the next login.
    • With aaa new-model, login local on a line is replaced by login authentication <list-name>. The default list applies to every line that has no named list.
    • A named list: aaa authentication login <list-name> local, then login authentication <list-name> on the lines. Use the exact list name the task gives.

    #Use a RADIUS or TACACS+ server

    In privileged EXEC mode on the router:

    configure terminal
aaa new-model
radius-server host <radius-server> key <radius-key>
aaa authentication login default group radius local
line vty 0 4
login authentication default
end
write memory

    For TACACS+ use tacacs-server host <tacacs-server> key <tacacs-key> and group tacacs+ local. On the Server-PT open Services > AAA, turn the service On, add the router as a client (Client Name = router hostname, Client IP = the router interface facing the server, Secret = the key, ServerType Radius or Tacacs), and add the users under User Setup. local at the end is the fallback if the server does not answer.

    #Add login failure protection

    In privileged EXEC mode:

    configure terminal
login block-for <block-seconds> attempts <attempts> within <within-seconds>
login on-failure log
login on-success log
ip ssh time-out <ssh-timeout>
ip ssh authentication-retries <ssh-retries>
end
write memory

    show login shows the block-for settings and whether the device is in quiet mode.

    #Restrict vty access to a management subnet

    In privileged EXEC mode:

    configure terminal
ip access-list standard <acl-name>
permit <network-address> <wildcard-mask>
exit
line vty 0 4
access-class <acl-name> in
end
write memory

    access-class goes on the line; ip access-group goes on an interface. A PC outside the permitted range gets % Connection refused by remote host.

    Grader gotchas for SSH and AAA

    • aaa new-model entered before any user exists: you are locked out of the console after logout.
    • privilege 15 added when not asked, or missing when the task says the user lands in privileged EXEC.
    • Router vty is 0 4; a 2960 or 3650 is 0 15. Configure every line the device has.
    • RADIUS key typed differently on the router and the server.
    PreviousUnused ports into a black-hole VLANNextNTP and syslog
    PT

    NTP and syslog

    jump:pt-adv-ntp-syslog

    Fast path

    1. On the Server-PT, open Services and turn NTP and SYSLOG On.

    2. Point the router or switch at the servers and timestamp the logs:

      configure terminal
ntp server <ntp-server>
ntp update-calendar
service timestamps log datetime msec
service timestamps debug datetime msec
logging host <syslog-server>
logging trap <logging-level>
end
write memory

    3. Wait (or Fast Forward Time) and check:

      show ntp status
show logging

    #Configure NTP

    • ntp update-calendar keeps the hardware clock in step; tasks from CCNA Security list it. Skip if PT rejects it on that model.
    • With NTP authentication, all four lines are needed:
    configure terminal
ntp authenticate
ntp authentication-key <ntp-key-id> md5 <ntp-key>
ntp trusted-key <ntp-key-id>
ntp server <ntp-server> key <ntp-key-id>
end
write memory

    On the Server-PT NTP page, enable Authentication with the same key number and password.

    Expected output:

    R1#show ntp status
Clock is synchronized, stratum 2, reference is 192.168.1.5

    show clock without a leading * means the time is authoritative. Clock is unsynchronized right after configuring is normal; wait or click Fast Forward Time.

    #Send logs to a syslog server

    • logging host <syslog-server> (older form logging <syslog-server>) sends messages to the server.
    • logging trap <logging-level> sets the lowest severity sent: warnings (4), notifications (5), informational (6), debugging (7).
    • Generate a test message by entering and leaving configuration mode, then open the Server-PT Services > SYSLOG page to see it.

    Grader gotchas for NTP and syslog

    • NTP or SYSLOG service left Off on the server.
    • Router cannot reach the server (no route), so status never synchronizes.
    • Timestamps set for log but the task also asked for debug.
    PreviousSSH, local AAA and login protectionNextDisable CDP, HTTP and other unneeded services
    PT

    Disable CDP, HTTP and other unneeded services

    jump:pt-adv-services

    Fast path

    1. Turn off the services the task names:

      configure terminal
no cdp run
no lldp run
no ip http server
no ip http secure-server
end
write memory

    2. For CDP on only one port (for example the ISP-facing port), use no cdp enable in that interface instead of no cdp run.

    3. Check:

      show cdp
show running-config | include http

    #Disable CDP globally or per port

    Command Mode Effect
    no cdp run Global CDP off on every port
    no cdp enable Interface CDP off on that port only
    no lldp run Global LLDP off (LLDP is off by default on most models)

    Expected output after no cdp run:

    R1#show cdp
% CDP is not enabled

    #Disable the HTTP server

    no ip http server and no ip http secure-server in global configuration mode. If PT rejects either line, that model has no web server to disable. show running-config | include http then shows no ip http server, or nothing at all.

    Grader gotchas for disabling services

    • no cdp run when the task said "on the interface connected to the ISP" (needs no cdp enable on that port).
    • Disabling CDP before you finish using show cdp neighbors to map the topology. Do it last.
    PreviousNTP and syslogNextStandard and extended ACLs
    PT

    Standard and extended ACLs

    jump:pt-adv-acl

    Fast path

    1. Write the ACL from the task, most specific lines first, and end with a permit if other traffic must pass:

      configure terminal
ip access-list extended <acl-name>
remark <acl-remark>
deny tcp <network-address> <wildcard-mask> host <server-ip> eq <port>
permit ip any any
exit
interface <interface>
ip access-group <acl-name> in
end
write memory

    2. Apply standard ACLs near the destination, extended ACLs near the source (unless the task names the interface and direction).

    3. Test the denied and permitted traffic, then read the match counters:

      show access-lists

    #Write a standard ACL

    Numbered (1-99), in privileged EXEC mode:

    configure terminal
access-list <acl-number> deny host <ip-address>
access-list <acl-number> permit <network-address> <wildcard-mask>
interface <interface>
ip access-group <acl-number> out
end
write memory

    Named:

    configure terminal
ip access-list standard <acl-name>
deny host <ip-address>
permit <network-address> <wildcard-mask>
exit
interface <interface>
ip access-group <acl-name> out
end
write memory

    Standard ACLs match the source address only.

    #Write an extended ACL

    Goal ACE
    Block web from a subnet to one server deny tcp 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 192.168.20.254 eq www
    Allow HTTPS permit tcp any host <server-ip> eq 443
    Allow FTP permit tcp any host <server-ip> eq ftp
    Block ping from a host deny icmp host 192.168.10.10 any echo
    Allow DNS permit udp any any eq domain
    Allow everything else permit ip any any

    Order: protocol, source, source wildcard, destination, destination wildcard, then eq <port> after the destination for the destination port. Numbered extended ACLs use 100-199.

    #Calculate a wildcard mask

    Wildcard = 255.255.255.255 minus the subnet mask.

    Mask Wildcard
    255.255.255.0 0.0.0.255
    255.255.255.192 0.0.0.63
    255.255.255.224 0.0.0.31
    255.255.255.240 0.0.0.15
    255.255.255.252 0.0.0.3
    255.255.255.255 0.0.0.0 (host)

    host 10.1.1.1 equals 10.1.1.1 0.0.0.0. any equals 0.0.0.0 255.255.255.255.

    #Edit a named ACL by sequence number

    In privileged EXEC mode, insert line 15 and delete line 20:

    configure terminal
ip access-list extended <acl-name>
15 permit tcp host <ip-address> host <server-ip> eq 22
no 20
end
write memory

    Numbered ACLs cannot be edited line by line in classic form: no access-list <acl-number> deletes the whole list. Rebuild it from a text editor.

    #Filter IPv6 traffic

    configure terminal
ipv6 access-list <acl-name>
deny tcp any host <ipv6-address> eq www
permit ipv6 any any
exit
interface <interface>
ipv6 traffic-filter <acl-name> in
end
write memory

    IPv6 ACLs are always named, and implicitly permit neighbor discovery before the final implicit deny.

    #Verify ACLs

    Expected output:

    R1#show access-lists
Standard IP access list 10
    10 deny host 192.168.10.10 (4 match(es))
    20 permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 (12 match(es))
Extended IP access list BLOCK-WEB
    10 deny tcp 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 192.168.20.254 eq www (6 match(es))
    20 permit ip any any (25 match(es))

    show ip interface <interface> shows Outgoing access list is and Inbound access list is with the applied names.

    Grader gotchas for ACLs

    • Missing permit ip any any (or permit any on a standard list): the implicit deny blocks everything else.
    • Applied in the wrong direction or on the wrong interface. in filters traffic entering the router on that port.
    • Wildcard written as a subnet mask (255.255.255.0).
    • ACL name case differs from the task.
    • ip access-group on a vty line is rejected; lines use access-class.
    PreviousDisable CDP, HTTP and other unneeded servicesNextNAT and PAT basics
    PT

    NAT and PAT basics

    jump:pt-adv-nat

    Fast path

    1. Mark the inside and outside interfaces, define the inside addresses, and turn on PAT on the outside interface address:

      configure terminal
access-list <acl-number> permit <network-address> <wildcard-mask>
ip nat inside source list <acl-number> interface <outside-interface> overload
interface <inside-interface>
ip nat inside
exit
interface <outside-interface>
ip nat outside
end
write memory

    2. Ping or browse from an inside PC to an outside address.

    3. Check translations:

      show ip nat translations

    #Configure static NAT for a server

    In privileged EXEC mode:

    configure terminal
ip nat inside source static <inside-local> <inside-global>
interface <inside-interface>
ip nat inside
exit
interface <outside-interface>
ip nat outside
end
write memory

    Outside hosts reach the server at <inside-global>.

    #Configure dynamic NAT or PAT with a pool

    In privileged EXEC mode:

    configure terminal
ip nat pool <pool-name> <start-ip> <end-ip> netmask <subnet-mask>
access-list <acl-number> permit <network-address> <wildcard-mask>
ip nat inside source list <acl-number> pool <pool-name> overload
interface <inside-interface>
ip nat inside
exit
interface <outside-interface>
ip nat outside
end
write memory

    Without overload this is one-to-one dynamic NAT and stops when the pool runs out.

    #Verify NAT

    Expected output after an inside PC pings out:

    R1#show ip nat translations
Pro  Inside global     Inside local       Outside local      Outside global
icmp 209.165.200.225:1 192.168.10.11:1    209.165.201.1:1    209.165.201.1:1
---  209.165.200.229   192.168.20.254     ---                ---

    The --- line is a static entry and is always present. Dynamic entries appear only after traffic. show ip nat statistics lists the inside and outside interfaces; check they are the right way round. clear ip nat translation * empties dynamic entries.

    Grader gotchas for NAT

    • ip nat inside and ip nat outside swapped.
    • ACL permits the wrong subnet or uses a subnet mask instead of a wildcard.
    • Outside router has no route back to the inside global address (it should not need a route to the private range).
    PreviousStandard and extended ACLsNextOSPFv2 single-area basics
    PT

    OSPFv2 single-area basics

    jump:pt-adv-ospf

    Fast path

    1. On each router, start OSPF with the given process ID and router ID, and advertise each connected network:

      configure terminal
router ospf <process-id>
router-id <router-id>
network <network-address> <wildcard-mask> area 0
passive-interface <interface>
end
write memory

    2. Repeat the network line for every directly connected network the task lists.

    3. Check neighbors reach FULL and routes appear:

      show ip ospf neighbor
show ip route ospf

    #Advertise networks with network or interface commands

    Method Example
    Network and wildcard network 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 area 0
    Exact interface IP network 192.168.10.1 0.0.0.0 area 0
    Interface command interface g0/0/0 then ip ospf 10 area 0

    Use the method the task shows. The process ID is local to the router; use the task's number.

    #Set router ID, passive interfaces and the default route

    In router configuration mode (router ospf <process-id>):

    Command Purpose
    router-id <router-id> Fixed router ID (dotted, for example 1.1.1.1)
    passive-interface <interface> No hellos out a LAN port; the network is still advertised
    passive-interface default then no passive-interface <interface> Passive everywhere except the links to neighbors
    default-information originate Share this router's default route (it must have one)
    auto-cost reference-bandwidth 1000 Cost based on 1 Gbps; set on every router

    A new router ID on a running process needs clear ip ospf process (it asks for confirmation; type it by hand and answer yes) or a save and reload.

    #Verify OSPF

    Expected output:

    R1#show ip ospf neighbor
Neighbor ID     Pri   State           Dead Time   Address         Interface
2.2.2.2           1   FULL/DR         00:00:36    10.1.1.2        GigabitEthernet0/0/1
3.3.3.3           0   FULL/  -        00:00:33    10.1.3.2        Serial0/1/0

    show ip route ospf lists O routes (and O*E2 for a shared default). show ip protocols shows the router ID, the networks and the passive interfaces.

    Grader gotchas for OSPF

    • Wildcard typed as a subnet mask.
    • The link between routers made passive: no neighbor forms.
    • Area typed as 1 on one side of a link.
    • Hello or dead timers changed on one side only.
    PreviousNAT and PAT basicsNextWireless router security with WPA2 Enterprise
    PT

    Wireless router security with WPA2 Enterprise

    jump:pt-adv-wireless-home

    Fast path

    1. Do the basic SSID, WPA2 Personal and admin password setup from wireless router and access point if the task asks for Personal.
    2. For WPA2 Enterprise, set the router: GUI > Wireless > Wireless Security, Security Mode WPA2 Enterprise, Encryption AES, RADIUS Server = the server's IP, Shared Secret = the task's secret. Click Save Settings.
    3. On the Server-PT: Services > AAA, Service On, add the wireless router as a client and add each user (server side).
    4. On each client, set WPA2 Enterprise with the user's name and password (client).
    5. Ping from a wireless client to the router LAN IP.

    #Set WPA2 Enterprise on the wireless router

    Field (Wireless > Wireless Security) Value
    Security Mode WPA2 Enterprise
    Encryption AES
    RADIUS Server Server IP from the addressing table
    RADIUS Port 1812 (default; change only if told)
    Shared Secret Exact secret from the task

    On the HomeRouter-PT-AC set it for each radio band the task names. In the Config tab the same settings are under the Wireless interface as Authentication WPA2, with RADIUS server and secret fields.

    #Set up the RADIUS server on a Server-PT

    1. Open the server, Services > AAA, set Service On.
    2. Network Configuration: Client Name = wireless router name, Client IP = the router's LAN IP (the address the RADIUS request comes from), Secret = the shared secret, ServerType = Radius. Click Add.
    3. User Setup: Username and Password for each user in the task. Click Add.

    The server must be reachable from the router's LAN IP. Usernames and passwords are case-sensitive.

    #Tune channel and radio settings

    Wireless > Basic Wireless Settings: set Network Mode, Standard Channel and Channel Width only as asked. Non-overlapping 2.4 GHz channels are 1, 6 and 11. Click Save Settings.

    Grader gotchas for wireless routers

    • Save Settings not clicked on one page.
    • Secret differs between router and server, or the server's client IP is not the router's LAN IP.
    • Only one band configured on a dual-band router when the task listed both.
    • Clients still on the old SSID or security; reconfigure each one.
    PreviousOSPFv2 single-area basicsNextWireless LAN controller WLANs
    PT

    Wireless LAN controller WLANs

    jump:pt-adv-wlc

    Fast path

    1. From the admin PC on the management subnet, open Desktop > Web Browser and go to https://<wlc-ip>. Log in with the task's credentials.
    2. If the WLAN needs its own VLAN, create the interface first: Controller > Interfaces > New (interface).
    3. WLANs > Create New > Go: Profile Name, SSID, ID. Apply. Tick Enabled and set Interface/Interface Group(G). Apply.
    4. Security > Layer 2: WPA+WPA2, WPA2 Policy, AES; Authentication Key Management PSK with the passphrase, or 802.1X with a RADIUS server under AAA Servers. Apply.
    5. Click Save Configuration (top right), then connect a wireless host and check it gets an address in the WLAN's subnet.

    The steps follow the SRWE 13.2.7 and 13.3.12 PT activities. In those files the WLC GUI is at https://192.168.200.254 with admin / Cisco123; use the values your task gives.

    #Create a dynamic interface for the WLAN VLAN

    1. Controller > Interfaces > New.
    2. Interface Name (for example WLAN-5) and VLAN Id (5). Apply.
    3. Port Number (1 in SRWE), IP Address, Netmask, Gateway (the router subinterface for that VLAN), Primary DHCP Server. Apply, then OK on the warning.
    4. Save Configuration.

    The switch port to the WLC must be a trunk that allows this VLAN and the management VLAN, and the router needs a subinterface (or SVI) for the VLAN.

    #Create and secure a WLAN

    Tab Field Value
    WLANs > New Type, Profile Name, SSID, ID WLAN, exact name, exact SSID, ID from task
    General Status Enabled (easy to miss)
    General Interface/Interface Group(G) The dynamic interface, for example WLAN-5
    Security > Layer 2 Layer 2 Security WPA+WPA2
    Security > Layer 2 WPA2 Policy, WPA2 Encryption Ticked, AES
    Security > Layer 2 Authentication Key Management PSK (then PSK Format ASCII and the passphrase) or 802.1X
    Advanced FlexConnect Local Switching, Local Auth Ticked in the SRWE files when the task says so

    Click Apply on each tab.

    #Add a RADIUS server for WPA2 Enterprise

    1. Security > AAA > RADIUS > Authentication > New: Server IP Address, Shared Secret and Confirm. Apply.
    2. WLANs > click the WLAN ID > Security > Layer 2: Authentication Key Management 802.1X.
    3. Security > AAA Servers: Authentication Servers, Server 1 = the RADIUS server. Apply.
    4. On the RADIUS Server-PT, add the WLC as an AAA client (its management IP and the same secret) and add the users.

    #Configure the WLC internal DHCP scope

    1. Controller > Interfaces > management: set Primary DHCP Server to the WLC management IP. Apply.
    2. Controller > Internal DHCP Server > DHCP Scope > New: name it (SRWE uses Wired Management). Apply.
    3. Open the scope: Pool Start and End Address, Network, Netmask, Default Routers, Status Enabled. Apply.
    4. Save Configuration. The LAPs then get addresses and build their CAPWAP tunnels (Fast Forward Time helps).

    #Add an SNMP trap receiver

    Management > SNMP > Trap Receivers > New: Community Name and IP Address. Apply.

    #Verify the WLC

    • Monitor > Summary: Access Point Summary shows the APs as up. Click Detail next to All APs.
    • WLANs list: the WLAN shows Enabled with the right SSID and security ([WPA2][Auth(PSK)] or [WPA2][Auth(802.1X)]).
    • Wireless host: ipconfig shows an address in the WLAN's VLAN subnet, and it can ping its gateway.

    Grader gotchas for WLCs

    • Enabled not ticked on the WLAN.
    • Interface left as management instead of the WLAN's interface, so clients get management-subnet addresses.
    • Save Configuration not clicked; a WLC reload loses the change.
    • Profile Name and SSID are separate graded values; do not mix them up.
    • LAP has no power: in the Physical tab add its power adapter if the switch port does not supply PoE.
    PreviousWireless router security with WPA2 EnterpriseNextEnd device configuration for later rounds
    PT

    End device configuration for later rounds

    jump:pt-adv-endpoints

    Fast path

    1. Open the device, Desktop > IP Configuration. Set IPv4 Static or DHCP as the task says, then fill address, mask, gateway and DNS exactly.
    2. In the IPv6 part, choose Automatic (SLAAC or DHCPv6) or Static with address, prefix length and gateway (often FE80::1).
    3. For wireless clients, use Config > Wireless0 or Desktop > PC Wireless to join the SSID with the right security.

    4. Check with Command Prompt:

      ipconfig /all

    The basic PC steps are in PCs, laptops and servers.

    #Join a WPA2 Personal network

    Config > Wireless0: SSID (exact), Authentication WPA2-PSK, PSK Pass Phrase, Encryption AES. Then set IP Configuration to DHCP. Or Desktop > PC Wireless > Connect tab, pick the SSID, Connect, enter the key.

    #Join a WPA2 Enterprise network

    Config > Wireless0: SSID, Authentication WPA2, User ID and Password from the task, Encryption AES. IP Configuration DHCP.

    Desktop > PC Wireless > Profiles > New, name the profile, select the network, Advanced Setup, Next, DHCP, Next, Security WPA2-Enterprise, Next, enter the login name and password, Next, Save, then Connect to Network.

    #Point hosts at the right gateway

    Topology PC IPv4 gateway PC IPv6 gateway
    One router LAN Router interface IP Router link-local (for example FE80::1) or its global address
    Router-on-a-stick That VLAN's subinterface IP That subinterface's link-local
    Layer 3 switch That VLAN's SVI IP SVI link-local
    HSRP The virtual IP Task value
    Home wireless router Router LAN IP (from DHCP) From the router

    Grader gotchas for end devices

    • DNS server field left empty when the table lists one.
    • Mask left at the auto-filled /24 default when the subnet is /26 or /27.
    • A PC set to DHCP still holding a 169.254 address: click Fast Forward Time, or toggle Static and back to DHCP.
    • IPv6 Static chosen when the task wanted Automatic, or the prefix length box left empty.
    PreviousWireless LAN controller WLANsNextTroubleshooting method for Packet Tracer networks
    PT

    Troubleshooting method for Packet Tracer networks

    jump:pt-adv-troubleshoot

    Fast path

    1. Ping from the failing PC to its gateway. If that fails, the problem is local (Layers 1-2 or host config). If it works, the problem is beyond the gateway (routing, ACL, NAT, far side).

    2. Run the four show commands on each device on the path:

      show ip interface brief
show vlan brief
show interfaces trunk
show ip route

    3. Compare every value with the addressing table and the task, digit by digit.

    4. Fix one thing, then ping again before changing anything else.
    5. Save with write memory after each fix.

    #Work up the layers

    Layer Check Command Bad looks like Fix
    1 Physical Link lights, interface state show ip interface brief, show interfaces status Red light, administratively down, down down, notconnect, err-disabled no shutdown, right cable and port, recover err-disabled
    2 Access port Port VLAN show vlan brief, show interfaces <interface> switchport PC port in VLAN 1 or the wrong VLAN, VLAN missing switchport access vlan <vlan-id>, create the VLAN
    2 Trunk Trunking, native, allowed show interfaces trunk Port missing from the output, native mismatch message, VLAN not in allowed list Static trunk both ends, match native, fix allowed list
    2 STP and channels Blocking, bundles show spanning-tree vlan <vlan-id>, show etherchannel summary Port BLK on the only path, Po1(SD), members (s) Fix channel modes and member settings
    2 Security Port security, snooping show port-security, show ip dhcp snooping Secure-shutdown, violation count rising, uplink not trusted Raise maximum, clear the port, trust uplink
    3 Addressing IPs, masks, gateways show ip interface brief, PC ipconfig /all Wrong subnet, wrong mask, gateway missing, 169.254 Correct values from the table
    3 Routing Routes both ways show ip route, show ipv6 route No C for a LAN, no route to the far network, no default route Static route, OSPF network, ip routing on a 3650
    3 Neighbors OSPF, HSRP show ip ospf neighbor, show standby brief No neighbor, both HSRP routers Active or Init Fix area, wildcard, passive interface, group or virtual IP
    3-4 Filtering ACL, NAT show access-lists, show ip nat translations Deny counter rising, no translations Fix ACE order, direction, inside/outside
    7 Services DHCP, DNS, SSH, web show ip dhcp binding, show ip ssh, PC nslookup No leases, SSH disabled, name not found Pool, helper address, keys, DNS record

    #Read the symptom

    Symptom Most likely
    PC cannot ping its own gateway Wrong VLAN on the port, port shut, trunk missing the VLAN, wrong IP or mask, subinterface VLAN typo
    PC pings gateway, not the far LAN Missing route on a router (either direction), ACL, far-side host gateway wrong
    Destination host unreachable from a router That router has no route to the destination
    Pings work by IP, not by name DNS server missing on PC, or DNS record missing on the server
    Some VLANs work across the trunk, others do not Allowed VLAN list or the VLAN not created on one switch
    Everything broke after a security change Port security max too low, DHCP snooping uplink not trusted, ACL missing a final permit, DAI on static hosts
    HSRP pair both Active Routers cannot reach each other on that LAN, or group or version mismatch
    First ping drops one or two replies Normal ARP; ping again

    #Troubleshooting challenge routine

    1. Treat the addressing table and VLAN table as correct; the devices are what is wrong.
    2. Collect show running-config from every device into a text editor and compare line by line with the tables.
    3. Make a list of every difference before fixing anything. Activities like ITN 17.8.3 and SRWE 4.4.8 hide several faults per device.
    4. Fix, ping, save, and check the completion percentage after each fix.
    5. Look for these common planted faults: wrong mask, swapped interface addresses, shutdown on an interface, wrong VLAN on an access port, trunk native or allowed mismatch, wrong encapsulation dot1Q number, missing ip routing, wrong next hop, wrong gateway on a PC or switch, wrong DNS server.
    Divide and conquer when the path is long

    Ping from the middle of the path (a router's own interfaces with ping <ip-address> source <interface>) to split the problem in half. If the router can reach the destination from its LAN interface address, the problem is between the PC and that router.

    PT

    Multi-device config templates for later rounds

    jump:pt-adv-templates

    Fast path

    1. Pick the template that matches the topology and copy it into a text editor.
    2. Replace every <...> value from the addressing and VLAN tables. Delete lines the task does not ask for.
    3. In the device CLI, type enable so the prompt ends in #, then click Paste.
    4. Scroll back and fix any line that starts with %.
    5. Run the verify commands under the template, then the device-security block from the secure baselines if the task wants it.

    Every block starts with configure terminal and ends with end and write memory. The baseline security lines (hostname, enable secret, SSH, banner) are in copy-paste config templates; paste that first, then the block here. Values typed into a placeholder on this page fill every block that uses the same name, so fill one device, paste, then change values for the next.

    REF

    Common ports and services

    jump:ref-ports

    To see what is listening on a port and which program owns it, use Program listening on a port.

    Port Protocol Service Notes for hardening
    20, 21 TCP FTP (data, control) Cleartext. Remove unless the README requires it; then disable anonymous login and require TLS.
    22 TCP SSH / SFTP Keep if required and harden sshd_config.
    23 TCP Telnet Cleartext remote shell. Remove.
    25 TCP SMTP Mail server. Remove if not required.
    53 TCP/UDP DNS Server role. Restrict zone transfers.
    67, 68 UDP DHCP server, client
    69 UDP TFTP No authentication. Remove.
    80 TCP HTTP Web server (Apache, nginx, IIS).
    88 TCP/UDP Kerberos Normal on a domain controller.
    110 TCP POP3 Cleartext mail.
    111 TCP/UDP rpcbind / portmapper Remove unless NFS is required.
    123 UDP NTP Time sync.
    135 TCP Microsoft RPC Normal on Windows.
    137-139 UDP/TCP NetBIOS Legacy Windows file sharing.
    143 TCP IMAP Cleartext mail.
    161, 162 UDP SNMP Remove unless required. Default community strings (public, private) are a finding.
    389, 636 TCP LDAP, LDAPS Domain controller.
    443 TCP HTTPS
    445 TCP SMB File sharing. Disable SMBv1.
    514 UDP Syslog
    631 TCP CUPS / IPP printing Linux printing. Remove if not needed.
    873 TCP rsync
    993, 995 TCP IMAPS, POP3S
    1433 TCP Microsoft SQL Server
    2049 TCP/UDP NFS
    3268, 3269 TCP Global Catalog Normal on a domain controller.
    3306 TCP MySQL / MariaDB Bind to 127.0.0.1 unless remote access is required.
    3389 TCP/UDP RDP Disable unless the README requires it; then require NLA.
    4444 TCP Metasploit default / common backdoor Investigate any listener.
    5353 UDP mDNS (avahi-daemon on Linux) Often removable on Mint if not needed.
    5432 TCP PostgreSQL
    5900+ TCP VNC Remote desktop. Remove unless required.
    5985, 5986 TCP WinRM HTTP, HTTPS
    8080, 8443 TCP Alternate HTTP, HTTPS, proxies Investigate.
    1337, 6667, 31337 TCP Common backdoor / IRC Investigate any listener.
